title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄序
皇上奉
天御極建元隆慶歲丁卯秋八月
適天下大比期先是陳事者
上言頃歲敎陵士競爲剽說
徼摯發洎試之理率不效方
今
===
聖作物覩敦尚本實宜
令中外執事文學官少正文體
兾裨實用
詔下禮官議可維時監察御史王
宗載奉
命按行閩事比抵所部則首以
明詔詔之閩士負鐫緣飾者自是
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄序

皇上奉天御極，建元隆慶。歲丁卯，秋八月，適天下大比期。先是，陳事者上言：「頃歲敎陵，士競爲剽說，徼摯發，洎試之理，率不效。方今聖作物覩，敦尚本實，宜令中外執事文學官少正文體，兾裨實用。」詔下禮官議可。維時監察御史王宗載奉命按行閩事，比抵所部，則首以明詔詔之。閩士負鐫緣飾者，自是
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

His Majesty, receiving Heaven’s mandate, ascended the throne and inaugurated the Longqing reign. In the eighth month of autumn in the dingmao year [1567], the time arrived for the triennial examinations throughout the realm. Earlier, someone submitting observations on affairs had memorialized: “In recent years, instruction has declined, and scholars have competed in producing derivative arguments, seeking distinction thereby [?]; when these are put to the test in government [?], they generally prove ineffective. Now that the sage has arisen and all look to him, placing firm emphasis on fundamentals and substance, the officials responsible for literary learning at court and in the provinces should be ordered to make some correction to literary style, in the hope of contributing to practical use.” An imperial edict referred the matter to the ritual officials, who deliberated and approved it.

At that time, Investigating Censor Wang Zongzai had received orders to conduct an inspection of affairs in Fujian. Upon reaching his jurisdiction, his first action was to proclaim the imperial edict to its people. From that time onward, those Fujian scholars who relied on elaborate literary carving and embellishment [?] …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
烝烝然知
皇上釐文務實意矣屆期萏等以
前御史胡維新聘來自四方
乃以萏曁敎授吳迪主試事
敎授何文明敎諭吳佐張篚
伍典鄭如瑾劉正綵同考試
事提調則左布政使劉光濟
===
左叅政楊準監試則按察使
劉子興副使宋儀望而御史
王宗載寔監臨焉諸凡耆事
之臣則旣簡於有位稽諸往
實益浚且恪矣御史乃前誓
衆曰際
熙時舉懿典人臣重負也有不協
punctuated: 烝烝然知皇上釐文務實意矣。屆期，萏等以前御史胡維新聘，來自四方，乃以萏曁敎授吳迪主試事，敎授何文明、敎諭吳佐、張篚、伍典、鄭如瑾、劉正綵同考試事。提調則左布政使劉光濟、左叅政楊準，監試則按察使劉子興、副使宋儀望，而御史王宗載寔監臨焉。諸凡耆事之臣，則旣簡於有位，稽諸往實，益浚且恪矣。御史乃前誓衆曰：「際熙時，舉懿典，人臣重負也。有不協
translation_en: …increasingly came to understand His Majesty’s intention to rectify literary writing and emphasize substance. When the appointed time arrived, Dan 萏 [?] and the others came from various regions at the invitation of the former Investigating Censor Hu Weixin. Dan and Prefectural School Professor Wu Di were then appointed Examiners; Prefectural School Professor He Wenming and County School Instructors Wu Zuo, Zhang Fei, Wu Dian, Zheng Rujin, and Liu Zhengcai served as Associate Examiners. The Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Liu Guangji and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Yang Zhun. Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Liu Zixing and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Song Yiwang supervised the examination proceedings, while Investigating Censor Wang Zongzai served as Supervising Official. All the officials charged with these duties [?] had been selected from among incumbent officeholders; measured against past practice, their work was still more thorough and conscientious [?]. The Investigating Censor then stepped forward and solemnly charged the assembled officials: “To conduct this splendid institution in an age of flourishing governance is a weighty responsibility for the sovereign’s servants. If anyone fails to accord with…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
於慎者大義謂何衆跫然以
諾遂進提學副使蔡國珍所
選士二千七百有奇如例試
之得人九十乃詮名氏幷文
之粹者籍
獻之御史授簡俾苘颺言以冠
其端苘不佞顧惟人才之汚
===
隆壹稟於世道自漢下逮緣
世屢遷姑毋論已三代盛時
周稱多士乃仲尼持議於數
百載後則惟上嘉唐虞以爲
僅一再見何者聖聖迭興道
化龐溢固其所漬漸者然哉
明自
punctuated:
於慎者，大義謂何？」衆跫然以諾。遂進提學副使蔡國珍所選士二千七百有奇，如例試之，得人九十。乃詮名氏，幷文之粹者，籍獻之。御史授簡，俾苘颺言以冠其端。
苘不佞，顧惟人才之汚隆，壹稟於世道。自漢下逮，緣世屢遷，姑毋論已。三代盛時，周稱多士，乃仲尼持議於數百載後，則惟上嘉唐虞，以爲僅一再見。何者？聖聖迭興，道化龐溢，固其所漬漸者然哉！明自
translation_en:
…with due care, what would that mean for the great moral obligation?” The assembled men eagerly voiced their assent. They then admitted the more than 2,700 candidates selected by Cai Guozhen, Vice Commissioner for Education, and examined them according to the established regulations, selecting ninety men. Their names, together with the finest of their compositions, were then compiled into a register and respectfully submitted. The Investigating Censor handed me writing tablets and charged me, Qing [?], to set forth some words to stand at its beginning.
Though lacking ability, I, Qing [?], reflect that the decline and flourishing of human talent depend entirely upon the moral condition of the age. From the Han onward, talent repeatedly changed with the times; let us leave that aside for now. During the flourishing Three Dynasties, the Zhou was renowned for its many worthy men. Yet Zhongni, judging several hundred years later, reserved his praise for the still earlier ages of Tang and Yu, considering such abundance to have appeared only once or twice. Why was this? Sages arose in succession, and the transforming influence of the Way spread abundantly: surely it was immersion in this influence that made it so! The Ming, from …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
二祖啓運
列聖相承人文炳著肆我
皇上聰明仁孝天縱
聖神繼體
先皇德妙符合頃者
嗣膺寶曆崇奬儒碩徵佚起廢開
經筵興禮樂天下人士莫不回
===
面拭目以覩
大聖人所作爲此卽勳華顯承之
際無以加者精醇所鍾淑喆
挺出故𬙊幸從執事後博觀
閩士之文則見其指閎而深
體疏而實攄布乎詩書禮樂
之華根極乎道德性命之奧
punctuated: 二祖啓運，列聖相承，人文炳著。肆我皇上聰明仁孝，天縱聖神，繼體先皇，德妙符合。頃者嗣膺寶曆，崇奬儒碩，徵佚起廢，開經筵，興禮樂，天下人士莫不回面拭目，以覩大聖人所作爲。此卽勳華顯承之際無以加者。精醇所鍾，淑喆挺出。故𬙊幸從執事後，博觀閩士之文，則見其指閎而深，體疏而實，攄布乎詩書禮樂之華，根極乎道德性命之奧，
translation_en: …the two founding ancestors inaugurated the dynasty’s destiny, and successive sage rulers carried it forward, making literary culture shine resplendently. Now our Emperor, intelligent, humane, and filial, endowed by Heaven with sagely insight, has succeeded the late Emperor and matches him perfectly in virtue. Recently, upon assuming the imperial succession, he has honored and encouraged eminent Confucian scholars, summoned those living in retirement, recalled those dismissed from office, inaugurated the Classics Colloquium, and promoted rites and music. Throughout the realm, scholars have turned toward him and wiped their eyes, eager to behold what the great sage will accomplish. Even the illustrious succession from Yao to Shun could not surpass this occasion. Wherever these purest influences concentrate, worthy and wise men emerge preeminent. Thus I, 𬙊 [name unclear], fortunate to follow in the service of the officials conducting the examination, have surveyed the writings of Fujian’s scholars extensively. I find their purport broad and profound, their composition spacious yet substantial. They unfold the splendors of poetry, documents, rites, and music, and reach to the deepest mysteries of the Way, virtue, human nature, and Heaven’s mandate…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
曉鬯
國體貫洽時務羣言浩穰悉軌
於正繇其文以辨其材蓋
聖世之盛後唐虞成周而繼見者
也夫閩古南粤地也禹貢不
志其域職方不齒其名雖唐
虞帝德光天海隅黎庶莫不
===
共臣成周化行南國至使中
林野人可為公侯腹心而閩
獨未與有宋開先賢哲始出
乃今虺谿蜃壑類能組文譚
藝尊信俎豆之業且其承風
嚮治尤能稡就本實而使文
獻甲於天下概其極蓋將軼
punctuated:
曉鬯國體，貫洽時務，羣言浩穰，悉軌於正。繇其文以辨其材，蓋聖世之盛，後唐虞成周而繼見者也。
夫閩，古南粤地也。禹貢不志其域，職方不齒其名。雖唐虞帝德光天，海隅黎庶莫不共臣；成周化行南國，至使中林野人可為公侯腹心，而閩獨未與。有宋開先，賢哲始出。乃今虺谿蜃壑，類能組文譚藝，尊信俎豆之業。且其承風嚮治，尤能稡就本實，而使文獻甲於天下。概其極，蓋將軼
translation_en:
…clearly comprehend the principles of government and thoroughly understand the affairs of the age. Their writings are vast and abundant, yet all follow the correct path. Judging their talents by their writing, this is surely a flowering of a sage’s age such as has appeared again in succession to the ages of Tang and Yu and the flourishing Zhou.
Now Min was anciently part of Nanyue. The “Tribute of Yu” does not record its territory, nor does the “Offices of the Regions” list its name. Although the imperial virtue of Tang and Yu illuminated all beneath Heaven, and the common people even at the ocean’s edge all became their subjects; and although the civilizing influence of the flourishing Zhou spread through the southern lands, so that even rustics dwelling in the forests could become trusted confidants of dukes and marquises, Min alone had no share in this. The Song dynasty opened the way, and worthy and wise men began to emerge. Now, even among its serpent-haunted streams and clam-filled ravines, people generally can compose elegant writing and discuss literary arts, reverently embracing the learning associated with ritual vessels. Moreover, in receiving the civilizing influence and turning toward good government, they are especially able to gather their efforts around fundamentals and substance, making their cultural achievements and worthy men foremost in the realm. Judging the ultimate extent of this development, it will surely surpass…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
盛際而駕之矣此其故何
主德茂而敎化醇也往者閩疆不
靖農棄其畚工稅其刃漁師
賈客罷寘宿資祗今還定安
集稍稍憩趾而徵輸露布昕
夕猶厪士獨保其故有槧簡
之功不奪於戈鋌咕吟之聲
===
不輟於枹鼓文明駿赫視古
昔毋少卻此豈有司能自求
多於諸士哉三路置堠五寨
設守
聖天子所以奠麗爾疆而佑啓人
文者惠至渥也諸士遊
帝王之世席太平之澤躡風雲之
punctuated: 盛際而駕之矣。此其故何？主德茂而敎化醇也。往者閩疆不靖，農棄其畚，工稅其刃，漁師賈客罷寘宿資。祗今還定安集，稍稍憩趾，而徵輸露布，昕夕猶厪。士獨保其故有，槧簡之功不奪於戈鋌，咕吟之聲不輟於枹鼓，文明駿赫，視古昔毋少卻。此豈有司能自求多於諸士哉？三路置堠，五寨設守，聖天子所以奠麗爾疆而佑啓人文者，惠至渥也。諸士遊帝王之世，席太平之澤，躡風雲之
translation_en: …surpass even the ages of greatest flourishing. What accounts for this? The sovereign’s virtue is abundant, and his transforming instruction is pure. Formerly, when Fujian’s territory was troubled, farmers abandoned their baskets, artisans laid down their blades, and fishermen and merchants ceased their work, setting aside their accumulated resources [?]. Now order has been restored and the people settled in peace; little by little they have gained respite. Yet levies, transport obligations, and military dispatches still cause concern morning and evening. The scholars alone have preserved their former pursuits: their labors with writing tablets and books have not been displaced by spears and javelins, nor have their voices in recitation [?] been silenced by the beating of war drums. Literary culture shines brilliantly, falling not the least short of antiquity. Could the responsible officials themselves possibly claim much credit for these scholars’ achievements? Watchposts have been established along the three routes, and defenses stationed at the five fortified camps. These are the means by which the sagely Son of Heaven secures your territory and fosters the flowering of literary culture: his beneficence is most generous. You scholars live in the age of an imperial sovereign, enjoy the blessings of great peace, and ride the winds and clouds of …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
會今旣與諸前哲接軫擊轂
矣然尚等之所以執筴而錄
之者文也視其文則人人能
矣異日通籍服官展采錯事
庳而效一命崇而翊
萬機外之則疆塲萌庶之繁内之
則鈞軸安攘之大言當其事
===
功副其期跡不違心履不愆
素勳望名實直與師師濟濟
者相揖讓則豈直士有休問
卽
國家且賴之主司亦可藉是以
報
天子矣若乃庸違其言學博行僞
punctuated: 會，今旣與諸前哲接軫擊轂矣。然尚等之所以執筴而錄之者，文也。視其文，則人人能矣。異日通籍服官，展采錯事，庳而效一命，崇而翊萬機，外之則疆塲萌庶之繁，内之則鈞軸安攘之大，言當其事，功副其期，跡不違心，履不愆素，勳望名實，直與師師濟濟者相揖讓，則豈直士有休問？卽國家且賴之，主司亦可藉是以報天子矣。若乃庸違其言，學博行僞，
translation_en: …opportunity, you have now joined the worthy men of earlier times, your carriage rails touching and your wheel hubs meeting theirs. Yet what has led us, Shang and his colleagues, to take up our tablets and record your names is your writing. Judged by that writing, every one of you is capable. In days to come, when your names enter the official registers and you take office, displaying your abilities and undertaking your duties, you may serve in the lowest rank or rise high to assist with the myriad affairs of government. Outside the capital, you will face the manifold concerns of the frontiers and the common people; within it, the weighty responsibilities of central government, securing peace at home and repelling threats from abroad. If your words suit the affairs at hand, your achievements fulfill expectations, your outward deeds accord with your hearts, and your conduct does not depart from your longstanding principles; if, in merit and reputation, name and substance, you stand as peers of those many worthy officials who emulate one another—then will it merely be you scholars who enjoy a fine reputation? The state itself will depend upon you, and those presiding over the examination may thereby repay the Emperor. But if your conduct contradicts your words, and your learning is broad while your actions are false…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
雖仲尼所嘆材盛之世猶不
免焉苟於諸士顧敢以其文
之有斐也而遂快然無懼耶
玉卮無當賤於瓦缶大阿不
割不直鉛刀甘言餌進無裨
世用甚或程行於不肖名實
偵悖而棄之則諸士之自鑿
===
於
國恩者厚矣事事者又安所逭
其責哉吾聞天以元命鼓鑄
羣品罔不含苞吐英應其時
也人以元日彈冠結綬錯酬
賡拜重其新也
皇上建元一詔至治煥然更新海
punctuated:
雖仲尼所嘆材盛之世，猶不免焉。苟於諸士，顧敢以其文之有斐也，而遂快然無懼耶？玉卮無當，賤於瓦缶；大阿不割，不直鉛刀。甘言餌進，無裨世用，甚或程行於不肖，名實偵悖而棄之，則諸士之自鑿於國恩者厚矣。事事者又安所逭其責哉？
吾聞天以元命鼓鑄羣品，罔不含苞吐英，應其時也；人以元日彈冠結綬，錯酬賡拜，重其新也。皇上建元，一詔至治，煥然更新，海
translation_en:
… Even in the age of abundant talent admired by Zhongni [Confucius], such failings could not be avoided. As for these gentlemen, dare we, merely because their writings are brilliant, become complacent and free of apprehension? A jade cup without a bottom is worth less than an earthenware jar; a Tai’e sword that cannot cut is worth less than a leaden knife. If they use pleasing words as bait for advancement, contribute nothing to the needs of the age, and even model their conduct on the unworthy [?], so that their reputations and actual deeds prove contradictory [?] and they are cast aside, then these gentlemen will have gravely cut themselves off from imperial favor. How, moreover, could those administering affairs escape responsibility?
I have heard that Heaven, through its primal mandate, molds the myriad beings, all of which form buds and put forth blossoms in response to their season. On New Year’s Day, people dust off their official caps and tie on their seals’ ribbons, exchanging courtesies and bowing in return, thereby honoring the new beginning. His Majesty has inaugurated a new reign era; with a single edict, consummate governance shines forth and all is renewed, throughout the seas …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
內垂髫載白之輩胥訢訢思
沐膏潤肖翹異質亦皆蕃躍
效靈士當茲世貞元際會脫
迹衡茅依馮
日月之光弼元化豎元功無負
帝臣腹心之選俾後世抽
天府之賢書論讚其盛則如仲尼
===
所以嘉樂唐虞成周者端在
是矣第令居則誦法孔孟出
則見知乎堯舜文武之
君而不以
盛世實用之材自命義將何擇夫
激羽流商不若下里寧爲雲
門突轅弛𨰠不若驪黃寧爲
punctuated: 內垂髫載白之輩，胥訢訢思沐膏潤；肖翹異質，亦皆蕃躍效靈。士當茲世，貞元際會，脫迹衡茅，依馮日月之光，弼元化，豎元功，無負帝臣腹心之選，俾後世抽天府之賢書，論讚其盛，則如仲尼所以嘉樂唐虞成周者，端在是矣。第令居則誦法孔孟，出則見知乎堯舜文武之君，而不以盛世實用之材自命，義將何擇？夫激羽流商，不若下里，寧爲雲門；突轅弛𨰠，不若驪黃，寧爲
translation_en:
…within the realm, young children with hanging forelocks and the white-haired alike rejoice, yearning to bathe in the beneficent rain. Even the smallest creatures, of every kind, flourish and leap, displaying their vitality. Scholars encountering this age, at the juncture of an ending and a new beginning, should emerge from their humble thatched dwellings and rely upon the radiance of the sun and moon—the sovereign. They should assist the great work of transformation and establish great achievements, proving worthy of their selection as the emperor’s trusted servants. Let later generations draw forth the registers of worthy men from the imperial archives and discuss and praise this flourishing age: precisely herein lies what Confucius delighted in and praised in the ages of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the perfected Zhou.
If, however, they merely recite and emulate Confucius and Mencius at home, and on entering service gain recognition from a ruler like Yao, Shun, King Wen, or King Wu, yet do not regard themselves as men of practical ability useful to a flourishing age, what choice would righteousness require? As for stirring the yu notes and sending forth the shang notes, though unequal to the rustic song “Lower Village,” one would rather perform “Cloud Gate” [?]; though thrusting against the carriage shafts and loosening the harness fittings [?], unequal to ordinary black and yellow horses, one would rather be …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
千里尺有所短寸有所長君
子曰寧舍短而取長凡以尚
實也諸士乘時奮藝由玆而
進如欲奉揚
上意以思報稱於萬一舍務實其
奚以哉是舉也提督巡撫右
僉都御史塗澤民輯寧武功
===
振敷文教提督南贛兵部右
侍郎吳百朋風猷遠宣士類
胥勸鎮守總兵官署都督同
知戚繼光整旅襄夷右文禮
士巡按江西等處監察御史
馬明謨奉節來旬觀法斯懋
刑部廣西司署郎中應存卓
punctuated:
千里。尺有所短，寸有所長。君子曰：「寧舍短而取長。」凡以尚實也。諸士乘時奮藝，由玆而進，如欲奉揚上意，以思報稱於萬一，舍務實，其奚以哉？
是舉也，提督巡撫右僉都御史塗澤民輯寧武功，振敷文教；提督南贛兵部右侍郎吳百朋風猷遠宣，士類胥勸；鎮守總兵官署都督同知戚繼光整旅襄夷，右文禮士；巡按江西等處監察御史馬明謨奉節來旬，觀法斯懋；刑部廣西司署郎中應存卓
translation_en:
…a thousand-li steed. A foot has its shortcomings; an inch has its strengths. The gentleman says, “Better to set aside the shortcomings and take the strengths.” All this is to esteem practical substance. You scholars have seized the opportunity to display your accomplishments and advance by this means. If you wish to uphold and carry forward His Majesty’s intentions, seeking to repay even one ten-thousandth of his favor, how could you do so without attending to practical substance?
For this examination, Tu Zemin, Grand Coordinator and Right Assistant Censor-in-chief, secured peace through military achievements and vigorously extended civil education. Wu Baipeng, Supreme Commander of Nan-Gan and Right Vice Minister of War, spread his exemplary influence and guidance far and wide, encouraging all scholars. Qi Jiguang, Regional Commander and Acting Vice Commissioner-in-chief, put his troops in order and subdued the barbarians [?], honored literary learning, and treated scholars with courtesy. Ma Mingmo, Investigating Censor assigned to inspect Jiangxi and other places, came bearing imperial credentials to conduct an inspection [?]; through observing his example, others were further encouraged. Ying Cunzhuo, Acting Director of the Guangxi Bureau in the Ministry of Justice…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
錄讞綏民儀刑攸寓前左布
政使今陞雲南右副都御史
陳大賓始事揆謀具悉成憲
右參政周賢宣副使張鳳來
左參議陳一松右參議李紀
僉事史嗣元袁大誠蘇愚趙
時齊徐作參將王如龍胡守
===
仁遊擊將軍張元勳署都指
揮僉事陳濠羅繼祖錢鳳翔
先後匡賛克成厥功右布政
使劉佃副使羅一道署都指
揮僉事傅應嘉耿宗元以入
賀行僉事黄可大以遷秩行皆
與聞盛媺例併書之
punctuated: 錄讞綏民，儀刑攸寓。前左布政使、今陞雲南右副都御史陳大賓，始事揆謀，具悉成憲。右參政周賢宣、副使張鳳來、左參議陳一松、右參議李紀、僉事史嗣元、袁大誠、蘇愚、趙時齊、徐作、參將王如龍、胡守仁、遊擊將軍張元勳、署都指揮僉事陳濠、羅繼祖、錢鳳翔，先後匡賛，克成厥功。右布政使劉佃、副使羅一道、署都指揮僉事傅應嘉、耿宗元，以入賀行；僉事黄可大，以遷秩行。皆與聞盛媺，例併書之。
translation_en:
…reviewed judicial cases and brought peace to the people, embodying exemplary standards. Chen Dabin, formerly Left Provincial Administration Commissioner and now promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-chief in Yunnan, planned and deliberated at the outset, with full knowledge of the established regulations.

Zhou Xianxuan, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Zhang Fenglai, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Chen Yisong, Left Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Li Ji, Right Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Shi Siyuan, Yuan Dacheng, Su Yu, Zhao Shiqi, and Xu Zuo, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; Wang Rulong and Hu Shouren, Brigade Commanders; Zhang Yuanxun, Mobile Corps Commander; and Chen Hao, Luo Jizu, and Qian Fengxiang, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners, all lent their assistance in succession and brought the undertaking to completion.

Liu Dian, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Luo Yidao, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and Fu Yingjia and Geng Zongyuan, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners, departed to offer congratulations at court. Huang Keda, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner, departed upon promotion. All had participated in this splendid undertaking, and their names are therefore recorded together here in accordance with precedent.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
法語之言能無從乎改之爲貴巽與之言
能無說乎繹之爲貴
齊明盛服非禮不動所以脩身也
原泉混混不舍晝夜盈科而後進放乎四
海有本者如是是之取爾
易
乾元者始而亨者也利貞者性情也乾始
===
能以美利利天下不言所利大矣哉大
哉乾乎剛健中正純粹精也
允升大吉上合志也
問焉而以言其受命也如嚮
黃帝堯舜氏作通其變使民不倦神而化
之使民宜之易窮則變變則通通則久
是以自天祐之吉无不利黃帝堯舜垂
衣裳而天下治蓋取諸乾坤
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

法語之言，能無從乎？改之爲貴。巽與之言，能無說乎？繹之爲貴。

齊明盛服，非禮不動，所以脩身也。

原泉混混，不舍晝夜，盈科而後進，放乎四海。有本者如是，是之取爾。

易

乾元者，始而亨者也；利貞者，性情也。乾始能以美利利天下，不言所利，大矣哉！大哉乾乎！剛健中正，純粹精也。

允升，大吉，上合志也。

問焉而以言，其受命也如嚮。

黃帝堯舜氏作，通其變，使民不倦；神而化之，使民宜之。易窮則變，變則通，通則久。是以自天祐之，吉无不利。黃帝堯舜垂衣裳而天下治，蓋取諸乾坤。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Can one fail to assent to words of sound admonition? What matters is to reform oneself. Can one fail to be pleased by words of gentle agreement? What matters is to draw out their meaning.

Purifying oneself, keeping the mind clear, wearing full ceremonial dress, and making no movement contrary to ritual propriety: these are the means of cultivating oneself.

Water from a spring gushes forth without ceasing, day or night. It fills each hollow before advancing, until it reaches the four seas. Such is that which has a source; this is the quality being commended.

Book of Changes

The primal power of Qian is that which initiates and brings things to fulfillment; its benefit and constancy are its inherent nature and disposition. Through its initiating power, Qian benefits all under Heaven with excellent benefits, without specifying what it benefits. How great it is! Great indeed is Qian: firm and vigorous, central and correct, pure and unalloyed, the very essence.

“Trusted in ascending: great good fortune.” This is because one's purpose accords with that of those above.

When questioned in words, it receives the charge and responds like an echo.

Huangdi, Yao, and Shun arose. They adapted institutions through change, so that the people did not grow weary; they transformed them with wondrous efficacy, so that the people found them fitting. In the Changes, reaching an extremity brings change; change brings passage; passage brings endurance. Thus, “Heaven itself assists him: good fortune, with nothing unfavorable.” Huangdi, Yao, and Shun let their upper and lower garments hang down, and all under Heaven was well governed. They presumably took this from Qian and Kun.

Book of Documents

===
羣黎百姓徧為爾德
文王孫子本支百世凡周之士不顯亦世
貽我來牟帝命率育無此疆爾界陳常于
時夏
春秋
夏單伯會伐宋〔莊公十有四年〕
秋九月齊侯宋公江人黃人盟于貫〔僖公〕
〔二年〕秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于陽穀
〔僖公三年〕
punctuated:
欽若昊天，曆象日月星辰。
惟事事，乃其有備；有備無患。
二、五事：一曰貌，二曰言，三曰視，四曰聽，五曰思。貌曰恭，言曰從，視曰明，聽曰聰，思曰睿。恭作肅，從作乂，明作哲，聰作謀，睿作聖。
政貴有恒，辭尚體要。

詩
彼君子兮，不素餐兮。
羣黎百姓，徧為爾德。
文王孫子，本支百世。凡周之士，不顯亦世。
貽我來牟，帝命率育。無此疆爾界，陳常于時夏。

春秋
夏，單伯會伐宋。〔莊公十有四年〕
秋九月，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫。〔僖公〕〔二年〕秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。〔僖公三年〕
translation_en:
Reverently accord with august Heaven; calculate and observe the sun, moon, stars, and celestial markers.
Attend to every affair, and there will be preparedness; with preparedness, there is no calamity.
Second, the five activities: the first is demeanor; the second, speech; the third, seeing; the fourth, hearing; and the fifth, thinking. Demeanor should be respectful; speech, compliant; vision, clear; hearing, acute; and thought, penetrating. Respect produces gravity; compliance produces orderly government; clear vision produces discernment; acute hearing produces sound deliberation; penetrating thought produces sageliness.
In government, constancy is prized; in speech, substance and concision are esteemed.

Book of Odes
That gentleman does not eat without earning his food.
The multitudes of the common people everywhere emulate your virtue.
The descendants of King Wen, both the main line and its branches, endure for a hundred generations. All the officers of Zhou—are they not illustrious, generation after generation?
He bequeathed to us wheat and barley; the Lord on High commanded that all be nourished. Without distinction between our boundaries and yours, the enduring order was established throughout this land of Xia.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In summer, Shan Bo, Earl of Shan, joined the campaign against Song. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Zhuang〕
In autumn, in the ninth month, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang made a covenant at Guan. 〔Duke Xi〕〔Second year〕 In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu. 〔Third year of Duke Xi〕

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
齊人侵我西鄙公追齊師至酅弗及僖公
二十有六年
冬公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕
子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭十
有二月已亥同盟于戲襄公九年夏公
會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷定公十年
禮記
司會以歲之成質於天子冢宰齊戒受質
大樂正大司寇市三官以其成從質於
===
天子大司徒大司馬大司空齊戒受質
百官各以其成質於三官大司徒大司
馬大司空以百官之成質於天子百官
齊戒受質
君子曰大德不官大道不器大信不約大
時不齊察於此四者可以有志於本矣
故樂行而倫清耳目聰明血氣和平移風
易俗天下皆寧
讓之三也象月之三日而成魄也
punctuated:
齊人侵我西鄙，公追齊師至酅，弗及。僖公二十有六年。
冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月，已亥，同盟于戲。襄公九年。夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。定公十年。
禮記
司會以歲之成質於天子，冢宰齊戒受質。大樂正、大司寇，市三官以其成從質於天子，大司徒、大司馬、大司空齊戒受質。百官各以其成質於三官，大司徒、大司馬、大司空以百官之成質於天子，百官齊戒受質。
君子曰：「大德不官，大道不器，大信不約，大時不齊。察於此四者，可以有志於本矣。」
故樂行而倫清，耳目聰明，血氣和平，移風易俗，天下皆寧。
讓之三也，象月之三日而成魄也。
translation_en:
The men of Qi invaded our western borderlands. The duke pursued the army of Qi as far as Xi but failed to catch it. The twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi.

In winter, the duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Xiaozhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, in attacking Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the day yihai [?], they concluded a joint covenant at Xi. The ninth year of Duke Xiang. In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu. The tenth year of Duke Ding.

Record of Rites

The Controller of Accounts submits the year's accomplishments to the Son of Heaven for assessment; the Grand Administrator purifies himself and fasts to receive the assessment. The Grand Music Master and the Minister of Justice—the text here reads “market, three officials” [?]—follow in submitting their accomplishments to the Son of Heaven for assessment. The Minister of Education, the Minister of War, and the Minister of Works purify themselves and fast to receive the assessment. The hundred officials each submit their accomplishments to these three ministers for assessment. The Minister of Education, the Minister of War, and the Minister of Works submit the accomplishments of the hundred officials to the Son of Heaven for assessment; the hundred officials purify themselves and fast to receive the assessment.

The gentleman says: “Great virtue is not confined to a particular office; the great Way is not confined to a particular implement; great trustworthiness requires no covenant; the great seasons do not proceed uniformly. By examining these four things, one may direct one's aspirations toward the fundamental.”

Thus, when music is practiced, human relationships become clear, the ears and eyes become keen, the blood and vital energies become harmonious and balanced, prevailing ways and customs are transformed, and all under Heaven is at peace.

Yielding precedence three times symbolizes the moon's forming its dark body on the third day.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
第貳場
論
君子深造之以道
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢始置五經博士詔〔建元五年〕
擬唐以李靖等爲黜陟大使分行天下誥
〔貞觀八年〕
擬宋學士孫奭進無逸圖表〔天聖五年〕
判語〔五條〕
===
增減官文書
市司評物價
宿衞人兵仗
老幼不考訊
造作不如法
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問二帝三王神聖皆天授也迺猶稽古敬
學惟日不足豈惟其心好之卽君師天
punctuated:
第貳場

論：君子深造之以道。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕：擬漢始置五經博士詔〔建元五年〕；擬唐以李靖等爲黜陟大使分行天下誥〔貞觀八年〕；擬宋學士孫奭進無逸圖表〔天聖五年〕。

判語〔五條〕：增減官文書；市司評物價；宿衞人兵仗；老幼不考訊；造作不如法。

第叁場

策〔五道〕

問：二帝三王，神聖皆天授也，迺猶稽古敬學，惟日不足，豈惟其心好之？卽君師天
translation_en:
Second Session

Discourse: “The gentleman pursues profound attainment by following the Way.”

Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔one topic in this category [?]〕:
Compose an edict in the voice of the Han emperor on first establishing Erudites for the Five Classics 〔fifth year of Jianyuan〕.
Compose a proclamation in the voice of the Tang emperor appointing Li Jing and others as Commissioners for Demotion and Promotion, to travel separately throughout the realm 〔eighth year of Zhenguan〕.
Compose a memorial in the voice of the Song Academician Sun Shi, presenting the Illustrations of “Against Luxurious Ease” (Wuyi) 〔fifth year of Tiansheng〕.

Legal judgments 〔five topics〕:
Adding to or deleting from official documents.
The Market Office’s assessment of commodity prices.
Weapons of palace guards.
Exemption of the elderly and young from interrogation under torture.
Manufacturing not in accordance with prescribed standards.

Third Session

Policy questions 〔five〕

Question: The spiritual wisdom and sageliness of the Two Emperors and Three Kings were all bestowed by Heaven. Yet they still examined antiquity and applied themselves reverently to learning, finding each day insufficient. Was this merely because their hearts delighted in it? Indeed, as rulers and teachers of all under Heaven …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
下之大任必有非學莫濟者不然何憂
惕相傳一揆耶漢唐宋英誼之君表章
誦法臨雍御講非盡不學也顧其道未
粹而治益去古遠無亦其所以學者非
歟抑諸侍從之臣論思未效也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝初戢干戈業已潛心
聖學其大者諭宋濂諭曾魯書洪範書衍義錄
存心錄省躬其義何居可得殫述之乎
列聖相承道同心一如
===
表章四書五經矣而著
心法以闡
鴻猷何至備也
編輯五倫全書矣而製
帝訓以貽
燕謀何至精也
文華大訓既以飭學爲先而猶御
經筵不輟於寒暑
闕里建廟既以尊師爲重而猶資講沃不忘
punctuated:
下之大任，必有非學莫濟者。不然，何憂惕相傳一揆耶？漢唐宋英誼之君，表章誦法，臨雍御講，非盡不學也。顧其道未粹，而治益去古遠，無亦其所以學者非歟？抑諸侍從之臣論思未效也？
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，初戢干戈，業已潛心聖學。其大者，諭宋濂、諭曾魯，書《洪範》、書《衍義》，錄《存心》、錄《省躬》，其義何居？可得殫述之乎？
列聖相承，道同心一。如表章《四書》《五經》矣，而著《心法》以闡鴻猷，何至備也！編輯《五倫全書》矣，而製《帝訓》以貽燕謀，何至精也！《文華大訓》既以飭學爲先，而猶御經筵，不輟於寒暑；闕里建廟既以尊師爲重，而猶資講沃，不忘
translation_en:
…the great responsibility of serving as ruler and teacher of all under Heaven must involve things that cannot be accomplished without learning. Otherwise, why did they transmit to one another the same standard of anxious vigilance? The illustrious and righteous [?] rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song honored and expounded the classics, recited and took them as models, visited the imperial academy, and attended lectures. It was not that they were all without learning. Yet their Way lacked purity, and their government departed ever further from antiquity. Might their manner of learning have been mistaken? Or had the deliberations and reflections of their attendant ministers failed to bear fruit?
We reverently consider that our Emperor Taizu Gao, when he had only just laid down his weapons, was already devoting himself to the learning of the sages. Among the chief instances were his admonitions to Song Lian and Zeng Lu, his writings on the Great Plan and the Extended Meaning, and his records on Preserving the Mind and Examining Oneself [?]. What meanings lay in these? Can they be fully expounded?
The successive sage emperors inherited this tradition, sharing one Way and one purpose. For example, they had already honored and expounded the Four Books and Five Classics, yet they also composed the Methods of the Mind to elucidate their grand designs: how consummately comprehensive! They had already compiled the Complete Book of the Five Human Relationships, yet they also composed the Imperial Instructions to bequeath plans for the security of their descendants: how consummately refined! The Grand Instructions of the Hall of Literary Brilliance already gave priority to diligence in learning, yet they continued to attend the Classics Colloquium without interruption through cold and heat. Building a temple at Queli already demonstrated the importance they attached to honoring the teacher, yet they continued to draw nourishment from lectures, never forgetting…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
於箴規此皆學術之章明較著者寧無
媲美於
聖祖乎暨我
世宗肅皇帝朝御
經筵退臨
書幄作敬一箴註四箴解心學淵源光揚佑
啓蔑以加矣今我
皇上以上聖之資撫中興之運
登極之初崇儒重道肇舉
===
經筵
親臨太學脩一代之曠典紹千古之真傳天下
臣民何幸復覩二帝三王時景象也諸
士有能對揚之者乎亦復有補於論思
者乎願聞其槩
問帝王之治天下專務以德化民而刑以
輔治者乃不得已而用之是故虞命士
師夏制常刑及周官司寇之掌邦禁尚
矣然舜之欽恤禹之泣罪成康之慎獄
punctuated:
於箴規。此皆學術之章明較著者，寧無媲美於聖祖乎？暨我世宗肅皇帝，朝御經筵，退臨書幄，作《敬一箴》，註《四箴解》，心學淵源，光揚佑啓，蔑以加矣。今我皇上，以上聖之資，撫中興之運，登極之初，崇儒重道，肇舉經筵，親臨太學，脩一代之曠典，紹千古之真傳。天下臣民，何幸復覩二帝三王時景象也！諸士有能對揚之者乎？亦復有補於論思者乎？願聞其槩。
問：帝王之治天下，專務以德化民，而刑以輔治者，乃不得已而用之。是故虞命士師，夏制常刑，及周官司寇之掌邦禁，尚矣。然舜之欽恤，禹之泣罪，成康之慎獄
translation_en:
…in admonition and remonstrance. These are all conspicuous manifestations of learning: do they not rival those of the sagely founder? Then our Emperor Shizong Su attended the Classics Colloquium at court and, upon withdrawing, entered his study. He composed the Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness and annotated the Explanations of the Four Admonitions. In illuminating the sources of the learning of the mind and guiding and enlightening later generations, nothing could surpass him. Now our reigning emperor, endowed with the qualities of a supreme sage, presides over an age of dynastic restoration. At the beginning of his reign, he honored Confucian learning and esteemed the Way, inaugurated the Classics Colloquium, and personally visited the Imperial University, restoring a grand ceremony long neglected in this dynasty and continuing the true transmission handed down through the ages. How fortunate are the officials and people of the realm to behold once more the scene of the age of the Two Emperors and Three Kings! Can any of you candidates fittingly respond to and extol these achievements? Can you also contribute to deliberation and reflection? We wish to hear the broad outlines of your views.
Question: In governing the realm, emperors and kings devote themselves above all to transforming the people through virtue; punishments, as an aid to government, are employed only when unavoidable. Thus, Yu’s appointment of a Judge, Xia’s establishment of regular punishments, and the Minister of Justice’s responsibility for the prohibitions of the state in the Offices of Zhou all have an ancient pedigree. Yet Shun’s reverent concern and compassion, Yu’s weeping over offenders, and Kings Cheng and Kang’s care in adjudicating cases…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
敬刑兹其仁心仁政可得而究言歟三
代而下或約法三章或詔除肉刑或奏
必五覆或親錄繫囚咸所以重民命致
天和良有足稱者然夷考當代之讞獄
果盡明刑之中與前聖相為脗合否耶
洪惟我
太祖高皇帝肇造區宇稽古定制旣詳且備矣
而
祖訓一書禁用墨劓剕宮之刑及戒諭比部諸
===
臣謂鞫獄當存平恕毋以刑殺立威是
其欽恤慎重之意同符舜禹成康眞足
以壽國脈於無疆也其詳可得聞歟逮
我
皇上嗣登
寶位軫念民生首當審决之期渙頒停免之
命是又遠契舜禹成康之心祗承
聖祖慈祥之訓中外臣民莫不歌咏熈皞而景
仰太和矣一時文法之吏孰不思將順
punctuated: 敬刑，兹其仁心仁政可得而究言歟？三代而下，或約法三章，或詔除肉刑，或奏必五覆，或親錄繫囚，咸所以重民命、致天和，良有足稱者。然夷考當代之讞獄，果盡明刑之中，與前聖相為脗合否耶？洪惟我太祖高皇帝肇造區宇，稽古定制，旣詳且備矣。而《祖訓》一書，禁用墨、劓、剕、宮之刑，及戒諭比部諸臣，謂鞫獄當存平恕，毋以刑殺立威。是其欽恤慎重之意，同符舜禹成康，眞足以壽國脈於無疆也。其詳可得聞歟？逮我皇上嗣登寶位，軫念民生，首當審决之期，渙頒停免之命。是又遠契舜禹成康之心，祗承聖祖慈祥之訓，中外臣民莫不歌咏熈皞而景仰太和矣。一時文法之吏，孰不思將順
translation_en:
…and their reverence in administering punishments: can their benevolent hearts and benevolent government be discussed exhaustively? After the Three Dynasties, some rulers reduced the laws to three articles; some decreed the abolition of mutilating punishments; some required five reviews and reports to the throne before an execution; and some personally reviewed the cases of prisoners in custody. All these measures served to value human life and bring about harmony with Heaven, and were indeed worthy of praise. Yet, upon dispassionately examining the adjudication of criminal cases in those times, did it invariably attain the proper balance in administering punishments, fully agreeing with the sages of antiquity?
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the realm and established its institutions by consulting antiquity, making them both detailed and comprehensive. Moreover, the book Ancestral Instructions prohibited tattooing, cutting off the nose, amputation of the feet, and castration as punishments. He also admonished the officials of the Ministry of Justice that, when investigating criminal cases, they should maintain impartiality and forbearance and should not establish their authority through punishment and execution. His spirit of reverent compassion and circumspection thus accorded with that of Shun, Yu, and Kings Cheng and Kang, and was truly sufficient to sustain the vitality of the dynasty without limit. May we hear the particulars?
When our present Emperor succeeded to the precious throne, he took the people's livelihood to heart. At the first season for reviewing cases and deciding executions, he graciously issued an order suspending executions and granting exemptions. This again accorded across the ages with the hearts of Shun, Yu, Cheng, and Kang, and reverently upheld the compassionate instructions of the sagely founder. Officials and subjects at court and throughout the realm all sing of this radiant peace and look up in admiration to its supreme harmony. Among the officials versed in legal statutes in our time, who would not think of supporting and carrying out…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
德意以措斯世於仁壽之域也然其重輕出
入豈盡得其平而無可議者歟夫上有
欽恤之仁則下有欽若之義兹欲刑期
無刑辟以止辟于以廣
皇上好生之德抑何道以致之爾多士其悉心
對揚以鳴
國家刑措之盛焉
問天下之大非賢不乂而官人之制則明
揚黜陟自虞廷已然矣三代之法至周
===
大備大司徒掌三物之敎而賓興之太
宰計羣吏之治而誅賞之固虞廷之遺
意也其法可歷數而稱之歟後世善治
惟漢唐宋其選舉之法則設科目以斂
天下之才漢之法大槩有三唐之法大
槩有二宋之中葉則併置一科其詳可
得聞歟與成周賓興之義亦有同歟考
課之法則較殿最以別天下之治漢有
奏事之六條唐有考功之九等宋以七
punctuated:
德意，以措斯世於仁壽之域也。然其重輕出入，豈盡得其平而無可議者歟？夫上有欽恤之仁，則下有欽若之義。兹欲刑期無刑，辟以止辟，于以廣皇上好生之德，抑何道以致之？爾多士其悉心對揚，以鳴國家刑措之盛焉。
問：天下之大，非賢不乂，而官人之制，則明揚黜陟，自虞廷已然矣。三代之法，至周大備。大司徒掌三物之敎而賓興之，太宰計羣吏之治而誅賞之，固虞廷之遺意也。其法可歷數而稱之歟？後世善治，惟漢唐宋。其選舉之法，則設科目以斂天下之才。漢之法大槩有三，唐之法大槩有二，宋之中葉則併置一科，其詳可得聞歟？與成周賓興之義，亦有同歟？考課之法，則較殿最以別天下之治。漢有奏事之六條，唐有考功之九等，宋以七
translation_en:
…the benevolent imperial intentions, so as to bring this age into a realm of humaneness and longevity. Yet in making punishments heavier or lighter, and in imposing or remitting convictions, has perfect equity invariably been achieved, leaving nothing open to question? When those above possess a reverent compassion, those below have a duty reverently to comply. We now wish to employ punishments with the aim of dispensing with punishment, and penalties to put an end to penalties, thereby extending His Majesty’s virtue of cherishing life. By what means can this be achieved? You assembled scholars should devote your whole minds to answering and giving expression to these intentions, proclaiming the flourishing condition of our state, in which punishments may be laid aside.
Question: The empire is vast, and without worthy men it cannot be governed. As for the system of appointing officials, the discerning promotion of worthy men, and the dismissal and advancement of officeholders, were already practiced at the court of Shun. The institutions of the Three Dynasties reached their fullest development under the Zhou. The Minister of Education directed instruction in the three categories and honored worthy men as guests before advancing them; the Minister of State assessed the administration of the assembled officials and punished or rewarded them. These indeed preserved the intent of Shun’s court. Can their procedures be enumerated and explained in turn? Among later dynasties, the Han, Tang, and Song excelled in government. Their methods of selecting men for office established examination categories to gather the talents of the empire. The Han system had broadly three categories, and the Tang system broadly two; in the middle period of the Song, these were consolidated into a single category. May we hear the details? Did these also share something of the intent of the mature Zhou practice of honoring worthy men as guests and advancing them? Their methods of evaluating officials compared the lowest and highest achievements to distinguish the quality of administration throughout the empire. The Han had six articles for reporting administrative affairs, and the Tang had nine grades for evaluating merit. The Song used seven…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
事考轉運提舉等官以九事考縣令其
詳可指言歟與成周大計之典亦有同
歟我
國家損益前代之制立爲成法取士以科目
矣而或懼其無實察吏以考課矣而或
恐其失眞豈流弊固然耶則舍二法又
何爲而可茲欲師虞周之意而叅酌乎
漢唐宋之法必使士有眞才吏有實政
其道安在二三子志存用世必籌之審
===
矣願試言之無讓
問儒者之學必體用具備而後可稱全才
是故學術者其體也事功者其用也固
未有學術旣正而不足於事功亦未有
事功旣著而不本於學術者何三代而
下學術事功判爲貳途也他未暇論且
以爾鄉之先哲言之自宋熙豐以來人
才始盛以理學名者則有若楊時游酢
李侗劉子翬朱熹蔡元定黃幹眞德秀
punctuated:
事考轉運提舉等官，以九事考縣令，其詳可指言歟？與成周大計之典亦有同歟？我國家損益前代之制，立爲成法，取士以科目矣，而或懼其無實；察吏以考課矣，而或恐其失眞。豈流弊固然耶？則舍二法，又何爲而可？茲欲師虞周之意，而叅酌乎漢唐宋之法，必使士有眞才，吏有實政，其道安在？二三子志存用世，必籌之審矣，願試言之，無讓。

問：儒者之學，必體用具備，而後可稱全才。是故學術者，其體也；事功者，其用也。固未有學術旣正而不足於事功，亦未有事功旣著而不本於學術者。何三代而下，學術事功判爲貳途也？他未暇論，且以爾鄉之先哲言之。自宋熙豐以來，人才始盛，以理學名者，則有若楊時、游酢、李侗、劉子翬、朱熹、蔡元定、黃幹、眞德秀
translation_en:
…criteria to evaluate officials such as transport commissioners and superintendents, and nine criteria to evaluate district magistrates. Can you explain these in detail? Did they also share features with the comprehensive evaluation system of the Zhou? Our dynasty has adapted the institutions of earlier dynasties and established them as standing regulations. It recruits men through examination categories, yet some fear that this yields no substantive results; it scrutinizes officials through performance evaluations, yet some fear that these fail to reveal the truth. Are such abuses inevitable? Yet if we abandon these two methods, what other course would be workable? If we now wish to follow the intent of the institutions of Shun and the Zhou, while weighing the methods of the Han, Tang, and Song, so as to ensure that scholars possess genuine ability and officials achieve substantive results in government, what path should we take? You gentlemen aspire to serve the world and must have considered this carefully. Please set forth your views without reserve.

Question: A Confucian scholar’s learning must encompass both substance and practical application before he can be called a man of complete talent. Scholarly learning is its substance; practical achievement is its application. Surely there has never been anyone whose learning was sound but who was incapable of practical achievement, nor anyone whose practical achievements were distinguished but were not rooted in learning. Why, then, since the Three Dynasties, have learning and practical achievement been divided into two separate paths? We have no time here to discuss other cases; let us speak of the earlier worthies of your own region. From the Xining and Yuanfeng eras of the Song onward, talented men began to flourish. Among those renowned for the Learning of Principle were Yang Shi, You Zuo, Li Tong, Liu Zihui, Zhu Xi, Cai Yuanding, Huang Gan, and Zhen Dexiu…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
輩以功業顯者則有若李綱曾公亮蔡
襄鄭俠陳襄劉子羽呂祉劉琠輩其所
以仰希賢聖而裨益君民者可舉其實
而第言之歟迨至
聖朝才賢輩出有以理學名者有以事功顯者
芳聲不磨遺軌猶在此固長老之所習
聞而諸士所景仰焉者可歷指而言之
歟其言行勛勣與前代諸賢果相似歟
以理學名者果適於用以事功顯者果
===
不負所學歟諸士之所脩莫非諸儒之
學術他日出而效用必有事功表著其
可岐而為貳耶抑志向各殊遭逢亦異
而有不容强同者歟願詳著於篇以覘
尚友之學
問東南財賦西北戎馬乃自昔稱之矣我
明定鼎燕京與虜為鄰其於邊防尤慎且重內
則有十二團營外則列為九邊當是時
猛將材官雲興雷奮稱極盛矣顧其時
punctuated:
輩；以功業顯者，則有若李綱、曾公亮、蔡襄、鄭俠、陳襄、劉子羽、呂祉、劉琠輩。其所以仰希賢聖而裨益君民者，可舉其實而第言之歟？迨至聖朝，才賢輩出，有以理學名者，有以事功顯者，芳聲不磨，遺軌猶在。此固長老之所習聞，而諸士所景仰焉者，可歷指而言之歟？其言行勛勣，與前代諸賢果相似歟？以理學名者果適於用，以事功顯者果不負所學歟？諸士之所脩，莫非諸儒之學術。他日出而效用，必有事功表著，其可岐而為貳耶？抑志向各殊，遭逢亦異，而有不容强同者歟？願詳著於篇，以覘尚友之學。
問：東南財賦，西北戎馬，乃自昔稱之矣。我明定鼎燕京，與虜為鄰，其於邊防尤慎且重。內則有十二團營，外則列為九邊。當是時，猛將材官，雲興雷奮，稱極盛矣。顧其時
translation_en:
…and others; those distinguished for their achievements included Li Gang, Zeng Gongliang, Cai Xiang, Zheng Xia, Chen Xiang, Liu Ziyu, Lü Zhi, Liu Tian, and others. Can you cite concrete examples and explain in order how they aspired to emulate the worthies and sages and benefited their rulers and people? Under our sagely dynasty, talented and worthy men have emerged in succession, some renowned for Learning of Principle, others distinguished for practical accomplishments. Their fine reputations remain undiminished, and the precedents they left are still with us. These are men whose deeds the elders have often heard recounted and whom you candidates admire. Can you identify them individually and discuss them? Were their words, conduct, and achievements indeed comparable to those of the worthies of earlier dynasties? Were those renowned for Learning of Principle truly suited to practical service, and did those distinguished for practical accomplishments truly live up to their learning? What you candidates cultivate is invariably the learning of these Confucian scholars. When you enter public service in days to come, you will surely have conspicuous practical achievements. Can learning and achievement be divided into two separate paths? Or do differences in aspirations and circumstances make it impossible to insist upon uniformity? Set this out fully in your essays, so that we may discern your learning through taking the worthies of the past as friends.
Question: “The southeast supplies wealth and revenues; the northwest supplies warriors and horses”—so it has been said since ancient times. Our Ming established its capital at Yanjing, with the northern barbarians as neighbors, and has exercised particular care over frontier defense and attached great importance to it. Within, there were the Twelve Regimental Camps; without, the frontier was organized into the Nine Border Commands. At that time, valiant generals and able soldiers arose like clouds and sprang into action like thunder: military strength was said to have reached its height. Yet at that time…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
司徒所入不加於今而太倉之粟足支
數十年
內帑之銀積至千餘萬諸司所藏亦略稱是
猶且頻年用兵費用不貲當時未聞以
兵力財用詘乏爲憂而減租蠲稅之
詔且屢下焉馴至今日團營之兵縮其大半九
邊營戍東抽西補歲無定額卒遇警報
惟兢兢爲固守計未聞以數萬營陣待
敵者動諉諸兵食未贍何歟夫兵與食
===
相因者也兵不足則食宜有餘矣乃今
太倉之儲
內帑之積視昔益稱空乏其故何歟建議者
謂京師冗食太多宜如嘉靖初年故事
汰除一切冗役歲可省粟數十萬其說
果可行歟九邊惟宣大爲急舊時所藉
屯田鹽法其要也今屯田虜歲踐蹂民
無所得息鹽法自括餘銀商人鮮至邊
者卽至亦苦於得粟其在各鎮亦然目
punctuated: 司徒所入不加於今，而太倉之粟足支數十年，內帑之銀積至千餘萬，諸司所藏亦略稱是。猶且頻年用兵，費用不貲，當時未聞以兵力財用詘乏爲憂，而減租蠲稅之詔且屢下焉。馴至今日，團營之兵縮其大半，九邊營戍東抽西補，歲無定額。卒遇警報，惟兢兢爲固守計，未聞以數萬營陣待敵者，動諉諸兵食未贍，何歟？夫兵與食相因者也，兵不足則食宜有餘矣。乃今太倉之儲、內帑之積，視昔益稱空乏，其故何歟？建議者謂京師冗食太多，宜如嘉靖初年故事，汰除一切冗役，歲可省粟數十萬，其說果可行歟？九邊惟宣大爲急，舊時所藉，屯田、鹽法，其要也。今屯田虜歲踐蹂，民無所得息；鹽法自括餘銀，商人鮮至邊者，卽至亦苦於得粟，其在各鎮亦然。目
translation_en:
…the revenue received by the Minister of Revenue was no greater than it is today, yet the grain in the Grand Granary was sufficient to support expenditure for several decades. Silver in the Palace Treasury accumulated to more than ten million taels, and the reserves held by the various offices were roughly comparable. Moreover, military campaigns were conducted year after year at immense expense. At that time, there was no report of concern over inadequate military strength or exhausted finances; indeed, edicts reducing land levies and remitting taxes were repeatedly issued.

By gradual stages we have reached the present situation: the troops of the capital’s regimental camps have been reduced by more than half, while the garrisons of the Nine Frontier Commands draw men from the east to replenish the west, with no fixed annual complement. When an alarm suddenly comes, they can only anxiously plan to hold their defenses. We never hear of their drawing up tens of thousands of men in battle formation to await the enemy. At every turn they plead insufficient troops and provisions. Why is this? Troops and provisions are interdependent: if troops are few, provisions ought to be plentiful. Yet today the reserves of the Grand Granary and the accumulations in the Palace Treasury are all the more depleted compared with former times. What accounts for this?

Those proposing measures say that too many people in the capital draw rations without useful service. They urge following the precedent of the early Jiajing reign by eliminating all superfluous service positions, thereby saving several hundred thousand measures of grain each year. Is their proposal truly practicable?

Among the Nine Frontier Commands, Xuanfu and Datong are the most urgent concerns. Of the arrangements on which they formerly relied, agricultural garrisons and the salt administration were the most important. Now enemy raiders trample the garrison farmlands every year, leaving the people no yield from which to sustain themselves. As for the salt administration, since the collection of surplus silver [?], few merchants come to the frontier; even those who do have difficulty obtaining grain. The situation is the same in each of the frontier commands. At present…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
前支持惟有
請討而已此坐困之術也不知此外有何長策
可采而行之歟諸士志抱先憂久矣願
盡言之以觀經世之術
punctuated: 前支持，惟有請討而已。此坐困之術也，不知此外有何長策可采而行之歟？諸士志抱先憂久矣，願盡言之，以觀經世之術。
translation_en: …at present, the only means of sustaining operations is to request further allocations. This is a course that leads only to helpless exhaustion. What other long-term measures might be adopted and put into practice? You gentlemen have long cherished the resolve to be the first to shoulder the realm’s concerns. Please express your views fully, so that we may assess your methods for governing the world.

text:
第壹場
四書
法語之言能無從乎改之爲貴巽與之言
能無說乎繹之爲貴
張履祥
同考試官教諭吳批發聖人立教之意殆盡而其
詞醇雅足爲多士式錄之
同考試官教授何批體製渾融文詞清逸雖不逞
才華而蔚然之光自莫可遏佳士佳士
===
考試官教授吳批意精詞粹宜錄以式
考試官教授李批文之順理者取之
聖人兩舉聽言之道在能自得於言也夫言足
以感人言之善者也使非改之繹之則亦何得
於言哉且夫君子能爲可用之言而不能必人
之用其言是在聽言者之自擇耳何者君子不
欲阿徇以爲容則凡過失相規不有法言乎言
而本之法則其論正其旨嚴侃侃然指陳之無
隱聽之者將憚於理之不可易而窮於說之無
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

法語之言，能無從乎？改之爲貴。巽與之言，能無說乎？繹之爲貴。

張履祥

同考試官教諭吳批：發聖人立教之意殆盡，而其詞醇雅，足爲多士式，錄之。

同考試官教授何批：體製渾融，文詞清逸，雖不逞才華，而蔚然之光自莫可遏。佳士！佳士！

考試官教授吳批：意精詞粹，宜錄以式。

考試官教授李批：文之順理者，取之。

聖人兩舉聽言之道，在能自得於言也。夫言足以感人，言之善者也。使非改之繹之，則亦何得於言哉？且夫君子能爲可用之言，而不能必人之用其言，是在聽言者之自擇耳。何者？君子不欲阿徇以爲容，則凡過失相規，不有法言乎？言而本之法，則其論正，其旨嚴，侃侃然指陳之無隱。聽之者將憚於理之不可易，而窮於說之無

First Session

Four Books

“When words accord with proper standards, can one fail to assent? What matters is reforming oneself. When words are gentle and accommodating, can one fail to be pleased? What matters is drawing out their meaning.”

Zhang Lüxiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: He brings out almost fully the Sage’s intention in establishing his teaching. His language is pure and elegant, sufficient to serve as a model for the many candidates. Include it.

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Professor: The composition is thoroughly integrated, and its language clear and graceful. Although he does not flaunt his literary talent, its abundant brilliance cannot be suppressed. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: Refined ideas and pure diction: it should be included as a model.

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: This composition accords with principle. Select it.

The Sage presents two approaches to listening to words; their point lies in being able to make what is said one’s own. Words that can move people are good words. Yet unless one reforms oneself and draws out their meaning, what does one gain from them? Moreover, the gentleman can offer words that can be put into practice, but he cannot ensure that others will put his words into practice. That rests with the listener’s own choice. Why is this? The gentleman does not wish to win acceptance through flattery and compliance. Thus, when people admonish one another about their faults, are there not words grounded in proper standards? When words are based on such standards, their reasoning is correct and their purport strict; they frankly point out and explain matters, concealing nothing. title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
所逃固未有拒而不從者然從特一時之感未
必能守之於爲也故必懲已往之愆而釋回以
增美求方來之益而舍舊以圖新則從之者非
面從而語之者匪虛語過失將自此而日寡矣
此所以改爲貴也夫從貴於改則以法言進者
豈徒望其能從已耶君子不欲激抗以爲直則
凡德業相勸不有巽言乎言而出之巽則其辭
婉其義微誾誾然開導之有方聽之者將動於
理之有可喻而喜於情之無所拂固未有逆而
===
不悅者然悅特一念之明未必能誠之於思也
故必因辭以逆意而反覆於思惟由顯以通微
而沉潛於念慮則悅之者誠心悅而言之者非
失言德業將自此而日進矣此所以繹爲貴也
夫悅貴於繹則以巽言進者豈徒望其能悅已
耶吁夫子斯言其所望於善學者良深切矣抑
因是而可以明獻納焉聖如舜禹宜無過可改
無善可加者然猶察邇言而用中聞昌言而必
拜非誠有得於改且繹乎以是知君子之學不
punctuated: 所逃，固未有拒而不從者。然從特一時之感，未必能守之於爲也。故必懲已往之愆，而釋回以增美；求方來之益，而舍舊以圖新。則從之者非面從，而語之者匪虛語，過失將自此而日寡矣。此所以改爲貴也。夫從貴於改，則以法言進者，豈徒望其能從已耶？君子不欲激抗以爲直，則凡德業相勸，不有巽言乎？言而出之巽，則其辭婉，其義微，誾誾然開導之有方。聽之者將動於理之有可喻，而喜於情之無所拂，固未有逆而不悅者。然悅特一念之明，未必能誠之於思也。故必因辭以逆意，而反覆於思惟；由顯以通微，而沉潛於念慮。則悅之者誠心悅，而言之者非失言，德業將自此而日進矣。此所以繹爲貴也。夫悅貴於繹，則以巽言進者，豈徒望其能悅已耶？吁！夫子斯言，其所望於善學者良深切矣！抑因是而可以明獻納焉。聖如舜禹，宜無過可改、無善可加者，然猶察邇言而用中，聞昌言而必拜，非誠有得於改且繹乎？以是知君子之學不
translation_en:
…nowhere to escape. Surely no one would reject such words and refuse to comply. Yet compliance is merely a momentary response; one may not necessarily sustain it in practice. Thus one must take warning from past faults, abandon perversity to increase goodness, seek further improvement, and relinquish old ways to pursue renewal. Then the listener’s compliance will not be merely outward, nor will the speaker’s words have been spoken in vain: faults will thereafter diminish day by day. This is why reform is prized. If reform is what makes compliance valuable, can someone who offers words of admonition grounded in proper standards hope merely that others will comply with him?

The gentleman does not wish to pass off vehement contention as uprightness. Thus, when encouraging others in virtue and achievement, does he not employ gentle words? When words are gently expressed, their phrasing is tactful and their meaning subtle; amiably and respectfully, the speaker guides others with skill. Listeners will be moved by principles they can understand and pleased that their feelings meet with no affront. Surely no one would resist such words and fail to take pleasure in them. Yet pleasure is merely a moment’s illumination; one may not necessarily make it sincere in one’s thinking. Thus one must seek the intention through the wording and ponder it repeatedly, proceed from what is manifest to comprehend what is subtle, and immerse oneself in reflection. Then the listener’s pleasure will be heartfelt, and the speaker’s words will not have been wasted: virtue and achievement will thereafter advance day by day. This is why drawing out the meaning is prized. If drawing out the meaning is what makes pleasure valuable, can someone who offers gentle words hope merely that others will be pleased with him?

Ah! In these words, the Master’s expectations of those who learn well are indeed profound and earnest! Moreover, through this we may clarify the offering and reception of counsel. Sages such as Shun and Yu would seem to have had no faults to reform and no goodness to add. Yet Shun still examined ordinary people’s words and applied the mean, while Yu invariably bowed upon hearing excellent counsel. Had they not truly gained something through reforming themselves and drawing out the meaning of what they heard? From this we know that the gentleman’s learning does not…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
難於無過而難於改過不貴於用一已之長而
貴於有以來天下之善此固夫子惓惓之餘意
也有聽言之責者當自得之
齊明盛服非禮不動所以脩身也
方沆
同考試官教諭伍批語意俊潔而渾成條理疏
暢而精密帝王慎脩之學闡明殆盡
同考試官教諭張批提掇精貫該括詳明文之
邃理者也取之
===
考試官教授吳批發脩身意瑩徹錄之
考試官教授李批詞理俱到
人君端本之道大居敬而已矣夫敬聖學之要
也此身無不敬而慎脩之能事畢矣茲非九經
之首務乎宜孔子舉以告魯君也意謂人君一
身為天下國家之本必脩身而後道立是身固
不可不脩矣而脩之宜何如是故有所以主此
身者必齊戒以潔其内操虛靈於不昧而常明
常覺不懈乎存養之功有所以章此身者必盛
punctuated:
難於無過，而難於改過；不貴於用一已之長，而貴於有以來天下之善。此固夫子惓惓之餘意也。有聽言之責者，當自得之。
齊明盛服，非禮不動，所以脩身也。
方沆
同考試官教諭伍批：語意俊潔而渾成，條理疏暢而精密，帝王慎脩之學闡明殆盡。
同考試官教諭張批：提掇精貫，該括詳明，文之邃理者也，取之。
考試官教授吳批：發脩身意瑩徹，錄之。
考試官教授李批：詞理俱到。
人君端本之道，大居敬而已矣。夫敬，聖學之要也。此身無不敬，而慎脩之能事畢矣。茲非九經之首務乎？宜孔子舉以告魯君也。意謂人君一身，為天下國家之本，必脩身而後道立，是身固不可不脩矣。而脩之宜何如？是故有所以主此身者，必齊戒以潔其内，操虛靈於不昧，而常明常覺，不懈乎存養之功；有所以章此身者，必盛
translation_en:
…finds the difficulty not in being without faults, but in correcting faults; he values not the exercise of his own particular strengths, but having the means to draw upon the goodness of all under Heaven. This, indeed, is the further purport of the Master's earnest concern. Those charged with listening to counsel should grasp it for themselves.
“Purifying oneself, maintaining clarity, wearing full ceremonial dress, and making no movement contrary to ritual propriety: these are the means of cultivating oneself.”
Fang Hang 方沆
Associate Examiner Wu, an Instructor, comments: “The language and meaning are elegant and clean, yet form an integrated whole; the organization is clear and fluent, yet precise and closely ordered. The learning by which emperors and kings diligently cultivate themselves is elucidated almost exhaustively.”
Associate Examiner Zhang, an Instructor, comments: “Its presentation of the essentials is incisive and coherent; its coverage is comprehensive and lucid. This is writing that penetrates deeply into principle. Accept it.”
Examiner Wu, a Professor, comments: “It develops the meaning of self-cultivation with crystalline clarity. Select it.”
Examiner Li, a Professor, comments: “Both expression and reasoning are fully realized.”
The ruler's way of setting the foundation right consists chiefly in abiding in reverent attentiveness. Reverent attentiveness is the essential point of the learning of the sages. When no aspect of one's person lacks it, the work of diligent self-cultivation is fully accomplished. Is this not the foremost duty among the nine guiding principles? It was fitting that Confucius should bring it forward in instructing the ruler of Lu. His meaning was that the ruler's own person is the foundation of all under Heaven, of the state, and of the family. Only after he cultivates himself is the Way established; thus he certainly cannot leave his person uncultivated. But how should he cultivate it? Accordingly, to govern his own person, he must purify himself through fasting and abstinence, cleansing his inner being, preserving the mind's receptive spiritual awareness undimmed, remaining constantly lucid and alert, and never slackening in the work of preserving and nurturing it. To give outward distinction to his person, he must wear full…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
服以飾其外肅瞻視於罔愆而可畏可象不褻
夫尊臨之體自其内無逸志而協以中正之規
則以禮制心有一念之不合於禮者不以動於
内也自其外無惰容而約以節文之度則以禮
制事有一事之不協於禮者不以動於外也若
此者非所以脩身乎蓋脩身以道而道合内外
者也故内外兼持正以納此身於軌物而善元
良之則脩已以敬而敬貫動靜者也故動靜交
養正以約此身於範圍而清化理之原篤恭不
===
顯惟皇之建極以貞所以脩德而行道者吾身
無餘功矣術豈多乎哉端拱無為惟后之綏猷
以定所以取人而立政者吾身有常度矣道豈
遠乎哉是則一敬立而文武之心法已全故一
身脩而文武之治法可舉矣公欲憲章文武其
尚知所先務乎且魯公一國之君也孔子告之
政猶必本諸身況天子一身與天地參而日月
竝百官萬民式焉脩之可不敬乎故記載朝廷
燕處行步升車各有禮度豈非以敬之為道無
punctuated: 服以飾其外，肅瞻視於罔愆，而可畏可象，不褻夫尊臨之體。自其内無逸志，而協以中正之規，則以禮制心，有一念之不合於禮者，不以動於内也；自其外無惰容，而約以節文之度，則以禮制事，有一事之不協於禮者，不以動於外也。若此者，非所以脩身乎？蓋脩身以道，而道合内外者也，故内外兼持，正以納此身於軌物，而善元良之則；脩已以敬，而敬貫動靜者也，故動靜交養，正以約此身於範圍，而清化理之原。篤恭不顯，惟皇之建極以貞，所以脩德而行道者，吾身無餘功矣，術豈多乎哉？端拱無為，惟后之綏猷以定，所以取人而立政者，吾身有常度矣，道豈遠乎哉？是則一敬立，而文武之心法已全，故一身脩，而文武之治法可舉矣。公欲憲章文武，其尚知所先務乎？且魯公一國之君也，孔子告之政，猶必本諸身；況天子一身，與天地參，而日月竝，百官萬民式焉，脩之可不敬乎？故記載朝廷、燕處、行步、升車，各有禮度，豈非以敬之為道無
translation_en:
…robes to adorn his outward appearance, making his gaze solemn and faultless, so that he inspires awe and serves as a model, without debasing the dignity with which he presides over others. Inwardly, he harbors no indolent intentions and accords with the rules of centrality and correctness: thus he regulates his heart through ritual propriety, allowing no thought inconsistent with it to stir within. Outwardly, he displays no careless demeanor and restrains himself by the measured forms of ritual: thus he regulates affairs through ritual propriety, allowing no undertaking inconsistent with it to find outward expression. Is this not the means of cultivating oneself?

Self-cultivation proceeds through the Way, and the Way unites the inward and the outward. Therefore, maintaining both together brings the self within proper norms and perfects the exemplary standard of supreme goodness. Cultivating oneself proceeds through reverence, and reverence pervades both activity and stillness. Therefore, nurturing both together keeps the self within due bounds and purifies the source of moral transformation and orderly government. Profoundly reverent without outward display, the sovereign establishes the supreme standard and makes it correct. In cultivating virtue and practicing the Way, no further exertion remains for me to undertake. How could the methods be many? Sitting upright with hands folded, governing without contrived action, the ruler secures his guiding principles and brings stability. In selecting men and establishing government, I possess a constant standard in my own person. How could the Way be distant?

Thus, once reverence is established, the teachings of Kings Wen and Wu concerning the heart are fully present; once the person is cultivated, their methods of government can be put into practice. If you, my lord, wish to take Wen and Wu as your models, surely you should recognize what must come first?

Moreover, the Duke of Lu ruled only a single state, yet when Confucius instructed him about government, he still insisted that its foundation lay in his own person. How much more does this apply to the Son of Heaven, whose person stands alongside Heaven and Earth and ranks with the sun and moon, and whom all officials and the myriad people take as their model! Could he cultivate himself without reverence? Thus the ritual records prescribe proper measures for conduct at court, in private repose, when walking, and when mounting a carriage. Is this not because, in the practice of reverence, there is no…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
微可忽而帝王之所以正百官正萬民者恒必
由之也噫孔子之愛君其至矣哉
原泉混混不舍晝夜盈科而後進放乎四
海有本者如是是之取爾
陳公相
同考試官教諭劉批造理淵源行文活潑豈涵
泳聖教而有得者耶錄之
同考試官教諭鄭批不費詞說曲盡本真如風
行水上自然成文有養之士也
===
考試官教授吳批詞氣冲澹理趣淵涵
考試官教授李批得聖人重本之思
大賢原聖人取水之意示人以務本之學也蓋
水惟有本故能不已而漸歸於海也聖人以此
取之可以見本之當務矣昔孟子因徐子之問
而告之若曰天下之道寓於物者流行之迹而
根於心者統會之源仲尼以心觀物而獨有取
於水者其有感於水之道乎今夫流水之爲物
也發端於原泉而泉之始達吾見其混混焉往
punctuated:
微可忽，而帝王之所以正百官、正萬民者，恒必由之也。噫！孔子之愛君，其至矣哉！

原泉混混，不舍晝夜，盈科而後進，放乎四海。有本者如是，是之取爾。
陳公相

同考試官教諭劉批：造理淵源，行文活潑，豈涵泳聖教而有得者耶？錄之。
同考試官教諭鄭批：不費詞說，曲盡本真，如風行水上，自然成文，有養之士也。
考試官教授吳批：詞氣冲澹，理趣淵涵。
考試官教授李批：得聖人重本之思。

大賢原聖人取水之意，示人以務本之學也。蓋水惟有本，故能不已而漸歸於海也。聖人以此取之，可以見本之當務矣。昔孟子因徐子之問而告之，若曰：天下之道，寓於物者流行之迹，而根於心者統會之源。仲尼以心觀物，而獨有取於水者，其有感於水之道乎？今夫流水之爲物也，發端於原泉，而泉之始達，吾見其混混焉，往
translation_en:
…nothing, however minute, may be neglected; this is invariably the way by which emperors and kings rectify the hundred officials and the myriad people. Ah! How profound was Confucius’s concern for his ruler!

“A spring’s waters well up abundantly, never ceasing day or night. They fill each hollow before advancing, flowing onward to the Four Seas. Such is that which has a source; this alone is what he valued.”
By Chen Gongxiang 陳公相.

Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “His exploration of principle reaches its deep sources, and his writing is lively. Could he be someone who has immersed himself in the sages’ teaching and gained an understanding of it? Include this essay.”
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Without expending words on explanations, he fully conveys the fundamental truth in all its subtleties. Like wind moving over water, his writing forms its patterns naturally. He is a scholar of cultivated character.”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “His language and tone are serene and restrained; his understanding of principle is deep and ample.”
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “He grasps the sage’s intention in emphasizing the root.”

The great worthy traced the sage’s intention in valuing water, thereby showing people a way of learning that attends to the root. Water, precisely because it has a source, can flow without ceasing and gradually make its way to the sea. The sage valued it for this reason, showing us that the root is what we must attend to. Formerly, in response to Master Xu’s question, Mencius explained it to him, as though saying: Of the Way under Heaven, what is lodged in things is the trace of its flowing operation, while what is rooted in the mind is the source that unifies it all. When Zhongni [Confucius] contemplated things with his mind and singled out water for appreciation, was it because he was moved by the Way embodied in water? Now, flowing water takes its beginning from a spring. As the spring first emerges, I see its waters welling up abundantly, flowing onward …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
過來續其出不窮而自晝及夜無一息之或停
坎止流行其進不驟而足此通彼至四海而後
已是充周莫禦者其流也而所以行其流者則
靜深而不可測夫是以莫遠於海而其勢必至
焉推行有漸者其委也而所以資其委者則渾
淪而不可窮夫是以莫大於海而其機必達焉
是水之有本如此而仲尼之取之也非以其本
哉蓋淵泉之理渾涵於聖心者常體物而不遺
故川流之化昭著於物象者自因心而有感在
===
川之嘆非特玩其流也遡流以窮源殆有獨觀
其深者焉是以稱之數耳臨河之美非特徇其
委也因委以求端殆有默契其本者焉是以取
之亟耳吁觀水之放乎海也始於有本則知學
之造其極也必先於務本矣本者何心而已聖
人之心一理渾然而措諸事業至於位天地育
萬物無所施而不可者皆此心之妙用也學者
欲求至乎聖人豈必求諸此心之外哉孟子甞
言心勿忘勿助長矣勿忘者猶水之不已也勿
punctuated: 過來續，其出不窮，而自晝及夜，無一息之或停。坎止流行，其進不驟，而足此通彼，至四海而後已。是充周莫禦者，其流也，而所以行其流者，則靜深而不可測。夫是以莫遠於海，而其勢必至焉。推行有漸者，其委也，而所以資其委者，則渾淪而不可窮。夫是以莫大於海，而其機必達焉。是水之有本如此，而仲尼之取之也，非以其本哉？蓋淵泉之理，渾涵於聖心者，常體物而不遺，故川流之化，昭著於物象者，自因心而有感。在川之嘆，非特玩其流也，遡流以窮源，殆有獨觀其深者焉，是以稱之數耳。臨河之美，非特徇其委也，因委以求端，殆有默契其本者焉，是以取之亟耳。吁！觀水之放乎海也，始於有本，則知學之造其極也，必先於務本矣。本者何？心而已。聖人之心，一理渾然，而措諸事業，至於位天地、育萬物，無所施而不可者，皆此心之妙用也。學者欲求至乎聖人，豈必求諸此心之外哉？孟子甞言：「心勿忘，勿助長矣。」勿忘者，猶水之不已也。勿
translation_en:
…what passes is succeeded by what comes: its outflow is inexhaustible, and from day into night it never pauses for even a breath. It stops at hollows and flows onward along its course, advancing without haste; it fills one place before passing to the next, stopping only when it reaches the Four Seas. What spreads everywhere and cannot be checked is its current; yet what enables that current to flow is still, deep, and unfathomable. Thus, although nothing is farther away than the sea, its momentum is certain to carry it there. What advances by degrees is its downstream flow; yet what supplies that flow is an undivided fullness that cannot be exhausted. Thus, although nothing is greater than the sea, its dynamic impulse is certain to reach it. Such is the way water possesses a source. Was it not for this source that Zhongni prized it?

The principle of the deep spring, comprehensively contained within the sage’s heart, gives substance to all things without omission. Thus the transformations of flowing streams, manifest in the forms of things, naturally stir a response in his heart. His sigh beside the stream was more than admiration for its flow: tracing the current upstream to fathom its source, he must have perceived its depths as no other did. That is why he spoke of it so often. His praise upon approaching the river was more than attention to its downstream course: following that course to seek its beginning, he must have silently apprehended its source. That is why he so frequently drew upon it.

Ah! When we observe that water’s discharge into the sea begins with its possession of a source, we understand that learning’s attainment of its highest point must begin with attending to the root. What is this root? The heart alone. In the sage’s heart, the single principle forms an undivided whole. When put into practice in affairs and undertakings—even to the point of establishing Heaven and Earth in their proper places and nurturing the myriad things—it is applicable everywhere. All this is the wondrous functioning of this heart. If learners wish to attain sagehood, why should they seek beyond this heart? Mengzi once said: “Do not let the heart forget; do not help growth along.” Not forgetting is like water’s ceaseless flow. Not…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
助者猶水之有漸也是皆所以善事吾心而學
爲聖人者也反是則義襲而取之所謂聲聞過
情者矣孰謂孟子斯言獨因徐子而發哉
易
允升大吉上合志也
李維岳
同考試官教諭張批此題作者多以詞勝易入
於庸是篇詞不費而意已躍如殆得諸心解矣
同考試官教諭吳批二陽合志以初六能巽而
===
然此作得本旨而詞復明潔佳士也
考試官教授吳批體認精切有味
考試官教授李批莊重簡潔易藝之粹也
初爻獲升之善由見孚於同志也夫君子不爲
苟合惟其志之同而已初爻以之其獲升之善
也宜哉小象之意若謂君子之致身也能爲可
進而不能使其身之必進其立志也能爲可合
而不能使其人之皆合惟升之初六秉和順之
德而適際乎大道爲公之時蘊康濟之猷而幸
punctuated:
助者，猶水之有漸也。是皆所以善事吾心而學爲聖人者也。反是，則義襲而取之，所謂聲聞過情者矣。孰謂孟子斯言獨因徐子而發哉？

易
允升，大吉，上合志也。
李維岳

同考試官教諭張批：此題作者多以詞勝，易入於庸。是篇詞不費而意已躍如，殆得諸心解矣。
同考試官教諭吳批：二陽合志，以初六能巽而然。此作得本旨，而詞復明潔，佳士也。
考試官教授吳批：體認精切，有味。
考試官教授李批：莊重簡潔，易藝之粹也。

初爻獲升之善，由見孚於同志也。夫君子不爲苟合，惟其志之同而已。初爻以之，其獲升之善也宜哉！小象之意若謂：君子之致身也，能爲可進，而不能使其身之必進；其立志也，能爲可合，而不能使其人之皆合。惟升之初六，秉和順之德，而適際乎大道爲公之時；蘊康濟之猷，而幸
translation_en:
…not forcing growth is like water’s gradual progress. These are all means of properly tending our own minds and learning to become sages. To act otherwise is to seize righteousness through isolated acts—the condition described as having a reputation that exceeds one’s actual worth. Who would say that these words of Mengzi were uttered solely on account of Master Xu?

Book of Changes
“Ascending with confidence: great good fortune. Those above share his purpose.”
Li Weiyue

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Most who write on this topic seek to excel through their wording and readily lapse into mediocrity. This essay uses words sparingly, yet its meaning already springs vividly forth. The author seems to have attained an understanding in his own mind.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: The two yang lines share his purpose because the six in the first place is able to be yielding. This composition grasps the fundamental meaning, and its language is also lucid and clean. Its author is a fine scholar.
Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: His grasp is precise and penetrating, with depth to savor.
Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: Dignified, concise, and lucid—the essence of examination writing on the Changes.

The first line attains the favorable outcome of ascent because it wins the trust of those who share its purpose. The gentleman does not seek agreement indiscriminately; he seeks only a shared purpose. The first line acts on this principle, so it is fitting that its ascent should prove favorable! The meaning of the Lesser Image Commentary seems to be this: in advancing into service, the gentleman can make himself worthy of advancement, but cannot ensure that he himself will advance; in establishing his purpose, he can make it worthy of others’ agreement, but cannot ensure that everyone will agree. Now the six in the first place of Ascending possesses the virtue of harmony and compliance, and happens to encounter a time when the Great Way serves the common good; it harbors plans to bring peace and succor to the world, and is fortunate…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
逢乎明良喜起之會其晉也莫或摧之而尚往
卽遇其主焉可以熈帝之載也其行也莫或尼
之而南征卽得其朋焉可以達吾之道也信乎
能升而大吉矣若是者豈偶然哉蓋二陽在上
方虛懷以引賢而初六始升能委身以從事上
焉爲德二陽之志則然也初則順以承之而所
以資其啓沃之忠者無弗合焉下焉爲民二陽
之志則然也初則巽以行之而思以贊乎阜成
之化者無弗合焉是其同道爲朋則相信益深
===
而其引之也必力置之左右而不以爲比也同
心共濟則相與益篤而其推之也恐後躋於大
僚而不以爲驟也是則初之所以能升者不惟
其時惟同志焉耳彼無因而干進苟合以取容
者可不戒哉雖然志可合也不可比也當升之
時上有貞吉之君下有升虛邑利用禴之相上
下相孚而德業成故君子樂於自效而以道爲
合九官十二牧師師濟濟之風可想見矣後世
彈冠結綬私相慶幸者比焉耳豈知升之義哉
punctuated: 逢乎明良喜起之會，其晉也莫或摧之，而尚往卽遇其主焉，可以熈帝之載也；其行也莫或尼之，而南征卽得其朋焉，可以達吾之道也。信乎能升而大吉矣！若是者豈偶然哉？蓋二陽在上，方虛懷以引賢，而初六始升，能委身以從事。上焉爲德，二陽之志則然也；初則順以承之，而所以資其啓沃之忠者，無弗合焉。下焉爲民，二陽之志則然也；初則巽以行之，而思以贊乎阜成之化者，無弗合焉。是其同道爲朋，則相信益深，而其引之也必力，置之左右而不以爲比也；同心共濟，則相與益篤，而其推之也恐後，躋於大僚而不以爲驟也。是則初之所以能升者，不惟其時，惟同志焉耳。彼無因而干進、苟合以取容者，可不戒哉？雖然，志可合也，不可比也。當升之時，上有貞吉之君，下有升虛邑、利用禴之相，上下相孚而德業成。故君子樂於自效，而以道爲合。九官十二牧師師濟濟之風，可想見矣。後世彈冠結綬、私相慶幸者，比焉耳，豈知升之義哉？
translation_en:
…encounters the happy conjunction of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers, rejoicing and rousing one another to action. No one obstructs his advancement: by pressing onward he meets his ruler and can bring lustre to the emperor’s undertakings. No one impedes his progress: by journeying south he finds his companions and can put his Way into practice. Truly, he can ascend and enjoy great good fortune! Could this be mere chance?

The two yang lines above are opening their minds to welcome worthy men, while the initial six, just beginning its ascent, can devote itself to service. Above, to advance virtue—such is the aspiration of the two yang lines. The initial line obediently supports them, wholly united with them in sustaining their loyal efforts to enlighten the ruler. Below, to serve the people—such is the aspiration of the two yang lines. The initial line acts with deference, wholly united with them in seeking to assist the transforming influence that brings prosperity and fulfilment. Sharing the same Way as companions, they trust one another ever more deeply. They therefore exert themselves to bring him forward, placing him at their side without regarding this as factional attachment. Working together with one heart, their mutual commitment grows ever stronger. They therefore hasten to recommend him, raising him to high office without regarding this as precipitous promotion. Thus, what enables the initial line to ascend is not simply the favorable time, but shared aspiration. Should those who seek advancement without grounds and compromise themselves to win acceptance not take warning?

Nevertheless, aspirations may unite; they must not become factional attachments. In the time of Ascending, above is a ruler whose steadfast correctness brings good fortune; below are ministers represented by ‘ascending into an empty city’ and ‘it is beneficial to offer the yue sacrifice.’ Ruler and ministers trust one another, and virtue and achievement come to fruition. Thus the gentleman gladly offers his services, joining with others through the Way. We can picture the noble bearing of the nine officials and twelve regional governors, learning from one another in dignified harmony. Those in later ages who dust off their caps and fasten their official sashes, privately congratulating one another on their good fortune, merely form factions. How could they understand the meaning of Ascending?

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
是故君子慎所以爲合
黄帝堯舜氏作通其變使民不倦神而化
之使民宜之易窮則變變則通通則久
是以自天祐之吉无不利黄帝堯舜垂
衣裳而天下治蓋取諸乾坤
莊敦義
同考試官教諭張批聖人神化與易道天道通
貫只一理此作深會其旨宜録以式
同考試官教諭吳批有融會有體裁三聖以經
===
法天此作能洩其秘亦化於文者矣
考試官教授吳批帝治無爲披文想見
考試官教授李批說理之文意象宛然
大傳詳言三聖因時以順治而明其取諸易焉
甚矣聖人不能違時也三聖所以因時而達之
治者非有取於乾坤哉大傳論制器尚象之事
至此若曰昔者聖王之繼世以出治也不先天
以開人各因時而立政是故黄帝堯舜嘗繼神
農氏而王矣於斯時也聖人知民情之趨不可
punctuated:
是故君子慎所以爲合。

黄帝堯舜氏作，通其變，使民不倦；神而化之，使民宜之。易窮則變，變則通，通則久，是以自天祐之，吉无不利。黄帝堯舜垂衣裳而天下治，蓋取諸乾坤。

莊敦義

同考試官教諭張批：「聖人神化與易道天道通貫只一理，此作深會其旨，宜録以式。」

同考試官教諭吳批：「有融會，有體裁，三聖以經法天，此作能洩其秘，亦化於文者矣。」

考試官教授吳批：「帝治無爲，披文想見。」

考試官教授李批：「說理之文，意象宛然。」

大傳詳言三聖因時以順治，而明其取諸易焉。甚矣，聖人不能違時也！三聖所以因時而達之治者，非有取於乾坤哉？大傳論制器尚象之事，至此若曰：昔者聖王之繼世以出治也，不先天以開人，各因時而立政。是故黄帝堯舜嘗繼神農氏而王矣。於斯時也，聖人知民情之趨不可
translation_en:
…Therefore the gentleman is cautious about the grounds on which he joins with others.

“When Huangdi, Yao, and Shun arose, they carried changes through, so that the people did not grow weary; through numinous transformation, they made these changes fitting for the people. In the Changes, reaching an impasse leads to change; change leads to free passage; free passage leads to endurance. Thus, ‘Heaven itself blesses him: good fortune, with nothing unfavorable.’ Huangdi, Yao, and Shun let their robes and skirts hang down, and all under Heaven was well governed. They presumably took this from Qian and Kun.”

Zhuang Dunyi.

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The sages’ numinous transformation, the Way of the Changes, and the Way of Heaven are connected throughout by a single principle. This composition deeply grasps that meaning and should be recorded as a model.”

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “It has integrated understanding and proper form. The three sages took Heaven as their model through enduring norms [?]; this composition reveals their secret. Its author, too, has attained transformation in writing.”

Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “The emperors’ government through nonaction: reading this composition, one can picture it.”

Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “A composition expounding principle, with vividly realized ideas and imagery.”

The Great Commentary explains in detail how the three sages followed the times to bring about harmonious government, and makes clear that they drew upon the Changes. How profoundly the sages were bound not to go against the times! Was it not from Qian and Kun that the three sages drew their means of following the times and attaining good government? The Great Commentary discusses the making of implements with regard for the images. At this point it seems to say: In antiquity, when sage kings succeeded one another through the generations and brought forth good government, they did not anticipate Heaven in enlightening the people; each established his administration in accordance with the times. Thus Huangdi, Yao, and Shun succeeded Shennong as sovereigns. At that time, the sages knew that the direction of the people’s dispositions could not…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
以襲故也於是化裁以達變而更之以維新之
治使民之變易以趨時者自鼓舞之不倦焉知
通變之術非所以强世也於是順化以宜民而
運之以自然之神使民之樂生而興行者自相
率以與能焉是理也本諸易者也易無終窮而
變以繼之是以推之卽準而可通也傳之無弊
而可久也雖聖人亦不能違乎易矣是道也合
於天者也天有顯道而順者佑之是以法天而
行動罔不吉也承天而治用無不利也雖天亦
===
不能違乎聖人矣然則黃帝堯舜夫何爲哉中
正爲觀但見其章之黼黻而已矣而民自喻於
不言之化恭默思治但見其示之法服而已矣
而世自底於從欲之風若此者寧非有取於乾
坤巳乎蓋無心而成化者乾坤所以妙乎物而
物不自知其爲功有心而無爲者聖人所以利
乎民而民不自知其爲利使聖人日斤斤然求
天下之變而更之則其神易息其化易窮而與
天地不相似矣嗟乎非三聖其孰能之雖然黃
punctuated: 以襲故也。於是化裁以達變，而更之以維新之治，使民之變易以趨時者，自鼓舞之不倦焉。知通變之術非所以强世也，於是順化以宜民，而運之以自然之神，使民之樂生而興行者，自相率以與能焉。是理也，本諸易者也。易無終窮，而變以繼之，是以推之卽準而可通也，傳之無弊而可久也。雖聖人亦不能違乎易矣。是道也，合於天者也。天有顯道，而順者佑之，是以法天而行，動罔不吉也；承天而治，用無不利也。雖天亦不能違乎聖人矣。然則黃帝堯舜夫何爲哉？中正爲觀，但見其章之黼黻而已矣，而民自喻於不言之化；恭默思治，但見其示之法服而已矣，而世自底於從欲之風。若此者，寧非有取於乾坤巳乎？蓋無心而成化者，乾坤所以妙乎物，而物不自知其爲功；有心而無爲者，聖人所以利乎民，而民不自知其爲利。使聖人日斤斤然求天下之變而更之，則其神易息，其化易窮，而與天地不相似矣。嗟乎！非三聖，其孰能之？雖然，黃
translation_en:
…continue adhering to old ways. Thus they adapted and regulated affairs to accommodate change, replacing the old with a renewed government, so that the people, changing to keep pace with the times, were themselves inspired to unflagging effort. They understood that the art of accommodating change was not a means of coercing the world. Thus they followed the course of transformation to meet the people's needs, setting it in motion through the wondrous efficacy of natural action, so that the people, delighting in life and rousing themselves to act, spontaneously led one another to contribute their abilities. This principle is rooted in the Book of Changes. The Changes never reaches an ultimate end: change carries it onward. Thus, when applied, it accords with the proper standard and works in every circumstance; when handed down, it remains free of defects and can endure. Even the sages could not depart from the Changes. This Way accords with Heaven. Heaven has a manifest Way and aids those who follow it. Thus, when they modeled their conduct on Heaven, none of their actions was inauspicious; when they governed in obedience to Heaven, nothing they undertook was without benefit. Even Heaven could not depart from the sages.

What, then, did Huangdi, Yao, and Shun actually do? Providing an example through their centrality and uprightness, they were seen only displaying their embroidered ceremonial robes; yet the people spontaneously understood their wordless transforming influence. Reverent and silent, intent on good government, they were seen only presenting themselves in their prescribed robes; yet the world spontaneously attained a condition in which people's desires were fulfilled. Could this have been anything other than drawing upon Qian and Kun? For accomplishing transformation without deliberate intent is how Qian and Kun wondrously act upon all things, while those things remain unaware of their achievement. Having intent yet acting without contrivance is how the sages benefit the people, while the people remain unaware of the benefit they confer. If the sages had busied themselves every day meticulously seeking out changes in the world and making alterations in response, their wondrous efficacy would readily have ceased, their transforming influence would readily have been exhausted, and they would no longer have resembled Heaven and Earth. Ah! Who but the three sages could have accomplished this? Nevertheless, Huang…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
帝遠矣今觀堯舜所以經世理物載在典謨至
詳備也要之運而不宰施而不設乾坤之理固
皆取足於一心矣後世不知此道騖紛更者拂
民情樂因循者昧權變又何異乎治不古若也
噫
書
欽若昊天曆象日月星辰
宋萬葉
同考試官教諭吳批不事彫琢而逸思粹語快
===
人心目書義之精者
同考試官教授何批曆象正所以欽若近作多析
為二事獨此渾成一意宜錄以式
考試官教授吳批深得帝堯命官之旨
考試官教授李批典雅可玩
聖君示作曆之本惟盡心以稽天文焉蓋天之
象數未易知也非敬順以稽之何以為作曆之
本哉帝堯首命羲和之意若曰帝王有代天之
責必有經天之政作曆政之首務也其要何在
punctuated:
帝遠矣！今觀堯舜所以經世理物，載在典謨，至詳備也。要之，運而不宰，施而不設，乾坤之理固皆取足於一心矣。後世不知此道，騖紛更者拂民情，樂因循者昧權變，又何異乎治不古若也？噫！

書
欽若昊天，曆象日月星辰。
宋萬葉

同考試官教諭吳批：「不事彫琢，而逸思粹語快人心目，書義之精者。」
同考試官教授何批：「曆象正所以欽若。近作多析為二事，獨此渾成一意，宜錄以式。」
考試官教授吳批：「深得帝堯命官之旨。」
考試官教授李批：「典雅可玩。」

聖君示作曆之本，惟盡心以稽天文焉。蓋天之象數未易知也，非敬順以稽之，何以為作曆之本哉？帝堯首命羲和之意，若曰：「帝王有代天之責，必有經天之政。作曆，政之首務也。其要何在
translation_en:
…Emperor lived long ago! Now, when we examine how Yao and Shun ordered the world and governed its affairs, we find this recorded in the Canons and Counsels in the fullest detail. In essence, they set things in motion without mastering them and bestowed benefits without contriving them: the principles of Qian and Kun—Heaven and Earth—were fully realized within their own minds. Later generations did not understand this Way. Those who pursued incessant changes offended the people’s feelings; those content to follow established practice failed to understand judicious adaptation. Why, then, should it be surprising that their government fell short of antiquity? Alas!

Book of Documents
“Reverently accord with August Heaven; calculate and observe the sun, moon, stars, and celestial markers.”
Song Wanye

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “Without resorting to ornamental carving and polishing, its soaring thoughts and refined language delight the mind and eye. An outstanding exposition of the Book of Documents.”
Comment by Associate Examiner He, Professor: “Calculating and observing are precisely the means of reverently according with Heaven. Recent compositions mostly divide these into two separate matters. This alone integrates them into a single conception; it should be recorded as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: “It profoundly grasps Emperor Yao’s purpose in commissioning his officials.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “Classically elegant and worthy of appreciative study.”

The sage ruler indicated the foundation of calendar-making: to devote one’s whole mind to examining celestial phenomena. For Heaven’s configurations and numerical patterns are not readily understood. Without examining them in reverent accord, how could one establish a foundation for making the calendar? The intention behind Emperor Yao’s initial commission to Xi and He was as though he said: “Emperors and kings bear the responsibility of acting on Heaven’s behalf and must therefore institute measures to order celestial affairs. Making the calendar is the foremost task of government. Where does its essential principle lie…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
哉今夫天之高也固廣遠而難知日月星辰繫
焉則有故而可考也使以慢易拂逆之私稽之
非所以求端於天而爲治曆之本矣汝必兢業
不忘而運之心思者奉順其自然之運嚴恭匪
懈而詳之制作者祗若乎本體之常日月星辰
之定數即昊天之數也則有曆以紀之而布算
之惟密不紊乎周天之行日月星辰之成象即
昊天之象也則有象以觀之而窺測之惟精不
爽乎麗天之運雖遲速順逆之不定循吾一定
===
之法以求之俾人文立而天文具在人時由之
以準也此其所關爲甚大而可以易心乘之耶
雖經緯次舍之靡常即吾有常之法以推之俾
物象具而天象可徵民功由之以定也此其所
係爲甚重而可以私心拂之耶觀此則帝堯敬
天之心不爲虛而授時有其地矣雖然堯豈爲
作曆敬天耶天道無私而普物帝王一敬以合
天均非有意于間也使因治曆而後有意于敬
天則敬爲未純而求其術不違天也難矣是故
punctuated: 哉？今夫天之高也，固廣遠而難知；日月星辰繫焉，則有故而可考也。使以慢易拂逆之私稽之，非所以求端於天而爲治曆之本矣。汝必兢業不忘，而運之心思者奉順其自然之運；嚴恭匪懈，而詳之制作者祗若乎本體之常。日月星辰之定數，即昊天之數也，則有曆以紀之，而布算之惟密，不紊乎周天之行；日月星辰之成象，即昊天之象也，則有象以觀之，而窺測之惟精，不爽乎麗天之運。雖遲速順逆之不定，循吾一定之法以求之，俾人文立而天文具在人時由之以準也。此其所關爲甚大，而可以易心乘之耶？雖經緯次舍之靡常，即吾有常之法以推之，俾物象具而天象可徵，民功由之以定也。此其所係爲甚重，而可以私心拂之耶？觀此，則帝堯敬天之心不爲虛，而授時有其地矣。雖然，堯豈爲作曆敬天耶？天道無私而普物，帝王一敬以合天，均非有意于間也。使因治曆而後有意于敬天，則敬爲未純，而求其術不違天也難矣。是故
translation_en:
…wherein does its essential principle lie? Now, Heaven in its height is indeed vast, remote, and difficult to comprehend. Yet the sun, moon, and stars are attached to it, and thus there are principles that can be investigated.
