If you investigate them with the selfish dispositions of negligence, carelessness, resistance, and defiance, this will provide no means of seeking the beginnings in Heaven and establishing a foundation for calendrical work. You must remain vigilant and never forget your duty, so that what you work out in your thoughts accords respectfully with their natural movements; you must be solemnly reverent and untiring, so that what you elaborate in your arrangements reverently follows the constancy of their fundamental nature. The fixed numerical regularities of the sun, moon, and stars are those of August Heaven itself. Thus there must be a calendar to record them, with calculations so meticulous that they do not confuse the movements around the celestial circuit. The configurations formed by the sun, moon, and stars are those of August Heaven itself. Thus there must be an astronomical instrument with which to observe them, with scrutiny and measurement so precise that they do not err concerning the movements of the bodies arrayed in Heaven.

Though their slowness and speed, direct and retrograde motions vary, we follow our fixed methods to investigate them, thereby establishing human patterns and making celestial patterns fully present, so that the seasons of human activity may be regulated accordingly [?]. What is at stake here is very great: could one approach it with a careless mind? Though their celestial coordinates and stations vary, we apply our constant methods to calculate them, thereby making the configurations of things complete and celestial phenomena verifiable, so that the people's labors may be scheduled accordingly. What depends upon this is of great consequence: could one oppose it with a selfish mind? Viewed in this light, Emperor Yao's reverence for Heaven was not empty, and his promulgation of the seasons had a firm foundation.

Yet did Yao revere Heaven merely for the sake of making a calendar? The Way of Heaven is impartial and extends to all things; emperors and kings, through undivided reverence, accord with Heaven. Neither introduces deliberate interference [?]. If only because of calendrical work one subsequently formed the intention to revere Heaven, that reverence would be impure, and it would be difficult to ensure that one's techniques did not run counter to Heaven. Therefore…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
堯之敬天不特見於治曆而放勳事業咸自此
推故曰敬者帝王傳心之要法
二五事一曰貌二曰言三曰視四曰聽五
曰思貌曰恭言曰從視曰明聽曰聰思
曰睿恭作肅從作乂明作哲聰作謀睿
作聖
陳文質
同考試官教諭張批天人合一之理發明殆盡善
潛心聖學而有得者
===
同考試官教授何批鋪敘得法詞不煩而意自貫
可以語天人之學矣
考試官教授吳批深得箕子演疇之旨
考試官教授李批詞義精切
君子衍五事之疇而誠身之道備矣蓋君道以
誠身為本也觀五事之目而德與用之兼全焉
存誠之功容可緩乎箕子衍疇之意蓋謂人君
一身位乎天人之中則必盡乎形性之理洪範
次二為五事果何如哉彼人得天之五行以生
punctuated:
堯之敬天不特見於治曆，而放勳事業咸自此推。故曰：敬者，帝王傳心之要法。
二、五事：一曰貌，二曰言，三曰視，四曰聽，五曰思。貌曰恭，言曰從，視曰明，聽曰聰，思曰睿。恭作肅，從作乂，明作哲，聰作謀，睿作聖。
陳文質
同考試官教諭張批：天人合一之理，發明殆盡，善潛心聖學而有得者。
同考試官教授何批：鋪敘得法，詞不煩而意自貫，可以語天人之學矣。
考試官教授吳批：深得箕子演疇之旨。
考試官教授李批：詞義精切。
君子衍五事之疇，而誠身之道備矣。蓋君道以誠身為本也。觀五事之目，而德與用之兼全焉，存誠之功容可緩乎？箕子衍疇之意，蓋謂人君一身位乎天人之中，則必盡乎形性之理。《洪範》次二為五事，果何如哉？彼人得天之五行以生
translation_en:
…Yao’s reverence for Heaven was manifest not merely in regulating the calendar: all the undertakings of this ruler of “Far-reaching Achievement” proceeded from it. Thus it is said: reverence is the essential method by which emperors and kings transmit the understanding of the heart.
“Second, the five personal matters: the first is demeanor; the second, speech; the third, sight; the fourth, hearing; the fifth, thought. Demeanor should be respectful; speech, compliant; sight, clear; hearing, acute; thought, penetrating. Respectfulness produces solemnity; compliance produces order; clarity produces discernment; acuteness produces good counsel; penetration produces sageliness.”
Chen Wenzhi 陳文質
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “He elucidates almost exhaustively the principle that Heaven and humanity form a unity. Here is someone skilled in devoting himself to the learning of the sages and attaining insight into it.”
Comment by Associate Examiner He, Professor: “The exposition is well ordered; the language is not prolix, yet the meaning runs coherently throughout. One may discuss the learning concerning Heaven and humanity with him.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: “He has deeply grasped Jizi’s purpose in expounding the categories.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “The language and meaning are precise and apt.”
When the gentleman elaborates the category of the five personal matters, the way of making oneself sincere is fully set forth. For the ruler’s way rests upon making himself sincere. Considering the items comprising the five personal matters, we find both virtue and its operation fully present. Can the work of preserving sincerity possibly be deferred? Jizi’s purpose in expounding the categories was, presumably, to say that the ruler, in his own person, occupies the position between Heaven and humanity and must therefore fully realize the principles of bodily form and inherent nature. The second category of the Great Plan consists of the five personal matters: what, precisely, does this mean? Human beings receive Heaven’s five phases and thereby come into being…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
也有五事焉自其始生而形具也故一曰貌形
具而氣揚也故二曰言三則發散而爲目之視
也四則翕聚而爲耳之聽也至於五則精氣之
會而思以通之焉蓋發見有先後之序而妙合
無理氣之殊全體大用胥此出矣故物則一原
也貌淑慎而恭言和順而從視之明無所蔽也
聽之聰無所壅也思則幾微悉通而恭從明聰
皆由之以貫徹矣是成形之內而成性者具焉
天之與於人者此其渾然畢具矣乎然體用一
===
致也恭以著乎端莊之度從以顯乎條理之章
明之所照而智識不眩也聰之所達而謀度不
遺也睿則神妙不測而肅乂哲謀皆由之以極
致矣是藏用之中而顯仁者行焉人之得於天
者此其燦然各足矣乎夫踐形盡性理固原於
至一以人合天機則通於無間然非主之以敬
亦安能以立極而敘倫哉大抵人道以聖爲極
也洪範衍五事而極於作聖是具形性者皆可
以爲聖而聖之不易至者豈其性殊哉亦弗思
punctuated: 也，有五事焉。自其始生而形具也，故一曰貌；形具而氣揚也，故二曰言；三則發散而爲目之視也；四則翕聚而爲耳之聽也；至於五，則精氣之會而思以通之焉。蓋發見有先後之序，而妙合無理氣之殊，全體大用胥此出矣。故物則一原也：貌淑慎而恭，言和順而從，視之明無所蔽也，聽之聰無所壅也；思則幾微悉通，而恭從明聰皆由之以貫徹矣。是成形之內而成性者具焉，天之與於人者，此其渾然畢具矣乎！然體用一致也：恭以著乎端莊之度，從以顯乎條理之章，明之所照而智識不眩也，聰之所達而謀度不遺也；睿則神妙不測，而肅乂哲謀皆由之以極致矣。是藏用之中而顯仁者行焉，人之得於天者，此其燦然各足矣乎！夫踐形盡性，理固原於至一；以人合天，機則通於無間。然非主之以敬，亦安能以立極而敘倫哉？大抵人道以聖爲極也。《洪範》衍五事而極於作聖，是具形性者皆可以爲聖，而聖之不易至者，豈其性殊哉？亦弗思
translation_en:
…there are five affairs. From the moment a person is born, bodily form is complete; thus the first is called demeanor. Once form is complete, vital energy issues forth; thus the second is called speech. Third, it disperses outward to become the eyes’ seeing. Fourth, it gathers inward to become the ears’ hearing. As for the fifth, essential vital energies converge, and thought brings them into communication. Although their manifestations follow a sequence, in their wondrous union there is no separation between principle and vital energy. The complete substance and its full functioning both emerge from this. Thus things and their normative principles have a single source: demeanor is virtuous and circumspect, and hence reverent; speech is harmonious and compliant, and hence accordant; clear vision is unobscured; acute hearing is unobstructed. Thought penetrates every incipient movement and subtle detail, and through it reverence, accordance, clarity, and acuity are all integrated. Thus, within the completed bodily form, all that constitutes one’s nature is present. Is this not the complete, undivided endowment that Heaven bestows upon human beings?

Yet substance and function form a unity. Reverence manifests itself in dignified bearing; accordance reveals itself in orderly expression. Where clarity illuminates, understanding is not confused; where acuity reaches, deliberation overlooks nothing. Penetrating insight is wondrous beyond fathoming, and through it seriousness, good order, wisdom, and deliberation all attain their fullest realization. Thus, within the concealed functioning, manifest benevolence operates. Is this not the endowment that human beings receive from Heaven, each aspect brilliantly sufficient in itself?

To fulfill one’s bodily form and fully realize one’s nature: the principle of this assuredly originates in ultimate unity. To bring the human into accord with Heaven: their workings communicate without any gap. Yet unless reverent attentiveness governs these, how could one establish the ultimate standard and set human relationships in order? Broadly speaking, the human Way takes sagehood as its ultimate standard. The Great Plan elaborates the five affairs and culminates in becoming a sage. This means that all who possess bodily form and nature can become sages. If sagehood is difficult to attain, can it be because their natures differ? They simply fail to reflect…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
耳矣然造就之功則係之君君身皇極之主也
敬而思之則聰明睿知皆從此出與天之五氣
相合而休徵應矣故五事以思爲要而聖人以
合天爲能
詩
羣黎百姓徧爲爾德
黃國彥
同考試官教諭鄭批善形容化成氣象而納誨
之意溢于言表必有忠愛之忱者非直取其文也
===
同考試官教諭伍批此題助君爲德之意最難
體貼子能渾融詩意以寓祝願之情取之
考試官教授吳批善發臣子祝君之意
考試官教授李批詞理俱精
人君之福合天下而成德也蓋天下化成皆君
德之所及也而王道之多助見矣玆非人君之
全福乎周臣託神貺以答君賜也若曰人君聯
屬天下以成其身則亦幷包天下以爲之福神
之福君豈特民俗之淳而已哉彼羣黎百姓莫
punctuated:
耳矣。然造就之功，則係之君。君身，皇極之主也。敬而思之，則聰明睿知皆從此出，與天之五氣相合，而休徵應矣。故五事以思爲要，而聖人以合天爲能。

詩
羣黎百姓，徧爲爾德。
黃國彥

同考試官教諭鄭批：善形容化成氣象，而納誨之意溢于言表，必有忠愛之忱者，非直取其文也。
同考試官教諭伍批：此題助君爲德之意最難體貼，子能渾融詩意，以寓祝願之情，取之。
考試官教授吳批：善發臣子祝君之意。
考試官教授李批：詞理俱精。

人君之福，合天下而成德也。蓋天下化成，皆君德之所及也，而王道之多助見矣。玆非人君之全福乎？周臣託神貺以答君賜也，若曰：人君聯屬天下以成其身，則亦幷包天下以爲之福。神之福君，豈特民俗之淳而已哉？彼羣黎百姓，莫
translation_en:
…that is all. Yet the work of bringing people to fulfillment depends upon the ruler. The ruler himself presides over the August Ultimate. If he reflects with reverence, acuity of hearing, clarity of sight, sagacity, and wisdom all spring from this. They accord with Heaven’s five vital forces, and auspicious signs respond. Thus, among the Five Activities, reflection is essential, and the sage’s ability lies in according with Heaven.

Book of Odes
“The multitudes of the common people all practice your virtue.”
Huang Guoyan

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: He skillfully portrays the condition of a people fully transformed by moral influence, while his intention to offer admonition reaches beyond his words. He must possess sincere loyalty and devotion. My selection rests on more than his literary accomplishment alone.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu 伍, Instructor: The intention of helping the ruler cultivate virtue implicit in this topic is particularly difficult to grasp. You have harmoniously integrated the meaning of the ode to convey wishes for the ruler’s blessings. I select this answer.
Comment by Examiner Wu 吳, Professor: He skillfully brings out the subject’s intention of wishing blessings upon his ruler.
Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: Both expression and reasoning are refined.

The ruler’s blessing consists in uniting all under Heaven in the fulfillment of virtue. For the moral transformation of all under Heaven is entirely the reach of the ruler’s virtue, and therein one sees the many sources of support for the kingly Way. Is this not the ruler’s complete blessing? A subject of Zhou invokes blessings bestowed by the spirits to requite his ruler’s gifts, as though saying: The ruler binds all under Heaven together to bring his own person to fulfillment; thus his blessings likewise embrace all under Heaven. Can the spirits’ blessing of the ruler consist merely in the purity of popular customs? Among those multitudes of the common people, there are none…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
非王民也則民之德亦莫非王化也使民德未
新是王化有未洽矣王化未洽是君福有未全
矣玆惟先公先王體吾王弘化之心而神道之
感通有以綏夫從欲之治牖斯民孚惠之念而
天機之默相有以動其敏德之風惟皇建極矣
民亦象之而歸極焉興仁興讓無一人不協於
化中惟聖成能矣民亦則之而與能焉遵道遵
路無一方不躋於順治近而畿甸則覲耿光之
下濟咸訓行而不違道德一而風俗同自朝廷
===
達之四國翕如也百姓之昭明孰非帝則之默
順乎遠而海隅則仰文命之覃敷咸鼓舞而不
倦敎化行而習俗美自邦畿達之萬方藹如也
黎民之於變孰非帝德之廣運乎是其始也以
一人之德風乎天下而若或啓之上下一心德
之至也其旣也以天下之德歸於一人而若或
助之君民一德治之極也如是而後爲吾王大
同之福如是而後爲明神詒福之全吾人對揚
之情藉此其少伸乎噫天保臣子以是答君其
punctuated: 非王民也，則民之德亦莫非王化也。使民德未新，是王化有未洽矣；王化未洽，是君福有未全矣。玆惟先公先王體吾王弘化之心，而神道之感通有以綏夫從欲之治；牖斯民孚惠之念，而天機之默相有以動其敏德之風。惟皇建極矣，民亦象之而歸極焉，興仁興讓，無一人不協於化中；惟聖成能矣，民亦則之而與能焉，遵道遵路，無一方不躋於順治。近而畿甸，則覲耿光之下濟，咸訓行而不違，道德一而風俗同，自朝廷達之四國，翕如也。百姓之昭明，孰非帝則之默順乎？遠而海隅，則仰文命之覃敷，咸鼓舞而不倦，敎化行而習俗美，自邦畿達之萬方，藹如也。黎民之於變，孰非帝德之廣運乎？是其始也，以一人之德風乎天下，而若或啓之，上下一心，德之至也；其旣也，以天下之德歸於一人，而若或助之，君民一德，治之極也。如是而後爲吾王大同之福，如是而後爲明神詒福之全。吾人對揚之情，藉此其少伸乎？噫！《天保》臣子以是答君，其
translation_en:
…are the king’s subjects; thus the people’s virtue, too, is entirely the result of the king’s transforming influence. If the people’s virtue has not been renewed, the king’s transforming influence has not yet reached everywhere; if that influence has not reached everywhere, the ruler’s blessings are not yet complete. Thus the former lords and kings enter into our king’s desire to extend his transforming influence: through the responsive communion of the spirits, they secure a government that accords with his wishes. They awaken in the people thoughts of trust and obedience, and through the unseen assistance of Heaven’s workings, stir them to diligent pursuit of virtue.

The sovereign establishes the supreme standard; the people emulate him and turn toward that standard. They rise to benevolence and deference, and not a single person fails to accord with his transforming influence. The sage fully develops his capacities; the people likewise take him as their model and share in that achievement. They follow the Way and its paths, and no region fails to attain orderly government. Nearby, in the royal domain, they behold his brilliant radiance reaching down to them; all follow his instruction without deviation. Moral principles are unified and customs become alike: from the court to the lands in all four directions, all is harmonious. How could the people’s enlightenment be anything other than their unspoken conformity to the sovereign’s standard? Far away, at the edges of the seas, they look up to the far-reaching spread of his civil commands; all are inspired and tireless. Moral instruction prevails and customs improve: from the royal domain to the myriad regions, all flourishes. How could the common people’s transformation be anything other than the far-reaching operation of the sovereign’s virtue?

At the outset, the virtue of the one man moves all under Heaven, as though some unseen power were opening the way for him. Those above and below are of one mind: this is virtue at its utmost. Subsequently, the virtue of all under Heaven converges upon the one man, as though some unseen power were assisting him. Ruler and people share one virtue: this is government at its highest perfection. Only thus are our king’s blessings of universal concord realized; only thus are the blessings bestowed by the luminous spirits complete. Might our desire to acknowledge and extol his bounty find some small expression through this? Ah! With this, the subject who composed “Heaven Protects” answered his ruler; surely he…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
亦善承休德者矣抑祝君之福而及於民德者
何也蓋崇高富貴人君已自有其福矣惟夫百
姓興行天下太平然後盛大之福永言保之故
箕疇斂福而繼曰會極歸極亦此意也然欲民
之歸德非君之脩德又何以致之此固詩人立
言之㫖也保大而思永者尚有取於斯哉
文王孫子本支百世凡周之士不顯亦世
葉明元
同考試官教諭鄭批理明辭達格整意新且首
末歸重於文王深得經㫖
===
同考試官教諭伍批子孫臣庶之福皆文王敬
德格天所致此作發明天人相與之意甚𭻍取之
考試官教授吳批詞意莊重得告君體
考試官教授李批文有思致
天之命周君臣世濟其美也蓋德隆則命從而
隆也合子孫臣庶而永孚於休天之命周寧有
窮乎宜周公述此以戒成王也若曰天命聖德
相為感應者也以文德之亹亹而天之敷錫豈
punctuated:
亦善承休德者矣。抑祝君之福而及於民德者，何也？蓋崇高富貴，人君已自有其福矣。惟夫百姓興行，天下太平，然後盛大之福，永言保之。故箕疇斂福，而繼曰會極歸極，亦此意也。然欲民之歸德，非君之脩德，又何以致之？此固詩人立言之㫖也。保大而思永者，尚有取於斯哉！

文王孫子，本支百世。凡周之士，不顯亦世。
葉明元

同考試官教諭鄭批：理明辭達，格整意新，且首末歸重於文王，深得經㫖。
同考試官教諭伍批：子孫臣庶之福，皆文王敬德格天所致。此作發明天人相與之意，甚𭻍，取之。
考試官教授吳批：詞意莊重，得告君體。
考試官教授李批：文有思致。

天之命周，君臣世濟其美也。蓋德隆，則命從而隆也。合子孫臣庶而永孚於休，天之命周寧有窮乎？宜周公述此以戒成王也。若曰：天命聖德，相為感應者也。以文德之亹亹，而天之敷錫豈
translation_en:
…were also adept at receiving and carrying forward their ruler’s beneficent virtue. Yet why, in wishing blessings upon the ruler, does the poem extend its concern to the people’s virtue? Lofty station, wealth, and honor are blessings that the ruler already possesses. Only when the common people are stirred to virtuous conduct and all under Heaven enjoys peace can these abundant blessings be preserved forever. Thus, in the Plan transmitted by Jizi, the gathering of blessings is followed by the words concerning assembling at and returning to the supreme standard: this conveys the same meaning. Yet if one wishes the people to turn toward virtue, how can this be brought about unless the ruler cultivates his own virtue? This is surely the poet’s purpose in framing these words. Those who would preserve their greatness and seek its perpetuity may still find something to draw upon here!

“King Wen’s descendants: the main line and collateral branches endure for a hundred generations. All the officers of Zhou—are they not illustrious, generation after generation?”
Ye Mingyuan

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The reasoning is clear and the language expressive; the structure is orderly and the conception fresh. Moreover, both the opening and the conclusion place the emphasis on King Wen, showing a deep understanding of the classic’s purport.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “The blessings of descendants, ministers, and common people were all brought about by King Wen’s reverent cultivation of virtue, which reached Heaven. This composition elucidates the meaning of the mutual relationship between Heaven and humanity. It is very [unclear character: 𭻍; ?]; I accept it.”

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: “The language and thought are dignified and weighty, achieving the proper manner for addressing a ruler.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “The composition shows thoughtful conception.”

In Heaven’s granting the mandate to Zhou, rulers and ministers carried forward its excellence from generation to generation. For when virtue is exalted, the mandate is correspondingly exalted. With descendants, ministers, and common people all together enduring in blessedness, could Heaven’s mandate to Zhou ever have an end? It was fitting that the Duke of Zhou should recount this to admonish King Cheng. It is as though he said: Heaven’s mandate and the sage’s virtue call forth responses in one another. Given King Wen’s unremitting cultivation of virtue, could Heaven’s abundant bestowal possibly…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
惟尊榮其身已哉誠以文王孫子今固宜君宜
王矣由今而百世皆文王一體之親也而天之
敷錫猶夫初焉謨烈重光膺景命於有僕祚胤
永錫衍奕業於無疆爲本宗者順帝則而不違
世總威福之柄也爲支庶者謹侯度而罔忒世
守屏翰之司也以建皇極以奉王章而螽斯麟
趾之祥蓋與天相爲無極矣是在子孫承之固
爲勿替之休而在文王垂之不爲有秩之祜乎
凡周之士今固有德有造矣由今而百世皆文
===
王一體之臣也而天之陳錫猶夫今焉喜起交
孚世際譽髦之盛親賢並茂永資篤棐之忠在
諸侯則世脩六德而亮采有邦也在大夫則世
脩三德而浚明有家也以翊王室以佐侯封而
菁莪棫樸之士蓋與周相爲匹休矣是在臣庶
受之固爲承家之慶而在我周得之不爲輔國
之資乎吁以百世之遠而子孫臣庶皆能脩德
以承休者莫非文德之所貽也嗣王可不念之
哉抑創業固難守成尤不易矧成王以冲年而
punctuated:
惟尊榮其身已哉？誠以文王孫子，今固宜君宜王矣。由今而百世，皆文王一體之親也，而天之敷錫猶夫初焉。謨烈重光，膺景命於有僕；祚胤永錫，衍奕業於無疆。爲本宗者，順帝則而不違，世總威福之柄也；爲支庶者，謹侯度而罔忒，世守屏翰之司也。以建皇極，以奉王章，而螽斯麟趾之祥，蓋與天相爲無極矣。是在子孫承之，固爲勿替之休，而在文王垂之，不爲有秩之祜乎？

凡周之士，今固有德有造矣。由今而百世，皆文王一體之臣也，而天之陳錫猶夫今焉。喜起交孚，世際譽髦之盛；親賢並茂，永資篤棐之忠。在諸侯，則世脩六德，而亮采有邦也；在大夫，則世脩三德，而浚明有家也。以翊王室，以佐侯封，而菁莪棫樸之士，蓋與周相爲匹休矣。是在臣庶受之，固爲承家之慶，而在我周得之，不爲輔國之資乎？

吁！以百世之遠，而子孫臣庶皆能脩德以承休者，莫非文德之所貽也。嗣王可不念之哉？抑創業固難，守成尤不易，矧成王以冲年而
translation_en:
…could it merely have been to confer honor and glory upon his own person? Indeed, King Wen’s descendants are already fit to be lords and kings. From now through a hundred generations, all are his kin, forming one body with him, and Heaven will bestow its gifts just as it did at the beginning. His wise plans and glorious achievements will shine anew, and his descendants will receive the great mandate in its fullness [?]; blessings upon his lineage will be bestowed forever, extending his splendid enterprise without limit. Those of the principal line will follow the Supreme Lord’s standards without deviation, wielding the authority to punish and reward generation after generation. Those of the collateral lines will carefully observe the rules for feudal lords without error, maintaining their charge as protective bulwarks generation after generation. Thus they will establish the sovereign’s supreme standard and uphold royal regulations. The auspicious promise of the “Locusts” and “The Qilin’s Hooves”—of flourishing and virtuous descendants—will be as boundless as Heaven itself. As inherited by his descendants, this is indeed an unfailing blessing; as handed down by King Wen, is it not an enduring bounty?

All the officers of Zhou already possess virtue and accomplishment. From now through a hundred generations, all will be ministers who form one body with King Wen, and Heaven will lavish its gifts just as it does today. Ruler and ministers, joyful and eager in their duties, will trust one another; every generation will enjoy an abundance of eminent and talented men. Royal kinsmen and worthy men alike will flourish, providing lasting support through their loyal and devoted assistance. Among the feudal lords, successive generations will cultivate the six virtues and faithfully discharge their duties in their states. Among the grand masters, successive generations will cultivate the three virtues and display profound discernment in governing their households. Thus they will support the royal house and assist the lords in their domains. The officers celebrated in “Luxuriant Southernwood” and “The Yu and Pu Trees” will share in Zhou’s enduring glory. As received by ministers and subjects, this is indeed the blessing of perpetuating their houses; as gained by our Zhou, is it not a resource for sustaining the state?

Ah! That even a hundred generations hence, descendants, ministers, and subjects should all be able to cultivate virtue and thereby inherit these blessings is entirely the legacy of King Wen’s virtue. Can the succeeding king fail to bear this in mind? Yet founding a dynasty is certainly difficult, and preserving its achievements is still harder, especially when King Cheng, at so tender an age,…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
承大業其於天人相與之際尤有不可忽者故
周公戒之惓惓以天命祖德爲言無非欲其敬
天法祖而脩德以凝命也卒至成王學懋於緝
熈命基於宥密而爲守成之令主孰非周公輔
相之功哉噫若周之君臣眞可爲萬世法矣
春秋
秋九月齊侯宋公江人黃人盟于貫〔僖公〕
〔二年〕秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于陽穀
〔僖公三年〕
===
林繼志
同考試官教諭伍批盟會江黃皆爲攘楚計
茲作渾融題意詞語謹嚴宜錄以式
同考試官教諭吳批此題上主盟重慮義下主
會重奇正是作發明精確而詞亦嚴整
考試官教授吳批簡健渾成經義之佳者
考試官教授李批語精義正深得經旨
春秋於霸主有予其結遠以制外者有與其定
謀以攘外者此桓欲伐楚而先結江黃謀定陽
punctuated:
承大業，其於天人相與之際，尤有不可忽者。故周公戒之惓惓，以天命祖德爲言，無非欲其敬天法祖，而脩德以凝命也。卒至成王學懋於緝熈，命基於宥密，而爲守成之令主，孰非周公輔相之功哉？噫！若周之君臣，眞可爲萬世法矣！

春秋

秋九月，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫。〔僖公〕〔二年〕秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。〔僖公三年〕

林繼志

同考試官教諭伍批：盟會江黃，皆爲攘楚計。茲作渾融題意，詞語謹嚴，宜錄以式。

同考試官教諭吳批：此題上主盟，重慮義；下主會，重奇正。是作發明精確，而詞亦嚴整。

考試官教授吳批：簡健渾成，經義之佳者。

考試官教授李批：語精義正，深得經旨。

春秋於霸主，有予其結遠以制外者，有與其定謀以攘外者。此桓欲伐楚，而先結江黃，謀定陽
translation_en:
…inheriting the great enterprise, he had particular reason to neglect nothing concerning the interaction of Heaven and humanity. Thus the Duke of Zhou earnestly admonished him, speaking of Heaven’s Mandate and his ancestors’ virtue, solely to make him revere Heaven, emulate his ancestors, and cultivate virtue to secure the Mandate. Eventually King Cheng became diligent in learning to perpetuate enlightenment, established the Mandate upon profound tranquillity, and became an excellent ruler who preserved the achievements of his predecessors. What part of this was not due to the Duke of Zhou’s assistance? Ah! Such rulers and ministers as those of Zhou truly can serve as models for all generations!

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In autumn, in the ninth month, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and men of Jiang and Huang made a covenant at Guan.” 〔Second year of Duke Xi.〕 “In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and men of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu.” 〔Third year of Duke Xi.〕

Lin Jizhi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu 伍, Instructor: “The covenant and meeting with Jiang and Huang were both plans to repel Chu. This composition thoroughly integrates the meaning of the topic, and its language is careful and rigorous. It should be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu 吳, Instructor: “The first part of this topic centers on the covenant, emphasizing deliberation and righteousness [?]; the second centers on the meeting, emphasizing unconventional and conventional strategy. This composition elucidates these points precisely, and its language is also rigorous and orderly.”

Comment by Examiner Wu 吳, Professor: “Concise, vigorous, and thoroughly integrated: an excellent exposition of the classic’s meaning.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “The language is refined and the interpretation correct, penetrating deeply into the classic’s purport.”

In its treatment of hegemonic rulers, the Spring and Autumn Annals sometimes approves their forging ties with distant states to restrain external powers, and sometimes approves their settling plans to repel external powers. Here, Duke Huan wished to attack Chu, so he first formed ties with Jiang and Huang, and settled his plans at Yang…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
穀安攘之略見矣故春秋兩予之且貫澤曷盟
也桓結江黃也聞八國皆在矣獨舉江黃者何
曰許是盟也蓋攘夷之道非用兵之難而力有
弗協之患楚固崛强也使黨有未攜焉楚可得
而撓乎幸而桓有貫之盟焉偕我宋公離彼服
屬之黨結彼江黃成我掎角之勢在楚人則斷
其右臂而勢以孤在中國則免於左衽而義以
著此可見桓見天下之大勢而制楚無遺慮矣
故盟雖春秋所不取而貫澤之盟經獨言遠國
===
者許桓之能結遠也陽穀曷會也桓謀伐楚也
聞諸侯大會矣末言江黃者何曰善是謀也蓋
攘夷之道非克敵之難而謀有弗豫之患諸侯
皆新附也使約弗再申焉楚可得而伐乎幸而
桓有陽穀之會焉定八國為正兵以當其前分
江黃為奇兵以擬其後正則敦陳整旅而進無
所乘奇則藏機設伏而退無所據此可見桓識
天下之大機而服楚有勝算矣故會雖諸侯不
得為而陽穀之會經末言江黃者善桓之能定
punctuated:
穀，安攘之略見矣，故春秋兩予之。且貫澤曷盟也？桓結江黃也。聞八國皆在矣，獨舉江黃者何？曰：許是盟也。蓋攘夷之道，非用兵之難，而力有弗協之患。楚固崛强也，使黨有未攜焉，楚可得而撓乎？幸而桓有貫之盟焉，偕我宋公，離彼服屬之黨，結彼江黃，成我掎角之勢。在楚人則斷其右臂而勢以孤，在中國則免於左衽而義以著。此可見桓見天下之大勢，而制楚無遺慮矣。故盟雖春秋所不取，而貫澤之盟，經獨言遠國者，許桓之能結遠也。

陽穀曷會也？桓謀伐楚也。聞諸侯大會矣，末言江黃者何？曰：善是謀也。蓋攘夷之道，非克敵之難，而謀有弗豫之患。諸侯皆新附也，使約弗再申焉，楚可得而伐乎？幸而桓有陽穀之會焉，定八國為正兵以當其前，分江黃為奇兵以擬其後。正則敦陳整旅而進無所乘，奇則藏機設伏而退無所據。此可見桓識天下之大機，而服楚有勝算矣。故會雖諸侯不得為，而陽穀之會，經末言江黃者，善桓之能定
translation_en:
…at Yanggu, his strategy for securing the central states and repelling outsiders became apparent. Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals commends him on both occasions. Why was there a covenant at Guanze? Duke Huan was forming an alliance with Jiang and Huang. We hear that all eight states were present; why, then, are Jiang and Huang alone singled out? The answer is that this signifies approval of the covenant. For in repelling outsiders, the difficulty lies less in deploying troops than in the danger that their efforts will not be coordinated. Chu was certainly formidable. If its allies had not been drawn away, could Chu have been checked? Fortunately, Duke Huan held the covenant at Guan. Together with our Duke of Song, he detached Chu’s subordinate allies and allied with Jiang and Huang, establishing a position from which to attack on converging fronts. For Chu, this meant having its right arm severed and becoming isolated; for the central states, it meant escaping the left-fastened robes of foreign rule and making righteousness manifest. This shows that Duke Huan understood the overall configuration of power in the realm and overlooked nothing in his plans to restrain Chu. Thus, although the Spring and Autumn Annals generally disapproves of covenants, its naming only the distant states in recording the covenant at Guanze commends Duke Huan’s ability to ally with distant states.

Why was there a meeting at Yanggu? Duke Huan was planning to attack Chu. We hear that the regional lords assembled in great numbers; why, then, are Jiang and Huang mentioned at the end? The answer is that this signifies approval of the plan. For in repelling outsiders, the difficulty lies less in defeating the enemy than in the danger of failing to plan beforehand. The regional lords had all only recently joined him. If their agreement had not been reaffirmed, could Chu have been attacked? Fortunately, Duke Huan held the meeting at Yanggu. He designated the eight states as the regular force to confront Chu’s front and assigned Jiang and Huang separately as an unconventional force to threaten its rear. The regular force would strengthen its formations and put its troops in order, leaving Chu no opening to exploit in advancing; the unconventional force would conceal its designs and lay ambushes, leaving Chu no secure position upon retreating. This shows that Duke Huan understood the crucial strategic opportunities in the realm and had sound calculations for victory in subduing Chu. Thus, although the regional lords were not entitled to convene such meetings, the Classic’s mentioning Jiang and Huang at the end of its account of the meeting at Yanggu praises Duke Huan’s ability to settle…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
謀也是則始而盟貫以結遠子之繼而爲會以
定謀子之聖人惓惓攘夷安夏之意其精矣乎
抑貫之盟陽穀之會桓得江黃則足以制楚矣
楚旣受盟而志巳驕溢再乎陽穀之會寵樂竝
行而桓覇衰矣噫勿怠勿荒王者事也桓何足
以語之獨江黃以向義而蒙辜焉可惜也夫
冬公會晋侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕
子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭十
有二月已亥同盟于戲襄公九年夏公
===
會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷定公十年
蔡應科
同考試官敎諭伍批發揮王道伯功語有分曉而
體格平正經學之優者
同考試官敎諭吳批此題諸士類多填塞事實是
作刋落時藝而詞意明盡讀之令人爽然宜錄以式
考試官敎授吳批詞意純正取之
考試官敎授李批發不戰不師意明切
聖賢之相君皆得待敵之道焉此見智筭以謀
punctuated:
謀也。是則始而盟貫以結遠，子之；繼而爲會以定謀，子之。聖人惓惓攘夷安夏之意，其精矣乎！抑貫之盟、陽穀之會，桓得江黃，則足以制楚矣。楚旣受盟，而志巳驕溢；再乎陽穀之會，寵樂竝行，而桓覇衰矣。噫！勿怠勿荒，王者事也，桓何足以語之？獨江黃以向義而蒙辜焉，可惜也夫！
冬，公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月，已亥，同盟于戲。襄公九年。夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。定公十年。
蔡應科
同考試官敎諭伍批：發揮王道伯功，語有分曉，而體格平正，經學之優者。
同考試官敎諭吳批：此題諸士類多填塞事實，是作刋落時藝，而詞意明盡，讀之令人爽然，宜錄以式。
考試官敎授吳批：詞意純正，取之。
考試官敎授李批：發不戰不師意明切。
聖賢之相君，皆得待敵之道焉。此見智筭以謀
translation_en:
…his planning. Thus, first, when he covenanted at Guan to establish ties with distant states, the text accorded their rulers the title of viscount; subsequently, when he held the meeting to settle his plans, it again accorded them that title. How subtle was the sage’s earnest concern to repel the outsiders and bring peace to the Xia states! Yet through the covenant at Guan and the meeting at Yanggu, Duke Huan secured Jiang and Huang as allies and thereby gained sufficient strength to check Chu. Once Chu had accepted the covenant, however, his ambition swelled into arrogance. At a further meeting at Yanggu [?], favoritism and pleasure went hand in hand, and Duke Huan’s hegemony declined. Alas! To be neither negligent nor dissipated is the business of a true king: how could Huan measure up to this? Only Jiang and Huang, who suffered punishment for turning toward righteousness, deserve our sorrow!
“In winter, the duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, to attack Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the jihai day [?], they jointly covenanted at Xi.” Ninth year of Duke Xiang. “In summer, the duke met with the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu.” Tenth year of Duke Ding.
Cai Yingke.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu 伍, Instructor: “It expounds the kingly Way and the achievements of hegemons with clear distinctions in its wording, while its structure and style are balanced and correct. An excellent example of classical scholarship.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu 吳, Instructor: “Most candidates addressing this topic merely cram their essays with historical facts. This composition strips away the conventions of contemporary examination writing, expressing its meaning clearly and fully. Reading it is refreshing. It should be recorded as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Wu 吳, Professor: “Its wording and ideas are pure and correct. Accept it.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “It elucidates clearly and precisely the meaning of achieving results without battle or the deployment of armies.”
When sages and worthies assisted their rulers, they all grasped the proper way to deal with an enemy. Here we see Zhi Ying [?], through strategic planning…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
駕楚孔子以禮化齊皆春秋中之僅見者乎且
待敵之道王者尚德伯者尚謀春秋時知此道
者鮮矣何幸於智罃孔子見之耶以智罃言之
方晉悼之伐鄭也楚救未至鄭人行成將待强
而民是庇矣使好戰者處此則兵刃旣接大勞
其有艾乎幸智罃之相悼也而善陣之法明焉
許盟旋師欲以養我之銳分軍逆來務以摧彼
之鋒凡所以駕楚者不以戰而以謀也彼楚雖
橫也寧不爲謀阻耶自是驕悍者力屈攜貳者
===
心服不謂之善謀之效不可也美哉罃也非賢
而能若是乎以孔子言之方夾谷之講會也兩
君就壇犁彌獻策將辱魯而加之兵矣使昧禮
者處此則鼓譟一起俘獲其能免乎幸孔子之
相定也而古人之道明焉不曰干盟偪好以啓
其衷則曰不祥愆義以糾其失凡所以感齊者
不以師而以禮也彼齊雖强也寧不爲禮動耶
由是景公悔過而遽止定公飲至而復安不謂
之明禮之功不可也大哉孔子也非聖而能若
punctuated: 駕楚，孔子以禮化齊，皆春秋中之僅見者乎？且待敵之道，王者尚德，伯者尚謀，春秋時知此道者鮮矣，何幸於智罃、孔子見之耶！以智罃言之，方晉悼之伐鄭也，楚救未至，鄭人行成，將待强而民是庇矣。使好戰者處此，則兵刃旣接，大勞其有艾乎？幸智罃之相悼也，而善陣之法明焉。許盟旋師，欲以養我之銳；分軍逆來，務以摧彼之鋒。凡所以駕楚者，不以戰而以謀也。彼楚雖橫也，寧不爲謀阻耶？自是驕悍者力屈，攜貳者心服，不謂之善謀之效不可也。美哉，罃也！非賢而能若是乎？以孔子言之，方夾谷之講會也，兩君就壇，犁彌獻策，將辱魯而加之兵矣。使昧禮者處此，則鼓譟一起，俘獲其能免乎？幸孔子之相定也，而古人之道明焉。不曰干盟偪好以啓其衷，則曰不祥愆義以糾其失。凡所以感齊者，不以師而以禮也。彼齊雖强也，寧不爲禮動耶？由是景公悔過而遽止，定公飲至而復安，不謂之明禮之功不可也。大哉，孔子也！非聖而能若
translation_en:
…to master Chu, while Kongzi transformed Qi through ritual propriety: were these not rare achievements in the Spring and Autumn period? In dealing with enemies, the true king esteems virtue, while the hegemon esteems strategy. Few in the Spring and Autumn period understood this way. How fortunate that we see it in Zhi Ying and Kongzi!

Take Zhi Ying. When Duke Dao of Jin attacked Zheng, reinforcements from Chu had not yet arrived, and the people of Zheng sued for peace. They intended to await the stronger power and thereby shelter their people. Had someone fond of warfare faced this situation, once blades crossed, would the great toil ever have ended? Fortunately, Zhi Ying assisted Duke Dao, and the art of skillful military deployment became manifest. He accepted the covenant and withdrew the army, intending to preserve his own troops’ vigor; he divided the forces to meet the approaching enemy, seeking to blunt its spearhead. All his means of mastering Chu relied on strategy rather than battle. Though Chu was overbearing, how could it escape being checked by strategy? Thereafter, the arrogant and fierce were exhausted in strength, and those wavering in allegiance submitted in their hearts. This must be called the effect of skillful strategy. Admirable indeed was Ying! Could anyone but a worthy have achieved this?

Take Kongzi. At the diplomatic meeting at Jiagu, the two rulers ascended the platform, and Li Mi offered a scheme to humiliate Lu and bring armed force against it. Had someone ignorant of ritual propriety faced this situation, once the drumming and shouting began, could he have escaped capture? Fortunately, Kongzi assisted Duke Ding, and the way of the ancients became manifest. He spoke of violating the covenant and coercing a friendly state to awaken their conscience, and of inauspicious conduct and offenses against righteousness to correct their faults. All his means of moving Qi relied on ritual propriety rather than troops. Though Qi was strong, how could it remain unmoved by ritual propriety? Consequently, Duke Jing regretted his wrongdoing and abruptly halted the proceedings, while Duke Ding returned to celebrate with the customary drinking rite and was secure once more. This must be called the achievement of understanding ritual propriety. Great indeed was Kongzi! Could anyone but a sage have achieved such…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
是乎夫至難駕者楚也智罃能以謀敝之至難
服者齊也孔子能以禮化之聖賢之有益於人
國也固如是夫抑駕楚者固智罃之功也然治
楚未幾而通吳之使繼至豈智罃不在側耶化
齊者固孔子之力也然能使萊人之不我侮而
不能使女樂之不受能使三田之歸而不能使
成邑之墮豈其致治之難耶蓋孔子之能行者
道也而道之所以行者則存乎其君也治功之
不成要亦定公用聖道之不專耳若晉之通吳
===
雖悼公之失而智罃諸臣不得不執其咎
禮記
君子曰大德不官大道不器大信不約大
時不齊察於此四者可以有志於本矣
潘維岳
同考試官教諭張批天道聖人以有本而充是作
體貼瑩徹而詞亦足以發之文之有本者也
同考試官教諭劉批平實中有逸趣冲淡中有
精思布帛菽粟之文也
punctuated:
是乎？夫至難駕者楚也，智罃能以謀敝之；至難服者齊也，孔子能以禮化之。聖賢之有益於人國也，固如是夫！抑駕楚者固智罃之功也，然治楚未幾，而通吳之使繼至，豈智罃不在側耶？化齊者固孔子之力也，然能使萊人之不我侮，而不能使女樂之不受；能使三田之歸，而不能使成邑之墮，豈其致治之難耶？蓋孔子之能行者道也，而道之所以行者則存乎其君也。治功之不成，要亦定公用聖道之不專耳。若晉之通吳，雖悼公之失，而智罃諸臣不得不執其咎。

禮記
君子曰：「大德不官，大道不器，大信不約，大時不齊。察於此四者，可以有志於本矣。」
潘維岳

同考試官教諭張批：「天道聖人以有本而充，是作體貼瑩徹，而詞亦足以發之，文之有本者也。」

同考試官教諭劉批：「平實中有逸趣，冲淡中有精思，布帛菽粟之文也。」
translation_en:
…like this? Chu was exceedingly difficult to restrain, yet Zhi Ying could wear it down through strategy; Qi was exceedingly difficult to subdue, yet Confucius could transform it through ritual propriety. Such indeed are the benefits that sages and worthies bring to a state! Yet although restraining Chu was certainly Zhi Ying’s achievement, scarcely had Chu been brought under control when envoys establishing relations with Wu arrived in succession. Was Zhi Ying not at his ruler’s side? Transforming Qi was certainly due to Confucius’s efforts. Yet although he could prevent the men of Lai from insulting us, he could not prevent the acceptance of the female musicians; although he could secure the return of the three territories, he could not bring about the demolition of Cheng’s fortifications. Was achieving good government really so difficult? What Confucius could put into practice was the Way, but whether the Way was put into practice depended upon his ruler. The failure to achieve good government ultimately arose simply from Duke Ding’s lack of single-minded commitment to employing the Way of the sage. As for Jin’s establishing relations with Wu, although this was Duke Dao’s error, Zhi Ying and the other ministers could not escape responsibility for it.

Record of Rites
The gentleman said: “Great virtue is not confined to a single office; the great Way is not confined to a single implement; great trustworthiness requires no covenant; perfect timeliness follows no uniform rule. By discerning these four things, one may set one’s purpose upon the root.”
Pan Weiyue

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “The Way of Heaven and the sage attain their fullness because they have a root. This composition apprehends this with lucid penetration, and its language is fully adequate to express it. Here is writing that itself has a root.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Within its plain solidity there is an untrammeled charm; within its quiet simplicity there is refined thought. This is writing like cloth, silk, beans, and grain—the essentials of daily life.”

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授吳批會註成文深得本旨
考試官敎授李批是知務本者
記者歷舉天人有本之用而示人以本之當務
焉蓋聖人天道之用皆以有本而充也君子察
於是焉本其容於不務哉昔記者以務本之學
望天下也意曰體立用行固天人合一之理而
明體適用尤君子進脩之功是故道得於心之
謂德而德之大者則日新以裕富有之業官不
足以拘之也理率於性之謂道而道之大者則
===
溥博以協時措之宜器不足以泥之也自其大
信而言之誠意懇惻而眞精孚於有素期約孰
得而囿乎自其大時而言之元氣周流而化醇
妙於不測分限孰得而齊乎是聖道之用雖順
事無情也而所以綱維之者必有以為聖之本
矣天道之用雖普物無心也而所以主宰之者
必有以為天之本矣君子者以聖人天道為已
責者也而可以弗察耶必遠宗諸聖冀以窮其
應感之由而上律於天期以玩其流行之故有
punctuated:
考試官敎授吳批：會註成文，深得本旨。
考試官敎授李批：是知務本者。
記者歷舉天人有本之用，而示人以本之當務焉。蓋聖人天道之用，皆以有本而充也。君子察於是焉，本其容於不務哉？昔記者以務本之學望天下也，意曰：體立用行，固天人合一之理；而明體適用，尤君子進脩之功。是故道得於心之謂德，而德之大者，則日新以裕富有之業，官不足以拘之也。理率於性之謂道，而道之大者，則溥博以協時措之宜，器不足以泥之也。自其大信而言之，誠意懇惻，而眞精孚於有素，期約孰得而囿乎？自其大時而言之，元氣周流，而化醇妙於不測，分限孰得而齊乎？是聖道之用，雖順事無情也，而所以綱維之者，必有以為聖之本矣；天道之用，雖普物無心也，而所以主宰之者，必有以為天之本矣。君子者，以聖人天道為已責者也，而可以弗察耶？必遠宗諸聖，冀以窮其應感之由，而上律於天，期以玩其流行之故。有
translation_en:
Examiner Wu, Prefectural School Instructor, comments: “The commentaries are brought together into a composition that profoundly grasps the fundamental meaning.”
Examiner Li, Prefectural School Instructor, comments: “Here is someone who understands attending to the root.”
The compiler of the Record of Rites enumerates the workings of Heaven and humanity that have a root, showing people that they should attend to that root. For the workings of the sage and of Heaven’s Way attain their fullness because they have a root. Once the gentleman perceives this, how could he fail to attend to the root? In former times, the compiler expected all under Heaven to pursue learning directed toward the root. His meaning was this: establishing the substance and putting its functioning into practice is indeed the principle by which Heaven and humanity are united; illuminating that substance and applying its functioning appropriately is especially the work through which the gentleman advances his self-cultivation.
Thus, the Way attained within the heart is called virtue. When virtue is great, it renews itself daily, enriching its abundant accomplishments; no official function can confine it. Principle followed in accordance with one’s nature is called the Way. When the Way is great, it is broad and encompassing, meeting the requirements of timely application; no vessel can constrain it. Speaking of great trustworthiness, its sincerity is earnest and heartfelt, and its genuine essence inspires confidence long established: how could stipulated agreements circumscribe it? Speaking of great timeliness, primal vital energy circulates everywhere, and the subtlety of its consummate transformations is unfathomable: how could fixed divisions and limits make it uniform?
Thus, although the functioning of the sage’s Way responds to affairs without private feeling, what orders and sustains it must constitute the root of sagehood. Although the functioning of Heaven’s Way extends to all things without conscious intent, what governs it must constitute the root of Heaven. The gentleman takes the sage and Heaven’s Way as his own responsibility; how could he fail to examine them? He must look far back to the sages as his models, hoping to fathom the source of their responses to what moves them, and take Heaven above as his standard, seeking to contemplate the reason for its ceaseless circulation. Having …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
見於聖道之淵源也而下學以達希聖之功藏
脩游息之有事將不務聖心之所蓄極者而同
其舍弘也哉有見於天道之於穆也而盡人以
體合天之撰正業居學之不倦將不契化機之
所充塞者而符其妙運也哉吁天人之用必有
本而周君子之功以探本而密學者其務之哉
抑志本者爲已之功而吾心獨覺之地尤大本
之所從出者是故君子防嚴於幽獨以慎察乎
莫見莫顯之機則聖人天道將於吾心而凝其
===
原矣否則情以欲動心以物交其所謂本者何
自而察哉此聖人之立人極必曰主靜而存天
之心者恒於復乎見之故善務本者其要只在
謹獨
故樂行而倫清耳目聰明血氣和平移風
易俗天下皆寧
陳相
同考試官教諭張批以樂行總承天人常變士子
類能言之而此作獨貫串有條流暢不滯盖經義之難得者
punctuated:
見於聖道之淵源也，而下學以達希聖之功，藏脩游息之有事，將不務聖心之所蓄極者，而同其舍弘也哉？有見於天道之於穆也，而盡人以體合天之撰，正業居學之不倦，將不契化機之所充塞者，而符其妙運也哉？吁！天人之用必有本而周，君子之功以探本而密，學者其務之哉！抑志本者，爲已之功，而吾心獨覺之地，尤大本之所從出者。是故君子防嚴於幽獨，以慎察乎莫見莫顯之機，則聖人天道將於吾心而凝其原矣。否則，情以欲動，心以物交，其所謂本者何自而察哉？此聖人之立人極必曰主靜，而存天之心者恒於復乎見之，故善務本者，其要只在謹獨。
故樂行而倫清，耳目聰明，血氣和平，移風易俗，天下皆寧。
陳相
同考試官教諭張批：以樂行總承天人常變，士子類能言之，而此作獨貫串有條，流暢不滯，盖經義之難得者。
translation_en:
…perceiving the profound source of the Way of the sages, one learns below in order to attain the achievement of aspiring to sagehood. Through study and cultivation, recreation and rest, would one not attend to what the sage’s mind has stored up to the utmost, and share its expansive capacity [?]? Perceiving the profound mystery of the Way of Heaven, one exhausts human capacities to embody and accord with Heaven’s workings. Tireless in pursuing the proper curriculum and dwelling in learning, would one not accord with that which the motive force of transformation pervades, and match its wondrous operation? Ah! The workings of Heaven and humanity must have a root if they are to be all-embracing; the gentleman’s efforts become thorough through seeking that root. Let students devote themselves to this!
Moreover, setting one’s purpose on the root is an effort undertaken for oneself, and the place where one’s mind alone is aware is precisely where the great root originates. Thus the gentleman guards himself strictly in solitude, carefully examining those incipient movements than which nothing is more visible or manifest. Then the source of the ways of the sages and Heaven will become firmly established within his own mind. Otherwise, when feelings are stirred by desires and the mind becomes entangled with things, how can one discern this supposed root? This is why, in establishing the ultimate standard for humanity, the sage necessarily speaks of making stillness the guiding principle; and why those who preserve Heaven’s mind invariably perceive it in Return. Thus, for those skilled in attending to the root, the essential point lies solely in vigilance when alone.
“Thus, when music is put into practice, human relationships become clear, the ears and eyes become keen, the blood and vital energies become harmonious and balanced, prevailing practices and customs are transformed, and all under Heaven is at peace.”
Chen Xiang
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Taking ‘music is put into practice’ as the overarching phrase encompassing Heaven and humanity, constancy and change, is something candidates can generally discuss. This composition, however, is exceptionally coherent and orderly, flowing freely without impediment. It is indeed a rare achievement among essays on the meaning of the Classics.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭劉批格調平正詞理疏鬯讀之有金
石音可謂深於樂者矣
考試官教授吳批敷揚樂化順暢可嘉
考試官教授李批得和平之旨
記者論樂教之行極其功用之大焉甚矣樂之
感人深也則夫功用之無所不周其亦樂化之
自致者歟見于樂記者其旨若曰大樂之在天
下不觀其始固無以探制作之原不究其終亦
無以徵功用之盛然則先王作樂以廣化果何
===
如耶今夫樂也者通於倫理統夫吾身而達之
天下者也惟患樂教之未行耳苟協乎天人而
緣情以達文者流行而莫禦備乎常變而盡制
以宣和者充周而不窮是以見諸倫也其羣分
也文以相接而彝倫昭攸敘之則其類聚也恩
以相維而人紀著肇脩之休倫其有弗清乎自
其化之及于人身也吾見聽德惟聰視遠惟明
謀哲竝行而耳目之官得其職矣剛氣不怒柔
氣不懾德性用事而血氣之運中其節矣雖人
punctuated:
同考試官教諭劉批：格調平正，詞理疏鬯，讀之有金石音，可謂深於樂者矣。
考試官教授吳批：敷揚樂化，順暢可嘉。
考試官教授李批：得和平之旨。
記者論樂教之行，極其功用之大焉。甚矣，樂之感人深也！則夫功用之無所不周，其亦樂化之自致者歟？見于樂記者，其旨若曰：大樂之在天下，不觀其始，固無以探制作之原；不究其終，亦無以徵功用之盛。然則先王作樂以廣化，果何如耶？今夫樂也者，通於倫理，統夫吾身而達之天下者也。惟患樂教之未行耳。苟協乎天人而緣情以達文者，流行而莫禦；備乎常變而盡制以宣和者，充周而不窮。是以見諸倫也，其羣分也，文以相接，而彝倫昭攸敘之則；其類聚也，恩以相維，而人紀著肇脩之休。倫其有弗清乎？自其化之及于人身也，吾見聽德惟聰，視遠惟明，謀哲竝行，而耳目之官得其職矣；剛氣不怒，柔氣不懾，德性用事，而血氣之運中其節矣。雖人
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “The style is balanced and upright, and the wording and reasoning lucid and fluent. Reading it, one hears the resonance of bells and chime stones. Its author may indeed be called one who understands music profoundly.”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “It expounds the transforming influence of music with a commendable ease and fluency.”
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “It captures the purport of harmony and balance.”
The author of the Record discusses the practice of musical instruction, fully setting forth the greatness of its effects. How profoundly music moves people! That its effects extend everywhere—is this not the natural outcome of its transforming influence? The meaning of the passage in the Record of Music is something like this: as for great music in the world, unless we examine its beginnings, we cannot explore the origins of its creation; unless we investigate its ultimate results, we cannot verify the fullness of its effects. How, then, did the former kings create music to extend their transforming influence?
Music permeates the principles of human relationships, encompassing our own persons and extending throughout the world. Our only concern is that musical instruction has yet to be put into practice. If that which harmonizes Heaven and humanity and follows the feelings to give them patterned expression flows unchecked, and that which accommodates both constancy and change and fully realizes its forms to spread harmony pervades everything without exhaustion, then its effects become visible in human relationships. Where people are divided into groups, they engage one another through cultivated forms, and the enduring relationships clearly display the rules by which they are ordered. Where people gather according to kind, affection binds them together, and the bonds of human society manifest the beauty of their cultivation. Could human relationships then fail to be clear?
As its transforming influence reaches the human person, I see acuity in hearing virtue and clarity in seeing far; deliberation and wisdom operate together, and the faculties of hearing and sight fulfill their offices. The strong vital energies do not erupt in anger, and the yielding vital energies do not succumb to fear. Moral nature governs, and the circulation of blood and vital energy attains its proper measure. Although the human …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
之形體自有本然之良而所以啓順正之機者
謂非樂有以助之哉自其化之被於天下也吾
見挽頹風以歸正易流俗以還淳而興仁興讓
既盡夫人而不變焉由是溥至治於無疆顯時
雍於有象而大順大化自舉斯世而咸寧焉雖
天下之風俗固有自然之應而所以廣孚化之
神者非樂其何以成之哉夫樂一也而以惇人
倫以脩吾身以維世道胥于此乎繫焉其功用
亦大矣乎是以先王隆之也雖然此特就其感
===
化言之耳而本不與焉蓋聖王於樂之未作反
情以和志比類以成行而無聲之樂在我夫然
後以和賛和而家齊國治天下平舉而措之裕
如耳是以協和風動必本諸欽明濬哲而永清
導化亦自徽柔懿恭者得之也故語曰樂云樂
云鐘鼓云乎哉欲作樂以宣化者可以知所本
矣
第貳場
論
punctuated:
之形體自有本然之良，而所以啓順正之機者，謂非樂有以助之哉？自其化之被於天下也，吾見挽頹風以歸正，易流俗以還淳，而興仁興讓，既盡夫人而不變焉。由是溥至治於無疆，顯時雍於有象，而大順大化，自舉斯世而咸寧焉。雖天下之風俗固有自然之應，而所以廣孚化之神者，非樂其何以成之哉？夫樂一也，而以惇人倫，以脩吾身，以維世道，胥于此乎繫焉。其功用亦大矣乎！是以先王隆之也。雖然，此特就其感化言之耳，而本不與焉。蓋聖王於樂之未作，反情以和志，比類以成行，而無聲之樂在我。夫然後以和賛和，而家齊、國治、天下平，舉而措之裕如耳。是以協和風動，必本諸欽明濬哲；而永清導化，亦自徽柔懿恭者得之也。故語曰：「樂云樂云，鐘鼓云乎哉？」欲作樂以宣化者，可以知所本矣。

第貳場

論
translation_en:
…the human body inherently possesses its original goodness, yet can one say that music does not help awaken its disposition toward accord and rectitude? As for its transforming influence spreading throughout the realm, I see it reverse declining customs and restore correctness, change prevailing habits and recover simplicity. It promotes benevolence and deference, encompassing all people without change [?]. Thus it spreads consummate order without limit and gives visible expression to universal harmony; through great concord and transformation, the whole world is brought to peace. Although the customs of the realm naturally respond, without music how could the wondrous power of transformation be extended everywhere? Music is one thing, yet strengthening human relationships, cultivating oneself, and sustaining the moral order of the world all depend upon it. How great its efficacy is! This is why the former kings exalted it.

Nevertheless, this speaks only of its power to influence and transform; its foundation has not yet been addressed. Before instituting music, the sage king returns to his true feelings to harmonize his intentions and aligns himself with what is of the same kind to perfect his conduct. Thus soundless music resides within him. Only then does he use harmony to assist harmony, readily bringing order to the family, good government to the state, and peace to the realm. Accordingly, bringing people into concord and moving them as the wind moves things must be rooted in reverence, illumination, profound insight, and wisdom. Likewise, lasting peace and guidance through moral transformation arise from gracious gentleness, admirable virtue, and reverence. Hence the saying: “Music, music—is it merely bells and drums?” Those who wish to institute music to spread moral transformation may thereby understand where its foundation lies.

Second Session

Discourse

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
君子深造之以道
陳公相
同考試官教諭伍批氣格渾涵理致精確非灼見
道體者不能為此語敬服敬服
同考試官教諭張批深造處正自得之學故下文
資深逢原皆在本體上求之是篇指出真源足破常談
考試官教授吳批理學精深出自心得
考試官教授李批氣勢昌大議論高古
斯道有本然之體也君子學以致道者亦惟求
===
以契其體焉耳夫斯道昭布於天下而人之求
道者孰不以為道最淺近可以徑造之也而不
知道原於天維天之命於穆不已此道之所自
來也故道雖充周而不可窮而其體實深遠而
不可測惟知其本深而于其深者造之則不離
乎深以造於道而亦不徑造以求其深斯之謂
善契其體而其所得者不淺矣彼舍其道而不
求者固不知所謂造而從事於道者乃或滯於
聞見狃於事為彷佛於矯飾卜度之私遂以為
punctuated:
君子深造之以道
陳公相

同考試官教諭伍批：氣格渾涵，理致精確，非灼見道體者不能為此語。敬服！敬服！
同考試官教諭張批：深造處正自得之學，故下文資深逢原，皆在本體上求之。是篇指出真源，足破常談。
考試官教授吳批：理學精深，出自心得。
考試官教授李批：氣勢昌大，議論高古。

斯道有本然之體也，君子學以致道者，亦惟求以契其體焉耳。夫斯道昭布於天下，而人之求道者，孰不以為道最淺近，可以徑造之也？而不知道原於天，「維天之命，於穆不已」，此道之所自來也。故道雖充周而不可窮，而其體實深遠而不可測。惟知其本深，而于其深者造之，則不離乎深以造於道，而亦不徑造以求其深。斯之謂善契其體，而其所得者不淺矣。彼舍其道而不求者，固不知所謂造；而從事於道者，乃或滯於聞見，狃於事為，彷佛於矯飾卜度之私，遂以為
translation_en:
“The gentleman advances deeply into it in accordance with the Way”
Chen Gongxiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “The writing’s spirit and style are ample and profound, its reasoning precise. Only someone with a penetrating vision of the substance of the Way could speak thus. Admirable! Admirable!”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Advancing deeply is precisely the learning through which one attains understanding for oneself. Thus the subsequent phrases about drawing deeply upon one’s resources and encountering the source wherever one turns must all be sought in the fundamental substance. This essay identifies the true source and is fully capable of overturning commonplace explanations.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: “Its understanding of the learning of principle is refined and profound, arising from personal insight.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “Its force is expansive and grand; its argument lofty and imbued with the spirit of antiquity.”

This Way has an inherent substance. When the gentleman studies to attain the Way, he seeks only to accord with that substance. Now, this Way is manifest throughout the world. Among those who seek it, who does not suppose that it is utterly simple and accessible, and that one can advance directly to it? Yet they do not understand that the Way originates in Heaven: “The mandate of Heaven—how profound and unceasing!” This is the source from which the Way comes. Thus, although the Way pervades everything and cannot be exhausted, its substance is truly profound and far-reaching, beyond all fathoming. Only by recognizing its fundamental depth and advancing into that depth can one approach the Way without departing from its profundity, rather than seek its profundity by a direct advance. This is what it means to accord well with its substance; what one gains thereby is not shallow.

Those who abandon the Way and do not seek it certainly do not understand what advancing means. Yet even those who devote themselves to the Way may become confined by what they have heard and seen, habituated to practical activity, and caught up in vague approximations born of the private impulses to affect appearances and conjecture [?]. They thereupon suppose that…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
道在是而不知道之體不若是之淺矣竟亦何
得於道哉孟子曰君子深造之以道請以是而
繹其意今夫道根於性情顯于事物昭著于人
倫日用之間而愚夫愚婦可以與知與能固若
是其淺且近也苟有以造之亦不出乎淺近而
可至者而何以深造爲哉故索隱行怪雖有述
而不爲而人之爲道而遠人不可以爲道宜不
必深求之也而不知道雖不離於淺近而其體
則至淺而深焉所謂愚夫愚婦可知可能而聖
===
人天地有所不能盡者此也故必知此者而後
可以造于道使不知道之所以爲道則雖造之
亦無當於道也巳不觀之掘井者乎彼語天下
之至深者水之體也故掘井者不欲得水則巳
矣苟欲得水必由漸而至九仞而及泉焉則水
之本體可得而井渫爲可汲矣苟非有九仞之
功則雖日汲汲而求水不免爲棄井耳蓋水之
體本深而淺求之不可也深者本由於淺而驟
求之亦不可也然則道猶水也道之體猶水之
punctuated: 道在是，而不知道之體不若是之淺矣，竟亦何得於道哉？孟子曰：「君子深造之以道。」請以是而繹其意。今夫道根於性情，顯于事物，昭著于人倫日用之間，而愚夫愚婦可以與知與能，固若是其淺且近也。苟有以造之，亦不出乎淺近而可至者，而何以深造爲哉？故索隱行怪，雖有述而不爲；而人之爲道而遠人，不可以爲道，宜不必深求之也。而不知道雖不離於淺近，而其體則至淺而深焉。所謂愚夫愚婦可知可能，而聖人天地有所不能盡者，此也。故必知此者，而後可以造于道。使不知道之所以爲道，則雖造之，亦無當於道也巳。不觀之掘井者乎？彼語天下之至深者，水之體也。故掘井者不欲得水則巳矣，苟欲得水，必由漸而至九仞而及泉焉，則水之本體可得，而井渫爲可汲矣。苟非有九仞之功，則雖日汲汲而求水，不免爲棄井耳。蓋水之體本深，而淺求之不可也；深者本由於淺，而驟求之亦不可也。然則道猶水也，道之體猶水之
translation_en:
…that the Way lies in these things, without knowing that its essential nature is not so shallow. What, in the end, can they gain of the Way? Mengzi said: “The gentleman advances deeply into it by following the Way.” Let us draw out his meaning through these words. The Way is rooted in human nature and feelings, manifests itself in affairs and things, and is plainly evident in human relationships and everyday life. Even ordinary men and women can share in knowing and practicing it. It certainly seems so simple and accessible. If there is a means of attaining it, this too should fall within what is simple, accessible, and attainable. Why, then, must one advance deeply? Thus, one does not probe into the obscure or perform strange deeds, even though these may win mention by later generations. Moreover, when someone pursues the Way in a manner remote from human beings, this cannot constitute the Way. It would seem, then, that there is no need to seek it deeply. Yet this fails to recognize that, although the Way never departs from what is simple and accessible, its essential nature is profound even in its utmost simplicity. This is what is meant by saying that ordinary men and women can know and practice it, yet even sages and Heaven and Earth cannot exhaust it. Only after understanding this can one advance toward the Way. If one does not understand what makes the Way the Way, then even one's efforts to attain it will fail to accord with it.

Have you not considered those who dig wells? What is spoken of here as among the deepest things under Heaven is the essential nature of water [?]. If a well-digger does not wish to obtain water, there is nothing more to be said. But if he does wish to obtain it, he must proceed gradually until he reaches a depth of nine ren and comes to a spring. Then water itself can be obtained, and the well, cleared out, is fit for drawing water. Without the labor of digging nine ren, however anxiously he seeks water day after day, he will merely end up abandoning the well. Water itself lies deep, and one cannot find it by seeking only near the surface. Yet depth must be reached by starting near the surface, and neither can it be attained all at once. Thus, the Way is like water, and the essential nature of the Way is like water’s…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
深也知掘井之義則知所以造道矣何也道原
於天上天之載無聲無臭而體備於人夫固至
近而遠至淺而深者也世之學者苟非暴棄之
甚而自諉於不爲者夫孰不欲造於道哉然而
求之于聞見者則以貫穿爲功而不知道不如
是之支也求之於事爲者則以鋪張爲務而不
知道不如是之粗也求之於矯飾卜度之間者
則以矜持見解爲有得而不知道不如是之虛
且擾也以是而造道則是善于買櫝而不善于
===
買珠其與足蹄涔而忘井養之不窮者埒也不
亦淺之乎其爲道哉故君子不欲造道則已矣
苟欲造于道其可不識其所謂深者而造之乎
是故道本無聲而涉於聲者非道也則洗心退
藏以求合其不覩之理道本無臭而涉於臭者
非道也則反觀默識以求契其不聞之眞由是
由知而好由好而樂其序不可亂也莫非所以
造其深也由善信而美大由美大而聖神其功
不可缺也莫非所以造其深也由志學而立由
punctuated:
深也。知掘井之義，則知所以造道矣。何也？道原於天，上天之載，無聲無臭，而體備於人，夫固至近而遠、至淺而深者也。世之學者，苟非暴棄之甚而自諉於不爲者，夫孰不欲造於道哉？然而求之于聞見者，則以貫穿爲功，而不知道不如是之支也；求之於事爲者，則以鋪張爲務，而不知道不如是之粗也；求之於矯飾卜度之間者，則以矜持見解爲有得，而不知道不如是之虛且擾也。以是而造道，則是善于買櫝而不善于買珠，其與足蹄涔而忘井養之不窮者埒也。不亦淺之乎，其爲道哉？
故君子不欲造道則已矣，苟欲造于道，其可不識其所謂深者而造之乎？是故道本無聲，而涉於聲者非道也，則洗心退藏，以求合其不覩之理；道本無臭，而涉於臭者非道也，則反觀默識，以求契其不聞之眞。由是，由知而好，由好而樂，其序不可亂也，莫非所以造其深也；由善信而美大，由美大而聖神，其功不可缺也，莫非所以造其深也；由志學而立，由
translation_en:
…depth. Once one understands the meaning of digging a well, one understands how to attain the Way. Why is this? The Way originates in Heaven. The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell, yet the Way is fully embodied in human beings. It is indeed utterly near yet distant, utterly shallow yet deep. Among the scholars of this world, unless they have gone so far in neglecting and abandoning themselves that they excuse themselves from making any effort, who does not wish to attain the Way? Yet those who seek it through what they hear and see take comprehensive learning as their achievement, unaware that the Way is not so fragmented. Those who seek it in practical affairs make elaborate display their business, unaware that the Way is not so coarse. Those who seek it amid affectation and conjecture regard studied restraint and intellectual understanding as genuine attainment, unaware that the Way is not so empty and agitated. To approach the Way in this fashion is to be good at buying the casket but not at buying the pearl. Such people are on a par with those who are content with water in a hoofprint and forget the inexhaustible sustenance of a well. Is their pursuit of the Way not shallow indeed?
Thus, if the gentleman does not wish to attain the Way, there is nothing more to say. But if he does wish to attain it, can he fail to recognize what is meant by its depth and advance into it? The Way is fundamentally without sound, and what involves sound is not the Way; therefore he cleanses his mind and withdraws into concealment, seeking accord with its unseen principle. The Way is fundamentally without smell, and what involves smell is not the Way; therefore he turns his gaze inward and apprehends in silence, seeking accord with its unsmelled reality. Accordingly, he progresses from knowing it to loving it, and from loving it to delighting in it. This sequence must not be disrupted: every stage is a means of attaining its depths. He progresses from goodness and sincerity to beauty and greatness, and from beauty and greatness to sagehood and spiritual profundity. No part of this effort may be omitted: every stage is a means of attaining its depths. He progresses from setting his heart on learning to taking his stand, and from…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
立而不惑由不惑而知命而耳順而從心其幾
不容息也莫非所以造其深也至是則即其深
以爲造而其造者以深由所造以求深而其深
者以得愈深而愈有所造愈造而愈見其深是
之謂深造而非以淺近求之也是之謂深造以
道而非以躐等得之也將見其功愈密其用愈
神資深逢原一以貫之而於穆不已之妙將與
天道而同體矣不猶浚井之深者功全於九仞
而得井洌寒泉之盛者乎故善掘井者求之深
===
而得水善求道者亦求之深而得道否則深者
不造而所造者非深則雖日從事於道而與道
邈不相干矣其何以爲道哉然深造之學孟子
非徒言之亦允蹈之者也彼其語養氣旣曰氣
難言而又以有事勿正心勿忘勿助長繼之夫
豈不欲徑造頓悟以成配塞之功哉蓋曰難言
者正以其體之深也有事勿忘者所以造其深
也勿正而勿助長者所謂造之以道而不以有
我累之也不然何義惟其集而不惟其襲哉知
punctuated:
立而不惑，由不惑而知命，而耳順，而從心，其幾不容息也，莫非所以造其深也。至是，則即其深以爲造，而其造者以深；由所造以求深，而其深者以得。愈深而愈有所造，愈造而愈見其深。是之謂深造，而非以淺近求之也；是之謂深造以道，而非以躐等得之也。將見其功愈密，其用愈神，資深逢原，一以貫之，而於穆不已之妙，將與天道而同體矣。不猶浚井之深者，功全於九仞，而得井洌寒泉之盛者乎？故善掘井者求之深而得水，善求道者亦求之深而得道。否則，深者不造，而所造者非深，則雖日從事於道，而與道邈不相干矣，其何以爲道哉？

然深造之學，孟子非徒言之，亦允蹈之者也。彼其語養氣，旣曰氣難言，而又以有事勿正、心勿忘、勿助長繼之，夫豈不欲徑造頓悟，以成配塞之功哉？蓋曰難言者，正以其體之深也；有事勿忘者，所以造其深也；勿正而勿助長者，所謂造之以道，而不以有我累之也。不然，何義惟其集，而不惟其襲哉？知
translation_en:
…from standing firm to freedom from perplexity, from freedom from perplexity to knowing Heaven’s mandate, then to an attuned ear, and then to following the heart’s desires: this progression permits no cessation. All of these are ways of reaching the Way’s depths. At this point, one takes those depths as the goal of advancement, and one’s attainments thereby deepen; one seeks depth through what one has attained, and thereby makes that depth one’s own. The deeper one goes, the greater one’s attainment; the greater one’s attainment, the more one perceives its depth. This is called advancing deeply, rather than seeking it through what is shallow and readily accessible. This is called advancing deeply by the proper way, rather than attaining it by skipping stages. One will then see one’s efforts become ever more meticulous and their efficacy ever more wondrous. Drawing on deeply accumulated resources, one encounters the source wherever one turns; a single thread runs through it all. In the mystery of its profound and unceasing operation, one will become one with the Way of Heaven. Is this not like someone who digs a well deeply, completing the work at nine ren and obtaining an abundance of clear, cold spring water? Thus, those skilled at digging wells seek deeply and obtain water; those skilled at seeking the Way likewise seek deeply and obtain the Way. Otherwise, if one fails to reach what is deep, and what one reaches is not deep, then even though one engages daily in the pursuit of the Way, one remains far removed from it and has no connection with it. How could this count as pursuing the Way?

Yet Mencius did not merely speak of the learning that advances deeply: he also truly practiced it. When speaking of nourishing qi, he first said that qi was difficult to describe, and then continued with the injunctions to keep working at it without anticipating results, not to forget it in one’s heart, and not to force its growth. Would he not have wished to advance directly and awaken at once, thereby accomplishing the cultivation of qi that matches righteousness and the Way and fills the space between Heaven and Earth? His saying that it was difficult to describe was precisely because of the depth of its substance. Keeping at the task and not forgetting it are the means of reaching its depths. Neither anticipating results nor forcing growth is what is meant by advancing by the proper way, without encumbering it with the self. Otherwise, why must righteousness be accumulated, rather than seized through an isolated act? To know…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
所謂集義則知所謂深造以道而孟子之所以
能自得者此矣其諸造道者之準乎雖然天道
雖無聲臭然易知而大生者未嘗息焉特其主
張是者於穆而已矣君子亦豈能外淺近易見
者以求深哉不過卽日用事物之中專於爲己
而去其務外爲人之私卽所以爲深造耳故觀
於自得之義則知深造卽龍蛇之蟄而非窅冥
之謂也如欲離去日用而別求所謂深其不流
而爲枯寂者幾希矣故深造者又不可離淺以
===
爲深
表
擬宋學士孫奭進無逸圖表天聖五年
張履祥
同考試官教諭劉批布格莊嚴含情剴切不挃而
麗不斲而工是能以忠愛自獻者宜錄以式
同考試官教授何批無逸之書帝王之龜鑑子能
本周公納誨之旨發明進圖之意而詞復駢麗可誦足占素
養矣
punctuated:
所謂集義，則知所謂深造以道，而孟子之所以能自得者此矣。其諸造道者之準乎！雖然，天道雖無聲臭，然易知而大生者未嘗息焉，特其主張是者於穆而已矣。君子亦豈能外淺近易見者以求深哉？不過卽日用事物之中，專於爲己，而去其務外爲人之私，卽所以爲深造耳。故觀於自得之義，則知深造卽龍蛇之蟄，而非窅冥之謂也。如欲離去日用而別求所謂深，其不流而爲枯寂者幾希矣。故深造者又不可離淺以爲深。
表
擬宋學士孫奭進無逸圖表，天聖五年。
張履祥
同考試官教諭劉批：布格莊嚴，含情剴切，不挃而麗，不斲而工，是能以忠愛自獻者，宜錄以式。
同考試官教授何批：《無逸》之書，帝王之龜鑑。子能本周公納誨之旨，發明進圖之意，而詞復駢麗可誦，足占素養矣。
translation_en:
…to know what is meant by “accumulating righteousness” is to know what is meant by “advancing deeply through the Way.” This is how Mencius was able to attain understanding for himself. Surely it is the standard for those who advance in the Way! Nevertheless, although the Way of Heaven has neither sound nor smell, its workings, readily known and bringing forth life abundantly, never cease. What presides over them is simply profound and silent. How, then, could the gentleman seek depth outside what is near at hand and readily apparent? Simply to devote oneself to one's own cultivation amid everyday affairs and things, removing the selfish desire to pursue external things and act for others' approval—this is how one advances deeply. Thus, by considering the meaning of attaining understanding for oneself, we know that advancing deeply is like the hibernation of dragons and snakes; it does not mean obscure abstraction. If one wishes to abandon everyday life and seek something called “depth” elsewhere, there is scarcely any chance of avoiding a descent into barren stillness. Therefore, those who advance deeply must not abandon the shallow in order to achieve depth.
Memorial
A memorial presenting the Illustrations of “Against Idleness,” composed in the person of Sun Shi, Academician of the Song dynasty, in the fifth year of Tiansheng [1027].
By Zhang Lüxiang.
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: The composition is dignified in structure and earnest in sentiment, beautiful without forced embellishment [?] and accomplished without chiseling. Here is someone able to offer himself through loyalty and loving concern for his ruler. It should be recorded as a model.
Comment by Associate Examiner He, Professor: “Against Idleness” is a guide and mirror for emperors and kings. You have grounded your work in the Duke of Zhou's purpose in offering admonition and elucidated the intention behind presenting the illustrations. Moreover, the language is beautifully parallel and worthy of recitation. This amply reveals your longstanding cultivation.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授吳批意深調雅菁華絶類
考試官敎授李批詞意懇到得獻納體
天聖五年某月某日龍圖閣學士臣孫奭
謹以所繪無逸圖
上進者伏以
運際豐亨
聖主勵勤民之治道存乾惕詞臣效匡
辟之猷論思取象於前言觀省期資於
上智仰呈
===
睿鑒俯竭愚衷臣奭誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊惟
君民一體君心之無怠由念切於憂民今
古一揆今事之罔愆由學先於稽古況持
盈保泰在初服之勵精而憂治危明係老
成之却慮故篤忠貞如元聖僝勤規戒於
成王念王業本自艱難顧聖學宜先寅畏
爰陳無逸用代有終俯恤民依備敘田功
之疾苦仰欽天命歷陳國祚之短長義取
守文迪哲鑒四人之戒志存繩武克艱述
punctuated:
考試官敎授吳批：意深調雅，菁華絶類。
考試官敎授李批：詞意懇到，得獻納體。
天聖五年某月某日，龍圖閣學士臣孫奭，謹以所繪《無逸圖》上進者。伏以運際豐亨，聖主勵勤民之治；道存乾惕，詞臣效匡辟之猷。論思取象於前言，觀省期資於上智。仰呈睿鑒，俯竭愚衷。臣奭誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊惟君民一體，君心之無怠，由念切於憂民；今古一揆，今事之罔愆，由學先於稽古。況持盈保泰，在初服之勵精；而憂治危明，係老成之却慮。故篤忠貞如元聖，僝勤規戒於成王。念王業本自艱難，顧聖學宜先寅畏。爰陳《無逸》，用代有終。俯恤民依，備敘田功之疾苦；仰欽天命，歷陳國祚之短長。義取守文迪哲，鑒四人之戒；志存繩武克艱，述
translation_en:
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “The conception is profound and the tone refined; its brilliance is beyond compare.”
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “The language and intent are earnest and fully realized, befitting the presentation of counsel to the throne.”
On a certain day of a certain month in the fifth year of Tiansheng, your servant Sun Shi, Academician of the Longtu Pavilion, respectfully presents the illustrated Admonitions against Idleness that he has had painted.
I humbly consider that, in an age of abundance and prosperity, our sagely sovereign diligently pursues government devoted to the people. Since the Way requires unceasing vigilance, your literary servant offers counsel to guide his ruler aright. In deliberation and reflection, I take earlier teachings as my model; through viewing and self-examination, I hope to assist Your Majesty’s supreme wisdom. Looking upward, I submit this to your discerning scrutiny; bowing low, I exhaust my humble sincerity. Your servant Shi, in utmost fear and trembling, bows his head to the ground and repeatedly kowtows.
I venture to reflect that ruler and people form one body: the ruler’s heart remains unremitting because his concern for the people is deeply felt. Present and past follow one standard: present affairs are free from error because learning begins with examining antiquity. Moreover, sustaining plenitude and preserving peace depend upon vigorous effort at the beginning of a reign; concern amid good government and apprehension amid clarity [?] depend upon the foresight of seasoned elders. Thus the primal sage, so steadfast in loyalty and integrity, devoted his efforts to admonishing King Cheng. He reflected that the royal enterprise had its origins in hardship, and considered that reverent caution should come first in a sage ruler’s learning. He therefore set forth Admonitions against Idleness, thereby securing a good conclusion [?]. Looking downward with compassion upon the people’s means of subsistence, he fully described the hardships of agricultural labor. Looking upward in reverence for Heaven’s Mandate, he successively recounted the long and short durations of dynastic rule. His meaning was to preserve inherited institutions and advance in wisdom, taking warning from the examples of four rulers; his purpose was to follow his predecessors’ footsteps and master difficulties, recounting …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
三后之傳理正詞嚴語不嫌於忌諱憂深
思遠道有裨於勸懲馴至三代以來惟成
周之治爲盛故今千載而下稱周公之功
不衰慨自謇諤風微遂致憂勤日懈因得
賢而獻頌奚裨時幾緣王會以進圖祗恣
逸豫千秋一鑑莫開内照之明□□六箴
無救外遊之侈惟逆耳之言不用故格心
之效罕聞非際
昌期曷伸忠悃玆蓋伏遇
===
〇〇〇〇
仁孝因心
誠明盡性禮隆
慈幄常朝每謹於問安學懋
經筵盛暑不倦於
御講重民而却異物念切如傷策士而取直言
懷虛若渴
克勤克儉惜夏禹之分陰
亦保亦臨勞周文之旲日憂常先於天下惠
punctuated: 三后之傳。理正詞嚴，語不嫌於忌諱；憂深思遠，道有裨於勸懲。馴至三代以來，惟成周之治爲盛，故今千載而下，稱周公之功不衰。慨自謇諤風微，遂致憂勤日懈。因得賢而獻頌，奚裨時幾？緣王會以進圖，祗恣逸豫。千秋一鑑，莫開内照之明；□□六箴，無救外遊之侈。惟逆耳之言不用，故格心之效罕聞。非際昌期，曷伸忠悃？玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，仁孝因心，誠明盡性。禮隆慈幄，常朝每謹於問安；學懋經筵，盛暑不倦於御講。重民而却異物，念切如傷；策士而取直言，懷虛若渴。克勤克儉，惜夏禹之分陰；亦保亦臨，勞周文之旲日。憂常先於天下，惠
translation_en:
…the tradition handed down by the three sovereigns. His principles were correct and his language stern; his words did not shrink from taboo subjects. His concern was profound and his thought far-reaching; his teaching aided encouragement and admonition. Thus, among the governments of the Three Dynasties, that of Zhou reached the greatest flourishing. Hence, even a thousand years later, praise for the achievements of the Duke of Zhou has not diminished.
Alas, once the practice of forthright remonstrance weakened, anxious diligence daily slackened. What help in addressing the critical circumstances of the time was an ode presented to celebrate the acquisition of worthy men? A picture presented on the occasion of a royal assembly merely indulged ease and pleasure. A Mirror for a Thousand Autumns could not awaken the clarity of inward reflection; the six admonitions, □□ [?], could not curb extravagant excursions. Because words displeasing to the ear went unheeded, the achievement of correcting the ruler’s heart was seldom heard of. Without encountering a flourishing age, how could one express one’s loyal sincerity?
Now, prostrate, we have the good fortune to encounter 〇〇〇〇 [four circles in the transcription]. Your benevolence and filial devotion spring from the heart; through sincerity and understanding, you fully realize your nature. You exalt the rites toward the maternal apartments, carefully inquiring after Her Majesty’s well-being at every regular court attendance. You diligently pursue learning at the Classics Colloquium, attending imperial lectures without weariness even in the height of summer. You cherish the people and reject exotic objects, caring for them as tenderly as if they were injured. You examine scholars through policy questions and accept forthright speech, receiving counsel with an open mind as eagerly as one thirsting for water. Diligent and frugal, you prize every fraction of time, as did Yu of Xia. Both protecting and overseeing, you toil through the long day [?], as did King Wen of Zhou. Your concern always precedes that of all under Heaven; your beneficence…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
允浹於民間但
聖敬緝熈雖已嚴於穆穆而臣愚勤懇猶欲效
其區區伏念臣奭學非博古志切匡時微
言謬採於賢科薄技僭登於胄監早遇
先皇之眷愧叨良弼之稱說命三篇偶講讀之
悟
主抗疏十事恐封祀之勞民幸荷
優涵俾塵
法從仰
===
萬幾之重徒抱杞憂懷一得之愚每思芹獻
雖泰華不增高於土壤而涓流竊委潤於
滄溟謂治慎無虞怠勝無如敬勝之吉而
道形有象聞知不若見知之眞逸戒爰取
諸周書圖畫因屬之繪事矢心模寫極意
編摩察閭里之怨咨務曲盡其情狀考廟
堂之鑒戒巳備極其形容上下七君理亂
安危之畢備後先二代吉凶修短之俱陳
于遊于田展卷足為永戒攸訓攸若披圖
punctuated: 允浹於民間。但聖敬緝熈，雖已嚴於穆穆，而臣愚勤懇，猶欲效其區區。伏念臣奭，學非博古，志切匡時。微言謬採於賢科，薄技僭登於胄監。早遇先皇之眷，愧叨良弼之稱。《說命》三篇，偶講讀之悟主；抗疏十事，恐封祀之勞民。幸荷優涵，俾塵法從。仰萬幾之重，徒抱杞憂；懷一得之愚，每思芹獻。雖泰華不增高於土壤，而涓流竊委潤於滄溟。謂治慎無虞，怠勝無如敬勝之吉；而道形有象，聞知不若見知之眞。逸戒爰取諸《周書》，圖畫因屬之繪事。矢心模寫，極意編摩。察閭里之怨咨，務曲盡其情狀；考廟堂之鑒戒，巳備極其形容。上下七君，理亂安危之畢備；後先二代，吉凶修短之俱陳。于遊于田，展卷足為永戒；攸訓攸若，披圖
translation_en:
…truly reaches throughout the populace. Yet, although Your Majesty’s reverence continually shines forth, already manifest in solemn dignity, your foolish servant, in his earnest devotion, still wishes to offer his humble service. I respectfully reflect that I, your servant Shi, lack broad learning in antiquity, but am deeply committed to setting the affairs of the age aright. My slight words were undeservedly accepted in the examination for worthy men, and my meager abilities presumptuously gained me a place in the Directorate of Education. Early on, I received the late emperor’s favor, and, to my shame, undeservedly acquired the designation of a worthy counselor. In lecturing upon and reading the three chapters of “The Charge to Yue,” I happened to bring understanding to my sovereign; I boldly submitted a memorial on ten matters, fearing that the sacrifices to Heaven and Earth would burden the people. Fortunately, I received generous forbearance and was permitted to occupy a place among the imperial attendants.

Looking up to the weight of Your Majesty’s myriad affairs, I can only harbor the groundless anxieties of the man of Qi; cherishing the single insight that even a fool may possess, I constantly think of offering my humble gift of cress. Though a little earth adds nothing to the height of Mount Tai or Mount Hua, a tiny stream may still contribute its moisture to the vast sea. I hold that government requires vigilance when there seems no cause for concern: allowing negligence to prevail cannot compare with the good fortune of letting reverence prevail. And when the Way takes visible form, knowledge gained by hearing is less true than knowledge gained by seeing.

I therefore took warnings against ease from the Documents of Zhou and entrusted their illustration to painters. I devoted myself to reproducing these accounts and applied my utmost care to compiling them. In examining the grievances and lamentations of the villages, I sought to convey their circumstances and feelings in full detail; in investigating the lessons and warnings for the court, I have already depicted them as fully as possible. Across seven rulers, every circumstance of order and disorder, security and danger is represented; through two successive dynasties, good and ill fortune, and long and short reigns, are all set forth. When going on excursions or hunts, unrolling the scroll will provide an enduring warning; as for what to take as instruction and what to follow, opening the illustrations…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
已有明徵無煩告語之再三足備
鑒觀於萬一思如馭朽在觸目以驚心慮若臨
深貴由象而得意倘蒙置諸
座右可希戸牖之銘若常接於
御前庶比韋弦之義學非口耳道切身心未敢
謂臣之言可比周公之言惟日冀
君之治遠邁成王之治伏願
德隆廣運
業懋永圖
===
祗若乎無聲無臭之天
敬愼於不覩不聞之地
春祈秋報思周公之訓夢寐不忘
日就月將達成王之聰羹牆如見臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以所繪無逸圖奉
表隨
進以
聞
punctuated: 已有明徵，無煩告語之再三，足備鑒觀於萬一。思如馭朽，在觸目以驚心；慮若臨深，貴由象而得意。倘蒙置諸座右，可希戸牖之銘；若常接於御前，庶比韋弦之義。學非口耳，道切身心。未敢謂臣之言可比周公之言，惟日冀君之治遠邁成王之治。伏願德隆廣運，業懋永圖，祗若乎無聲無臭之天，敬愼於不覩不聞之地。春祈秋報，思周公之訓，夢寐不忘；日就月將，達成王之聰，羹牆如見。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹以所繪《無逸圖》奉表隨進以聞。
translation_en:
…there is already clear evidence, requiring no repeated verbal admonitions and supplying at least a small measure of material for Your Majesty’s scrutiny. To remain mindful as though driving with rotten reins, one must let what meets the eye startle the heart; to exercise caution as though standing above an abyss, one must grasp the meaning through the images. If this work should be placed beside Your Majesty’s seat, it might serve like the admonitory inscriptions on doors and windows; if it should constantly come before Your Majesty, it might fulfill the purpose of the leather thong and bowstring, reminders to temper one’s disposition. Learning is no mere matter of mouth and ears; the Way bears directly upon body and mind. I dare not claim that your servant’s words compare with those of the Duke of Zhou. I hope each day only that Your Majesty’s government may far surpass that of King Cheng.

I humbly wish that Your Majesty’s virtue may be exalted, far-reaching, and all-embracing, and that your accomplishments may flourish according to enduring plans; that you may reverently follow Heaven, which has neither sound nor scent, and remain watchful and cautious even where nothing is seen or heard. At the spring prayers and autumn thanksgivings, may you ponder the Duke of Zhou’s instructions, never forgetting them even in dreams. Advancing daily and progressing monthly, may you attain King Cheng’s discerning understanding, as though seeing the sage before you in your soup and upon the wall.

Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, cannot contain his intense emotion and reverent trepidation. I respectfully submit the illustrated Admonitions against Idleness (Wuyi tu) that I have prepared, together with this accompanying memorial, for Your Majesty’s attention.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
第叁場
策
第一問
李繼華
同考試官教諭吳批揄揚
聖學歸本於敬是涵濡
至教而有得者且美不忘規忠愛勃勃錄而薦之可以奉大對矣
同考試官教諭張批
聖學淵源子能揄揚其盛而末寓規諷語復諄切是大有裨於論思者取
===
之非但以文也
考試官教授吳批縫掖之士有能鋪張
盛美陳見悃忱如子者耶敬服敬服
考試官教授李批得論思之旨取之
聖人所以繼天立極而君師乎天下者本
之以持敬之心而務學以明之虛受以廣
之夫是以德進於無疆而業垂於有永也
何也天之生人衆矣而顧以神聖授之一
人是天之獨厚之也天之所以獨厚之者
punctuated:
第叁場
策
第一問
李繼華

同考試官教諭吳批：揄揚聖學，歸本於敬，是涵濡至教而有得者。且美不忘規，忠愛勃勃，錄而薦之，可以奉大對矣。

同考試官教諭張批：聖學淵源，子能揄揚其盛，而末寓規諷，語復諄切，是大有裨於論思者。取之非但以文也。

考試官教授吳批：縫掖之士，有能鋪張盛美、陳見悃忱如子者耶？敬服！敬服！

考試官教授李批：得論思之旨，取之。

聖人所以繼天立極而君師乎天下者，本之以持敬之心，而務學以明之，虛受以廣之。夫是以德進於無疆，而業垂於有永也。何也？天之生人衆矣，而顧以神聖授之一人，是天之獨厚之也。天之所以獨厚之者，
translation_en:
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Li Jihua

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: In extolling the imperial learning, you trace its foundation to reverent attentiveness. This shows that you have been steeped in the highest teaching and gained insight from it. Moreover, in praising, you do not forget to admonish; loyalty and affection brim over. Selected and recommended, you may fittingly offer a grand response before the throne.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: You are able to extol the flourishing of imperial learning and its deep sources, while embedding admonition at the close. Your words are also earnest and pointed. This is of great benefit to deliberation and reflection in service of the throne. I select it for more than its literary merit.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: Among scholars in their broad-sleeved robes, is there anyone who can set forth the splendor of imperial virtue and express heartfelt sincerity as you do? I admire you! I admire you!

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: It grasps the purpose of deliberation and reflection in service of the throne. Select it.

The sage succeeds Heaven, establishes the supreme standard, and acts as ruler and teacher of all under Heaven by taking a heart of reverent attentiveness as his foundation, diligently pursuing learning to illuminate it, and receiving others’ counsel with an open mind to broaden it. Thus his virtue advances without limit, and his achievements endure forever. Why is this? Heaven brings forth a multitude of people, yet bestows divine sagacity upon just one person: this is Heaven’s particular favor toward him. The reason Heaven particularly favors him …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
豈慮一人之身非神聖不足以成之哉正
以天下之衆而非有神聖者以作之君師
則固無以治而教之耳是天之所以厚聖
人者乃所以厚天下也天以其厚天下者
而萃於聖人之一身聖人以其萃於一身
者而推之天下是天地聖人之心互相體
會若有意以營乎其間而必欲斯世斯民
之得所也然則聖人之心上以受命於天
而下以立命於民是其心宜有以自豫矣
===
而何必於憂惕之不遑其心宜有以自足
自用矣而何必於問學之不倦聽納之不
疑也殊不知聖人不以天之厚我者自恃
而常以天之所以厚我者自懼一日萬幾
懼吾未有以勝之也而豈容以不敬義理
無窮懼吾未有以明之也而豈容以不學
忠言逆耳懼吾未有以受之也而豈容以
不虛以是而考之古之帝王若堯舜禹湯
文武神聖天授莫之與京矣而其心則曷
punctuated: 豈慮一人之身非神聖不足以成之哉？正以天下之衆，而非有神聖者以作之君師，則固無以治而教之耳。是天之所以厚聖人者，乃所以厚天下也。天以其厚天下者而萃於聖人之一身，聖人以其萃於一身者而推之天下，是天地聖人之心互相體會，若有意以營乎其間，而必欲斯世斯民之得所也。然則聖人之心，上以受命於天，而下以立命於民，是其心宜有以自豫矣，而何必於憂惕之不遑？其心宜有以自足自用矣，而何必於問學之不倦、聽納之不疑也？殊不知聖人不以天之厚我者自恃，而常以天之所以厚我者自懼。一日萬幾，懼吾未有以勝之也，而豈容以不敬？義理無窮，懼吾未有以明之也，而豈容以不學？忠言逆耳，懼吾未有以受之也，而豈容以不虛？以是而考之古之帝王，若堯舜禹湯文武，神聖天授，莫之與京矣，而其心則曷
translation_en:
…Could Heaven have been concerned that this one individual could not attain fulfillment without divine sagacity? It was precisely because the multitudes under Heaven, without someone of divine sagacity to serve as their ruler and teacher, would have no one to govern and instruct them. Thus Heaven’s generosity toward the sage is its means of being generous toward all under Heaven. Heaven concentrates in the person of the sage that with which it would benefit the world; the sage extends to the world what has been concentrated in his own person. In this way, the intentions of Heaven and Earth and those of the sage accord with and embody one another, as though deliberately working together to ensure that this age and its people find their proper place.

Since the sage’s heart thus receives Heaven’s mandate above and secures the people’s livelihood and destiny below, surely he might allow himself contentment. Why, then, must he remain so anxiously vigilant that he has no leisure? Surely he might feel sufficient unto himself and rely on his own judgment. Why, then, must he be tireless in inquiry and learning, and unhesitating in hearing and accepting counsel? This overlooks the fact that the sage does not take Heaven’s generosity toward him as grounds for self-confidence, but constantly regards the purpose of that generosity as grounds for apprehension. With ten thousand affairs arising each day, he fears that he may be unequal to them: how could he permit himself to lack reverent attentiveness? With moral principles inexhaustible, he fears that he may not yet understand them: how could he permit himself not to study? With loyal counsel grating on the ear, he fears that he may not be able to accept it: how could he permit himself not to remain open-minded?

If we examine the ancient emperors and kings in this light—Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu—their divine sagacity was bestowed by Heaven, and none could equal them. Yet in their hearts, how could they…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
甞以之自恃哉故人知其治化之成於天
下者有雍和熈皥之盛而不知其本原之
地隱微之中固有曰嚴曰愼而非人之所
能窺者是故曰兢兢曰業業曰祗台曰昭
格曰緝熈執競此其持敬之心所以畏天
者不敢怠也曰允執厥中曰惟精惟一曰
不自滿假曰日新又新曰望道未見敬義
交修此其務實之學所以憲天者不容已
也夫既有神聖之資而存之以無敢暇豫
===
之心濟之以惟日不足之學則德業之盛
固已各臻其極而當時輔理成化之臣宜
無有能增益之者然皐陶之謨益稷之戒
伊尹之訓周召之誥每惓惓焉蓋不因其
君之已聖而遂忘其獻納之忠而爲之君
者亦不自以爲聖而遂忽於聽受之益此
其君臣交相儆戒而均之以畏天爲心上
下互相資益而均之以憲天爲學唐虞三
代之治所以臻於隆盛之極而數聖人者
