To entice them to come and then forbid the course they pursue; to complete their instruction and then reject the use of what they have learned—this is to expect something other than what one has planted. It surely cannot work.

I humbly believe that those who nurture scholars must give weight to the selection of scholarly teachers and reinforce instruction grounded in substance. When examining students on the meaning of the Classics, they should assess how students put it into practice themselves, rather than merely prize literary brilliance. When examining them on contemporary affairs, they must seek practical application, rather than merely encourage lofty talk. Virtue, conduct, the Way, and practical arts should be visibly cultivated in balanced measure, as in what Hu Yuan called the study of the meaning of the Classics and the management of affairs. Educational officials should then record their achievements, and censorial officials assess their attainments. Although selection through the examinations rests exclusively on their writing, their cultivation of conduct and practical arts will already be complete. The tasks entrusted to them in the future will be precisely what they are taught today. How, then, could there still be talented men unfit for service, or grounds for fearing that worthy men have been overlooked? Thus, in examination recruitment, nothing takes precedence over making moral instruction clear. The present assessments of officials are already thoroughly impartial, yet you, sir, still…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
倖位是惓惓之誠是也愚則以方今之法
毫舉櫛剔視周官之日成月要不啻密矣
挽江河而洒滌之一垢一瘢無不立見而
何倖位之有雖然有一說焉立法貴嚴持
法貴公而賢否之辨則不係是也必也核
名實乎今夫稱農者視其穀稱牧者視其
畜察之各以業也周官考課之法有待其
治者以定其始有逆其治者以稽其終待
於先即以責驗其終逆於後即以鉤考其
===
始是以其實無所遜而其虛不可飾眞才
可得而見也今也進賢如恐弗勝退不肖
如恐弗及非不日較著章明也然因人言
以爲進退采風聞以定是非勢亦有不免
矣人情有愛憎而言未必公風聞多影響
而事未必實此爲所察非所業也必不得
矣竊以爲課吏者必核其職業之守而擴
吾通闥之見其事治其民安非貪慢之吏
所能辦也毁之者勿聽其事不治其民不
punctuated:
倖位，是惓惓之誠是也。愚則以方今之法，毫舉櫛剔，視周官之日成月要，不啻密矣。挽江河而洒滌之，一垢一瘢，無不立見，而何倖位之有？雖然，有一說焉：立法貴嚴，持法貴公，而賢否之辨則不係是也。必也核名實乎！今夫稱農者視其穀，稱牧者視其畜，察之各以業也。周官考課之法，有待其治者以定其始，有逆其治者以稽其終。待於先，即以責驗其終；逆於後，即以鉤考其始。是以其實無所遜，而其虛不可飾，眞才可得而見也。
今也，進賢如恐弗勝，退不肖如恐弗及，非不日較著章明也。然因人言以爲進退，采風聞以定是非，勢亦有不免矣。人情有愛憎，而言未必公；風聞多影響，而事未必實。此爲所察非所業也，必不得矣。竊以爲課吏者，必核其職業之守，而擴吾通闥之見。其事治，其民安，非貪慢之吏所能辦也，毁之者勿聽；其事不治，其民不
translation_en:
…holding office undeservedly: this expresses earnest concern [?]. In my humble view, the laws now in force scrutinize every minute detail and sift out every fault; they are at least as exacting as the daily accounts and monthly summaries prescribed in the Offices of Zhou. It is as though the waters of rivers were drawn upon to wash everything clean: every speck of dirt and every blemish immediately becomes visible. How, then, could anyone hold office undeservedly? Nevertheless, there is something further to say. Laws should be framed strictly and administered impartially, but distinguishing the worthy from the unworthy does not depend upon these things alone. Surely one must examine whether names accord with realities! If someone is called a farmer, inspect his grain; if a herdsman, inspect his livestock. Each is assessed according to his occupation. The methods of evaluating performance in the Offices of Zhou include anticipating an official’s administration to establish its initial requirements, and reviewing his administration to assess its final results. Expectations set beforehand serve to demand verification at the end; retrospective examination serves to trace matters back to their beginning. Thus actual performance cannot evade scrutiny, nor can emptiness be disguised, and genuine ability becomes apparent.
Today, the worthy are advanced as though there were fear that not enough could be promoted, and the unworthy dismissed as though there were fear of falling behind. It is not that distinctions are not made increasingly clear each day. Yet circumstances sometimes make it unavoidable to promote or dismiss men on the basis of others’ words, and to determine right and wrong from hearsay. Human feelings encompass affection and aversion, so statements are not necessarily impartial; hearsay is often mere shadow and echo, so reported matters are not necessarily true. This means that what is examined is not the work itself; sound assessment must therefore fail [?]. In my humble opinion, those who evaluate officials must examine how they discharge their official duties and broaden their own understanding [?]. When an official’s affairs are well managed and his people secure, these are achievements beyond the capacity of a greedy or negligent official: do not listen to those who malign him. When his affairs are not well managed and his people are not…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
安非廉明之吏所宜有也譽之者亦勿聽
事蹟功罪斷斷不渝如齊威所爲烹阿封
卽墨者斯則名不以疏逖而不章實不以
彌縫而可匿雖課典之行裁之自我而情
狀在彼則旣悉矣飾名不得以求功巧文
不得以逃罪尚何吏治之不可飭而倖位
是憂乎是故考課莫貴乎核名實也噫敎
化行則舉不失人而吾之明益著名實核
則法無倖免而吾之公益彰明以擇之於
===
先不才者不得以倖進公以核之於後倖
進者不得以苟容賢者進則庶職脩矣不
肖者不容則治道粹矣明主恭己而無爲
大臣布公而弘化率是道也故夫師古之
意而不泥其法由今之法而獲古之治惟
公與明者得之若夫下之自處則如之何
學患不能成毋患有司之不明業患不能
精毋患有司之不公愚生切以爲自誦焉
方今
punctuated:
安，非廉明之吏所宜有也，譽之者亦勿聽。事蹟功罪，斷斷不渝，如齊威所爲烹阿、封卽墨者。斯則名不以疏逖而不章，實不以彌縫而可匿。雖課典之行裁之自我，而情狀在彼則旣悉矣。飾名不得以求功，巧文不得以逃罪，尚何吏治之不可飭而倖位是憂乎？是故考課莫貴乎核名實也。
噫！敎化行，則舉不失人，而吾之明益著；名實核，則法無倖免，而吾之公益彰。明以擇之於先，不才者不得以倖進；公以核之於後，倖進者不得以苟容。賢者進，則庶職脩矣；不肖者不容，則治道粹矣。明主恭己而無爲，大臣布公而弘化，率是道也。故夫師古之意而不泥其法，由今之法而獲古之治，惟公與明者得之。若夫下之自處，則如之何？學患不能成，毋患有司之不明；業患不能精，毋患有司之不公。愚生切以爲自誦焉。
方今
translation_en:
…are not at peace: this is not a condition that an upright and discerning official should allow, and those who praise him should likewise go unheard. Judge actual deeds, merits, and offenses with unwavering resolution, as King Wei of Qi did when he boiled the official of A and enfeoffed the official of Jimo. Then a man's reputation will not remain obscure because he is distant, nor can the truth be concealed by patching over faults. Although I myself decide how the rules of performance evaluation are applied, the circumstances of those evaluated will already be fully known. Embellishing one's reputation will not secure credit, and artful paperwork will not permit escape from punishment. What further concern need there be that official administration cannot be put in order, or that men hold office through undeserved good fortune? Thus, in evaluating officials, nothing is more valuable than checking reputation against reality.
Ah! When moral instruction takes effect, recommendations do not fail to identify the right men, and my discernment becomes still more evident. When reputation is checked against reality, none escape the law through good fortune, and my impartiality becomes still more manifest. With discernment I select them beforehand, so that the untalented cannot advance through good fortune; with impartiality I examine them afterward, so that those who have advanced through good fortune cannot merely be suffered to remain. When worthy men advance, the duties of all offices are fulfilled; when the unworthy are not tolerated, the way of governance becomes pure. The enlightened ruler maintains a reverent bearing and governs without action; his great ministers extend impartiality and spread moral transformation. All follow this way. Thus, to emulate the intent of antiquity without becoming bound to its methods, and to employ present methods while attaining the good government of antiquity—only the impartial and discerning can achieve this. As for how those below should conduct themselves, what should they do? Worry that your learning may not reach completion; do not worry that the responsible officials lack discernment. Worry that your studies may not attain mastery; do not worry that the responsible officials lack impartiality. I, an unworthy student, earnestly take these words as an admonition to recite to myself.
At this present time…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖皇御極名世應會
上懷側席之誠下切拔茅之願耆舊之臣協和
於
朝草莽之士踴躍於野此亦虞廷師師周室
濟濟千載之一時也所以感召而鼓舞之
者徒法云乎徒善云乎愚何幸躬逢其
盛
第四問
黃萼
===
同考試官教諭吳批考究既詳品藻尤當至論尚
友又得趨向之正一鄉善士非所以限子矣取之
同考試官教諭劉批以鄉之先哲為問正欲探諸士
願學之志此作獨知所折衷足占素養矣
考試官教授吳批能道其景行之心取之
考試官教授李批敘述詳明評品精確
儒者之學合體用而未始有二致也通顯
晦而未始有二心也夫學術者所以養此
心於未用也然而純駁異其材事功者所
punctuated:
聖皇御極，名世應會。上懷側席之誠，下切拔茅之願。耆舊之臣協和於朝，草莽之士踴躍於野。此亦虞廷師師、周室濟濟，千載之一時也。所以感召而鼓舞之者，徒法云乎？徒善云乎？愚何幸躬逢其盛！

第四問
黃萼

同考試官教諭吳批：「考究既詳，品藻尤當。至論尚友，又得趨向之正。一鄉善士，非所以限子矣。取之。」
同考試官教諭劉批：「以鄉之先哲為問，正欲探諸士願學之志。此作獨知所折衷，足占素養矣。」
考試官教授吳批：「能道其景行之心，取之。」
考試官教授李批：「敘述詳明，評品精確。」

儒者之學，合體用而未始有二致也；通顯晦而未始有二心也。夫學術者，所以養此心於未用也，然而純駁異其材；事功者，所
translation_en:
…the sage emperor occupies the throne, and men of distinction have arisen to meet the occasion. Above, he sincerely longs for worthy men, leaving a place beside him; below, they keenly desire advancement together, like interlinked roots of thatch pulled up together. Veteran ministers work harmoniously at court, while scholars outside official service eagerly respond in the countryside. This, too, is like the mutual deference of the court of Shun and the throng of worthy men in the Zhou royal house—a moment encountered once in a thousand years. Can what inspires and rouses them be called mere institutions? Mere goodness? How fortunate I am to witness such flourishing in person!

Fourth Question
Huang E

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “Your investigation is detailed, and your appraisals particularly apt. When discussing taking the ancients as friends, you also show the right direction of aspiration. Being a good scholar of one district is no limit for you. Accept this answer.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “In asking about the earlier worthies of this province, we intended precisely to probe the candidates’ aspirations to learn from them. This answer alone knows how to arrive at a balanced judgment, sufficiently revealing the cultivation accumulated through long study.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: “He successfully expresses his desire to emulate lofty conduct. Accept this answer.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “The exposition is detailed and clear; the appraisals are precise.”

The learning of the Confucian scholar unites substance and function, never pursuing two divergent ends; it extends through prominence and obscurity, never admitting two different commitments. Learning is the means of nourishing this mind before it is put to use; yet men’s capacities differ in their purity or admixture. Practical achievements are that by which…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
以推此心於已用也然而顯晦殊其遇材
者天之所賦而遇者時之所遭是可以强
而同之乎然而學者所以學道於心也道
貫乎一身而心周於萬事可小可大可崇
可卑可常可變可窮可達脩之於身而措
之於事業未始不合而爲一也是故殊途
而同歸一致而百慮者言乎其本原也其
學術之不足於事功云者是訓詁詞章之
習失之謏聞寡識流而爲迂且蔽也事功
===
===
之不本於學術云者是權謀術數之習失
之競名射利流而爲隘與詐也君子弗論
矣執事以體用合一之學下問愚也拘方
之士何足以與此然於鄉之先哲蓋嘗景
仰其一二矣請就正焉今夫世之學者自
其窮居未遇之日皆知志伊周而宗孔孟
矣伊尹耕莘而樂堯舜之道周公思兼而
成文武之德孔子之事業賢於堯舜而顏
子之易地能爲禹稷蓋聖賢之學合體用
punctuated:
以推此心於已用也，然而顯晦殊其遇。材者，天之所賦，而遇者，時之所遭，是可以强而同之乎？然而學者，所以學道於心也。道貫乎一身，而心周於萬事，可小可大，可崇可卑，可常可變，可窮可達。脩之於身，而措之於事業，未始不合而爲一也。是故殊途而同歸，一致而百慮者，言乎其本原也。其學術之不足於事功云者，是訓詁詞章之習，失之謏聞寡識，流而爲迂且蔽也；事功之不本於學術云者，是權謀術數之習，失之競名射利，流而爲隘與詐也。君子弗論矣。
執事以體用合一之學下問，愚也拘方之士，何足以與此？然於鄉之先哲，蓋嘗景仰其一二矣，請就正焉。今夫世之學者，自其窮居未遇之日，皆知志伊周而宗孔孟矣。伊尹耕莘而樂堯舜之道，周公思兼而成文武之德，孔子之事業賢於堯舜，而顏子之易地能爲禹稷。蓋聖賢之學合體用
translation_en:
…through which this mind is extended into practice; yet prominence and obscurity differ according to the opportunities one encounters. Capacities are endowed by Heaven, while opportunities arise from the times. Can these be forcibly made the same? Nevertheless, learning is the means of studying the Way within the mind. The Way pervades one's whole person, and the mind encompasses all affairs: small or great, exalted or humble, constant or changing, in adversity or in success. Cultivating it in oneself and applying it in one's undertakings have never failed to form a unity. Thus, different paths leading to the same destination, and a hundred deliberations converging upon one end, speak to their common source. As for learning said to be inadequate for practical achievement, this is the habitual pursuit of textual glosses and literary composition: its failing lies in scant learning and narrow understanding, and it degenerates into impracticality and blindness. As for practical achievement said to be ungrounded in learning, this is the habitual pursuit of stratagems and manipulative techniques: its failing lies in competing for fame and seeking profit, and it degenerates into narrowness and deceit. The gentleman does not discuss such things.
You, sir, have condescended to question me about learning that unites substance and function. A foolish scholar confined within fixed limits, how could I be worthy of taking part in this discussion? Yet among the earlier worthies of our province, there are indeed one or two whom I have long admired. Allow me to submit my views for your correction. Scholars today, from the days when they live in obscurity without opportunity, all know to aspire to Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou and to take Confucius and Mencius as their masters. Yi Yin plowed in Shen and delighted in the Way of Yao and Shun; the Duke of Zhou sought to embrace their achievements and brought the virtue of Kings Wen and Wu to completion. Confucius's achievements surpassed those of Yao and Shun, while Master Yan, had he exchanged places with Yu and Ji, could have acted as they did. For the learning of sages and worthies unites substance and function…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
道顯晦而一之者也自是以降學術不明
事功日陋蘇秦張儀公孫衍淳于髠之徒
旣以縱橫遊說之學爲當世所鄙而晏嬰
管仲之功乃孔門所羞稱焉嗣後申韓之
徒主於刑名孫吳之徒主於權術雖足以
爭雄當時而聲施列國固未甞本於學術
也漢之敝也尚經術而流於訓詁唐之敝
也尚詩賦而流於詞章雖足以闡示幽微
而垂法藝苑固未能施之事功也揆之吾
===
儒體用合一之學益背馳而不可返矣惟
仲舒之三策本於正義明道武侯之事業
本於開誠布公陸贄之告德宗本於尊仁
義黜功利蓋庶幾王佐之材而於學術事
功爲無愧焉下逮於宋豪傑挺生周程之
理學韓范之勳業卓乎不可及矣夷考其
時則吾閩之繼軌而流芳者不無人焉以
理學言之吾道南矣則楊中立見許於穎
昌送歸之日德宇粹然則游定夫器重於
punctuated:
道顯晦而一之者也。自是以降，學術不明，事功日陋。蘇秦、張儀、公孫衍、淳于髠之徒，旣以縱橫遊說之學爲當世所鄙，而晏嬰、管仲之功，乃孔門所羞稱焉。嗣後申韓之徒主於刑名，孫吳之徒主於權術，雖足以爭雄當時，而聲施列國，固未甞本於學術也。漢之敝也，尚經術而流於訓詁；唐之敝也，尚詩賦而流於詞章。雖足以闡示幽微，而垂法藝苑，固未能施之事功也。揆之吾儒體用合一之學，益背馳而不可返矣。
惟仲舒之三策，本於正義明道；武侯之事業，本於開誠布公；陸贄之告德宗，本於尊仁義、黜功利。蓋庶幾王佐之材，而於學術事功爲無愧焉。下逮於宋，豪傑挺生，周程之理學，韓范之勳業，卓乎不可及矣。夷考其時，則吾閩之繼軌而流芳者，不無人焉。以理學言之，「吾道南矣」，則楊中立見許於穎昌送歸之日；「德宇粹然」，則游定夫器重於
translation_en:
…and unifies the Way in its manifestation and concealment. From that time onward, learning became obscured, and practical achievements grew ever more paltry. Men such as Su Qin, Zhang Yi, Gongsun Yan, and Chunyu Kun were already despised by their contemporaries for their learning in diplomatic alliances and persuasive lobbying; even the achievements of Yan Ying and Guan Zhong were such that the followers of Confucius were ashamed to speak of them. Subsequently, the followers of Shen Buhai and Han Fei concentrated on punishments and administrative accountability, while those of Sun Wu and Wu Qi concentrated on tactical expedients. Although these sufficed to contend for supremacy in their day and spread their fame among the various states, they had never been rooted in sound learning. The failing of the Han was to esteem classical learning but lapse into textual glossing; the failing of the Tang was to esteem poetry and rhapsodies but lapse into literary ornament. Although these pursuits sufficed to elucidate obscure subtleties and bequeath models to the literary world, they could not be applied to practical achievement. Measured against our Confucian learning, which unites substance and function, they diverged ever further, beyond recovery.
Only Dong Zhongshu’s three policy essays were rooted in rectifying righteousness and illuminating the Way; the undertakings of the Marquis of Wu, Zhuge Liang, in sincerity and impartiality; and Lu Zhi’s counsel to Emperor Dezong in honoring benevolence and righteousness and rejecting the pursuit of profit and advantage. These men came close to possessing the talents needed to assist a true king, and had nothing to be ashamed of in either learning or practical achievement. Coming down to the Song, outstanding men arose: the learning of principle of Zhou Dunyi and the Cheng brothers, and the meritorious achievements of Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan, stood so high as to be beyond reach. Examining that age impartially, we find that our Fujian, too, had men who followed in their tracks and left a fragrant legacy. Speaking of the learning of principle: “My Way goes south”—thus Yang Zhongli received praise on the day he was seen off home at Yingchang; “His moral bearing is pure”—thus You Dingfu was held in high esteem when …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
召職學事之初悟理一分殊之㫖造語中
形外之域均爲得道之深矣凝神靜坐則
李愿中觀氣象於未發之前佩服周旋則
劉彦冲示齋銘於不遠之復契一中之體
守三字之符均爲見道之的矣朱元晦繼
河洛之眞傳本之致知力行以崇實踐之
學蔡季通受四子之遺書發明經世潜虚
以探理數之原禮經屬藁黃直卿詳於民
彝物則之訓矣其何負於吾道之有託邪
===
衍義推明眞景元悉於祈天永命之道矣
其何愧於斯文之自任邪之數子者學術
之醇駁雖未必其盡同然而任祕書者聲
振外夷尉蕭山者練如素任應召而定安
攘之計守郡而致惠政之孚何嘗不足於
事功邪其不然者亦其時之未偶耳以事
功言之經理兩河李伯紀抗言於危疑之
日絕貢驕虜曾明仲主議於犯順之秋飭
兵防而國是定抑遼夏而主威張均之有
punctuated:
召職學事之初。悟理一分殊之㫖，造語中形外之域，均爲得道之深矣。凝神靜坐，則李愿中觀氣象於未發之前；佩服周旋，則劉彦冲示齋銘於不遠之復。契一中之體，守三字之符，均爲見道之的矣。朱元晦繼河洛之眞傳，本之致知力行，以崇實踐之學；蔡季通受四子之遺書，發明《經世》《潜虚》，以探理數之原。禮經屬藁，黃直卿詳於民彝物則之訓矣，其何負於吾道之有託邪？《衍義》推明，眞景元悉於祈天永命之道矣，其何愧於斯文之自任邪？之數子者，學術之醇駁，雖未必其盡同，然而任祕書者，聲振外夷；尉蕭山者，練如素任；應召而定安攘之計，守郡而致惠政之孚，何嘗不足於事功邪？其不然者，亦其時之未偶耳。

以事功言之，經理兩河，李伯紀抗言於危疑之日；絕貢驕虜，曾明仲主議於犯順之秋。飭兵防而國是定，抑遼夏而主威張，均之有
translation_en:
…when he was first summoned to an office concerned with scholarly affairs. They grasped the purport of the unity of principle and the differentiation of its manifestations, and attained the realm of inward expression and outward embodiment [?]; both thus attained a profound understanding of the Way. Concentrating his spirit in quiet sitting, Li Yuanzhong observed the disposition of the mind before feelings arose; embracing the teaching and adhering to it in every action, Liu Yanchong presented a studio inscription on returning before straying far. Apprehending the substance of unity and centrality, and observing a three-character watchword, both achieved a sure perception of the Way. Zhu Yuanhui continued the authentic transmission of the He and Luo schools, grounding it in extending knowledge and earnest action to honor learning through practice. Cai Jitong received the writings bequeathed by the four masters and elucidated Ordering the World (Jingshi) and Fathoming the Void (Qianxu), exploring the origins of principle and number. In drafting his work on the ritual classics, Huang Zhiqing treated fully the teachings concerning enduring human norms and the inherent standards of things. How could he have failed the Way entrusted to him? In his elucidations in the Extended Meaning (Yanyi), Zhen Jingyuan thoroughly explained the way to pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate. How could he have been unworthy of his self-assumed responsibility for this cultural tradition? These several masters may not have been entirely alike in the purity or admixture of their learning. Yet the one who served in the Palace Library won renown among foreign peoples; the one who served as district defender of Xiaoshan was as practiced as a seasoned incumbent. One answered a summons and settled plans for securing the realm and repelling outsiders; another governed a prefecture and won trust through benevolent administration. How were they ever deficient in practical accomplishments? Those who did not achieve such results merely lacked a timely opportunity.

As for practical accomplishments, Li Boji spoke out amid peril and uncertainty to organize the defense of the two He regions; Zeng Mingzhong led the argument for cutting off tribute to the arrogant enemy when it defied the rightful order. Military defenses were put in order and national policy settled; Liao and Xia were checked and the sovereign’s authority enhanced. Both thereby contributed …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
裨於朝政矣四諫馳聲蔡君謨倡敢言之
氣新法報罷鄭介夫進流民之圖減丁稅
而民利興攻惠卿而主心悟均之有補於
時事矣陳述古當神宗召對疏薦三十三
人於古靈先生之稱何忝劉彥脩以單騎
入秦召諸將分守要害其捍禦西蜀之功
居多呂安老知建康而有防守東南聯絡
淮甸荆蜀之議乃忠臣之謀國也劉仲偃
使金虜而貽主憂臣辱主辱臣死之書乃
===
節士之矢心也之數子者事功之難易未
必其一律然以上十事者明脩德之典擢
三府者審經術之訓講經筵而達知天之
說任防禦而植忠貞之操寧不本於學術
乎其不然者以其學之未純耳此則有宋
人才表著於一代而垂範於後世者也至
我
國家治敎休明英賢繼起尋考亭之緒而追
名德之烈者竊有聞焉以理學名者若蔡
punctuated:
裨於朝政矣。四諫馳聲，蔡君謨倡敢言之氣；新法報罷，鄭介夫進流民之圖；減丁稅而民利興，攻惠卿而主心悟，均之有補於時事矣。陳述古當神宗召對，疏薦三十三人，於古靈先生之稱何忝？劉彥脩以單騎入秦，召諸將分守要害，其捍禦西蜀之功居多。呂安老知建康，而有防守東南、聯絡淮甸荆蜀之議，乃忠臣之謀國也。劉仲偃使金虜，而貽「主憂臣辱，主辱臣死」之書，乃節士之矢心也。之數子者，事功之難易未必其一律，然以上十事者明脩德之典，擢三府者審經術之訓，講經筵而達知天之說，任防禦而植忠貞之操，寧不本於學術乎？其不然者，以其學之未純耳。此則有宋人才表著於一代，而垂範於後世者也。
至我國家，治敎休明，英賢繼起。尋考亭之緒而追名德之烈者，竊有聞焉。以理學名者，若蔡
translation_en:
…benefited the administration of the court. As the Four Remonstrators won renown, Cai Junmo fostered a spirit of fearless speech; when the New Policies were ordered discontinued, Zheng Jiefu had presented his Picture of Displaced People. Reducing the poll tax advanced the people's welfare, and attacking Huiqing brought the ruler to his senses: all these contributed to the affairs of their time. When Emperor Shenzong summoned Chen Shugu for an audience, Chen recommended thirty-three men in a memorial. How could he have been unworthy of the designation Master Guling? Liu Yanxiu rode alone into Qin and summoned the commanders to divide responsibility for holding strategic positions; his contribution to defending western Shu was considerable. While serving as prefect of Jiankang, Lü Anlao proposed defending the southeast and coordinating the Huai region, Jing, and Shu. This was a loyal minister's planning for the state. Liu Zhongyan went as envoy to the Jin invaders and sent a letter declaring, “When the ruler is troubled, his ministers are disgraced; when the ruler is disgraced, his ministers must die.” This was the avowed resolve of a man of integrity.
The difficulty of these men's achievements was not necessarily uniform. Yet the man who submitted ten proposals elucidated the principles of cultivating virtue; the man promoted to the three offices [?] carefully examined the teachings of classical learning. They lectured at the Classics Colloquium and expounded the doctrine of knowing Heaven; they undertook defensive duties and established their steadfast loyalty. Were these things not rooted in their learning? Where this was not so, it was simply because their learning was not yet pure. Such were the talented men of the Song, distinguished in their own age and leaving models for later generations.
Under our dynasty, government and moral instruction flourish, and outstanding worthy men arise in succession. I have heard something of those who follow the tradition of Kaoting [Zhu Xi] and emulate the accomplishments of men renowned for virtue. Among those celebrated for Learning of Principle is Cai…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
清之經義精到督學大江飭躬勵行而動
必準諸古人若陳眞晟之篤信好古詣闕
上書功先主敬而言有裨於正學淹貫詞
林一新士類介足以廉頑者其黃仲昭乎
隨事觀理詠歌一貫學足以貞俗者其周
瑛乎篤信力行求底無過者林拱也師道
尊嚴精於禮記者鄭閻也數君子之典刑
具在其有志游楊諸儒之學者乎以事功
顯者若楊榮之歷事四朝望重一代參謀
===
秘閣而剖決機務林聰之正色朝端風裁
屹立首重國本而疏言定儲轉輸不擾𦙍
顔敢諫論兵得上策而畏之如神明者非
陳俊乎茂敭中外名德益尊終日端坐以
求聖賢氣象者非彭韶乎詣闕登對以得
賢才爲國治之本者吳源也奏開鹽法以
助軍餉著旬宣之集者黃仲芳也數君子
之政績足稱其庶幾李曾諸公之軌者乎
雖然諸君子皆鄉之先哲也其學術事功
punctuated:
清之經義精到，督學大江，飭躬勵行，而動必準諸古人。若陳眞晟之篤信好古，詣闕上書，功先主敬，而言有裨於正學。淹貫詞林，一新士類，介足以廉頑者，其黃仲昭乎？隨事觀理，詠歌一貫，學足以貞俗者，其周瑛乎？篤信力行，求底無過者，林拱也。師道尊嚴，精於禮記者，鄭閻也。數君子之典刑具在，其有志游楊諸儒之學者乎？

以事功顯者，若楊榮之歷事四朝，望重一代，參謀秘閣，而剖決機務。林聰之正色朝端，風裁屹立，首重國本，而疏言定儲。轉輸不擾，𦙍顔敢諫，論兵得上策，而畏之如神明者，非陳俊乎？茂敭中外，名德益尊，終日端坐，以求聖賢氣象者，非彭韶乎？詣闕登對，以得賢才爲國治之本者，吳源也。奏開鹽法，以助軍餉，著旬宣之集者，黃仲芳也。數君子之政績足稱，其庶幾李曾諸公之軌者乎？

雖然，諸君子皆鄉之先哲也，其學術事功
translation_en:
…Qing’s (Cai Qing’s) interpretations of the Classics were penetrating and precise. Supervising education in Dajiang [?], he disciplined himself and cultivated his conduct, taking the ancients as his standard in every action. Chen Zhensheng was steadfast in conviction and devoted to antiquity. He went to the imperial court to submit a written petition, gave priority in his efforts to maintaining reverent attentiveness, and offered words beneficial to orthodox learning. Was it not Huang Zhongzhao whose comprehensive learning distinguished the literary ranks, who renewed the community of scholars, and whose integrity could inspire incorruptibility even in the morally obtuse? Was it not Zhou Ying who examined principle in each affair, celebrated in verse the single thread running through all things, and whose learning could rectify popular customs? Lin Gong was steadfast in conviction and earnest in practice, seeking to attain freedom from faults. Zheng Yan [?] upheld the dignity of the teacher’s way and was expert in the Book of Rites. The exemplary models of these gentlemen remain fully before us. Were they not men who aspired to the learning of such Confucian scholars as You and Yang?

Among those distinguished by practical achievements was Yang Rong, who served four successive reigns and commanded great esteem in his age. He participated in deliberations in the imperial library and resolved affairs of state. Lin Cong maintained a solemn bearing at court and stood firm in his moral authority. Giving foremost importance to the foundation of the state, he submitted a memorial urging that the heir apparent be designated. Was it not Chen Jun who managed supply transport without troubling the people, who dared to remonstrate with an earnest countenance [?], and whose discussions of military affairs yielded the best strategies, so that he was held in awe like a divinity? Was it not Peng Shao who won distinction in service both at court and in the provinces, whose reputation and virtue commanded ever greater respect, and who sat upright throughout the day in pursuit of the bearing of sages and worthies? Wu Yuan went to the imperial court and spoke in audience, holding that obtaining worthy talent was the foundation of good government. Huang Zhongfang petitioned for opening up the salt system to support military provisions and wrote the Collection on Proclaiming Imperial Instruction. The administrative achievements of these gentlemen deserve praise. Did they not come close to following the course of such men as Li and Zeng?

Nevertheless, these gentlemen were all earlier worthies of our native region. As for their learning and practical achievements…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
吾不得而優劣之矣然以思齊之志而尚
論乎有宋諸賢則學術以朱元晦爲準焉
事功以李伯紀爲準焉元晦之學本於致
知而主於居敬至於上陳封事則以天下
大本今日急務爲言蓋惓惓然用世之心
也伯紀之志在於攘夷而主於死守至於
平生所得則著爲易傳內外篇論語詳說
蓋惓惓然窮理之學也嗟乎學術之不講
此事功之所以日卑也蓋甞聞之位天地
===
育萬物而其功始於慎獨治國平天下而
其功始於致知此則體用合一吾儒之事
也是故以萬古爲一心而後其道明學術
端矣以萬物爲一體而後其道行事功顯
矣愚也竊有志焉毋曰卑之無甚高論
第五問
林庭植
同考試官教諭伍批推究兵食之弊在於本源
處省約切中時宜而末復歸重得人尤識大體取之
punctuated:
吾不得而優劣之矣。然以思齊之志而尚論乎有宋諸賢，則學術以朱元晦爲準焉，事功以李伯紀爲準焉。元晦之學，本於致知而主於居敬；至於上陳封事，則以天下大本、今日急務爲言，蓋惓惓然用世之心也。伯紀之志，在於攘夷而主於死守；至於平生所得，則著爲《易傳內外篇》、《論語詳說》，蓋惓惓然窮理之學也。嗟乎！學術之不講，此事功之所以日卑也。蓋甞聞之，位天地、育萬物，而其功始於慎獨；治國、平天下，而其功始於致知。此則體用合一，吾儒之事也。是故以萬古爲一心，而後其道明，學術端矣；以萬物爲一體，而後其道行，事功顯矣。愚也竊有志焉，毋曰：「卑之，無甚高論。」

第五問
林庭植

同考試官教諭伍批：推究兵食之弊，在於本源處省約，切中時宜，而末復歸重得人，尤識大體，取之。
translation_en:
… I cannot rank them as superior or inferior. Yet, with the aspiration to equal the worthy, if we discuss the worthies of the Song, we should take Zhu Yuanhui as our standard in learning and Li Boji as our standard in practical achievement. Yuanhui’s learning was rooted in extending knowledge and centered on maintaining reverent attentiveness. When he submitted sealed memorials to the throne, he spoke of the great foundation of the realm and the urgent tasks of the day: this reveals his earnest desire to serve the world. Boji’s ambition lay in repelling the barbarians, and his guiding resolve was to defend to the death. Yet he set down what he had learned throughout his life in the Inner and Outer Chapters of the Commentary on the Changes and the Detailed Explanation of the Analects: this reveals his earnest pursuit of learning through investigating principles. Alas! Neglect of learning is why practical achievements daily decline. I have heard that the work of bringing Heaven and Earth into their proper positions and nourishing the myriad things begins with watchfulness over oneself when alone; governing the state and bringing peace to all under Heaven begins with extending knowledge. This unites substance and function and is the task of us Confucian scholars. Thus, only by sharing one mind across all ages can the Way become clear and learning be set right; only by regarding the myriad things as one body can the Way be put into practice and practical achievements become manifest. Unworthy though I am, I privately aspire to this. Do not say, “Set your sights lower; do not discourse too loftily.”

Fifth Question
Lin Tingzhi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: He traces the problems of military affairs and provisions to their sources, proposing economy at the root, aptly addressing the needs of the time. At the end he returns to the importance of obtaining suitable men, showing an especially sound grasp of the larger considerations. Accept this essay.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教授何批兵食詘乏久矣比來欲得國
士共濟時艱子獨能推本弊源條陳經略豈其人耶
考試官教授吳批究心時政是抱先憂者
考試官教授李批經畫時務切中肯綮
執事以
國家大計下詢承學顧愚不足奉明問然竊
見鄉之父兄長老嘗歷事
先朝多能明習世故其於財賦兵馬盈縮强
弱之算往往條分縷析若指言家人事時
===
愚旣竊聽之以爲時事如此而當事者猶
或持之而不敢議何歟於是退而稽之史
冊則知古之忠臣智士其深謀遠慮每每
憂盛世而危明主非過計也以爲如此則
治不如此則亂當漢文時海內號稱乂安
矣乃賈誼則以爲今天下事勢譬如抱火
厝之積薪之下火未及燃因謂之安其戇
如此絳灌諸人忌之不卽見用殆其後卒
如誼言豈不有遺恨哉洪惟我
punctuated:
同考試官教授何批：兵食詘乏久矣，比來欲得國士共濟時艱。子獨能推本弊源，條陳經略，豈其人耶？

考試官教授吳批：究心時政，是抱先憂者。

考試官教授李批：經畫時務，切中肯綮。

執事以國家大計下詢承學，顧愚不足奉明問。然竊見鄉之父兄長老，嘗歷事先朝，多能明習世故，其於財賦兵馬盈縮强弱之算，往往條分縷析，若指言家人事。時，愚旣竊聽之，以爲時事如此，而當事者猶或持之而不敢議，何歟？於是退而稽之史冊，則知古之忠臣智士，其深謀遠慮，每每憂盛世而危明主，非過計也。以爲如此則治，不如此則亂。當漢文時，海內號稱乂安矣，乃賈誼則以爲今天下事勢，譬如抱火厝之積薪之下，火未及燃，因謂之安。其戇如此，絳灌諸人忌之，不卽見用，殆其後卒如誼言，豈不有遺恨哉！洪惟我
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: Military resources and provisions have long been deficient. Of late, we have sought men of outstanding national talent to help surmount the difficulties of the times. You alone have traced these failings to their source and set out strategic measures point by point. Might you be such a man?

Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: He devotes his mind to current government affairs: here is someone who takes the troubles of the realm to heart before others do.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: His plans for the affairs of the day strike precisely at the crucial points.

You, honored examiners, have condescended to consult students like myself on the great concerns of the state. I am scarcely capable of answering your discerning questions. Yet I have observed that the fathers, elder brothers, and elders of my native place who served in former reigns are often thoroughly versed in worldly affairs. In assessing the abundance or shortage of revenues and the strength or weakness of troops and horses, they frequently analyze every detail as readily as if discussing their own household affairs. Having listened to them, I wondered: if present circumstances are thus, why do those responsible sometimes still hold back and dare not discuss them? I then withdrew and examined the historical records. From these I learned that the loyal ministers and wise men of antiquity, in their profound planning and far-reaching deliberations, repeatedly found cause for concern in prosperous ages and perceived danger even under enlightened rulers. Their calculations were not excessive. They believed that acting in this way would bring order, while failing to do so would bring disorder.

In the time of Emperor Wen of the Han, all within the seas was said to enjoy peace and good order. Yet Jia Yi considered the state of the realm comparable to taking fire and placing it beneath a pile of firewood: because the flames had not yet caught, people therefore called it safe. Such was his bluntness. Jiang and Guan and their associates resented him, and he was not immediately given employment. When events later turned out just as Jia Yi had predicted, could there have been no lingering regret? We reverently consider our …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏建都金陵薄海内外悉
歸版圖財賦所入不可勝紀然邊防要害
獨重西北當時經略率皆勳舊重臣企我
成祖文皇帝再造邦家定鼎燕京金湯之固僅
隔山後與虜爲鄰其勢蓋岌岌矣
成祖深思遠處列爲重鎮以防守之猶且以兵
在内則内重在外則外重於是立爲三大
營以固根本以備征伐景泰以後又更爲
十二團營故當其時内自京師外自九邊
===
猛將材官雲興雷奮以討則强以守則固
執事所謂東南財賦西北戎馬蓋謂此也
然愚甞考當時太倉之粟在江南者其初
止運七十萬石其後乃運至二百四十萬
石乃其後則歲漕四百萬石矣折色之銀
每歲四百餘萬兩以其半輸在
内府至於馬價料銀供應之需又歲以數十
萬計此外又有抽分之稅餘鹽之括開納
之例財賦所入視昔不啻加倍矣
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏，建都金陵，薄海内外悉歸版圖，財賦所入不可勝紀。然邊防要害，獨重西北，當時經略率皆勳舊重臣。企我成祖文皇帝再造邦家，定鼎燕京，金湯之固，僅隔山後，與虜爲鄰，其勢蓋岌岌矣。成祖深思遠處，列爲重鎮以防守之，猶且以兵在内則内重，在外則外重，於是立爲三大營，以固根本，以備征伐。景泰以後，又更爲十二團營。故當其時，内自京師，外自九邊，猛將材官，雲興雷奮，以討則强，以守則固。執事所謂東南財賦、西北戎馬，蓋謂此也。
然愚甞考當時太倉之粟，在江南者，其初止運七十萬石，其後乃運至二百四十萬石，乃其後則歲漕四百萬石矣。折色之銀，每歲四百餘萬兩，以其半輸在内府。至於馬價、料銀、供應之需，又歲以數十萬計。此外，又有抽分之稅、餘鹽之括、開納之例，財賦所入，視昔不啻加倍矣。
translation_en:
…Emperor Taizu Gao founded his rule over the Chinese realm and established his capital at Jinling. All lands within and beyond the seas came within his domain, and revenues poured in beyond reckoning. Yet among the strategic points of frontier defense, the northwest alone held overriding importance. Those charged with its management at that time were mostly eminent ministers of long service and distinguished merit. Looking up to [?] our Emperor Chengzu Wen, he renewed the dynasty and established the capital at Yanjing. Its defenses, firm as metal walls and boiling moats, were separated from the northern foes only by the country behind the mountains [?]; with these foes as neighbors, its position was indeed precarious. Chengzu considered the matter deeply and planned for the long term, establishing a series of major garrisons to defend it. He further reasoned that stationing troops within would give weight to the center, while stationing them outside would give weight to the periphery. He therefore established the Three Great Training Divisions to secure the foundations of rule and prepare for military campaigns. After the Jingtai era, these were reorganized into the Twelve Regimental Training Divisions. Thus, at that time, from the capital within to the Nine Frontier Commands without, fierce generals and able soldiers rose like clouds and sprang into action like thunder: powerful in attack and secure in defense. This, presumably, is what you mean by “revenues from the southeast and military forces in the northwest.”
Yet I have examined the figures for grain supplied from Jiangnan to the Grand Granary at that time. Initially, only 700,000 shi were transported; later the amount reached 2,400,000 shi; and subsequently the annual grain tribute transported by water reached 4,000,000 shi. Silver paid in commutation of payments in kind amounted to more than four million taels each year, half of which was remitted to the palace treasury. Requirements for horse purchases, fodder allowances in silver, and supplies amounted to several hundred thousand more annually. Beyond these were levies on merchandise, collections from surplus salt, and provisions permitting payments in exchange for official privileges. Revenue receipts were more than double those of earlier times.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承皆以樽節愛養爲事嘉靖初年太倉
之粟足支數十年外庫之銀未甞匱乏
內帑積至數千餘萬諸司所藏亦略稱是愚
甞攷弘治以前公私盈足減租寬稅之
詔猶屢下焉馴至今日內外遂稱詘乏此其故
何也得非土木荐興而賞賚無算乎抑
請討多而物力屈也團營之兵舊稱十二萬景
泰間縮三之一在今則又縮焉至於各邊
之兵尤可寒心宣大薊鎮今日所最急者
===
===
然將領所部每不能足額數督撫者甞招
募矣而鮮有應之者此又何也愚觀
成祖時甞頻年用兵而兵力最盛景泰弘治間
亦屢用兵西北而累立戰功頃自庚戌之
變虜數內犯然內外諸將兢兢固守未聞
以數萬營陣待敵者也今內自團營外至
九邊動稱兵數不足東抽西補朝募夕招
是何廩廩然也得非軍政廢弛而變通未
講乎抑繩法過而事權輕也夫以財賦則
punctuated: 列聖相承，皆以樽節愛養爲事。嘉靖初年，太倉之粟足支數十年，外庫之銀未甞匱乏，內帑積至數千餘萬，諸司所藏亦略稱是。愚甞攷，弘治以前，公私盈足，減租寬稅之詔猶屢下焉。馴至今日，內外遂稱詘乏，此其故何也？得非土木荐興而賞賚無算乎？抑請討多而物力屈也？團營之兵，舊稱十二萬，景泰間縮三之一，在今則又縮焉。至於各邊之兵，尤可寒心。宣、大、薊鎮，今日所最急者，然將領所部，每不能足額數。督撫者甞招募矣，而鮮有應之者，此又何也？愚觀成祖時，甞頻年用兵，而兵力最盛；景泰、弘治間，亦屢用兵西北，而累立戰功。頃自庚戌之變，虜數內犯，然內外諸將兢兢固守，未聞以數萬營陣待敵者也。今內自團營，外至九邊，動稱兵數不足，東抽西補，朝募夕招，是何廩廩然也？得非軍政廢弛而變通未講乎？抑繩法過而事權輕也？夫以財賦則
translation_en:
The successive sage emperors all made economy and the nurturing of their people their concern. In the early Jiajing years, the grain in the Grand Granary was sufficient for several decades, and silver in the outer treasury was never lacking. The palace treasury accumulated more than several tens of millions of taels, and the stores of the various offices were roughly commensurate with this. I have examined the period before Hongzhi: public and private resources were abundant, yet edicts reducing land levies and easing taxes were still repeatedly issued. Gradually, however, we have reached the present situation, in which both inner and outer treasuries report shortages. Why is this? Is it perhaps because construction projects follow one another and rewards are bestowed without limit? Or because requests for disbursements [?] are numerous and material resources are exhausted?

The troops of the combined training camps formerly numbered, it was said, 120,000. During the Jingtai reign, their number was reduced by one third; now it has been reduced again. As for the troops along the various frontiers, their condition is still more alarming. Xuanfu, Datong, and Jizhen are the commands where the need is most urgent today, yet the forces under their commanders repeatedly fail to reach their prescribed strengths. The supreme commanders and grand coordinators have undertaken recruitment, but few respond. Why is this, too?

I observe that under Chengzu, campaigns were repeatedly conducted in successive years, yet military strength was at its height. During the Jingtai and Hongzhi reigns, campaigns were also repeatedly conducted in the northwest, and victories were achieved time and again. More recently, since the gengxu crisis of 1550, the enemy has repeatedly invaded our territory. Yet the generals both at the capital and outside it cautiously hold their defensive positions; we have heard of none deploying tens of thousands in camps and battle formations to await the enemy. Now, from the combined training camps at the capital to the Nine Frontier Commands outside it, there are constant claims of insufficient troops. Men are drawn from the east to fill gaps in the west; recruitment goes on morning and evening. Why such apprehension? Is it perhaps because military administration has fallen into neglect and means of adapting it have not been considered? Or because excessive legal restraints have diminished the commanders’ authority to act? As for fiscal revenues, then…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
如彼以兵力則如此然則謀國者計將安
出昔有大賈恃其貲裕而荒耽無度僕告
之曰財且匱矣乃驚愕莫知所計僕曰是
無庸慮但去其所以蠹財者耳主人聽之
不數年其裕如初愚竊謂今
國家亦有四蠹焉何者錦衣官校有常額亦
有常祿今傳陞日增投充無數此一蠹也
騰驤四衛卒皆冒遞廠衛緝訪無辜以冒
陞級廩秩日加倉庫日竭此二蠹也光祿
===
供應費用不貲傳奉口分有數十年仍在
冊者至於廚役多鑽籍冒領此三蠹也各
廠匠作影射百出不能計工程力而支討
眾多此四蠹也頃者言官疏言宜如嘉靖
初年故事汰除一切冗役歲可省粟數十
萬乃至今不見施行何也至於清查
內府儲積已有
明詔矣而尋復報罷自古小人欲蔽主聽而堅
私計不過曰是皆祖宗故事非外廷得與
punctuated:
如彼，以兵力則如此，然則謀國者計將安出？昔有大賈，恃其貲裕而荒耽無度。僕告之曰：「財且匱矣。」乃驚愕，莫知所計。僕曰：「是無庸慮，但去其所以蠹財者耳。」主人聽之，不數年，其裕如初。
愚竊謂今國家亦有四蠹焉。何者？錦衣官校有常額，亦有常祿，今傳陞日增，投充無數，此一蠹也。騰驤四衛卒皆冒遞，廠衛緝訪無辜以冒陞級，廩秩日加，倉庫日竭，此二蠹也。光祿供應，費用不貲，傳奉口分有數十年仍在冊者，至於廚役，多鑽籍冒領，此三蠹也。各廠匠作，影射百出，不能計工程力，而支討眾多，此四蠹也。
頃者言官疏言，宜如嘉靖初年故事，汰除一切冗役，歲可省粟數十萬，乃至今不見施行，何也？至於清查內府儲積，已有明詔矣，而尋復報罷。自古小人欲蔽主聽而堅私計，不過曰：「是皆祖宗故事，非外廷得與
translation_en:
…such is the state of fiscal resources, and such the state of military strength. What course, then, can those who plan for the state devise? Once there was a wealthy merchant who, trusting in his abundant assets, indulged himself without restraint. His servant told him, “Your wealth is about to run out.” Astonished, he did not know what to do. The servant said, “There is no need to worry about this. Simply eliminate whatever is eating away at your wealth.” The master followed his advice, and within a few years he was as wealthy as before.
In my humble view, the state today likewise has four things eating away at its resources. What are they? The officers and guardsmen of the Embroidered-uniform Guard have fixed quotas and fixed stipends. Yet promotions conveyed by imperial order increase daily, and countless men seek enrollment. This is the first drain. Soldiers of the four Tengxiang Guards all obtain their places through fraudulent substitution [?]. The depot and guard agencies investigate and arrest innocent people to secure promotions fraudulently. Expenditure on stipends increases daily, while the granaries and treasuries are daily depleted. This is the second drain. Supplies furnished by the Court of Imperial Entertainments entail enormous expense. Some rations granted by orally transmitted imperial orders remain on the registers for several decades; moreover, many kitchen workers contrive to get themselves entered on the rolls and fraudulently draw allowances. This is the third drain. In the various workshops, fraudulent claims involving artisans and their work take countless forms. The work and labor required cannot be properly reckoned, yet the claims for disbursements are numerous. This is the fourth drain.
Recently, remonstrance officials submitted memorials urging that the precedent of the early Jiajing years be followed and all superfluous service personnel be dismissed, thereby saving several hundred thousand units of grain annually. Why has this still not been implemented? As for auditing the stores accumulated in the palace treasuries, an explicit imperial edict had already been issued, yet shortly afterward the undertaking was again declared abandoned. Since ancient times, petty men wishing to keep information from their ruler and safeguard their private interests have said nothing more than: “These are all precedents established by the imperial ancestors; the outer court has no right to participate in…”

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
議也然此不難辨矣昔成周以冢宰制國
用玉府天府掌珠玉器寶外府掌布之出
入内府藏九貢九賦之貨賄此皆天子府
藏也而悉太宰掌之漢唐及宋一應財賦
咸掌外府天子未甞置私藏以奸古法惟
我
國家以天下財賦輸其半于
内府以備異時非常之用雖内外賞賜取給
于此而積蓄之富前世莫及長老習聞
===
祖宗所以厚爲貯積者其
淵衷微意所以爲無窮之慮至深遠也豈徒爲
賞賜玩好之資巳乎然事不總於户部登
耗之數至不可究詰言官所以屢乞查盤
者其慮深矣古者國無三年之蓄曰國非
其國今太倉之粟所贏僅僅如此假令遇
卒然之警漕運阻阨商販不至都城百萬
生靈翹首待哺將何所仰給乎神農之教
曰雖有石城拾仞湯池百步帶甲百萬而
punctuated:
議也。」然此不難辨矣。昔成周以冢宰制國用，玉府、天府掌珠玉器寶，外府掌布之出入，内府藏九貢九賦之貨賄，此皆天子府藏也，而悉太宰掌之。漢、唐及宋，一應財賦咸掌外府，天子未甞置私藏以奸古法。惟我國家以天下財賦輸其半于内府，以備異時非常之用。雖内外賞賜取給于此，而積蓄之富，前世莫及。長老習聞祖宗所以厚爲貯積者，其淵衷微意，所以爲無窮之慮，至深遠也，豈徒爲賞賜玩好之資巳乎？然事不總於户部，登耗之數至不可究詰。言官所以屢乞查盤者，其慮深矣。
古者國無三年之蓄，曰國非其國。今太倉之粟，所贏僅僅如此，假令遇卒然之警，漕運阻阨，商販不至，都城百萬生靈翹首待哺，將何所仰給乎？神農之教曰：「雖有石城拾仞，湯池百步，帶甲百萬，而
translation_en:
… to deliberate upon.” Yet this is not difficult to distinguish. Formerly, under the Zhou, the Chief Minister regulated state expenditure. The Jade Treasury and Celestial Treasury administered pearls, jade, precious vessels, and treasures; the Outer Treasury administered receipts and disbursements of currency; and the Inner Treasury stored the goods and valuables from the nine categories of tribute and nine categories of taxation. These were all the Son of Heaven’s treasuries, yet all were administered by the Grand Steward. Under the Han, Tang, and Song, all fiscal revenues were administered by the outer treasury. The Son of Heaven never established a private treasury in violation of the ancient institutions. Our dynasty alone transfers half the fiscal revenues of the realm to the Inner Treasury to provide for extraordinary needs that may arise in the future. Although rewards bestowed within and outside the court are supplied from it, the abundance of its accumulated reserves surpasses that of all previous ages. The elders have long heard that our imperial ancestors amassed such substantial stores out of profound and subtle intentions: their provision for the limitless future was exceedingly far-reaching. Could these stores have been intended merely to fund rewards and objects of amusement? Yet these affairs are not administered centrally by the Ministry of Revenue, so that even the amounts of increase and depletion cannot be ascertained. The repeated requests of the censorial officials for an inspection and inventory thus reflect deep concern.
In antiquity, a state without three years’ reserves was said to be no longer truly a state. Now the surplus grain in the Grand Granary amounts to scarcely this much. Suppose a sudden emergency arose, grain transport by canal was obstructed, and merchants failed to arrive: on what would the million inhabitants of the capital, looking up in expectation of food, depend for sustenance? Shennong’s teaching says: “Even with stone walls ten ren high, a moat of boiling water a hundred paces across, and a million armored soldiers, yet …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
無粟不能守也若是豈可不爲寒心哉今
夫庶民之家終歲經營必計口而議先期
而戒彼固未甞有敵國外患之虞也然猶
兢兢然若此而况公卿大夫爲
國家深長之思可以冥焉决事哉且愚所謂
四蠹者至易見也當事者固難之愚謂
主上所親信而尊禮貌者非左右與勳舊乎此
皆身享榮寵而世受爵祿也且當
主上虛心圖治臣子效忠之時而積蠹夙弊不
===
肯一洗而更之使當國之臣勞心焦思而
莫知所計臺諫之臣持議而不已此愚所
以竊致望於左右勳舊之臣也執事復謂
九邊惟宣大爲急當時所藉屯田鹽法今
皆廢壞督撫諸臣所以爲戰守計者非
請討則莫可爲計此誠今日坐困之術也顧愚
非知邊計者然甞竊聞宣大一鎭所以馴
致積弱而不可振起者其失有四而其弊
有五不可不知也何謂四失邊備久弛醜
punctuated:
無粟不能守也。」若是，豈可不爲寒心哉！今夫庶民之家，終歲經營，必計口而議，先期而戒。彼固未甞有敵國外患之虞也，然猶兢兢然若此，而况公卿大夫爲國家深長之思，可以冥焉决事哉？且愚所謂四蠹者，至易見也，當事者固難之。愚謂主上所親信而尊禮貌者，非左右與勳舊乎？此皆身享榮寵而世受爵祿也。且當主上虛心圖治、臣子效忠之時，而積蠹夙弊不肯一洗而更之，使當國之臣勞心焦思而莫知所計，臺諫之臣持議而不已。此愚所以竊致望於左右勳舊之臣也。
執事復謂九邊惟宣大爲急，當時所藉屯田、鹽法，今皆廢壞，督撫諸臣所以爲戰守計者，非請討則莫可爲計，此誠今日坐困之術也。顧愚非知邊計者，然甞竊聞宣大一鎭所以馴致積弱而不可振起者，其失有四，而其弊有五，不可不知也。何謂四失？邊備久弛，醜
translation_en:
…without grain, it cannot be defended.” If this is so, how can it fail to chill the heart? Now, ordinary households manage their affairs throughout the year, necessarily reckoning the mouths to be fed when making plans and preparing against needs beforehand. They have never faced the threat of enemy states or foreign troubles, yet they remain so vigilant. How much less may the highest ministers and other officials, charged with thinking deeply and far ahead for the state, decide matters blindly? Moreover, the four scourges I have mentioned are exceedingly easy to discern, yet those responsible find them difficult to address. Are those whom His Majesty trusts intimately and treats with respect and ceremonial honor not his close attendants and the longstanding meritorious houses? All these enjoy glory and favor in their own persons and receive titles and emoluments generation after generation. Yet, at a time when His Majesty seeks good government with an open mind and his servants should render loyal service, they refuse to sweep away accumulated abuses and longstanding evils and reform them. This leaves the ministers directing affairs anxiously taxing their minds, unable to devise a plan, while the censorial and remonstrance officials continue pressing their arguments without cease. This is why I venture privately to place my hopes in His Majesty’s close attendants and the ministers of longstanding meritorious houses.
You further state that, among the Nine Frontier Commands, only Xuanfu and Datong face urgent need. The military agricultural colonies and salt regulations on which they formerly relied have now all fallen into disrepair. The supreme commanders and grand coordinators can devise no means of providing for warfare and defense except to request funds and supplies. This is indeed a way to remain trapped in our present difficulties. I am no expert in frontier affairs, but I have heard that the Xuan-Da garrison has gradually sunk into entrenched weakness from which it cannot recover because of four failures and five abuses. These must be understood. What are the four failures? Frontier defenses have long been neglected, and the vile …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
虜跳梁擺邊築墻歲無寧日軍民所種屯
田虜歲蹂踐子粒所入不能侔本遂致拋
荒其失一也商人自括餘鹽爭趨便易邊
地苦寒孰肯委身荒塞以務耕作鹽法一
廢屯田愈壞其失二也山東河南坐派邊
糧逋負過半有司催迫後期法令不行其
失三也每歲糴買商人託藉勢要所買米
豆半係參和且拖欠數多雖重懲艾之莫
能止其失四也如是則邊費安得不耗
===
請討安得不困哉何謂五弊古者兵將同心乃
可制敵今各邊將領罷遷不常視所部卒
何異傳舍此一弊也兵法曰視卒如子乃
可俱死今各邊將領掊尅軍士習成故套
此二弊也兵法嚴隊伍均犒賞今挑選標
下名為選鋒隊伍缺亂賞賜偏異三軍之
心先自怨望如是欲其同冒矢石難矣此
三弊也妄報聲息輒移信地虛糜行糧習
為得計此四弊也醜虜內入競相規避及
punctuated:
虜跳梁，擺邊築墻，歲無寧日。軍民所種屯田，虜歲蹂踐，子粒所入不能侔本，遂致拋荒，其失一也。商人自括餘鹽，爭趨便易，邊地苦寒，孰肯委身荒塞以務耕作？鹽法一廢，屯田愈壞，其失二也。山東、河南坐派邊糧，逋負過半，有司催迫後期，法令不行，其失三也。每歲糴買，商人託藉勢要，所買米豆半係參和，且拖欠數多，雖重懲艾之，莫能止，其失四也。如是，則邊費安得不耗，請討安得不困哉？

何謂五弊？古者兵將同心，乃可制敵。今各邊將領罷遷不常，視所部卒，何異傳舍？此一弊也。兵法曰：「視卒如子，乃可俱死。」今各邊將領掊尅軍士，習成故套，此二弊也。兵法嚴隊伍，均犒賞。今挑選標下，名為選鋒，隊伍缺亂，賞賜偏異，三軍之心先自怨望。如是，欲其同冒矢石，難矣，此三弊也。妄報聲息，輒移信地，虛糜行糧，習為得計，此四弊也。醜虜內入，競相規避，及
translation_en:
…the enemy runs rampant. Troops are deployed along the frontier and walls are built, yet not a year passes in peace. The agricultural garrison lands cultivated by soldiers and civilians are trampled by the enemy every year. Grain yields cannot cover the cost, and the fields consequently fall into abandonment. This is the first failure. Since surplus salt began to be brought under official accounting [?], merchants have competed to pursue the easier opportunities. The frontier is bitterly cold: who would willingly commit himself to farming in those desolate borderlands? Once the salt system fell into disuse, agricultural garrisons deteriorated still further. This is the second failure. Shandong and Henan are assigned quotas of grain for the frontier, but more than half remains in arrears. Although the responsible officials press for payment, deadlines pass and the regulations go unenforced. This is the third failure. In the annual grain purchases, merchants rely on powerful patrons. Half the rice and beans purchased is adulterated, and substantial quantities remain overdue. Even severe punishment cannot put a stop to this. This is the fourth failure. Under these circumstances, how could frontier funds fail to be depleted, and requests for further supplies fail to run into difficulty?

What are the five abuses? In antiquity, soldiers and commanders shared a common purpose; only then could they overcome the enemy. Nowadays, commanders along the various frontiers are dismissed or transferred unpredictably. How is their regard for the troops under them any different from their regard for a posting station where they lodge briefly? This is the first abuse. The Art of War says: “Regard your soldiers as your children, and you can face death together.” Nowadays, commanders along the various frontiers extort from their soldiers, until the practice has become an established routine. This is the second abuse. Military principles require strict organization of units and equitable distribution of rewards. Nowadays, men are selected for the commander's personal force under the name of choosing elite troops, leaving the units depleted and disordered and rewards unevenly distributed. Resentment thus arises within the army before anything else. Under these circumstances, it is difficult to expect the men to brave arrows and stones together. This is the third abuse. They falsely report enemy movements and repeatedly shift from their assigned posts, needlessly consuming marching provisions, and habitually regard this as a clever stratagem. This is the fourth abuse. When the vile enemy penetrates the interior, they compete to evade him, and when…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
至退邀冒殺平民以報功次此五弊也如
此則邊政安得不壞兵勢安得不弱哉執
事者更欲求為長策以救目前愚則謂四
失不去五弊不除雖使孫吳為將良平畫
策恐亦難矣雖然請試言之夫三軍之命
在將將得其人則事可成功可就兵法能
制生殺之謂將能專予奪禍福之謂將今
各邊所置總督鎮巡皆古大將之任也顧
今不能殺一偏裨建一奇策稍有更張則
===
持議者且接踵矣是欲其彎弓落羽而束
之手也豈事理也哉雖然所謂大將者未
易言也必極選才望出羣者然後可以當
之選才望矣必專事權以任之事權專矣
又必久任以責之成昔漢宣任充國宋祖
任郭進讒言無所投謗毀無所加斯可謂
能任將矣愚觀頃年所置大將其初固皆
以才推也一遭人言非罪則罷此於
國家御將之體亦稍陵夷矣在今日所當急
punctuated: 至退，邀冒殺平民以報功次，此五弊也。如此，則邊政安得不壞，兵勢安得不弱哉？執事者更欲求為長策以救目前，愚則謂四失不去，五弊不除，雖使孫吳為將，良平畫策，恐亦難矣。雖然，請試言之。夫三軍之命在將，將得其人，則事可成，功可就。兵法，能制生殺之謂將，能專予奪禍福之謂將。今各邊所置總督鎮巡，皆古大將之任也。顧今不能殺一偏裨，建一奇策；稍有更張，則持議者且接踵矣。是欲其彎弓落羽而束之手也，豈事理也哉？雖然，所謂大將者未易言也。必極選才望出羣者，然後可以當之。選才望矣，必專事權以任之；事權專矣，又必久任以責之成。昔漢宣任充國，宋祖任郭進，讒言無所投，謗毀無所加，斯可謂能任將矣。愚觀頃年所置大將，其初固皆以才推也；一遭人言，非罪則罷。此於國家御將之體，亦稍陵夷矣，在今日所當急
translation_en:
…when the enemy withdraws, they seek to claim credit falsely, killing ordinary people and reporting these as military achievements [?]. This is the fifth abuse. With matters like this, how could frontier administration fail to deteriorate, and military strength fail to weaken? You gentlemen in charge further wish to find a lasting strategy to remedy the present situation. In my humble view, unless the four failings and five abuses are eliminated, even with Sun Wu and Wu Qi as generals, and Zhang Liang and Chen Ping devising strategies, success would probably remain difficult.

Nevertheless, allow me to attempt an explanation. The lives of the entire army depend upon its general. If the right man is appointed, undertakings can succeed and achievements can be secured. According to the principles of warfare, one who controls life and death is called a general; one who holds sole authority to grant and take away, to punish and reward, is called a general. The supreme commanders, regional commanders, and grand coordinators now appointed along the frontiers all hold responsibilities equivalent to those of the great generals of antiquity. Yet today they cannot execute even a subordinate commander or put forward an unconventional strategy. At the slightest change, critics follow one upon another. This is to expect a man to draw his bow and bring down a bird while binding his hands. How can this accord with reason?

Nevertheless, the appointment of such a commanding general is no simple matter. Only after the most careful selection of someone outstanding in ability and reputation can a man be found fit for the post. Having selected him for ability and reputation, one must entrust him with sole authority over affairs. Having given him that authority, one must also retain him long in office and hold him responsible for achieving results. In former times, Emperor Xuan of Han entrusted command to Zhao Chongguo, and the founding emperor of Song entrusted it to Guo Jin. Slander found no receptive ear, and defamation could gain no hold upon them. This may truly be called knowing how to employ generals.

I observe that the commanding generals appointed in recent years were all initially recommended for their abilities. Yet once they become targets of criticism, they are either punished or dismissed. In this respect, the state's manner of managing its generals has also gradually deteriorated. This is something that today urgently requires…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
圖也雖然愚前所謂四失五弊則何如以
處之亦曰誠得大將而任之專託之久而
又不能去四失除五弊是則將之罪也始
則切責之甚則罷斥之又甚則加罪焉恐
未有不思奮者矣雖然猶未也執事欲求
國家長久至計愚以爲其本不在邊鎮而在
朝廷其患不在夷狄而在紀綱執事倘與其
進則願更僕以對焉
punctuated: 圖也。雖然，愚前所謂四失五弊，則何如以處之？亦曰：誠得大將而任之專，託之久，而又不能去四失、除五弊，是則將之罪也。始則切責之，甚則罷斥之，又甚則加罪焉，恐未有不思奮者矣。雖然，猶未也。執事欲求國家長久至計，愚以爲其本不在邊鎮，而在朝廷；其患不在夷狄，而在紀綱。執事倘與其進，則願更僕以對焉。
translation_en:
…a matter that urgently requires attention today. Yet how should the four failings and five abuses I mentioned earlier be addressed? I would simply say: if a great commander is indeed found, given sole authority, and entrusted with his charge for a long tenure, but still cannot eliminate the four failings and five abuses, then the fault lies with that commander. First reprimand him sternly; in more serious cases dismiss him; in still more serious cases impose punishment. Surely none would fail to exert himself.

Yet even this is not enough. If you, sir, seek the best plan for the enduring security of the state, I humbly believe that its foundation lies not in the frontier garrisons but in the imperial court; the danger lies not in the foreign peoples but in the state's governing order and discipline. If you, sir, permit me to develop this further, I would gladly continue my reply, even at such length that the attendants would need to take turns.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄後序
是歲我
皇上文命肇敷屬天下有司大比
士閩雖遠在海隅顧其士業
已聞
皇上仁孝久及覩
登極以來
===
璽書頒布炳炳乎視聽一新莫不
響應景從願爲帝臣與天下
士相望奮翼起也雲龍風虎
兹非其期哉御史王宗載蓋
自
上前受
明詔來策有司諸執事有司諸執
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄後序

是歲，我皇上文命肇敷，屬天下有司大比士。閩雖遠在海隅，顧其士業已聞皇上仁孝久，及覩登極以來璽書頒布，炳炳乎視聽一新，莫不響應景從，願爲帝臣，與天下士相望，奮翼起也。雲龍風虎，兹非其期哉？御史王宗載蓋自上前受明詔，來策有司諸執事。有司諸執
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

This year, as Our Emperor first spread his civilizing mandate, the responsible officials throughout the realm were due to hold the triennial examination of scholars. Though Fujian lies far away in a corner of the coast, its scholars had long heard of Our Emperor’s benevolence and filial piety. When they witnessed the promulgation of imperial letters bearing his seal since his accession, their brilliant pronouncements renewed all that they saw and heard. All responded like an echo and followed like a shadow, wishing to become the Emperor’s servants. Looking toward their fellow scholars throughout the realm, they spread their wings and rose. Clouds follow the dragon, and winds follow the tiger: was this not the appointed moment for such a meeting of ruler and worthy men? The censor Wang Zongzai had received the illustrious edict in the imperial presence and came to spur on the responsible officials and all those charged with conducting the examination. The responsible officials and their functionaries…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
事莫不凛凛奉
詔冀得名實純粹之士而登用之
庶幾稱
上意事旣竣御史又率所得士就
有司賓禮之迪不佞從諸執
事後得有言曰夫士以一日
之遇至見賓禮有司則人人
===
以爲華卽有司者亦以爲人
人賢且能而收之華固宜也
將人人賢且能乎結軔入
帝庭當使閩重於九鼎大呂不則
徒豪舉耳迪竊懼焉蓋聞知
人則哲自昔難之故百年一
聖猶浹旬也千里一賢猶比
punctuated: 事莫不凛凛奉詔，冀得名實純粹之士而登用之，庶幾稱上意。事旣竣，御史又率所得士就有司賓禮之。迪不佞，從諸執事後，得有言曰：「夫士以一日之遇，至見賓禮有司，則人人以爲華。卽有司者，亦以爲人人賢且能而收之，華固宜也。將人人賢且能乎？結軔入帝庭，當使閩重於九鼎大呂；不則徒豪舉耳，迪竊懼焉。蓋聞知人則哲，自昔難之。故百年一聖，猶浹旬也；千里一賢，猶比
translation_en:
…the functionaries all reverently obeyed the imperial edict, hoping to find and advance men of unalloyed excellence in both reputation and substance, thereby perhaps fulfilling His Majesty’s wishes. When the proceedings were complete, the Censor also led the successful candidates to the responsible officials, who received them with the ceremonies due to honored guests. I, Di, unworthy though I am, followed behind the other functionaries and was afforded the opportunity to say:

“For scholars, through the good fortune of a single day’s encounter, to receive such ceremonial hospitality from the responsible officials is something each regards as an honor. The officials themselves, believing every one of these men to be worthy and capable, have selected them; such honor is certainly fitting. Yet will every one prove worthy and capable? As they ready their carriages [?] to enter the imperial court, they ought to make Fujian weightier than the Nine Tripods and the great Lü bell. Otherwise, this will merely have been a grand gesture in selecting men. I, Di, privately fear this outcome. I have heard that discerning men constitutes wisdom, yet since antiquity this has been considered difficult. Thus, to find one sage in a hundred years would be as though only ten days had elapsed; to find one worthy man in a thousand li would be as though they stood side by…”

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
肩也況一日而舉九十人又
欲人人賢且能不已過望乎
顧臣子以人事君之義誠欲
有所託以自效爾且閩故無
諸裔壤也入漢始以提封通
中國唐宋以來人文較著儒
術彬彬視鄒魯間逮我
===
國家政教畫一遠邇同文閩士
尤多崛起纓紱相屬金石流
輝非復無諸時風氣矣然文
勝則史聖人敝之今之閩士
豈患不文患文之過而掩質
其執宜亟挽也會
明詔方以質文取士士遂能以質
punctuated: 肩也。況一日而舉九十人，又欲人人賢且能，不已過望乎？顧臣子以人事君之義，誠欲有所託以自效爾。且閩故無諸裔壤也，入漢始以提封通中國。唐宋以來，人文較著，儒術彬彬，視鄒魯間。逮我國家，政教畫一，遠邇同文，閩士尤多崛起，纓紱相屬，金石流輝，非復無諸時風氣矣。然文勝則史，聖人敝之。今之閩士，豈患不文？患文之過而掩質，其執宜亟挽也。會明詔方以質文取士，士遂能以質
translation_en:
…stand shoulder to shoulder. How much more, then, when ninety men are selected in a single day: is it not expecting too much to wish that every one should be both worthy and capable? Yet, in keeping with a subject’s duty to serve his ruler by recommending men, I truly wish only to entrust this responsibility to others and thereby render service myself.

Moreover, Fujian was formerly the remote territory of Wuzhu. Only upon entering the Han realm did its lands begin to have intercourse with the Central Kingdom. Since the Tang and Song, its cultural accomplishments have been conspicuous, and Confucian learning has flourished, making it comparable to the lands of Zou and Lu. Under our dynasty, government and moral instruction have been unified, and places near and far share a common written culture. Scholars of Fujian have risen to prominence in especially great numbers; one after another has worn the cap strings and seal ribbons of office, and their glory has shone forth in inscriptions on bronze and stone. The prevailing ethos is no longer that of Wuzhu’s time.

Yet when refinement outweighs substance, one becomes a mere scribe: the Sage regarded this as a failing [?]. As for Fujian’s scholars today, how could the concern be that they lack refinement? The concern is that excessive refinement obscures substance; this tendency [?] should urgently be checked. Just then, an enlightened imperial edict called for selecting scholars on the basis of substance and refinement, and the scholars were consequently able to respond with substance…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
文應之譬則縣黎結綠不眩
而珍干將鏌铘不拭而銛其
俗犂然一變則
聖人之興風動之乎孟氏甞謂有
王者作其間必有名世者此
一時也士豈無以名世自待
具曰有司朢之過乎且夫元
===
聖誦讀于莘丘尚父屠釣于
棘澤非不至微賤也一遭湯
文則釋耒投竿舉商周而大
造之功加四海澤流無窮玆
我
皇上明聖在位鼎運方隆湯文不
足王矣然且拊髀降顏拔沈
punctuated: 文應之。譬則縣黎、結綠，不眩而珍；干將、鏌铘，不拭而銛。其俗犂然一變，則聖人之興風動之乎？孟氏甞謂：「有王者作，其間必有名世者。」此一時也，士豈無以名世自待，具曰有司朢之過乎？且夫元聖誦讀于莘丘，尚父屠釣于棘澤，非不至微賤也。一遭湯、文，則釋耒投竿，舉商、周而大造之，功加四海，澤流無窮。玆我皇上明聖在位，鼎運方隆，湯、文不足王矣。然且拊髀降顏，拔沈
translation_en:
…and refinement in response. They are like the precious stones Xuanli and Jielü, treasured without dazzling, or the swords Ganjiang and Moye, sharp without polishing. Their customs have undergone a marked transformation: has the rise of the sage moved them as the wind does? Master Meng once said, “Should a true king arise, there would certainly be men renowned in their age among them.” This is just such a time. Can scholars fail to expect renown in their age, all saying instead that the officials expect too much of them [?]?

Consider the Primal Sage, Yi Yin, reciting and studying at Shenqiu, and the Father of Esteem, Jiang Shang, slaughtering animals and fishing at Jize: their stations were indeed exceedingly humble. Yet once they encountered Tang and King Wen, they laid down their ploughs and cast aside their fishing rods, bringing great achievements to Shang and Zhou. Their accomplishments extended throughout the Four Seas, and their beneficence flowed on without end. Now our Emperor, enlightened and sagely, occupies the throne, and the fortunes of the dynasty are flourishing. Even Tang and Wen cannot match him as kings [?]. Yet still he pats his thigh in longing for worthy men, assumes a humble countenance, and raises those sunk in obscurity…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
搜逸思得莘丘棘澤之賢與
共理諸士得無意乎始迪得
士之文也其言侁侁便便各
軌於道計不須臾見其人今
予得士之容也其儀濟濟師
師各度于衷計不須臾試諸
事此無他心竊愛之故望之
===
不敢不過也謂言不足概則
叔向之薦鬷蔑魏子之舉賈
辛不惟其言乎謂容不足符
則胥臣之遇卻缺然明之知
國僑不惟其容乎至謂言與
容可以盡人則雖孔門之徒
猶以為失之宰予失之子羽
punctuated: 搜逸，思得莘丘、棘澤之賢，與共理，諸士得無意乎？始迪得士之文也，其言侁侁便便，各軌於道，計不須臾見其人。今予得士之容也，其儀濟濟師師，各度于衷，計不須臾試諸事。此無他，心竊愛之，故望之不敢不過也。謂言不足概，則叔向之薦鬷蔑、魏子之舉賈辛，不惟其言乎？謂容不足符，則胥臣之遇卻缺、然明之知國僑，不惟其容乎？至謂言與容可以盡人，則雖孔門之徒，猶以為失之宰予、失之子羽，
translation_en:
…seeking out men of hidden worth, hoping to find worthy men like those of Shenqiu and Jize with whom to govern. Can you gentlemen have no aspirations toward this?

When I, Di, first obtained the candidates’ writings, their words were abundant and fluent, each conforming to the Way; I reckoned that I would meet their authors before long. Now that I have seen the candidates’ bearing, their deportment is dignified and mutually respectful, each measured against inner rectitude; I reckon that before long they will be tested in practical affairs. There is no other reason for this: in my heart I cherish them, and therefore dare not refrain from setting my hopes for them exceedingly high.

If words are said to provide no adequate measure of a man, were not Shuxiang’s recommendation of Zong Mie and Wei Zi’s promotion of Jia Xin based precisely on their words? If outward bearing is said to offer no reliable indication, were not Xu Chen’s encounter with Que Que [?] and Ran Ming’s recognition of Guo Qiao based precisely on their bearing? Yet as for saying that words and bearing can reveal a man completely, even those of Confucius’s school acknowledged errors in judging Zai Yu and Ziyu…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
迪閔然滋惑矣此無他心竊
望之故懼之不敢不至也且
取士數十人一人爾遇者縣
次續食登名天府不遇者返
其蓬蒿居焉使遇者之言徒
以自媒而卒不爲賴於民社
即蓬蒿之士猶得脩其質而
===
全之比見自媒者之不爲賴
也且相與目笑之矣諸士其
圖之昔者宋人得寶於梧臺
之東周客索而觀之曰此燕
石也越人學遠射彎弓仰天
而發矢落五步之内諸士行
矣射當及遠且使有司者得
punctuated: 迪閔然滋惑矣。此無他，心竊望之，故懼之不敢不至也。且取士，數十人一人爾。遇者縣次續食，登名天府；不遇者返其蓬蒿居焉。使遇者之言徒以自媒，而卒不爲賴於民社，即蓬蒿之士猶得脩其質而全之。比見自媒者之不爲賴也，且相與目笑之矣。諸士其圖之！昔者宋人得寶於梧臺之東，周客索而觀之，曰：「此燕石也。」越人學遠射，彎弓仰天而發，矢落五步之内。諸士行矣！射當及遠，且使有司者得
translation_en:
…I, Di, am distressed and increasingly perplexed. There is no other reason for this: privately I place hopes in these men, and therefore cannot but feel the utmost apprehension for them. Moreover, in selecting men for office, only one out of several dozen is chosen. Those who find favor receive provisions at successive county stops and have their names entered in the registers of the imperial government; those who do not return to their humble dwellings amid the weeds. If the words of those selected serve merely to promote themselves, and they ultimately prove of no benefit to the people and the state, the scholars dwelling amid the weeds may still cultivate their character and preserve it intact. When they see that those who promoted themselves prove of no benefit, they will exchange glances and laugh at them. You scholars should consider this!

Once, a man of Song found what he thought was a treasure east of Wutai. A visitor from Zhou asked to examine it and said, “This is merely a stone from Yan.” A man of Yue learned to shoot at a distant target; he drew his bow, looked up at the sky, and let fly, but the arrow fell within five paces. Go forth, scholars! Your arrows should reach far, and ensure that the responsible officials may …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
無若宋人有失寶也豈不爲
愉快哉
江西廣信府儒學教授吳迪
謹序
punctuated:
無若宋人有失寶也，豈不爲愉快哉！

江西廣信府儒學教授吳迪謹序。
translation_en:
…not be like the man of Song, mistaken about his treasure. Would this not be a delight!

Preface respectfully written by Wu Di, Professor of the Prefectural Confucian School of Guangxin, Jiangxi.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text: 福建鄉試錄〔隆慶元年〕
punctuated: 福建鄉試錄〔隆慶元年〕
translation_en: Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination〔First year of the Longqing reign (1567)〕

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄序
皇上奉
天御極建元隆慶歲丁卯秋八月
適天下大比期先是陳事者
上言頃歲敎陵士競爲剽說
徼摯發洎試之理率不効方
今
===
聖作物覩敦尚本實宜
令中外執事文學官少正文體
冀裨實用
詔下禮官議可維時監察御史王
宗載奉
命按行閩事比抵所部則首以
明詔詔之閩士負鐫緣飾者自是
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄序

皇上奉天御極，建元隆慶。歲丁卯，秋八月，適天下大比期。先是，陳事者上言：「頃歲敎陵，士競爲剽說，徼摯發，洎試之理，率不効。方今聖作物覩，敦尚本實，宜令中外執事文學官少正文體，冀裨實用。」詔下禮官議可。維時監察御史王宗載奉命按行閩事，比抵所部，則首以明詔詔之。閩士負鐫緣飾者，自是
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

His Majesty received Heaven’s mandate and ascended the throne, establishing Longqing as the reign title. In the eighth month, in autumn of the dingmao year [1567], the time arrived for the triennial examinations throughout the empire. Previously, someone submitting observations on affairs had addressed the throne: “In recent years, education has declined, and scholars have competed in producing borrowed arguments, seeking advancement [?]; when put to the test in administration [?], they have generally proved ineffective. Now that a sage has arisen and all look to him, and substance and solid learning are esteemed, officials responsible for literary education at court and in the provinces should be instructed to make some correction to literary style, in hopes of promoting practical usefulness.” An imperial edict referred the matter to the ritual officials, who deliberated and approved it.

At this time, Investigating Censor Wang Zongzai had received orders to conduct an inspection of affairs in Fujian. Upon reaching his jurisdiction, he made it his first task to proclaim the imperial edict to the scholars there. Those Fujian scholars who relied on elaborate literary carving and ornamentation [?], from this time onward…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
烝烝然知
皇上釐文務實意矣屆期苘等以
前御史胡維新聘來自四方
乃以苘曁敎授吳迪主試事
敎授何文明敎諭吳佐張篚
伍典鄭如瑾劉正綵同考試
事提調則左布政使劉光濟
===
左叅政楊準監試則按察使
劉子興副使宋儀望而御史
王宗載寔監臨焉諸凡耆事
之臣則旣簡於有位稽諸往
實益浚且恪矣御史乃前誓
衆曰際
熙時舉懿典人臣重負也有不協
punctuated:
烝烝然知皇上釐文務實意矣。
屆期，苘等以前御史胡維新聘來自四方，乃以苘曁敎授吳迪主試事，敎授何文明、敎諭吳佐、張篚、伍典、鄭如瑾、劉正綵同考試事。提調則左布政使劉光濟、左叅政楊準，監試則按察使劉子興、副使宋儀望，而御史王宗載寔監臨焉。諸凡耆事之臣，則旣簡於有位，稽諸往實，益浚且恪矣。御史乃前誓衆曰：「際熙時，舉懿典，人臣重負也。有不協
translation_en:
… increasingly came to understand His Majesty’s intention to rectify literary style and attend to substance.
When the appointed time arrived, Qing 苘 [?] and others came from various regions at the invitation of the former Censor Hu Weixin [?]. Qing and Wu Di, a prefectural school instructor, were appointed Examiners. He Wenming, a prefectural school instructor, and Wu Zuo, Zhang Fei, Wu Dian, Zheng Rujin, and Liu Zhengcai, county school instructors, served as Associate Examiners. The Proctors were Liu Guangji, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Yang Zhun, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner. Supervision of the examination was entrusted to Liu Zixing, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Song Yiwang, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, while Censor Wang Zongzai served as the Supervising Official. All the officials experienced in these affairs [?] had been selected from among serving officeholders; measured against past practice, their work was still more thorough and conscientious [?]. The Censor then stepped forward and solemnly admonished the assembled officials: “To conduct this noble ceremony in a flourishing age is a weighty responsibility for subjects of the ruler. If there is anything that does not accord …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
於慎者大義謂何眾跫然以
諾遂進提學副使蔡國珍所
選士二千七百有奇如例試
之得人九十乃詮名氏幷文
之粹者籍
獻之御史授簡俾茼颺言以冠
其端茼不佞顧惟人才之污
===
隆壹稟於世道自漢下達緣
世屢遷姑毋論已三代盛時
周稱多士乃仲尼持議於數
百載後則惟上嘉唐虞以為
僅一再見何者聖聖迭興道
化龐溢固其所漬漸者然哉
明自
punctuated:
於慎者，大義謂何？」眾跫然以諾。遂進提學副使蔡國珍所選士二千七百有奇，如例試之，得人九十。乃詮名氏，幷文之粹者，籍獻之。御史授簡，俾茼颺言以冠其端。茼不佞，顧惟人才之污隆，壹稟於世道。自漢下達，緣世屢遷，姑毋論已。三代盛時，周稱多士，乃仲尼持議於數百載後，則惟上嘉唐虞，以為僅一再見。何者？聖聖迭興，道化龐溢，固其所漬漸者然哉！

明自
translation_en:
…in exercising due care, what would that mean for the great obligation we bear?” All emphatically [?] voiced their assent. Thereupon the more than 2,700 candidates selected by Cai Guozhen, the Education Intendant and Surveillance Vice Commissioner, were brought forward and examined according to the prescribed rules; ninety men were selected. Their names, together with the finest of their compositions, were then compiled into a register and respectfully submitted. The Censor handed me writing tablets and charged me, Tong [?], with setting forth some words to stand at the beginning of the volume.

Unworthy though I, Tong [?], am, I reflect that the decline and flourishing of human talent depend entirely upon the moral condition of the age. From the Han onward, talent repeatedly changed with the times; let us leave that aside for now. At the height of the Three Dynasties, the Zhou was renowned for its many worthy men. Yet Zhongni [Confucius], passing judgment several hundred years later, reserved his highest praise for the earlier ages of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], considering such an abundance to have appeared only once or twice. Why was this? Sage succeeded sage, and the transforming influence of the Way spread abundantly: surely it was immersion in that influence that made them so!

The Ming, since…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
二祖啓運
列聖相承人文炳著肆我
皇上聰明仁孝天縱
聖神繼體
先皇德妙符合頃者
嗣膺寶曆崇奬儒碩徵佚起廢開
經筵興禮樂天下人士莫不回
===
面拭目以覩
大聖人所作為此即勳華顯承之
際無以加者精醇所鍾淑喆
挺出故苘幸從執事後博觀
閩士之文則見其指閎而深
體疏而實攄布乎詩書禮樂
之華根極乎道德性命之奥
punctuated: 二祖啓運，列聖相承，人文炳著。肆我皇上聰明仁孝，天縱聖神，繼體先皇，德妙符合。頃者嗣膺寶曆，崇奬儒碩，徵佚起廢，開經筵，興禮樂。天下人士莫不回面拭目，以覩大聖人所作為。此即勳華顯承之際，無以加者。精醇所鍾，淑喆挺出。故苘幸從執事後，博觀閩士之文，則見其指閎而深，體疏而實，攄布乎詩書禮樂之華，根極乎道德性命之奥，
translation_en: …the two founding emperors inaugurated the dynasty’s destiny, and successive sage sovereigns carried it forward, making literary culture shine resplendently. Now Our Emperor is intelligent, benevolent, and filial, endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom. He has succeeded the late emperor, with whose virtue his own accords wondrously. Recently, upon assuming the imperial succession, he has honored and encouraged eminent Confucian scholars, summoned those living in retirement, restored those dismissed from office, convened the Classics Colloquium, and promoted rites and music. Throughout the realm, scholars have turned toward him and rubbed their eyes to behold what this great sage will accomplish. Even the glorious succession from Yao to Shun could not surpass this. Where pure and refined influences gather, worthy and wise men emerge in distinction. Thus I, Qing 苘 [?], have had the good fortune to follow those charged with conducting the examination and to survey widely the writings of Fujian’s scholars. I find their purport broad and profound, their composition open and ample yet substantial. They unfold the splendor of poetry, documents, rites, and music, and reach down to the deepest mysteries of the Way, virtue, human nature, and Heaven’s mandate…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
曉鬯
國體貫洽時務羣言浩穰悉軌
於正繇其文以辨其材蓋
聖世之盛後唐虞成周而繼見者
也夫閩古南粤地也禹貢不
志其域職方不齒其名雖唐
虞帝德光天海隅黎庶莫不
===
共臣成周化行南國至使中
林野人可為公侯腹心而閩
獨未與有宋開先賢哲始出
乃今虺谿蜃壑類能組文譚
藝尊信俎豆之業且其承風
嚮治尤能稡就本實而使文
獻甲於天下概其極蓋將軼
punctuated:
曉鬯國體，貫洽時務，羣言浩穰，悉軌於正。繇其文以辨其材，蓋聖世之盛，後唐虞成周而繼見者也。
夫閩，古南粤地也。《禹貢》不志其域，《職方》不齒其名。雖唐虞帝德光天，海隅黎庶莫不共臣；成周化行南國，至使中林野人可為公侯腹心，而閩獨未與。有宋開先，賢哲始出。乃今虺谿蜃壑，類能組文譚藝，尊信俎豆之業。且其承風嚮治，尤能稡就本實，而使文獻甲於天下。概其極，蓋將軼
translation_en:
…display a clear understanding of the essential principles of government and a thorough grasp of current affairs. Their abundant writings all conform to what is correct. Judging their talents through their writings, this is surely a flourishing of our sage age such as has appeared again only after the ages of Tang and Yu and the perfected Zhou.
Now, Fujian was anciently part of Nanyue. The Tribute of Yu (Yu gong) did not record its territory, and the Offices of the Regions (Zhi fang) did not list its name. Although the imperial virtue of Tang and Yu illuminated all beneath Heaven, and even the common people at the edges of the seas acknowledged themselves as subjects, and although the civilizing influence of the perfected Zhou reached the southern lands, so that even rustic men living deep in the woods could become trusted confidants of dukes and lords, Fujian alone had no part in this. The Song dynasty opened the way, and worthy and wise men began to emerge. Now, even among viper-haunted streams and clam-filled ravines, people generally can compose writings and discuss literary arts, reverently trusting in the pursuits of ritual learning. Moreover, in receiving the civilizing influence and turning toward good governance, they are especially able to concentrate on fundamentals and substance, making their writings and learned worthies foremost in the realm. Taking the full measure of their attainment, they seem about to surpass…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
盛際而駕之矣此其故何
主德茂而敎化醇也往者閩疆不
靖農棄其畚工稅其刃漁師
賈客罷寘宿資祗今還定安
集稍稍憩趾而徵輸露布昕
夕猶廑士獨保其故有槧簡
之功不奪於戈鋌咕吟之聲
===
不輟於枹鼓文明駿赫視古
昔毋少卻此豈有司能自求
多於諸士哉三路置堠五寨
設守
聖天子所以奠麗爾疆而佑啓人
文者惠至渥也諸士遊
帝王之世席太平之澤躡風雲之
punctuated: 盛際而駕之矣。此其故何？主德茂而敎化醇也。往者閩疆不靖，農棄其畚，工稅其刃，漁師賈客罷寘宿資。祗今還定安集，稍稍憩趾，而徵輸露布，昕夕猶廑。士獨保其故有，槧簡之功不奪於戈鋌，咕吟之聲不輟於枹鼓。文明駿赫，視古昔毋少卻。此豈有司能自求多於諸士哉？三路置堠，五寨設守，聖天子所以奠麗爾疆而佑啓人文者，惠至渥也。諸士遊帝王之世，席太平之澤，躡風雲之
translation_en:
…the flourishing ages and surpass them. What accounts for this? The ruler’s virtue is abundant, and his moral influence is pure. Formerly, when Fujian’s borders were troubled, farmers abandoned their baskets, artisans laid aside their blades, and fishermen and merchants ceased their occupations, leaving their accumulated resources idle [?]. Now order has been restored and the people settled in peace; little by little they find rest. Yet the collection and transport of levies and the issuing of military dispatches still occasion concern morning and evening. The scholars alone have preserved their former pursuits: their work with writing tablets has not been displaced by spears, nor have their voices in recitation [?] been interrupted by the beating of war drums. Literary culture shines brilliantly, falling not the slightest short of antiquity. How could the responsible officials claim for themselves much credit for these scholars’ achievements?

Watchposts have been established along the three routes, and defenses stationed at the five stockades. The sagely Son of Heaven has thereby secured your territory and fostered the flowering of literary culture: his beneficence is exceedingly generous. You scholars live in an age of imperial rule, enjoy the blessings of great peace, and step into an auspicious convergence of winds and clouds…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
會今既與諸前哲接軫擊轂
矣然尚等之所以執筴而錄
之者文也視其文則人人能
矣異日通籍服官展采錯事
庫而效一命崇而翊
萬機外之則疆場萌庶之繁内之
則鈞軸安攘之大言當其事
===
功副其期跡不違心履不愆
素勳望名實直與師師濟濟
者相揖讓則豈直士有休問
卽
國家且賴之主司亦可藉是以
報
天子矣若乃庸違其言學博行僞
punctuated: 會，今既與諸前哲接軫擊轂矣。然尚等之所以執筴而錄之者，文也。視其文，則人人能矣。異日通籍服官，展采錯事，庫而效一命，崇而翊萬機；外之則疆場萌庶之繁，内之則鈞軸安攘之大，言當其事，功副其期，跡不違心，履不愆素，勳望名實，直與師師濟濟者相揖讓，則豈直士有休問？卽國家且賴之，主司亦可藉是以報天子矣。若乃庸違其言，學博行僞，
translation_en: …this auspicious occasion, you have now joined the ranks of the illustrious predecessors, your carriage shafts touching and your hubs meeting theirs. Yet the basis on which we, Shang and the others [?], take up our tablets and record you is your writing. Judging by your writing, every one of you is capable. In days to come, when your names enter the official registers and you serve in office, displaying your talents and undertaking affairs, you may render service in a humble appointment [?] or, in high office, assist with the myriad affairs of government. Outside the court lie the manifold concerns of the frontiers and the common people; within it lie the great responsibilities of central government, securing peace at home and repelling threats abroad. If your words fit the matters at hand, your achievements fulfill expectations, your outward deeds accord with your hearts, and your conduct does not depart from your longstanding principles; if, in merit and reputation, name and substance, you stand as peers of those dignified officials who take one another as models—then will it be only you scholars who enjoy a good name? The state itself will depend upon you, and those presiding over the examination may thereby repay the Son of Heaven. But if your conduct contradicts your words, and your learning is broad while your actions are false…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
雖仲尼所嘆材盛之世猶不
免焉𦤺於諸士顧敢以其文
之有斐也而遂快然無懼耶
玉巵無當賤於瓦缶大阿不
割不直鉛刀甘言餌進無裨
世用甚或程行於不肖名實
傎悖而棄之則諸士之自𨺚
===
於
國恩者厚矣事事者又安所逭
其責哉吾聞天以元命鼓鑄
羣品罔不含苞吐英應其時
也人以元日彈冠結綬錯酬
賡拜重其新也
皇上建元一詔至治煥然更新海
punctuated:
雖仲尼所嘆材盛之世，猶不免焉。𦤺於諸士，顧敢以其文之有斐也，而遂快然無懼耶？玉巵無當，賤於瓦缶；大阿不割，不直鉛刀。甘言餌進，無裨世用，甚或程行於不肖，名實傎悖而棄之，則諸士之自𨺚於國恩者厚矣，事事者又安所逭其責哉？
吾聞天以元命鼓鑄羣品，罔不含苞吐英，應其時也；人以元日彈冠結綬，錯酬賡拜，重其新也。皇上建元一詔，至治煥然更新，海
translation_en:
…even in the age whose abundance of talent Zhongni praised, such failings could not be avoided. As for you gentlemen, dare you, merely because your compositions are polished, rest content and free of apprehension? A jade goblet without a bottom is worth less than an earthenware jar; a great Tai’e sword that cannot cut is worth less than a leaden knife. If you use pleasing words as bait for advancement, contribute nothing to practical affairs, and even model your conduct on the unworthy, so that reputation and reality are at odds and you are cast aside, then great indeed will be your self-exaltation in relation to the state’s grace [?]. And how could those conducting these affairs escape responsibility?
I have heard that Heaven, through its primal mandate, fashions all kinds of beings: all put forth buds and blossoms in response to their season. On New Year’s Day, people dust off their official caps and fasten their seal ribbons, exchanging toasts and bows, honoring the fresh beginning. With a single edict inaugurating his reign era, His Majesty has made perfect governance shine forth anew, and within the seas…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
内垂髫載白之輩胥訢訢思
沐膏潤肖翹異質亦皆蕃躍
效靈士當茲世貞元際會脫
迹衡茅依馮
日月之光弼元化豎元功無負
帝臣腹心之選俾後世抽
天府之賢書論讚其盛則如仲尼
所以嘉樂唐虞成周者端在
是矣第令居則誦法孔孟出
則見知乎堯舜文武之
君而不以
盛世實用之材自命義將何擇夫
激羽流商不若下里寧爲雲
門突轅弛𤐫不若驪黃寧爲
punctuated: 内垂髫載白之輩，胥訢訢思沐膏潤；肖翹異質，亦皆蕃躍效靈。士當茲世，貞元際會，脫迹衡茅，依馮日月之光，弼元化，豎元功，無負帝臣腹心之選，俾後世抽天府之賢書，論讚其盛，則如仲尼所以嘉樂唐虞成周者，端在是矣。第令居則誦法孔孟，出則見知乎堯舜文武之君，而不以盛世實用之材自命，義將何擇？夫激羽流商，不若下里，寧爲雲門；突轅弛𤐫，不若驪黃，寧爲
translation_en:
…within the empire, everyone, from children with hanging locks to the white-haired elderly, joyfully hopes to receive the nourishing bounty. Even the smallest creatures, diverse in form, thrive and leap about, manifesting auspicious powers. Scholars living in this age, at the juncture of renewal, should emerge from their humble dwellings, rely upon the radiance of the sun and moon, assist the great transforming work, and establish great achievements. They should not disappoint the choice that has selected them as the emperor’s trusted servants. Let later generations draw forth the registers of worthy men from the imperial archives and discuss and praise this flourishing age: precisely herein lies what Zhongni [Confucius] so admired and delighted in under Tang and Yu and the Zhou at its height.
If, however, they merely recite and emulate Confucius and Mencius in private life, and on entering service gain recognition from a ruler like Yao, Shun, Wen, or Wu, yet do not regard themselves as men of practical usefulness to a flourishing age, what course will duty lead them to choose? If stirring the yu notes and making the shang notes flow is no better than the rustic song “Xiali,” better to perform “Cloud Gate” [Yunmen]; if charging against the carriage shafts and racing like flame [?] is no better than ordinary black or yellow horses, better to be …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
千里尺有所短寸有所長君
子曰寧舍短而取長凡以尚
實也諸士乘時奮藝由茲而
進如欲奉揚
上意以思報稱於萬一舍務實其
奚以哉是舉也提督巡撫右
僉都御史塗澤民輯寧武功
===
振敷文教提督南贛兵部右
侍郎吳百朋風猷遠宣士類
胥勸鎮守總兵官署都督同
知戚繼光整旅襄夷右文禮
士巡按江西等處監察御史
馬明謨奉節來旬觀法斯懋
刑部廣西司署郎中應存卓
punctuated: 千里。尺有所短，寸有所長。君子曰：「寧舍短而取長。」凡以尚實也。諸士乘時奮藝，由茲而進，如欲奉揚上意，以思報稱於萬一，舍務實，其奚以哉？是舉也，提督巡撫右僉都御史塗澤民輯寧武功，振敷文教；提督南贛兵部右侍郎吳百朋風猷遠宣，士類胥勸；鎮守總兵官署都督同知戚繼光整旅襄夷，右文禮士；巡按江西等處監察御史馬明謨奉節來旬，觀法斯懋；刑部廣西司署郎中應存卓
translation_en:
…a thousand li. Even a foot has its shortcomings, and even an inch has its strengths.
