The gentleman says: “Better to discard the shortcomings and adopt the strengths.” All this is to esteem substance. You scholars have seized the occasion to display your accomplishments and will advance from here. If you wish to uphold and disseminate His Majesty’s intentions, hoping to repay even one ten-thousandth of his favor, how can you do so without attending to substantive achievement?

For this examination, Tu Zemin, Supreme Commander and Grand Coordinator, with the title of Right Assistant Censor-in-chief, secured peace through military achievements and vigorously spread civil instruction. Wu Baipeng, Supreme Commander of Nan’an and Ganzhou and Right Vice Minister of War, extended his exemplary influence and plans far afield, encouraging all the scholars. Qi Jiguang, Regional Commander and Acting Vice Commissioner-in-chief, put his troops in order and subdued the barbarians, esteemed literary learning, and treated scholars with courtesy. Ma Mingmo, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Jiangxi and other places, came bearing the credentials of his commission to conduct an inspection [?], thereby promoting emulation of good examples. Ying Cunzhuo, Acting Director of the Guangxi Bureau in the Ministry of Justice…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
錄讞綏民儀刑攸寓前左布
政使今陞雲南右副都御史
陳大賓始事揆謀具悉成憲
右參政周賢宣副使張鳳來
左參議陳一松右參議李紀
僉事史嗣元袁大誠蘇愚趙
時齊徐作參將王如龍胡守
===
仁遊擊將軍張元勳署都指
揮僉事陳濠羅繼祖錢鳳翔
先後匡抒克成厥功右布政
使劉佃副使羅一道署都指
揮僉事傅應嘉耿宗元以入
賀行僉事黃可大以遷秩行皆
與聞盛媺例併書之
punctuated: 錄讞綏民，儀刑攸寓。前左布政使、今陞雲南右副都御史陳大賓，始事揆謀，具悉成憲。右參政周賢宣、副使張鳳來、左參議陳一松、右參議李紀、僉事史嗣元、袁大誠、蘇愚、趙時齊、徐作、參將王如龍、胡守仁、遊擊將軍張元勳、署都指揮僉事陳濠、羅繼祖、錢鳳翔，先後匡抒，克成厥功。右布政使劉佃、副使羅一道、署都指揮僉事傅應嘉、耿宗元，以入賀行；僉事黃可大，以遷秩行。皆與聞盛媺，例併書之。
translation_en:
…reviewed judicial cases and brought peace to the people, embodying exemplary standards of justice. Chen Dabin, formerly Left Provincial Administration Commissioner and now promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief in Yunnan, planned and deliberated at the outset, with a thorough understanding of established regulations. Zhou Xianxuan, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Zhang Fenglai, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Chen Yisong, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner; Li Ji, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner; Shi Siyuan, Yuan Dacheng, Su Yu, Zhao Shiqi, and Xu Zuo, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; Wang Rulong and Hu Shouren, Regional Commanders; Zhang Yuanxun, Mobile Corps Commander; and Chen Hao, Luo Jizu, and Qian Fengxiang, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners, successively lent their support [?] and brought the undertaking to completion.

Liu Dian, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Luo Yidao, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and Fu Yingjia and Geng Zongyuan, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners, departed to offer congratulations at court. Huang Keda, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner, departed upon promotion. All had participated in this splendid undertaking, and their names are therefore recorded together here in accordance with precedent.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
直隸蘇州府儒學敎授李苘
謹序
punctuated: 直隸蘇州府儒學敎授李苘謹序。
translation_en: Li Qing 李苘, Instructor of the Confucian School of Suzhou Prefecture in Zhili, respectfully composed this preface.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
隆慶元年福建鄉試
監臨官
巡按福建監察御史王宗載〔時厚湖廣京山縣人壬戌進士〕
提調官
福建等處承宣布政使司左布政使劉光濟〔憲謙直隸江陰縣籍靖江縣人甲辰進士〕
福建等處承宣布政使司左叅政楊準〔汝宅直隸宜興縣人癸丑進士〕
監試官
福建等處提刑按察司按察使劉子興〔賓之廣東海陽縣人辛丑進士〕
福建等處提刑按察司副使宋儀望〔望之江西永豐縣人丁未進士〕
===
考試官
直隸蘇州府儒學教授李苘〔子藎山東壽光縣籍臨朐縣人壬戌進士〕
江西廣信府儒學教授吳迪〔子哲直隸歙縣人己酉貢士〕
同考試官
浙江台州府儒學教授何文明〔汝中江西金谿縣人辛卯貢士〕
浙江嘉興府嘉善縣儒學教諭吳佐〔懋中直隸吳縣籍長洲縣人戊午貢士〕
直隸揚州府高郵州寶應縣儒學教諭張篚〔子儀四川涪州人辛酉貢士〕

隆慶元年福建鄉試。

監臨官：巡按福建監察御史王宗載〔時厚，湖廣京山縣人，壬戌進士〕。

提調官：福建等處承宣布政使司左布政使劉光濟〔憲謙，直隸江陰縣籍，靖江縣人，甲辰進士〕。福建等處承宣布政使司左叅政楊準〔汝宅，直隸宜興縣人，癸丑進士〕。

translation_en:

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
法語之言能無從乎改之爲貴巽與之言
能無說乎繹之爲貴
齊明盛服非禮不動所以脩身也
原泉混混不舍晝夜盈科而後進放乎四
海有本者如是是之取爾
易
乾元者始而亨者也利貞者性情也乾始
===
能以美利利天下不言所利大矣哉大
哉乾乎剛健中正純粹精也
允升大吉上合志也
問焉而以言其受命也如嚮
黃帝堯舜氏作通其變使民不倦神而化
之使民宜之易窮則變變則通通則久
是以自天祐之吉无不利黃帝堯舜垂
衣裳而天下治蓋取諸乾坤
書
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

法語之言，能無從乎？改之爲貴。巽與之言，能無說乎？繹之爲貴。

齊明盛服，非禮不動，所以脩身也。

原泉混混，不舍晝夜，盈科而後進，放乎四海。有本者如是，是之取爾。

易

乾元者，始而亨者也；利貞者，性情也。乾始能以美利利天下，不言所利，大矣哉！大哉乾乎！剛健中正，純粹精也。

允升，大吉，上合志也。

問焉而以言，其受命也如嚮。

黃帝堯舜氏作，通其變，使民不倦；神而化之，使民宜之。易，窮則變，變則通，通則久。是以「自天祐之，吉无不利」。黃帝堯舜垂衣裳而天下治，蓋取諸乾坤。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Can one fail to assent to words of sound admonition? What matters is reforming oneself. Can one fail to delight in words of gentle agreement? What matters is drawing out their meaning.

Purifying oneself, keeping the mind clear, wearing ceremonial dress, and making no movement contrary to ritual propriety: these are the means of cultivating oneself.

Water from a spring flows abundantly, never ceasing day or night. It fills each hollow before advancing and flows onward to the four seas. Such is that which has a source; this is the quality being singled out.

Book of Changes

The primal power of Qian is that which initiates and brings to flourishing; its beneficialness and steadfast correctness are its inherent nature and disposition. Through its initiating power, Qian benefits all under Heaven with its excellent bounty, without naming what it benefits. How great it is! Great indeed is Qian! Firm and vigorous, central and correct, pure and unalloyed: it is the utmost refinement.

“Ascending with confidence: greatly auspicious.” This means that one's purpose accords with that of those above.

When questioned in words, it responds to the charge it receives like an echo.

Huangdi, Yao, and Shun arose. They adapted institutions through change, so that the people did not grow weary; they transformed them with wondrous efficacy, so that the people found them fitting. In the Changes, when a limit is reached, change follows; through change comes free passage; through free passage comes endurance. Thus, “Heaven itself assists him: auspicious, with nothing unfavorable.” Huangdi, Yao, and Shun let their upper and lower garments hang down, and all under Heaven was well governed. They presumably took this from Qian and Kun.

Book of Documents

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
欽若昊天曆象日月星辰
惟事事乃其有備有備無患
二五事一曰貌二曰言三曰視四曰聽五
曰思貌曰恭言曰從視曰明聽曰聰思
曰睿恭作肅從作乂明作哲聰作謀睿
作聖
政貴有恒辭尚體要
詩
彼君子兮不素餐兮
===
羣黎百姓徧為爾德
文王孫子本支百世凡周之士不顯亦世
貽我來牟帝命率育無此疆爾界陳常于
時夏
春秋
夏單伯會伐宋莊公十有四年
秋九月齊侯宋公江人黃人盟于貫僖公
二年秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于陽穀
僖公三年
punctuated:
欽若昊天，曆象日月星辰。
惟事事乃其有備，有備無患。
二、五事：一曰貌，二曰言，三曰視，四曰聽，五曰思。貌曰恭，言曰從，視曰明，聽曰聰，思曰睿。恭作肅，從作乂，明作哲，聰作謀，睿作聖。
政貴有恒，辭尚體要。

詩
彼君子兮，不素餐兮。
羣黎百姓，徧為爾德。
文王孫子，本支百世。凡周之士，不顯亦世。
貽我來牟，帝命率育。無此疆爾界，陳常于時夏。

春秋
夏，單伯會伐宋。莊公十有四年。
秋九月，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫。僖公二年。秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。僖公三年。
translation_en:
Reverently follow august Heaven; calculate and represent the movements of the sun, moon, stars, and constellations.
Attend to every affair, and there will be preparedness; with preparedness, there is no calamity.
Second, the five activities: the first is demeanor, the second speech, the third seeing, the fourth hearing, and the fifth thinking. Demeanor should be respectful; speech, compliant; seeing, clear; hearing, acute; and thinking, penetrating. Respectfulness produces gravity; compliance produces order; clarity produces discernment; acuity produces good counsel; and penetrating thought produces sageliness.
In government, constancy is prized; in speech, substance and essentials are esteemed.

Book of Odes
That gentleman does not eat without earning his food!
The multitudes of the people everywhere emulate your virtue.
The descendants of King Wen, the main line and its branches, endure for a hundred generations. All the officers of Zhou—are they not illustrious, generation after generation?
He bestowed wheat and barley upon us; the Lord on High commanded that all be nourished. Without distinction between our boundaries and yours, the enduring order was established throughout these lands of Xia.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In summer, the Earl of Shan joined in attacking Song. Fourteenth year of Duke Zhuang.
In autumn, in the ninth month, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and men of Jiang and Huang made a covenant at Guan. Second year of Duke Xi. In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and men of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu. Third year of Duke Xi.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
齊人侵我西鄙公追齊師至酅弗及〔僖公二十有六年〕
冬公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕
子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭十
有二月己亥同盟于戲〔襄公九年〕夏公
會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷〔定公十年〕
禮記
司會以歲之成質於天子冢宰齋戒受質
大樂正大司寇市三官以其成從質於
===
天子大司徒大司馬大司空齋戒受質
百官各以其成質於三官大司徒大司
馬大司空以百官之成質於天子百官
齋戒受質
君子曰大德不官大道不器大信不約大
時不齊察於此四者可以有志於本矣
故樂行而倫清耳目聰明血氣和平移風
易俗天下皆寧
讓之三也象月之三日而成魄也
punctuated:
齊人侵我西鄙，公追齊師至酅，弗及。〔僖公二十有六年〕冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月己亥，同盟于戲。〔襄公九年〕夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。〔定公十年〕

禮記

司會以歲之成質於天子，冢宰齋戒受質。大樂正、大司寇、市三官以其成從質於天子，大司徒、大司馬、大司空齋戒受質。百官各以其成質於三官，大司徒、大司馬、大司空以百官之成質於天子，百官齋戒受質。

君子曰：「大德不官，大道不器，大信不約，大時不齊。察於此四者，可以有志於本矣。」

故樂行而倫清，耳目聰明，血氣和平，移風易俗，天下皆寧。

讓之三也，象月之三日而成魄也。
translation_en:
The men of Qi invaded our western borderlands. The duke pursued the army of Qi as far as Xi but did not catch up with it. 〔Twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi.〕 In winter, the duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi 杞, the Viscount of Xiao Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi 齊, in attacking Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the jihai day, they jointly entered into a covenant at Xi 戲. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xiang.〕 In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding.〕

Book of Rites

The Accounts Manager submits the year's results to the Son of Heaven for examination; the Grand Steward purifies himself and fasts before receiving the submission. The three officials—the Music Director, the Minister of Justice, and the market official—follow with submissions of their results to the Son of Heaven. The Minister of Education, the Minister of War, and the Minister of Works purify themselves and fast before receiving the submissions. The various officials each submit their results to these three ministers for examination. The Minister of Education, the Minister of War, and the Minister of Works submit the results of all the officials to the Son of Heaven; all the officials purify themselves and fast before receiving his assessment.

The gentleman says: “Great virtue is not confined to a particular office; the great Way is not confined to a particular instrument; great trustworthiness requires no covenant; action perfectly suited to its time follows no uniform pattern. By discerning these four things, one may set one's aspirations upon the root.”

Thus, when music is practiced, human relationships become clear, the ears and eyes become keen, and the vital energies become harmonious and balanced. Prevailing ways and customs are transformed, and all under Heaven is at peace.

The three acts of yielding emulate the moon, whose body takes form on the third day.

問：二帝三王，神聖皆天授也，廼猶稽古敬學，惟日不足。豈惟其心好之？即君師天
translation_en:
Second Session

Discourse
“The gentleman pursues profound attainment through the Way.”

Imperial Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One topic from among these [?]〕
Compose an edict in the voice of the Han emperor on first establishing Erudites for the Five Classics. 〔Fifth year of Jianyuan〕
Compose a proclamation in the voice of the Tang emperor appointing Li Jing and others as Commissioners for Demotion and Promotion, to travel separately throughout the realm. 〔Eighth year of Zhenguan〕
Compose a memorial in the voice of the Song Academician Sun Shi, presenting the Illustration of “Against Idleness” (Wuyi). 〔Fifth year of Tiansheng〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items〕
Adding to or deleting from official documents.
The market office’s assessment of commodity prices.
Weapons of palace guards.
Exemption of the elderly and young from interrogation under torture.
Manufacture and construction that do not conform to regulations.

Third Session

Policy Questions 〔Five questions〕
Question: The divine sagacity of the Two Emperors and Three Kings was in every case Heaven-bestowed. Yet they still investigated antiquity and applied themselves reverently to learning, finding each day insufficient. Was this merely because their hearts delighted in it? Indeed, in serving as rulers and teachers of all under Heaven…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
下之大任必有非學莫濟者不然何憂
惕相傳一揆耶漢唐宋英誼之君表章
誦法臨雍御講非盡不學也顧其道未
粹而治益去古遠無亦其所以學者非
歟抑諸侍從之臣論思未效也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝初戢干戈業已潛心
聖學其大者諭宋濂諭曾魯書洪範書衍義錄
存心錄省躬其義何居可得殫述之乎
列聖相承道同心一如
===
表章四書五經矣而著
心法以闡
鴻猷何至備也
編輯五倫全書矣而製
帝訓以貽
燕謀何至精也
文華大訓旣以飭學爲先而猶御
經筵不輟於寒暑
闕里建廟旣以尊師爲重而猶資講沃不忘
punctuated:
下之大任，必有非學莫濟者。不然，何憂惕相傳一揆耶？漢唐宋英誼之君，表章誦法，臨雍御講，非盡不學也。顧其道未粹，而治益去古遠，無亦其所以學者非歟？抑諸侍從之臣論思未效也？洪惟我太祖高皇帝初戢干戈，業已潛心聖學。其大者，諭宋濂、諭曾魯，書《洪範》、書《衍義》，錄存心、錄省躬，其義何居？可得殫述之乎？
列聖相承，道同心一。如表章《四書》《五經》矣，而著《心法》以闡鴻猷，何至備也！編輯《五倫全書》矣，而製《帝訓》以貽燕謀，何至精也！《文華大訓》旣以飭學爲先，而猶御經筵，不輟於寒暑；闕里建廟旣以尊師爲重，而猶資講沃，不忘
translation_en:
…the great responsibility of serving as ruler and teacher of all under Heaven must involve things that cannot be accomplished without learning. Otherwise, why would their anxious vigilance have been transmitted from one to another according to a single standard? The illustrious and righteous [?] rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song honored the classics, recited them and took them as models, visited the imperial academy, and attended lectures. They were certainly not all without learning. Yet their Way remained impure, and their government departed ever further from antiquity. Might their approach to learning have been mistaken? Or had the deliberations and reflections of their attendant officials failed to produce results?
We reverently consider how our Emperor Taizu Gao, when he had only just laid aside arms, was already devoting himself to sagely learning. Among the major instances were his instructions to Song Lian and Zeng Lu, his writings on the Great Plan and the Extended Meaning, and his records concerning preserving the mind and examining oneself [?]. What significance lay in these? Can you expound it exhaustively?
The successive sage emperors shared one Way and one purpose. For example, they had already honored the Four Books and Five Classics, yet also composed the Methods of the Mind to elucidate their grand designs—how comprehensive! They had already compiled the Complete Book of the Five Relationships, yet also composed the Imperial Instructions to bequeath plans for their descendants’ security—how refined! The Great Admonitions of the Hall of Literary Brilliance already gave priority to diligence in learning, yet they continued to attend the Classics Colloquium without interruption through winter’s cold and summer’s heat. The establishment of a temple at Queli already emphasized honoring the teacher, yet they continued to draw nourishment from lectures, never forgetting …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
於箴規此皆學術之章明較著者寧無
媲美於
聖祖乎曁我
世宗肅皇帝朝御
經筵退臨
書幄作敬一箴註四箴解心學淵源光揚佑
啓蔑以加矣今我
皇上以上聖之資撫中興之運
登極之初崇儒重道肇舉
===
經筵
親臨大學脩一代之曠典紹千古之真傳天下
臣民何幸復覩二帝三王時景象也諸
士有能對揚之者乎亦復有補於論思
者乎願聞其槩
問帝王之治天下專務以德化民而刑以
輔治者乃不得已而用之是故虞命士
師夏制常刑及周官司寇之掌邦禁尚
矣然舜之欽恤禹之泣罪成康之慎獄
punctuated:
於箴規。此皆學術之章明較著者，寧無媲美於聖祖乎？曁我世宗肅皇帝，朝御經筵，退臨書幄，作敬一箴，註四箴解，心學淵源，光揚佑啓，蔑以加矣。今我皇上，以上聖之資，撫中興之運，登極之初，崇儒重道，肇舉經筵，親臨大學，脩一代之曠典，紹千古之真傳。天下臣民何幸復覩二帝三王時景象也！諸士有能對揚之者乎？亦復有補於論思者乎？願聞其槩。

問：帝王之治天下，專務以德化民，而刑以輔治者，乃不得已而用之。是故虞命士師，夏制常刑，及周官司寇之掌邦禁，尚矣。然舜之欽恤，禹之泣罪，成康之慎獄
translation_en:
…in admonition and correction. These are all clear and conspicuous manifestations of his learning. Surely they bear comparison with those of the sagely founding ancestor? Then came our Emperor Shizong, posthumously titled Su: in the morning he attended the Classics Colloquium, and afterward withdrew to his study. He composed the Admonition on Single-minded Reverence and annotated the Explanations of the Four Admonitions [?]. In illuminating the sources of the learning of the mind and guiding and enlightening posterity, nothing could surpass him.

Now our Emperor, endowed with the qualities of a supreme sage, has taken charge at a time of dynastic resurgence. At the very beginning of his reign, he honored Confucian learning and esteemed the Way, inaugurated the Classics Colloquium, and personally visited the Imperial University. He has revived a grand ceremony long neglected in this dynasty and continued the true transmission of the ages. How fortunate are the empire’s subjects to witness once more the scenes of the age of the Two Emperors and Three Kings! Can any of you candidates fittingly respond to and extol these achievements? Can you also contribute to deliberation and reflection? I wish to hear the broad outlines of your views.

Question: In governing the world, emperors and kings devote themselves above all to transforming the people through virtue; punishments, which assist government, are employed only when unavoidable. Thus Yu’s appointment of a judicial officer, the Xia’s establishment of regular punishments, and the Minister of Justice’s responsibility for the state’s prohibitions among the offices of Zhou all have ancient precedents. Yet Shun’s reverent care and compassion, Yu’s weeping over offenders, and Kings Cheng and Kang’s caution in adjudicating cases…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
敬刑玆其仁心仁政可得而究言歟三
代而下或約法三章或詔除肉刑或奏
必五覆或親錄繫囚咸所以重民命致
天和良有足稱者然夷考當代之讞獄
果盡明刑之中與前聖相為脗合否耶
洪惟我
太祖高皇帝肇造區宇稽古定制旣詳且備矣
而
祖訓一書禁用墨劓剕宮之刑及戒諭比部諸
===
臣謂鞫獄當存平恕毋以刑殺立威是
其欽恤愼重之意同符舜禹成康眞足
以壽國脈於無疆也其詳可得聞歟逮
我
皇上嗣登
寶位軫念民生首當審决之期渙頒停免之
命是又遠契舜禹成康之心祇承
聖祖慈祥之訓中外臣民莫不歌咏熈皡而景
仰太和矣一時文法之吏孰不思將順
punctuated: 敬刑，玆其仁心仁政，可得而究言歟？三代而下，或約法三章，或詔除肉刑，或奏必五覆，或親錄繫囚，咸所以重民命、致天和，良有足稱者。然夷考當代之讞獄，果盡明刑之中，與前聖相為脗合否耶？洪惟我太祖高皇帝肇造區宇，稽古定制，旣詳且備矣。而《祖訓》一書，禁用墨、劓、剕、宮之刑，及戒諭比部諸臣，謂鞫獄當存平恕，毋以刑殺立威。是其欽恤愼重之意，同符舜、禹、成、康，眞足以壽國脈於無疆也。其詳可得聞歟？逮我皇上嗣登寶位，軫念民生，首當審决之期，渙頒停免之命，是又遠契舜、禹、成、康之心，祇承聖祖慈祥之訓。中外臣民莫不歌咏熈皡，而景仰太和矣。一時文法之吏，孰不思將順
translation_en:
…and reverence in administering punishments: can their benevolent hearts and benevolent governance be discussed exhaustively? After the Three Dynasties, some rulers reduced the laws to three articles; some decreed the abolition of mutilating punishments; some required five submissions to the throne for review before an execution; and some personally reviewed the cases of imprisoned offenders. All these measures served to value the lives of the people and bring about Heaven’s harmony, and indeed deserve praise. Yet, impartially examining the adjudication of criminal cases in those times, did it invariably attain the proper balance in the discerning administration of punishments and accord with the sages of earlier ages?

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the realm and consulted antiquity to establish institutions, making them both detailed and comprehensive. Moreover, the book Ancestral Instructions prohibited tattooing, cutting off the nose, amputation of the feet, and castration as punishments. He also admonished the officials of the Ministry of Justice that, in trying cases, they should preserve fairness and forbearance and should not establish their authority through punishment and execution. His concern for compassion and caution thus accorded with that of Shun, Yu, and Kings Cheng and Kang, and was truly sufficient to sustain the dynasty’s vitality without end. May we hear the particulars?

When our present Emperor succeeded to the precious throne, he was deeply concerned for the people’s welfare. At the first season for reviewing capital cases and carrying out executions, he graciously issued an order suspending executions and granting exemptions. This again accorded across the ages with the hearts of Shun, Yu, and Kings Cheng and Kang, and reverently upheld the compassionate instructions of the sagely founder. Officials and common people, at court and throughout the realm, all sing of this radiant prosperity and look up in admiration to its supreme harmony. Among the officials versed in statutes in our day, who would not wish to support and carry forward…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
德意以措斯世於仁壽之域也然其重輕出
入豈盡得其平而無可議者歟夫上有
欽恤之仁則下有欽若之義兹欲刑期
無刑辟以止辟于以廣
皇上好生之德抑何道以致之爾多士其悉心
對揚以鳴
國家刑措之盛焉
問天下之大非賢不乂而官人之制則明
揚黜陟自虞廷巳然矣三代之法至周
===
大備大司徒掌三物之敎而賓興之大
宰計羣吏之治而誅賞之固虞廷之遺
意也其法可歷數而稱之歟後世善治
惟漢唐宋其選舉之法則設科目以斂
天下之才漢之法大槩有三唐之法大
槩有二宋之中葉則倂置一科其詳可
得聞歟與成周賓興之義亦有同歟考
課之法則較殿最以別天下之治漢有
奏事之六條唐有考功之九等宋以七
punctuated:
德意，以措斯世於仁壽之域也。然其重輕出入，豈盡得其平而無可議者歟？夫上有欽恤之仁，則下有欽若之義。兹欲刑期無刑，辟以止辟，于以廣皇上好生之德，抑何道以致之？爾多士其悉心對揚，以鳴國家刑措之盛焉。
問：天下之大，非賢不乂，而官人之制，則明揚黜陟，自虞廷巳然矣。三代之法，至周大備。大司徒掌三物之敎而賓興之，大宰計羣吏之治而誅賞之，固虞廷之遺意也。其法可歷數而稱之歟？後世善治，惟漢唐宋。其選舉之法，則設科目以斂天下之才。漢之法大槩有三，唐之法大槩有二，宋之中葉則倂置一科，其詳可得聞歟？與成周賓興之義亦有同歟？考課之法，則較殿最以別天下之治。漢有奏事之六條，唐有考功之九等，宋以七
translation_en:
…the benevolent intentions of the sovereign, so as to bring this age into a realm of humanity and longevity. Yet, in making punishments heavier or lighter and in convicting or acquitting, has perfect equity invariably been achieved, leaving nothing open to question? When those above possess the benevolence of reverent care for those facing punishment, those below have a duty of reverent obedience. We now wish to make punishment serve the aim of having no punishment, and to use penalties to end the need for penalties, thereby extending His Majesty’s virtue of cherishing life. By what means can this be accomplished? You candidates should devote your whole minds to answering and extolling this intent, proclaiming the flourishing condition of a state whose punishments lie unused.
Question: The vast realm cannot be governed without worthy men. As for the system of appointing officials, the clear recognition and advancement of talent, and the demotion and promotion of officials, were already practiced at the court of Shun. The institutions of the Three Dynasties reached their fullest development under the Zhou. The Minister of Education directed instruction in the three categories and honored worthy men as guests before advancing them; the Grand Steward assessed the administration of the assembled officials and punished or rewarded them. These practices surely preserved the intent of Shun’s court. Can you enumerate and describe their rules in detail? Among later dynasties, the Han, Tang, and Song excelled in government. Their methods of selecting men for office established examination categories to gather the talent of the realm. The Han system broadly comprised three methods, and the Tang system two; by the middle of the Song, these were consolidated into a single examination category. May we hear the details? Did these also share something of the principles underlying the Zhou practice of honoring worthy men as guests and advancing them? As for the system of evaluating officials, it compared the poorest and best performances to distinguish the quality of administration throughout the realm. The Han had six articles for reporting official business, and the Tang had nine grades for evaluating merit. The Song used seven…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
事考轉運提舉等官以九事考縣令其
詳可指言歟與成周大計之典亦有同
歟我
國家損益前代之制立為成法取士以科目
矣而或懼其無實察吏以考課矣而或
恐其失眞豈流弊固然耶則舍二法又
何為而可茲欲師虞周之意而參酌乎
漢唐宋之法必使士有眞才吏有實政
其道安在二三子志存用世必籌之審
===
矣願試言之無讓
問儒者之學必體用具備而後可稱全才
是故學術者其體也事功者其用也固
未有學術旣正而不足於事功亦未有
事功旣著而不本於學術者何三代而
下學術事功判為貳途也他未暇論且
以爾鄉之先哲言之自宋熙豐以來人
才始盛以理學名者則有若楊時游酢
李侗劉子翬朱熹蔡元定黃幹眞德秀
punctuated:
事考轉運提舉等官，以九事考縣令，其詳可指言歟？與成周大計之典亦有同歟？我國家損益前代之制，立為成法，取士以科目矣，而或懼其無實；察吏以考課矣，而或恐其失眞。豈流弊固然耶？則舍二法，又何為而可？茲欲師虞周之意，而參酌乎漢唐宋之法，必使士有眞才，吏有實政，其道安在？二三子志存用世，必籌之審矣，願試言之，無讓。

問：儒者之學，必體用具備，而後可稱全才。是故學術者，其體也；事功者，其用也。固未有學術旣正而不足於事功，亦未有事功旣著而不本於學術者。何三代而下，學術事功判為貳途也？他未暇論，且以爾鄉之先哲言之。自宋熙豐以來，人才始盛，以理學名者，則有若楊時、游酢、李侗、劉子翬、朱熹、蔡元定、黃幹、眞德秀
translation_en:
…criteria to evaluate officials such as Transport Commissioners and Superintendents, and nine criteria to evaluate District Magistrates. Can you explain these in detail? Were there also similarities to the comprehensive evaluation system of the Zhou? Our dynasty has modified the institutions of previous ages and established settled regulations. It recruits scholars through examinations, yet some fear that these lack substance; it scrutinizes officials through performance evaluations, yet some fear that these fail to reflect the truth. Are such abuses inevitable? Yet if we abandon these two methods, what workable alternative is there? We now wish to take as our model the intentions of Shun and the Zhou, while weighing the methods of the Han, Tang, and Song, so as to ensure that scholars possess genuine ability and officials achieve substantive results in government. How can this be accomplished? You gentlemen aspire to serve the world and must have considered this carefully. Please offer your views without reserve.

Question: A Confucian scholar’s learning must encompass both substance and application before he can be called a person of complete ability. Thus scholarly learning is its substance, and practical achievement its application. There has surely never been anyone whose learning was correct yet inadequate for practical achievement, nor anyone whose practical achievements were distinguished yet ungrounded in learning. Why, then, have learning and practical achievement diverged into two paths since the Three Dynasties? Leaving other matters aside for now, let us speak of the earlier worthies of your own region. From the Xining and Yuanfeng reign periods of the Song onward, men of talent began to flourish. Those renowned for the Learning of Principle included Yang Shi, You Zuo, Li Tong, Liu Zihui, Zhu Xi, Cai Yuanding, Huang Gan, and Zhen Dexiu…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
輩以功業顯者則有若李綱曾公亮蔡
襄鄭俠陳襄劉子羽呂祉劉韐輩其所
以仰希賢聖而裨益君民者可舉其實
而第言之歟迨至
聖朝才賢輩出有以理學名者有以事功顯者
芳聲不磨遺軌猶在此固長老之所習
聞而諸士所景仰焉者可歷指而言之
歟其言行勛勣與前代諸賢果相似歟
以理學名者果適於用以事功顯者果
===
不負所學歟諸士之所脩莫非諸儒之
學術他日出而效用必有事功表著其
可岐而為貳耶抑志向各殊遭逢亦異
而有不容强同者歟願詳著於篇以覘
尚友之學
問東南財賦西北戎馬乃自昔稱之矣我
明定鼎燕京與虜為鄰其於邊防尤慎且重內
則有十二團營外則列為九邊當是時
猛將材官雲興雷奮稱極盛矣顧其時
punctuated:
輩。以功業顯者，則有若李綱、曾公亮、蔡襄、鄭俠、陳襄、劉子羽、呂祉、劉韐輩。其所以仰希賢聖而裨益君民者，可舉其實而第言之歟？迨至聖朝，才賢輩出，有以理學名者，有以事功顯者，芳聲不磨，遺軌猶在。此固長老之所習聞，而諸士所景仰焉者，可歷指而言之歟？其言行勛勣，與前代諸賢果相似歟？以理學名者果適於用，以事功顯者果不負所學歟？諸士之所脩，莫非諸儒之學術。他日出而效用，必有事功表著，其可岐而為貳耶？抑志向各殊，遭逢亦異，而有不容强同者歟？願詳著於篇，以覘尚友之學。

問：東南財賦，西北戎馬，乃自昔稱之矣。我明定鼎燕京，與虜為鄰，其於邊防尤慎且重。內則有十二團營，外則列為九邊。當是時，猛將材官，雲興雷奮，稱極盛矣。顧其時
translation_en:
…and others. Those distinguished for their achievements include Li Gang, Zeng Gongliang, Cai Xiang, Zheng Xia, Chen Xiang, Liu Ziyu, Lü Zhi, Liu Ge, and others. Can you cite concrete instances of how they aspired to emulate the worthies and sages and benefited their rulers and people, and discuss them in order? Under our sagely dynasty, talented and worthy men have emerged in succession: some renowned for learning in the School of Principle, others distinguished for practical accomplishments. Their good reputations remain undiminished, and the examples they left endure. These are surely men of whom your elders have often heard and whom you candidates admire. Can you identify and discuss them one by one? Were their words, deeds, and achievements indeed comparable to those of the worthies of earlier dynasties? Were those renowned for learning in the School of Principle truly capable of putting it to use, and did those distinguished for practical accomplishments truly live up to their learning? What you candidates cultivate is none other than the learning of these Confucian scholars. When you enter service in the future and put your abilities to use, you will surely have conspicuous practical accomplishments. How, then, can learning and accomplishment be divided into two separate paths? Or do differences in aspirations and circumstances make it impossible to insist on uniformity? Set this out fully in your essays, so that we may discern your learning in taking the worthies of the past as friends.

Question: “The southeast supplies revenue; the northwest supplies troops and horses”—so it has been said since ancient times. Our Ming established its capital at Yanjing, with the barbarians as neighbors, and has therefore exercised particular care over frontier defense and attached great importance to it. Within are the twelve regimental camps; beyond are the nine frontier commands. At that time, fierce generals and able soldiers arose like clouds and sprang into action like thunder; military strength was said to have reached its height. Yet at that time…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
司徒所入不加於今而太倉之粟足支
數十年
內帑之銀積至千餘萬諸司所藏亦略稱是
猶且頻年用兵費用不貲當時未聞以
兵力財用詘乏爲憂而減租蠲稅之
詔且屢下焉馴至今日團營之兵縮其大半九
邊營戍東抽西補歲無定額卒遇警報
惟兢兢爲固守計未聞以數萬營陣待
敵者動諉諸兵食未贍何歟夫兵與食
===
===
相因者也兵不足則食宜有餘矣乃今
太倉之儲
內帑之積視昔益稱空乏其故何歟建議者
謂京師冗食太多宜如嘉靖初年故事
汰除一切冗役歲可省粟數十萬其說
果可行歟九邊惟宣大爲急舊時所藉
屯田鹽法其要也今屯田虜歲踐蹂民
無所得息鹽法自括餘銀商人鮮至邊
者卽至亦苦於得粟其在各鎮亦然目
punctuated: 司徒所入不加於今，而太倉之粟足支數十年，內帑之銀積至千餘萬，諸司所藏亦略稱是。猶且頻年用兵，費用不貲，當時未聞以兵力財用詘乏爲憂，而減租蠲稅之詔且屢下焉。馴至今日，團營之兵縮其大半，九邊營戍東抽西補，歲無定額。卒遇警報，惟兢兢爲固守計，未聞以數萬營陣待敵者，動諉諸兵食未贍，何歟？夫兵與食相因者也，兵不足則食宜有餘矣。乃今太倉之儲、內帑之積，視昔益稱空乏，其故何歟？建議者謂京師冗食太多，宜如嘉靖初年故事，汰除一切冗役，歲可省粟數十萬，其說果可行歟？九邊惟宣大爲急，舊時所藉，屯田、鹽法其要也。今屯田虜歲踐蹂，民無所得息；鹽法自括餘銀，商人鮮至邊者，卽至亦苦於得粟，其在各鎮亦然。目
translation_en:
…the revenues received by the Minister of Revenue were no greater than today, yet the grain in the Imperial Granary sufficed for several decades, the silver accumulated in the palace treasury amounted to more than ten million taels, and the stores held by the various offices were likewise roughly commensurate. Moreover, military campaigns were conducted year after year at immense expense. Yet at that time one heard no concern about shortages of military strength or financial resources, and edicts reducing land taxes and remitting other taxes were repeatedly issued.

Gradually, matters have reached their present state: the troops of the combined training camps have been reduced by more than half, while garrison troops along the Nine Frontiers are withdrawn from one place to make up shortages elsewhere, with no fixed annual complement. When an alarm suddenly comes, they anxiously plan only to hold their positions securely; one hears of none deploying tens of thousands in camps and battle formations to await the enemy. At every turn they plead insufficient troops and provisions. Why is this? Troops and provisions are mutually dependent. If troops are insufficient, provisions ought to be abundant. Yet the reserves in the Imperial Granary and the accumulations in the palace treasury are now all the more depleted compared with the past. What is the reason?

Those offering proposals say that too many superfluous personnel are supported in the capital. They urge following the precedent of the early Jiajing years by eliminating all unnecessary service posts, thereby saving several hundred thousand units of grain annually. Can this proposal really be put into practice?

Among the Nine Frontiers, Xuanfu and Datong face the most pressing needs. Of the resources on which they formerly relied, military agricultural colonies and the salt administration were the most important. Now the enemy tramples the colony lands every year, leaving the people unable to obtain any yield. Since the collection of surplus silver under the salt system began, few merchants have come to the frontier; even those who do come find it difficult to obtain grain. The situation is the same in each of the frontier commands. At present…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
前支持惟有
請討而已此坐困之術也不知此外有何長策
可采而行之歟諸士志抱先憂久矣願
盡言之以觀經世之術
punctuated: 前支持惟有請討而已，此坐困之術也。不知此外有何長策可采而行之歟？諸士志抱先憂久矣，願盡言之，以觀經世之術。
translation_en: …at present, keeping things going depends solely on requesting funds. This is a course that leads only to helpless impoverishment. What other long-term strategies might be adopted and put into practice? You gentlemen have long cherished the resolve to take thought for the realm’s troubles before others do. Please set forth your views fully, so that we may assess your understanding of statecraft.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
法語之言能無從乎改之爲貴巽與之言
能無說乎繹之爲貴
張履祥
同考試官教諭吳批發聖人立教之意殆盡而其
詞醇雅足爲多士式錄之
同考試官教授何批體製渾融文詞清逸雖不逞
才華而蔚然之光自莫可遏佳士佳士
===
考試官教授吳批意精詞粹宜錄以式
考試官教授李批文之順理者取之
聖人兩舉聽言之道在能自得於言也夫言足
以感人言之善者也使非改之繹之則亦何得
於言哉且夫君子能爲可用之言而不能必人
之用其言是在聽言者之自擇耳何者君子不
欲阿徇以爲容則凡過失相規不有法言乎言
而本之法則其論正其旨嚴侃侃然指陳之無
隱聽之者將憚於理之不可易而窮於說之無
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

法語之言，能無從乎？改之爲貴。巽與之言，能無說乎？繹之爲貴。

張履祥

同考試官教諭吳批：發聖人立教之意殆盡，而其詞醇雅，足爲多士式，錄之。

同考試官教授何批：體製渾融，文詞清逸，雖不逞才華，而蔚然之光自莫可遏。佳士！佳士！

考試官教授吳批：意精詞粹，宜錄以式。

考試官教授李批：文之順理者，取之。

聖人兩舉聽言之道，在能自得於言也。夫言足以感人，言之善者也；使非改之繹之，則亦何得於言哉？且夫君子能爲可用之言，而不能必人之用其言，是在聽言者之自擇耳。何者？君子不欲阿徇以爲容，則凡過失相規，不有法言乎？言而本之法，則其論正，其旨嚴，侃侃然指陳之無隱。聽之者將憚於理之不可易，而窮於說之無
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Can one fail to assent to words of principled admonition? What matters is reforming oneself. Can one fail to take pleasure in gentle, accommodating words? What matters is drawing out their meaning.”

Zhang Lüxiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: This brings out almost completely the sage’s intention in establishing his teaching. Its language is pure and elegant, sufficient to serve as a model for the candidates. Include it.

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Professor: Its structure is thoroughly integrated, and its language lucid and untrammeled. Although it does not flaunt literary talent, its abundant brilliance cannot be suppressed. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: Its ideas are refined and its language pure. It should be included as a model.

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: This essay accords with principle. Select it.

The sage sets forth two ways of listening to words; their point lies in one’s ability to gain a personal understanding through those words. Words capable of moving people are good words. Yet unless one reforms oneself and draws out their meaning, what does one actually gain from them? Moreover, the gentleman can offer words that may be put to use, but he cannot ensure that others will put his words to use. That rests solely with the listener’s own choice. Why is this? The gentleman does not wish to win acceptance through flattery and compliance. Thus, when people admonish one another concerning their faults, are there not words grounded in proper standards? When speech is based on such standards, its reasoning is upright and its purport stern; it forthrightly points matters out without concealment. Those who hear it will stand in awe of reasoning that cannot be altered and find that their excuses offer no …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
所逃固未有拒而不從者然從特一時之感未
必能守之於爲也故必懲已往之愆而釋回以
增美求方來之益而舍舊以圖新則從之者非
面從而語之者匪虛語過失將自此而日寡矣
此所以改爲貴也夫從貴於改則以法言進者
豈徒望其能從已耶君子不欲激抗以爲直則
凡德業相勸不有巽言乎言而出之巽則其辭
婉其義微誾誾然開導之有方聽之者將動於
理之有可喻而喜於情之無所拂固未有逆而
===
不悅者然悅特一念之明未必能誠之於思也
故必因辭以逆意而反覆於思惟由顯以通微
而沉潛於念慮則悅之者誠心悅而言之者非
失言德業將自此而日進矣此所以繹爲貴也
夫悅貴於繹則以巽言進者豈徒望其能悅已
耶吁夫子斯言其所望於善學者良深切矣抑
因是而可以明獻納焉聖如舜禹宜無過可改
無善可加者然猶察邇言而用中聞昌言而必
拜非誠有得於改且繹乎以是知君子之學不
punctuated: 所逃，固未有拒而不從者。然從特一時之感，未必能守之於爲也。故必懲已往之愆，而釋回以增美；求方來之益，而舍舊以圖新。則從之者非面從，而語之者匪虛語，過失將自此而日寡矣。此所以改爲貴也。夫從貴於改，則以法言進者，豈徒望其能從已耶？君子不欲激抗以爲直，則凡德業相勸，不有巽言乎？言而出之巽，則其辭婉，其義微，誾誾然開導之有方。聽之者將動於理之有可喻，而喜於情之無所拂，固未有逆而不悅者。然悅特一念之明，未必能誠之於思也。故必因辭以逆意，而反覆於思惟；由顯以通微，而沉潛於念慮。則悅之者誠心悅，而言之者非失言，德業將自此而日進矣。此所以繹爲貴也。夫悅貴於繹，則以巽言進者，豈徒望其能悅已耶？吁！夫子斯言，其所望於善學者良深切矣。抑因是而可以明獻納焉。聖如舜禹，宜無過可改、無善可加者，然猶察邇言而用中，聞昌言而必拜，非誠有得於改且繹乎？以是知君子之學不
translation_en:
…any escape, so surely no one would reject such words and refuse to follow them. Yet compliance is merely a momentary response; one may not necessarily sustain it in practice. Thus one must take warning from past faults, abandon perversity to increase one's goodness, seek benefit in what lies ahead, and relinquish old ways to pursue renewal. Then those who comply will not merely comply outwardly, and those who offer advice will not have spoken in vain. Faults will thereafter diminish day by day. This is why reform is prized. If reform is what makes compliance valuable, can those who offer words grounded in proper standards hope merely that others will comply with them?

The gentleman does not seek to appear upright through vehemence and defiance. Thus, in encouraging others in virtue and accomplishment, does he not use gentle words? When words are expressed gently, their phrasing is tactful and their meaning subtle; with courteous candor, he guides others skillfully. Listeners will be moved by principles they can understand and pleased that their feelings encounter no affront. Surely none will resist and fail to take pleasure in them. Yet pleasure is merely the illumination of a single thought; one may not necessarily make it sincere in one's reflections. Thus one must infer the intention from the words and ponder it repeatedly, proceeding from the evident to comprehend the subtle and dwelling deeply upon it in thought. Then those who take pleasure will do so sincerely, and those who speak will not have wasted their words. Virtue and accomplishment will thereafter advance day by day. This is why thoughtful examination is prized. If thoughtful examination is what makes pleasure valuable, can those who offer gentle words hope merely that others will be pleased with them?

Ah! In these words, the Master's expectations of those who learn well are indeed profound and earnest. From this we may also understand the presentation of counsel to the ruler. Sages such as Shun and Yu might be thought to have had no faults to reform and no goodness to add. Yet Shun still examined the words of ordinary people and applied the mean, while Yu invariably bowed upon hearing excellent counsel. Did they not truly gain something through reform and thoughtful examination? From this we know that in the gentleman's learning, it is not…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
難於無過而難於改過不貴於用一己之長而
貴於有以來天下之善此固夫子惓惓之餘意
也有聽言之責者當自得之
齊明盛服非禮不動所以脩身也
方沆
同考試官教諭伍批語意俊潔而渾成條理疏
暢而精密帝王慎脩之學闡明殆盡
同考試官教諭張批提掇精貫該括詳明文之
邃理者也取之
===
考試官教授吳批發脩身意瑩徹錄之
考試官教授李批詞理俱到
人君端本之道大居敬而已矣夫敬聖學之要
也此身無不敬而慎脩之能事畢矣茲非九經
之首務乎宜孔子舉以告魯君也意謂人君一
身為天下國家之本必脩身而後道立是身固
不可不脩矣而脩之宜何如是故有所以主此
身者必齊戒以潔其內操虛靈於不昧而常明
常覺不懈乎存養之功有所以章此身者必盛
punctuated:
難於無過，而難於改過；不貴於用一己之長，而貴於有以來天下之善。此固夫子惓惓之餘意也。有聽言之責者，當自得之。

齊明盛服，非禮不動，所以脩身也。
方沆。
同考試官教諭伍批：語意俊潔而渾成，條理疏暢而精密，帝王慎脩之學，闡明殆盡。
同考試官教諭張批：提掇精貫，該括詳明，文之邃理者也，取之。
考試官教授吳批：發脩身意瑩徹，錄之。
考試官教授李批：詞理俱到。

人君端本之道，大居敬而已矣。夫敬，聖學之要也。此身無不敬，而慎脩之能事畢矣。茲非九經之首務乎？宜孔子舉以告魯君也。意謂人君一身，為天下國家之本，必脩身而後道立，是身固不可不脩矣。而脩之宜何如？是故有所以主此身者，必齊戒以潔其內，操虛靈於不昧，而常明常覺，不懈乎存養之功。有所以章此身者，必盛
translation_en:
…the difficulty lies in correcting faults, rather than in having none; what is prized is the ability to draw upon the goodness of all under Heaven, rather than the use of one’s own strengths. This, indeed, is the further meaning of the Master’s earnest concern. Those responsible for listening to counsel should grasp it for themselves.

“Purifying oneself, maintaining clarity, wearing full ceremonial dress, and making no movement contrary to ritual propriety: these are the means of cultivating oneself.”
By Fang Hang.

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “The language and meaning are elegant and clear, yet form an integrated whole. The organization is lucid and fluent, yet precise and close-knit. The learning through which emperors and kings cultivate themselves with care is elucidated almost exhaustively.”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Its exposition is refined and coherent, its coverage comprehensive and clear. This is writing that penetrates deeply into principle. Accept it.”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “It develops the meaning of self-cultivation with crystalline clarity. Admit it.”
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.”

The ruler’s way of rectifying the root lies chiefly in abiding in reverence. Reverence is the essential point of sagely learning. When nothing in one’s person lacks reverence, all that careful self-cultivation can accomplish is fulfilled. Is this not the foremost task among the nine guiding principles? It was fitting that Confucius should have raised it in instructing the ruler of Lu. His meaning was that the ruler’s own person is the root of all under Heaven, of the state, and of the family. Only after he cultivates himself can the Way be established; thus his person certainly cannot go uncultivated. But how should he cultivate it? Accordingly, to govern his own person, he must purify himself through fasting and abstinence, cleansing his inner being. He must keep his receptive spiritual awareness unobscured, remaining constantly clear and alert, never slackening in the work of preserving and nourishing it. To give outward distinction to his person, he must wear full ceremonial…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
服以飾其外肅瞻視於罔愆而可畏可象不褻
夫尊臨之體自其内無逸志而協以中正之規
則以禮制心有一念之不合於禮者不以動於
内也自其外無惰容而約以節文之度則以禮
制事有一事之不協於禮者不以動於外也若
此者非所以脩身乎蓋脩身以道而道合内外
者也故内外兼持正以納此身於軌物而善元
良之則脩己以敬而敬貫動靜者也故動靜交
養正以約此身於範圍而清化理之原篤恭不
===
顯惟皇之建極以貞所以脩德而行道者吾身
無餘功矣術豈多乎哉端拱無為惟后之綏猷
以定所以取人而立政者吾身有常度矣道豈
遠乎哉是則一敬立而文武之心法已全故一
身脩而文武之治法可舉矣公欲憲章文武其
尚知所先務乎且魯公一國之君也孔子告之
政猶必本諸身况天子一身與天地參而日月
竝百官萬民式焉脩之可不敬乎故記載朝廷
燕處行步升車各有禮度豈非以敬之為道無
punctuated: 服以飾其外，肅瞻視於罔愆，而可畏可象，不褻夫尊臨之體。自其内無逸志，而協以中正之規，則以禮制心，有一念之不合於禮者，不以動於内也；自其外無惰容，而約以節文之度，則以禮制事，有一事之不協於禮者，不以動於外也。若此者，非所以脩身乎？蓋脩身以道，而道合内外者也，故内外兼持，正以納此身於軌物，而善元良之則；脩己以敬，而敬貫動靜者也，故動靜交養，正以約此身於範圍，而清化理之原。篤恭不顯，惟皇之建極以貞，所以脩德而行道者，吾身無餘功矣，術豈多乎哉？端拱無為，惟后之綏猷以定，所以取人而立政者，吾身有常度矣，道豈遠乎哉？是則一敬立，而文武之心法已全，故一身脩，而文武之治法可舉矣。公欲憲章文武，其尚知所先務乎？且魯公，一國之君也，孔子告之政，猶必本諸身；况天子一身，與天地參而日月竝，百官萬民式焉，脩之可不敬乎？故記載朝廷、燕處、行步、升車，各有禮度，豈非以敬之為道無
translation_en:
…robes to adorn his outward appearance, making his gaze solemn and free of fault, so that he inspires awe and serves as an example, never debasing the dignity with which he presides over others. Inwardly, he harbors no idle intentions and accords with the standards of centrality and correctness: thus he regulates his mind through ritual propriety, allowing no thought inconsistent with it to stir within. Outwardly, he displays no indolence and restrains himself according to the measured forms of ritual: thus he regulates affairs through ritual propriety, allowing no action inconsistent with it to manifest without. Is this not the means of cultivating oneself?

Self-cultivation proceeds through the Way, and the Way unites the inner and the outer. Therefore, maintaining both together serves precisely to bring oneself within proper standards and perfect the model of sovereign excellence. One cultivates oneself through reverence, and reverence pervades activity and stillness. Therefore, nurturing oneself in both serves precisely to keep oneself within due bounds and purify the source of moral transformation and good government. Profoundly reverent without outward display, the sovereign establishes the supreme standard and thereby makes things correct. In cultivating virtue and practicing the Way, no further work remains for me to perform upon myself. Can the methods really be many? With hands folded, governing without intervention, the ruler brings his plans to settled order. In selecting men and establishing government, I possess in my own person an enduring standard. Can the Way really be distant?

Thus, once reverence is established, the entire teaching of Kings Wen and Wu concerning the mind is already present; once the ruler's person is cultivated, their methods of government can be put into practice. If you, my lord, wish to take Kings Wen and Wu as your models, surely you should recognize what must come first?

Moreover, the Duke of Lu was the ruler of a single state, yet when Kongzi instructed him about government, he still insisted that it be rooted in his own person. How much more does this apply to the Son of Heaven, whose person stands alongside Heaven and Earth and ranks with the sun and moon, and whom all officials and the myriad people take as their model! Can he cultivate himself without reverence? Hence the ritual records prescribe appropriate measures for conduct at court, in private repose, when walking, and when mounting a carriage. Is this not because, in the way of reverence, there is no…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
微可忽而帝王之所以正百官正萬民者恒必
由之也噫孔子之愛君其至矣哉
原泉混混不舍晝夜盈科而後進放乎四
海有本者如是是之取爾
陳公相
同考試官教諭劉批造理淵源行文活潑豈涵
泳聖教而有得者耶錄之
同考試官教諭鄭批不費詞說曲盡本直如風
行水上自然成文有養之士也
===
考試官教授吳批詞氣冲澹理趣淵涵
考試官教授李批得聖人重本之思
大賢原聖人取水之意示人以務本之學也蓋
水惟有本故能不已而漸歸於海也聖人以此
取之可以見本之當務矣昔孟子因徐子之問
而告之若曰天下之道寓於物者流行之迹而
根於心者統會之源仲尼以心觀物而獨有取
於水者其有感於水之道乎今夫流水之爲物
也發端於原泉而泉之始達吾見其混混焉往
punctuated:
微可忽，而帝王之所以正百官、正萬民者，恒必由之也。噫！孔子之愛君，其至矣哉！

「原泉混混，不舍晝夜，盈科而後進，放乎四海。有本者如是，是之取爾。」
陳公相

同考試官教諭劉批：「造理淵源，行文活潑，豈涵泳聖教而有得者耶？錄之。」
同考試官教諭鄭批：「不費詞說，曲盡本直，如風行水上，自然成文，有養之士也。」
考試官教授吳批：「詞氣冲澹，理趣淵涵。」
考試官教授李批：「得聖人重本之思。」

大賢原聖人取水之意，示人以務本之學也。蓋水惟有本，故能不已而漸歸於海也。聖人以此取之，可以見本之當務矣。昔孟子因徐子之問而告之，若曰：天下之道，寓於物者，流行之迹；而根於心者，統會之源。仲尼以心觀物，而獨有取於水者，其有感於水之道乎？今夫流水之爲物也，發端於原泉，而泉之始達，吾見其混混焉，往
translation_en:
…nothing, however minute, may be neglected, and this is invariably the means by which emperors and kings must set right the hundred officials and the myriad people. Ah! How profound was Confucius’s solicitude for his ruler!

“Water from a source wells up abundantly, never ceasing day or night. It fills each hollow before advancing and flows onward to the four seas. Such is what has a source; this alone is what he prized.”
By Chen Gongxiang.

Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “His exploration of principle reaches its deepest sources, and his writing is lively and fluent. Might he be one who has immersed himself in the sage’s teachings and gained insight from them? Select this essay.”
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Without elaborate exposition, he fully brings out every aspect of the fundamental meaning [?]. Like wind moving over water, his writing forms its patterns naturally. He is a scholar of cultivation.”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “His diction and tone are serene and restrained; his understanding of principle is deep and ample.”
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “He grasps the sage’s concern for the root.”

The great worthy traced the sage’s intention in prizing water, showing people a learning devoted to attending to the root. It is precisely because water has a source that it can flow unceasingly and gradually make its way to the sea. That the sage prized it for this reason shows us that the root must be our concern. In former times, Mencius responded to Xuzi’s question, telling him, in effect: The Way of all under Heaven, as embodied in things, manifests itself in the traces of its flowing activity; as rooted in the mind, it is the source that unifies and brings all together. When Zhongni observed things through his mind and singled out water for appreciation, was he not moved by the Way exemplified in water? Now, flowing water begins at a spring, and when the spring first issues forth, I see it welling up abundantly, flowing away…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
過來續其出不窮而自晝及夜無一息之或停
坎止流行其進不驟而足此通彼至四海而後
已是充周莫禦者其流也而所以行其流者則
靜深而不可測夫是以莫遠於海而其勢必至
焉推行有漸者其委也而所以資其委者則渾
淪而不可窮夫是以莫大於海而其機必達焉
是水之有本如此而仲尼之取之也非以其本
哉蓋淵泉之理渾涵於聖心者常體物而不遺
故川流之化昭著於物象者自因心而有感在
===
川之嘆非特玩其流也遡流以窮源殆有獨觀
其深者焉是以稱之數耳臨河之美非特徇其
委也因委以求端殆有默契其本者焉是以取
之亟耳吁觀水之放乎海也始於有本則知學
之造其極也必先於務本矣本者何心而已聖
人之心一理渾然而措諸事業至於位天地育
萬物無所施而不可者皆此心之妙用也學者
欲求至乎聖人豈必求諸此心之外哉孟子甞
言心勿忘勿助長矣勿忘者猶水之不已也勿
punctuated: 過來續，其出不窮，而自晝及夜，無一息之或停。坎止流行，其進不驟，而足此通彼，至四海而後已。是充周莫禦者，其流也；而所以行其流者，則靜深而不可測。夫是以莫遠於海，而其勢必至焉。推行有漸者，其委也；而所以資其委者，則渾淪而不可窮。夫是以莫大於海，而其機必達焉。是水之有本如此，而仲尼之取之也，非以其本哉？蓋淵泉之理，渾涵於聖心者，常體物而不遺；故川流之化，昭著於物象者，自因心而有感。在川之嘆，非特玩其流也；遡流以窮源，殆有獨觀其深者焉，是以稱之數耳。臨河之美，非特徇其委也；因委以求端，殆有默契其本者焉，是以取之亟耳。吁！觀水之放乎海也，始於有本，則知學之造其極也，必先於務本矣。本者何？心而已。聖人之心，一理渾然，而措諸事業，至於位天地、育萬物，無所施而不可者，皆此心之妙用也。學者欲求至乎聖人，豈必求諸此心之外哉？孟子甞言心勿忘勿助長矣。勿忘者，猶水之不已也；勿
translation_en:
…what passes is succeeded by what comes; its outflow is inexhaustible, and from day into night it never stops for even a moment. It rests in hollows and flows onward; its advance is never precipitate. Filling one place, it passes into the next, stopping only when it reaches the Four Seas. What spreads everywhere and cannot be checked is its flow; yet that which sets its flow in motion is still, deep, and unfathomable. Thus, though nothing is more distant than the sea, its momentum inevitably carries it there. What advances by degrees is its downstream course; yet that which supplies this course is an undivided fullness that cannot be exhausted. Thus, though nothing is greater than the sea, its motive power inevitably reaches it. Such is the rootedness of water: was it not for this root that Zhongni valued it? The principle of the deep spring, fully contained within the sage’s mind, invariably embodies all things without omission. Hence the transformations of the flowing river, manifest in the forms of things, naturally stir a response in his mind. His sigh beside the stream was more than an appreciation of its flow. Following the current back to its source, he must have discerned its depths as he alone could; this is why he spoke of it so often. His praise beside the river was more than attention to its downstream course. Seeking its beginning through its course, he must have silently apprehended its root; this is why he repeatedly drew upon it.

Ah! Observing that water’s discharge into the sea begins with its possession of a source, we know that learning’s attainment of its ultimate goal must begin with attention to the root. What is this root? The mind, and nothing more. In the sage’s mind, the single principle forms an undivided whole. When put into practice in affairs and undertakings, it extends even to settling Heaven and Earth in their proper places and nurturing the myriad things. That it can be applied everywhere without failing is entirely the wondrous functioning of this mind. If learners wish to attain sagehood, why should they seek beyond this mind? Mengzi once spoke of neither forgetting in the mind nor helping growth along. Not forgetting is like water’s never ceasing; not…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
助者猶水之有漸也是皆所以善事吾心而學
爲聖人者也反是則義襲而取之所謂聲聞過
情者矣孰謂孟子斯言獨因徐子而發哉
易
允升大吉上合志也
李維岳
同考試官教諭張批此題作者多以詞勝易入
於庸是篇詞不費而意已躍如殆得諸心解矣
同考試官教諭吳批二陽合志以初六能巽而
===
然此作得本旨而詞復明潔佳士也
考試官教授吳批體認精切有味
考試官教授李批莊重簡潔易藝之粹也
初爻獲升之善由見孚於同志也夫君子不爲
苟合惟其志之同而已初爻以之其獲升之善
也宜哉小象之意若謂君子之致身也能爲可
進而不能使其身之必進其立志也能爲可合
而不能使其人之皆合惟升之初六秉和順之
德而適際乎大道爲公之時蘊康濟之猷而幸
punctuated:
助者，猶水之有漸也。是皆所以善事吾心而學爲聖人者也。反是，則義襲而取之，所謂聲聞過情者矣。孰謂孟子斯言獨因徐子而發哉？

易
允升，大吉，上合志也。
李維岳

同考試官教諭張批：此題作者多以詞勝，易入於庸。是篇詞不費而意已躍如，殆得諸心解矣。
同考試官教諭吳批：二陽合志，以初六能巽而然。此作得本旨，而詞復明潔，佳士也。
考試官教授吳批：體認精切，有味。
考試官教授李批：莊重簡潔，易藝之粹也。

初爻獲升之善，由見孚於同志也。夫君子不爲苟合，惟其志之同而已。初爻以之，其獲升之善也宜哉！小象之意，若謂君子之致身也，能爲可進，而不能使其身之必進；其立志也，能爲可合，而不能使其人之皆合。惟升之初六，秉和順之德，而適際乎大道爲公之時；蘊康濟之猷，而幸
translation_en:
…not forcing growth resembles water’s gradual progress. These are all ways to tend our hearts well and learn to become sages. To do the reverse is to seize upon righteousness through isolated acts—the condition described as having a reputation that exceeds the reality. Who would say that these words of Mengzi were spoken solely on account of Master Xu?

Book of Changes
“Trusted in ascending: great good fortune. Those above share his purpose.”
Li Weiyue

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Most writers on this topic seek to excel through their language and readily lapse into the commonplace. This essay uses words sparingly, yet its meaning already stands vividly forth. It seems to derive from an understanding gained within the heart.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: The two yang lines share its purpose because the initial six can be yielding. This composition grasps the fundamental meaning, and its language is also clear and clean. Its author is an excellent scholar.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: His apprehension is precise and penetrating, and rewards reflection.

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: Dignified, concise, and clear: the finest kind of examination essay on the Book of Changes.

The first line obtains the benefit of ascending because it enjoys the trust of those who share its purpose. The gentleman does not seek agreement indiscriminately; he seeks only a shared purpose. The first line acts on this principle, so it is fitting that it should obtain the benefit of ascending! The meaning of the Lesser Image Commentary seems to be this: in advancing himself, the gentleman can make himself worthy of promotion, but cannot ensure that he will actually be promoted; in establishing his purpose, he can make it worthy of others’ agreement, but cannot ensure that everyone will agree with him. The initial six of Ascending possesses the virtues of harmony and compliance, and happens to encounter a time when the Great Way serves the common good. It harbors plans to bring peace and succor to the people, and fortunately…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
逢乎明良喜起之會其晉也莫或摧之而尚往
卽遇其主焉可以熈帝之載也其行也莫或尼
之而南征卽得其朋焉可以達吾之道也信乎
能升而大吉矣若是者豈偶然哉蓋二陽在上
方虛懷以引賢而初六始升能委身以從事上
焉爲德二陽之志則然也初則順以承之而所
以資其啟沃之忠者無弗合焉下焉爲民二陽
之志則然也初則巽以行之而思以賛乎阜成
之化者無弗合焉是其同道爲朋則相信益深
===
而其引之也必力置之左右而不以爲比也同
心共濟則相與益篤而其推之也恐後躋於大
僚而不以爲驟也是則初之所以能升者不惟
其時惟同志焉耳彼無因而干進苟合以取容
者可不戒哉雖然志可合也不可比也當升之
時上有貞吉之君下有升虛邑利用禴之相上
下相孚而德業成故君子樂於自效而以道爲
合九官十二牧師師濟濟之風可想見矣後世
彈冠結綬私相慶幸者比焉耳豈知升之義哉
punctuated: 逢乎明良喜起之會。其晉也，莫或摧之，而尚往卽遇其主焉，可以熈帝之載也；其行也，莫或尼之，而南征卽得其朋焉，可以達吾之道也。信乎能升而大吉矣！若是者，豈偶然哉？蓋二陽在上，方虛懷以引賢，而初六始升，能委身以從事。上焉爲德，二陽之志則然也，初則順以承之，而所以資其啟沃之忠者，無弗合焉；下焉爲民，二陽之志則然也，初則巽以行之，而思以賛乎阜成之化者，無弗合焉。是其同道爲朋，則相信益深，而其引之也必力，置之左右而不以爲比也；同心共濟，則相與益篤，而其推之也恐後，躋於大僚而不以爲驟也。是則初之所以能升者，不惟其時，惟同志焉耳。彼無因而干進、苟合以取容者，可不戒哉？雖然，志可合也，不可比也。當升之時，上有貞吉之君，下有升虛邑、利用禴之相，上下相孚而德業成，故君子樂於自效，而以道爲合。九官十二牧，師師濟濟之風，可想見矣。後世彈冠結綬、私相慶幸者，比焉耳，豈知升之義哉？
translation_en:
…to encounter a time when an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers joyfully rouse one another to action. In his advancement, none obstructs him; proceeding upward, he meets his lord and can bring lustre to the sovereign’s undertakings. In his progress, none impedes him; journeying south, he finds companions and can put his Way into practice. Truly, he can ascend and enjoy great good fortune! Could this be merely accidental?

The two yang lines above are opening their minds to welcome worthy men, while the initial six, beginning its ascent, can devote itself to service. In relation to those above, their purpose is to cultivate virtue: such is the intent of the two yang lines. The initial line compliantly supports them, and all that it contributes to their loyal efforts to enlighten and nourish the ruler’s mind accords with that intent. In relation to those below, their purpose is to serve the people: such is the intent of the two yang lines. The initial line acts with deference, and all its plans to assist the transforming influence that brings prosperity and fulfilment accord with that intent. Sharing the same Way as companions, they trust one another ever more deeply. They therefore exert themselves fully to bring him forward, placing him at their side without considering this factional favouritism. United in purpose and working together toward success, they support one another ever more firmly. They therefore promote him with an eagerness that fears falling behind, raising him to high office without considering his advancement precipitous. Thus, what enables the initial line to ascend is not merely the occasion, but shared purpose. Should those who seek advancement without grounds and compromise themselves to win acceptance not take warning?

Nevertheless, purposes may be united, but must not become factional. At the time of Ascending, above there is a ruler whose constancy brings good fortune; below there are ministers represented by ‘ascending into an empty city’ and ‘it is beneficial to offer the yue sacrifice.’ Those above and below trust one another, and achievements in virtue and governance are accomplished. Thus the gentleman gladly offers his services and makes the Way the basis of his association with others. We can imagine the spirit of the nine officials and twelve regional governors, learning from one another in dignified harmony. Those in later ages who dust off their official caps and tie on their seal cords, privately congratulating one another on their good fortune, are merely forming factions. How could they understand the meaning of Ascending?

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
是故君子慎所以爲合
黄帝堯舜氏作通其變使民不倦神而化
之使民宜之易窮則變變則通通則久
是以自天祐之吉无不利黄帝堯舜垂
衣裳而天下治蓋取諸乾坤
莊敦義
同考試官教諭張批聖人神化與易道天道通
貫只一理此作深會其㫖宜錄以式
同考試官教諭吳批有融會有體裁三聖以經
===
法天此作能洩其秘亦化於文者矣
考試官教授吳批帝治無爲披文想見
考試官教授李批說理之文意象宛然
大傳詳言三聖因時以順治而明其取諸易焉
甚矣聖人不能違時也三聖所以因時而達之
治者非有取於乾坤哉大傳論制器尚象之事
至此若曰昔者聖王之繼世以出治也不先天
以開人各因時而立政是故黄帝堯舜嘗繼神
農氏而王矣於斯時也聖人知民情之趨不可
punctuated:
是故君子慎所以爲合。

黄帝、堯、舜氏作，通其變，使民不倦；神而化之，使民宜之。易，窮則變，變則通，通則久。是以「自天祐之，吉无不利」。黄帝、堯、舜垂衣裳而天下治，蓋取諸乾坤。

莊敦義

同考試官教諭張批：「聖人神化與易道、天道通貫，只一理。此作深會其㫖，宜錄以式。」

同考試官教諭吳批：「有融會，有體裁。三聖以經法天，此作能洩其秘，亦化於文者矣。」

考試官教授吳批：「帝治無爲，披文想見。」

考試官教授李批：「說理之文，意象宛然。」

大傳詳言三聖因時以順治，而明其取諸易焉。甚矣，聖人不能違時也！三聖所以因時而達之治者，非有取於乾坤哉？大傳論制器尚象之事，至此若曰：昔者聖王之繼世以出治也，不先天以開人，各因時而立政。是故黄帝、堯、舜嘗繼神農氏而王矣。於斯時也，聖人知民情之趨不可
translation_en:
…Thus the gentleman is careful about the basis on which he joins with others.

The Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun arose. They carried changes through, so that the people did not grow weary; they transformed them with spiritlike efficacy, so that the people found their circumstances fitting. In the Changes, when a course reaches its limit, it changes; through change it finds passage; through passage it endures. Thus, “Heaven itself assists him: good fortune, with nothing unfavorable.” The Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun let their robes hang down, and all under Heaven was well governed. They presumably took this from Qian and Kun.

Zhuang Dunyi

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “The sages’ spiritlike transformation, the Way of the Changes, and the Way of Heaven are connected throughout by a single principle. This composition deeply grasps that meaning and should be included as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “It displays both integrated understanding and appropriate literary form. The three sages used the Classic to model themselves on Heaven [?]. This composition reveals their secret; its author, too, has attained transformative mastery in writing.”

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: “The emperors governed through nonaction. Reading this composition, one can envision it.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “A composition expounding principle, with vividly realized ideas and images.”

The Great Commentary explains in detail how the three sages followed the times to achieve harmonious government, making clear that they drew upon the Changes. How utterly impossible it is for sages to go against the times! Was it not from Qian and Kun that the three sages drew the means to follow the times and attain good government? In discussing the making of implements with regard for the images, the Great Commentary seems at this point to say: In antiquity, when sage kings succeeded one another and brought forth good government, they did not anticipate Heaven in enlightening the people; each established his administration in accordance with the times. Thus the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun succeeded Shennong as rulers. At that time, the sages knew that, given the direction of the people’s dispositions, it was impossible to…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
以襲故也於是化裁以達變而更之以維新之
治使民之變易以趨時者自鼓舞之不倦焉知
通變之術非所以强世也於是順化以宜民而
運之以自然之神使民之樂生而興行者自相
率以與能焉是理也本諸易者也易無終窮而
變以繼之是以推之卽準而可通也傳之無弊
而可久也雖聖人亦不能違乎易矣是道也合
於天者也天有顯道而順者佑之是以法天而
行動罔不吉也承天而治用無不利也雖天亦
===
不能違乎聖人矣然則黃帝堯舜夫何爲哉中
正爲觀但見其章之黼黻而已矣而民自喻於
不言之化恭默思治但見其示之法服而已矣
而世自底於從欲之風若此者寧非有取於乾
坤巳乎蓋無心而成化者乾坤所以妙乎物而
物不自知其爲功有心而無爲者聖人所以利
乎民而民不自知其爲利使聖人日斤斤然求
天下之變而更之則其神易息其化易窮而與
天地不相似矣嗟乎非三聖其孰能之雖然黃
punctuated: 以襲故也。於是化裁以達變，而更之以維新之治，使民之變易以趨時者，自鼓舞之不倦焉。知通變之術非所以强世也，於是順化以宜民，而運之以自然之神，使民之樂生而興行者，自相率以與能焉。是理也，本諸易者也。易無終窮，而變以繼之，是以推之卽準而可通也，傳之無弊而可久也。雖聖人亦不能違乎易矣。是道也，合於天者也。天有顯道，而順者佑之，是以法天而行，動罔不吉也；承天而治，用無不利也。雖天亦不能違乎聖人矣。然則黃帝堯舜夫何爲哉？中正爲觀，但見其章之黼黻而已矣，而民自喻於不言之化；恭默思治，但見其示之法服而已矣，而世自底於從欲之風。若此者，寧非有取於乾坤巳乎？蓋無心而成化者，乾坤所以妙乎物，而物不自知其爲功；有心而無爲者，聖人所以利乎民，而民不自知其爲利。使聖人日斤斤然求天下之變而更之，則其神易息，其化易窮，而與天地不相似矣。嗟乎！非三聖，其孰能之？雖然，黃
translation_en:
…to perpetuate the old ways. They therefore adapted and regulated things to accommodate change, replacing the old with a renewed order of government, so that the people, changing to keep pace with the times, were themselves inspired to unflagging activity. They knew that the art of accommodating change was not a means of coercing the world. Thus they followed the course of transformation to suit the people and directed it with the subtle efficacy of spontaneity, so that the people, delighting in life and rousing themselves to action, led one another to exercise their abilities.

This principle was rooted in the Book of Changes. Change has no final limit: transformation continues it. Thus, when applied, it accords with the proper standard and can operate freely; when transmitted, it remains free of defects and can endure. Even the sages could not go against the Changes. This Way accords with Heaven. Heaven has a manifest Way and aids those who follow it. Thus, when they patterned their conduct on Heaven, none of their actions was inauspicious; when they governed in obedience to Heaven, none of their undertakings was without benefit. Even Heaven could not go against the sages.

What, then, did Huangdi, Yao, and Shun actually do? They presented an example of centrality and correctness: all that could be seen was their display of embroidered ceremonial robes, yet the people understood of themselves the transforming influence of wordless teaching. Reverent and silent, they contemplated good government: all that could be seen was their display of prescribed ceremonial dress, yet the world naturally attained a condition in which people's desires were fulfilled. Surely this drew upon Qian and Kun, the Creative and the Receptive?

For accomplishing transformation without conscious intent is how Qian and Kun work their wonders upon things, while things themselves remain unaware of that achievement. Having conscious intent yet acting without contrivance is how the sages benefit the people, while the people themselves remain unaware of that benefit. If the sages were to seek out changes throughout the world day after day with painstaking concern and make alterations accordingly, their subtle efficacy would readily cease, their transforming influence would readily be exhausted, and they would no longer resemble Heaven and Earth. Ah! Who but these three sages could accomplish this? Nevertheless, Huang…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
帝遠矣今觀堯舜所以經世理物載在典謨至
詳備也要之運而不宰施而不設乾坤之理固
皆取足於一心矣後世不知此道騖紛更者拂
民情樂因循者昧權變又何異乎治不古若也
噫
書
欽若昊天曆象日月星辰
宋萬葉
同考試官教諭吳批不事彫琢而逸思粹語快
人心目書義之精者
===
同考試官教授何批曆象正所以欽若近作多析
為二事獨此渾成一意宜錄以式
考試官教授吳批深得帝堯命官之旨
考試官教授李批典雅可玩
聖君示作曆之本惟盡心以稽天文焉蓋天之
象數未易知也非敬順以稽之何以為作曆之
本哉帝堯首命羲和之意若曰帝王有代天之
責必有經天之政作曆政之首務也其要何在
punctuated:
帝遠矣。今觀堯舜所以經世理物，載在典謨，至詳備也。要之，運而不宰，施而不設，乾坤之理固皆取足於一心矣。後世不知此道，騖紛更者拂民情，樂因循者昧權變，又何異乎治不古若也？噫！
書
欽若昊天，曆象日月星辰。
宋萬葉
同考試官教諭吳批：不事彫琢，而逸思粹語，快人心目，書義之精者。
同考試官教授何批：曆象正所以欽若。近作多析為二事，獨此渾成一意，宜錄以式。
考試官教授吳批：深得帝堯命官之旨。
考試官教授李批：典雅可玩。
聖君示作曆之本，惟盡心以稽天文焉。蓋天之象數未易知也，非敬順以稽之，何以為作曆之本哉？帝堯首命羲和之意，若曰：帝王有代天之責，必有經天之政，作曆，政之首務也。其要何在？
translation_en:
…the Yellow Emperor is far removed from us. Now, when we examine how Yao and Shun ordered the world and governed its affairs, the records in the Canons and Counsels are exceedingly detailed and complete. In essence, they set things in motion without dominating them and bestowed benefits without contrivance: the principles of Heaven and Earth were fully available within their own minds. Later generations did not understand this Way. Those intent on incessant changes went against the people's feelings, while those content to follow established practices failed to understand adaptation to circumstances. How, then, could it be surprising that their government fell short of antiquity? Alas!
Book of Documents
“Reverently accord with August Heaven; calculate and observe the sun, moon, stars, and celestial markers.”
Song Wanye
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: Without resorting to elaborate embellishment, its soaring ideas and refined language delight the mind and eye. An outstanding exposition of the meaning of the Book of Documents.
Comment by Associate Examiner He, Professor: Calculating and observing are precisely the means of reverently according with Heaven. Recent compositions mostly divide these into two separate matters. This one alone integrates them into a single conception; it should be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: It thoroughly grasps Emperor Yao's purpose in appointing officials.
Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: Classical and elegant, it rewards attentive appreciation.
The sage ruler indicated the foundation of calendar-making: devoting one's whole mind to examining celestial patterns. For the configurations and numerical regularities of Heaven are not easily understood. Unless one examines them with reverence and compliance, how can one establish a foundation for calendar-making? The intent of Emperor Yao's initial charge to Xi and He was as though he said: “Emperors and kings bear the responsibility of acting on Heaven's behalf and must therefore institute measures for ordering celestial affairs. Making the calendar is the foremost task of government. Where does its essence lie…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
哉今夫天之高也固廣遠而難知日月星辰繫
焉則有故而可考也使以慢易拂逆之私稽之
非所以求端於天而爲治曆之本矣汝必兢業
不忘而運之心思者奉順其自然之運嚴恭匪
懈而詳之制作者祗若乎本體之常日月星辰
之定數卽昊天之數也則有曆以紀之而布算
之惟密不紊乎周天之行日月星辰之成象卽
昊天之象也則有象以觀之而窺測之惟精不
爽乎麗天之運雖遲速順逆之不定循吾一定
===
之法以求之俾人文立而天文具在人時由之
以準也此其所關爲甚大而可以易心乘之耶
雖經緯次舍之靡常卽吾有常之法以推之俾
物象具而天象可徵民功由之以定也此其所
係爲甚重而可以私心拂之耶觀此則帝堯敬
天之心不爲虛而授時有其地矣雖然堯豈爲
作曆敬天耶天道無私而普物帝王一敬以合
天均非有意于間也使因治曆而後有意于敬
天則敬爲未純而求其術不違天也難矣是故
punctuated:
哉？今夫天之高也，固廣遠而難知；日月星辰繫焉，則有故而可考也。使以慢易拂逆之私稽之，非所以求端於天而爲治曆之本矣。汝必兢業不忘，而運之心思者奉順其自然之運；嚴恭匪懈，而詳之制作者祗若乎本體之常。日月星辰之定數，卽昊天之數也，則有曆以紀之，而布算之惟密，不紊乎周天之行；日月星辰之成象，卽昊天之象也，則有象以觀之，而窺測之惟精，不爽乎麗天之運。雖遲速順逆之不定，循吾一定之法以求之，俾人文立而天文具，在人時由之以準也。此其所關爲甚大，而可以易心乘之耶？雖經緯次舍之靡常，卽吾有常之法以推之，俾物象具而天象可徵，民功由之以定也。此其所係爲甚重，而可以私心拂之耶？觀此，則帝堯敬天之心不爲虛，而授時有其地矣。
雖然，堯豈爲作曆敬天耶？天道無私而普物，帝王一敬以合天均，非有意于間也。使因治曆而後有意于敬天，則敬爲未純，而求其術不違天也難矣。是故
translation_en:
…? Now Heaven in its height is indeed vast, remote, and difficult to comprehend. Yet the sun, moon, and stars are attached to it, and thus there are underlying principles that can be investigated. If you investigate them with the selfish dispositions of carelessness and defiance, this is no way to seek the guiding principle in Heaven and establish the foundation for regulating the calendar. You must remain vigilant and diligent, never forgetting your charge, so that what you work out in your thoughts accords reverently with their natural movements. You must remain solemnly respectful and untiring, so that what you elaborate in your instruments and arrangements reverently follows the constancy of their fundamental nature. The fixed numerical measures of the sun, moon, and stars are the numerical measures of August Heaven itself. Thus, let there be a calendar to record them, and perform the calculations with such exactitude that they do not confuse the movements through the circuit of Heaven. The configurations formed by the sun, moon, and stars are the configurations of August Heaven itself. Thus, let there be a celestial model through which to observe them, and conduct observations and measurements with such precision that they do not deviate from the movements of the bodies arrayed in Heaven. Although their slow and swift, forward and retrograde movements are variable, investigate them according to our fixed methods, so that human patterns are established and celestial patterns fully set forth, providing a standard for the seasons of human activity. What is involved here is exceedingly great: can one approach it with a careless mind? Although their longitudinal and latitudinal positions and their stations and lodges continually vary, calculate them by our constant methods, so that the configurations of things are fully represented and celestial configurations can be verified, thereby determining the times for the people's labors. What depends upon this is exceedingly weighty: can one oppose it with a selfish mind? Viewed in this light, Emperor Yao's reverence for Heaven was no empty sentiment, and his bestowal of the seasons upon the people had a firm foundation.
Nevertheless, did Yao revere Heaven merely in order to construct a calendar? The Way of Heaven is impartial and extends to all things; emperors and kings, through undivided reverence, accord with Heaven's impartial ordering, without interposing deliberate intentions. If it were only because of regulating the calendar that one formed the intention to revere Heaven, then that reverence would not be pure, and it would be difficult to ensure that one's techniques did not contravene Heaven. Therefore…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
堯之敬天不特見於治曆而放勳事業咸自此
推故曰敬者帝王傳心之要法
二五事一曰貌二曰言三曰視四曰聽五
曰思貌曰恭言曰從視曰明聽曰聰思
曰睿恭作肅從作乂明作哲聰作謀睿
作聖
陳文質
同考試官教諭張批天人合一之理發明殆盡蓋
潛心聖學而有得者
===
同考試官教授何批鋪敘得法詞不煩而意自貫
可以語天人之學矣
考試官教授吳批深得箕子演疇之旨
考試官教授李批詞義精切
君子衍五事之疇而誠身之道備矣蓋君道以
誠身為本也觀五事之目而德與用之兼全焉
存誠之功容可緩乎箕子衍疇之意蓋謂人君
一身位乎天人之中則必盡乎形性之理洪範
次二為五事果何如哉彼人得天之五行以生
punctuated:
堯之敬天不特見於治曆，而放勳事業咸自此推。故曰：敬者，帝王傳心之要法。

二、五事：一曰貌，二曰言，三曰視，四曰聽，五曰思。貌曰恭，言曰從，視曰明，聽曰聰，思曰睿。恭作肅，從作乂，明作哲，聰作謀，睿作聖。

陳文質

同考試官教諭張批：天人合一之理，發明殆盡，蓋潛心聖學而有得者。

同考試官教授何批：鋪敘得法，詞不煩而意自貫，可以語天人之學矣。

考試官教授吳批：深得箕子演疇之旨。

考試官教授李批：詞義精切。

君子衍五事之疇，而誠身之道備矣。蓋君道以誠身為本也。觀五事之目，而德與用之兼全焉，存誠之功容可緩乎？箕子衍疇之意，蓋謂人君一身位乎天人之中，則必盡乎形性之理。《洪範》次二為五事，果何如哉？彼人得天之五行以生
translation_en:
…Yao’s reverence for Heaven was manifest not only in regulating the calendar: all the achievements of the illustrious Yao proceeded from this. Thus it is said: reverence is the essential method through which emperors and kings transmit the heart’s teaching.

“Second, the five activities: the first is demeanor; the second, speech; the third, sight; the fourth, hearing; the fifth, thought. Demeanor should be respectful; speech, compliant; sight, clear; hearing, acute; thought, discerning. Respect produces gravity; compliance produces good order; clarity produces wisdom; acuity produces sound counsel; discernment produces sagehood.”

Chen Wenzhi

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, County School Instructor: “The principle of the unity of Heaven and humanity is elucidated almost exhaustively. This is surely the work of someone who has devoted himself to the learning of the sages and gained insight into it.”

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Prefectural School Instructor: “The exposition is skillfully arranged; the wording is economical, yet the meaning runs coherently throughout. One may indeed discuss the learning of Heaven and humanity with this writer.”

Comment by Examiner Wu, Prefectural School Instructor: “This deeply grasps Jizi’s intent in expounding the categories.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Prefectural School Instructor: “The wording and meaning are refined and precise.”

When the gentleman expounds the category of the five activities, the way of making oneself sincere is fully set forth. For the way of the ruler takes making oneself sincere as its foundation. Considering the particulars of the five activities, we find that virtue and its application are both fully encompassed therein. Can the work of preserving sincerity possibly be deferred? Jizi’s intent in expounding the categories was surely to say that the ruler, in his own person, occupies a position between Heaven and humanity and must therefore fully realize the principles of bodily form and inherent nature. In the Great Plan, the second category is the five activities. What, precisely, does this mean? Human beings receive Heaven’s five phases and thereby come into being…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
也有五事焉自其始生而形具也故一曰貌形
具而氣揚也故二曰言三則發散而爲目之視
也四則翕聚而爲耳之聽也至於五則精氣之
會而思以通之焉蓋發見有先後之序而妙合
無理氣之殊全體大用胥此出矣故物則一原
也貌淑慎而恭言和順而從視之明無所蔽也
聽之聰無所壅也思則幾微悉通而恭從明聰
皆由之以貫徹矣是成形之內而成性者具焉
天之與於人者此其渾然畢具矣乎然體用一
===
致也恭以著乎端莊之度從以顯乎條理之章
明之所照而智識不眩也聰之所達而謀度不
遺也睿則神妙不測而肅乂哲謀皆由之以極
致矣是藏用之中而顯仁者行焉人之得於天
者此其燦然各足矣乎夫踐形盡性理固原於
至一以人合天機則通於無間然非主之以敬
亦安能以立極而敘倫哉大抵人道以聖爲極
也洪範衍五事而極於作聖是具形性者皆可
以爲聖而聖之不易至者豈其性殊哉亦弗思
punctuated: 也，有五事焉。自其始生而形具也，故一曰貌；形具而氣揚也，故二曰言；三則發散而爲目之視也；四則翕聚而爲耳之聽也；至於五，則精氣之會而思以通之焉。蓋發見有先後之序，而妙合無理氣之殊，全體大用胥此出矣。故物則一原也，貌淑慎而恭，言和順而從，視之明無所蔽也，聽之聰無所壅也，思則幾微悉通，而恭從明聰皆由之以貫徹矣。是成形之內而成性者具焉，天之與於人者，此其渾然畢具矣乎！然體用一致也，恭以著乎端莊之度，從以顯乎條理之章，明之所照而智識不眩也，聰之所達而謀度不遺也，睿則神妙不測，而肅乂哲謀皆由之以極致矣。是藏用之中而顯仁者行焉，人之得於天者，此其燦然各足矣乎！夫踐形盡性，理固原於至一；以人合天，機則通於無間。然非主之以敬，亦安能以立極而敘倫哉？大抵人道以聖爲極也。《洪範》衍五事而極於作聖，是具形性者皆可以爲聖，而聖之不易至者，豈其性殊哉？亦弗思
translation_en:
…there are five affairs. From the beginning of human life, bodily form is complete; hence the first is called demeanor. Once form is complete, vital energy issues forth; hence the second is called speech. Third, it radiates outward to become the eyes’ seeing. Fourth, it gathers inward to become the ears’ hearing. As for the fifth, essential vital energies converge, and thought brings them into communication. Their manifestations thus follow a sequence, yet in their wondrous union there is no separation between principle and vital energy. The complete substance and its great functioning both issue from this. Thus things and their norms share a single source. Demeanor is good and circumspect, and therefore reverent; speech is harmonious and compliant, and therefore accords with what is right. Clear sight is unobstructed; keen hearing is unimpeded. Thought comprehends every subtle incipience, and through it reverence, accordance, clarity, and keenness are all connected and carried through. Thus, within the completed bodily form, all that constitutes one’s nature is present. Is this not the full, undivided presence of everything Heaven bestows upon human beings?

Yet substance and function form a unity. Reverence manifests itself in a dignified bearing; accordance displays itself in orderly arrangement. Where clarity illuminates, understanding is not confused; where keenness reaches, deliberation omits nothing. Penetrating insight is spiritually wondrous and unfathomable, and through it solemnity, orderliness, wisdom, and planning all attain their fullest realization. Thus, within concealed functioning, that which manifests benevolence is put into action. Is this not the radiant and individual completeness of everything human beings receive from Heaven?

In fulfilling one’s bodily form and fully realizing one’s nature, principle has its source in ultimate unity; in bringing the human into accord with Heaven, the workings communicate without any gap. Yet unless reverent attentiveness governs them, how can one establish the ultimate standard and order human relationships? In general, the human Way takes sagehood as its highest standard. The Great Plan expounds the five affairs and culminates in becoming a sage. Thus all who possess bodily form and human nature can become sages. If sagehood is difficult to attain, can it be because their natures differ? They merely fail to reflect…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
耳矣然造就之功則係之君君身皇極之主也
敬而思之則聰明睿知皆從此出與天之五氣
相合而休徵應矣故五事以思爲要而聖人以
合天爲能
詩
羣黎百姓徧爲爾德
黃國彥
同考試官敎諭鄭批善形容化成氣象而納誨
之意溢于言表必有忠愛之忱者非直取其文也
===
同考試官敎諭伍批此題助君爲德之意最難
體貼子能渾融詩意以寓祝願之情取之
考試官敎授吳批善發臣子祝君之意
考試官敎授李批詞理俱精
人君之福合天下而成德也蓋天下化成皆君
德之所及也而王道之多助見矣玆非人君之
全福乎周臣託神貺以答君賜也若曰人君聯
屬天下以成其身則亦幷包天下以爲之福神
之福君豈特民俗之淳而已哉彼羣黎百姓莫
punctuated:
耳矣。然造就之功，則係之君。君身皇極之主也，敬而思之，則聰明睿知皆從此出，與天之五氣相合，而休徵應矣。故五事以思爲要，而聖人以合天爲能。
詩
「羣黎百姓，徧爲爾德。」
黃國彥
同考試官敎諭鄭批：善形容化成氣象，而納誨之意溢于言表，必有忠愛之忱者，非直取其文也。
同考試官敎諭伍批：此題助君爲德之意最難體貼。子能渾融詩意，以寓祝願之情，取之。
考試官敎授吳批：善發臣子祝君之意。
考試官敎授李批：詞理俱精。
人君之福，合天下而成德也。蓋天下化成，皆君德之所及也，而王道之多助見矣。玆非人君之全福乎？周臣託神貺以答君賜也，若曰：人君聯屬天下以成其身，則亦幷包天下以爲之福。神之福君，豈特民俗之淳而已哉？彼羣黎百姓，莫
translation_en:
…that is all. Yet the work of bringing people to fulfillment depends upon the ruler. The ruler himself presides over the Supreme Standard. If he reflects with reverence, keenness of hearing, clarity of vision, sagacity, and wisdom all proceed from this; they accord with Heaven’s five vital energies, and auspicious signs respond. Thus, among the Five Activities, reflection is essential, and the sage’s capacity lies in achieving accord with Heaven.
Book of Odes
“The multitudes of the common people all practice your virtue.”
Huang Guoyan
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “He skillfully depicts the condition of a people fully transformed by moral influence, while his intent to offer admonition is apparent beyond the words themselves. He must possess sincere loyalty and affection for his ruler; I select him for more than his writing alone.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu 伍, Instructor: “The intent of this topic—to assist the ruler in cultivating virtue—is especially difficult to apprehend. You have thoroughly integrated the meaning of the ode and conveyed through it your feelings of blessing and good wishes. I select this essay.”
Comment by Examiner Wu 吳, Professor: “He skillfully brings out the subject’s intention to offer blessings to his ruler.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “Both expression and reasoning are refined.”
The ruler’s blessing lies in uniting all under Heaven to bring virtue to fulfillment. For the moral transformation of all under Heaven results entirely from the reach of the ruler’s virtue, and therein one sees the many sources of support for the Kingly Way. Is this not the ruler’s complete blessing? A subject of Zhou invokes the spirits’ blessings to repay his ruler’s gifts, as though saying: The ruler binds all under Heaven together to perfect his own person; likewise, his blessings encompass all under Heaven. When the spirits bless the ruler, can their blessing consist merely in the purity of the people’s customs? Among those multitudes of common people, there is none …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
非王民也則民之德亦莫非王化也使民德未
新是王化有未洽矣王化未洽是君福有未全
矣茲惟先公先王體吾王弘化之心而神道之
感通有以綏夫從欲之治牖斯民孚惠之念而
天機之默相有以動其敏德之風惟皇建極矣
民亦象之而歸極焉興仁興讓無一人不協於
化中惟聖成能矣民亦則之而與能焉遵道遵
路無一方不躋於順治近而畿甸則覲耿光之
下濟咸訓行而不違道德一而風俗同自朝廷
===
達之四國翕如也百姓之昭明孰非帝則之默
順乎遠而海隅則仰文命之覃敷咸鼓舞而不
倦敎化行而習俗美自邦畿達之萬方藹如也
黎民之於變孰非帝德之廣運乎是其始也以
一人之德風乎天下而若或啓之上下一心德
之至也其旣也以天下之德歸於一人而若或
助之君民一德治之極也如是而後爲明神詒
福之全吾王大
同之福如是而後爲吾人對揚
之情藉此其少伸乎噫天保臣子以是答君其
punctuated: 非王民也，則民之德亦莫非王化也。使民德未新，是王化有未洽矣；王化未洽，是君福有未全矣。茲惟先公先王體吾王弘化之心，而神道之感通有以綏夫從欲之治；牖斯民孚惠之念，而天機之默相有以動其敏德之風。惟皇建極矣，民亦象之而歸極焉，興仁興讓，無一人不協於化中；惟聖成能矣，民亦則之而與能焉，遵道遵路，無一方不躋於順治。近而畿甸，則覲耿光之下濟，咸訓行而不違，道德一而風俗同，自朝廷達之四國，翕如也。百姓之昭明，孰非帝則之默順乎？遠而海隅，則仰文命之覃敷，咸鼓舞而不倦，敎化行而習俗美，自邦畿達之萬方，藹如也。黎民之於變，孰非帝德之廣運乎？是其始也，以一人之德風乎天下，而若或啓之，上下一心，德之至也；其旣也，以天下之德歸於一人，而若或助之，君民一德，治之極也。如是而後爲明神詒福之全。吾王大同之福如是，而後爲吾人對揚之情，藉此其少伸乎！噫！天保臣子以是答君，其
translation_en:
…none are other than the king’s people; thus the people’s virtue, too, is entirely the product of the king’s transforming influence. If the people’s virtue has not been renewed, the king’s transforming influence has not yet reached everywhere; if that influence has not reached everywhere, the ruler’s blessings are not yet complete. Here the former lords and kings understand our king’s desire to extend his transforming influence. Through the responsive communion of the spirits, they sustain a government that accords with his wishes. They awaken in the people a disposition toward sincerity and compliance, and through the unseen assistance of Heaven’s workings, stir them to the diligent practice of virtue.

The sovereign establishes the supreme standard; the people emulate him and converge upon that standard. They rise to benevolence and deference, and not one person fails to accord with the mean embodied in his transforming influence. The sage perfects his capacities; the people take him as their model and share in those capacities. They follow the Way and its paths, and no region fails to attain harmonious government. Nearby, in the royal domain, they behold his brilliant light reaching down to them. All follow his instruction without deviation; moral principles are unified and customs made alike. From the court to the states in all four directions, all are in harmony. Whose enlightenment among the common people is not an unspoken conformity to the sovereign’s standard? Far away, at the edges of the seas, they look up to the broad extension of his civilizing commands. All are inspired and stirred to tireless effort. Moral instruction spreads and customs become admirable; from the royal domain to every quarter, its influence flourishes everywhere. What transformation among the common people is not the far-reaching operation of the sovereign’s virtue?

At the outset, the virtue of the one man influences all under Heaven, as though some unseen power were opening the way for it. Those above and below share one heart: this is virtue at its utmost. In the end, the virtue of all under Heaven converges upon the one man, as though some unseen power were assisting him. Ruler and people share one virtue: this is government at its highest perfection. Only thus are the blessings bestowed by the luminous spirits complete. With our king’s blessing of great concord thus realized, may our feelings of grateful acknowledgment and praise find some small expression through this! Ah! With this, the servants and subjects who composed “Heaven Protects” (Tian bao) answered their ruler; surely they…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
亦善承休德者矣抑祝君之福而及於民德者
何也蓋崇高富貴人君已自有其福矣惟夫百
姓興行天下太平然後盛大之福永言保之故
箕疇斂福而繼曰會極歸極亦此意也然欲民
之歸德非君之脩德又何以致之此固詩人立
言之旨也保大而思永者尚有取於斯哉
文王孫子本支百世凡周之士不顯亦世
葉明元
同考試官教諭鄭批理明辭達格整意新且首
===
末歸重於文王深得經旨
同考試官教諭伍批子孫臣庶之福皆文王敬
德格天所致此作發明天人相與之意甚𤏡取之
考試官教授吳批詞意莊重得告君體
考試官教授李批文有思致
天之命周君臣世濟其美也蓋德隆則命從而
隆也合子孫臣庶而永孚於休天之命周寧有
窮乎宜周公述此以戒成王也若曰天命聖德
相為感應者也以文德之亹亹而天之敷錫豈
punctuated:
亦善承休德者矣。抑祝君之福而及於民德者，何也？蓋崇高富貴，人君已自有其福矣。惟夫百姓興行，天下太平，然後盛大之福永言保之。故箕疇斂福，而繼曰會極歸極，亦此意也。然欲民之歸德，非君之脩德，又何以致之？此固詩人立言之旨也。保大而思永者，尚有取於斯哉！
文王孫子，本支百世。凡周之士，不顯亦世。
葉明元
同考試官教諭鄭批：理明辭達，格整意新，且首末歸重於文王，深得經旨。
同考試官教諭伍批：子孫臣庶之福，皆文王敬德格天所致。此作發明天人相與之意甚𤏡，取之。
考試官教授吳批：詞意莊重，得告君體。
考試官教授李批：文有思致。
天之命周，君臣世濟其美也。蓋德隆則命從而隆也。合子孫臣庶而永孚於休，天之命周寧有窮乎？宜周公述此以戒成王也。若曰：天命聖德，相為感應者也。以文德之亹亹，而天之敷錫豈
translation_en:
