…they too were skilled in receiving and carrying forward this beneficent virtue. Yet why does a blessing upon the ruler extend to the virtue of the people? Lofty rank, wealth, and honor already constitute blessings possessed by the ruler himself. Only when the common people rise to virtuous conduct and all under Heaven enjoys peace can these great blessings be preserved forever. Thus, in Jizi’s exposition of the Great Plan, the gathering of blessings is followed by words about assembling at and returning to the Supreme Standard: this conveys the same meaning. Yet if one wishes the people to turn toward virtue, how can this be achieved unless the ruler cultivates his own virtue? This, indeed, is the intent behind the poet’s words. Those who would preserve their greatness and consider its enduring continuance may surely find something to draw upon here!
“King Wen’s descendants: the main line and the branches endure for a hundred generations. All the officers of Zhou: are they not illustrious, generation after generation?”
Ye Mingyuan
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The reasoning is clear and the language expressive; the structure is orderly and the conception fresh. Moreover, both beginning and end place the emphasis on King Wen, profoundly grasping the meaning of the Classic.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu 伍, Instructor: “The blessings enjoyed by descendants, ministers, and common people all resulted from King Wen’s reverent cultivation of virtue, which reached Heaven. This composition elucidates the meaning of the mutual engagement of Heaven and humanity with great [?]. I accept it.”
Comment by Examiner Wu 吳, Professor: “The language and ideas are dignified and weighty, fitting the manner of addressing a ruler.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “The composition shows thoughtful conception.”
In Heaven’s granting the mandate to Zhou, rulers and ministers carried forward their excellence from generation to generation. For when virtue is exalted, the mandate becomes correspondingly exalted. With descendants, ministers, and common people together abiding forever in blessing, could Heaven’s mandate to Zhou ever come to an end? It was fitting that the Duke of Zhou should recount this to admonish King Cheng. It is as though he said: Heaven’s mandate and sagely virtue stimulate and respond to one another. Given King Wen’s unremitting virtue, could Heaven’s abundant bestowal possibly…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
惟尊榮其身已哉誠以文王孫子今固宜君宜
王矣由今而百世皆文王一體之親也而天之
敷錫猶夫初焉謨烈重光膺景命於有僕祚胤
永錫衍奕業於無疆爲本宗者順帝則而不違
世總威福之柄也爲支庶者謹侯度而罔忒世
守屏翰之司也以建皇極以奉王章而螽斯麟
趾之祥蓋與天相爲無極矣是在子孫承之固
爲勿替之休而在文王垂之不爲有秩之祜乎
凡周之士今固有德有造矣由今而百世皆文
===
王一體之臣也而天之陳錫猶夫今焉喜起交
孚世際譽髦之盛親賢並茂永資篤棐之忠在
諸侯則世脩六德而亮采有邦也在大夫則世
脩三德而浚明有家也以翊王室以佐侯封而
菁莪棫樸之士蓋與周相爲匹休矣是在臣庶
受之固爲承家之慶而在我周得之不爲輔國
之寶乎吁以百世之遠而子孫臣庶皆能脩德
以承休者莫非文德之所貽也嗣王可不念之
哉抑創業固難守成尤不易矧成王以冲年而
punctuated: 惟尊榮其身已哉？誠以文王孫子，今固宜君宜王矣。由今而百世，皆文王一體之親也，而天之敷錫猶夫初焉。謨烈重光，膺景命於有僕；祚胤永錫，衍奕業於無疆。爲本宗者，順帝則而不違，世總威福之柄也；爲支庶者，謹侯度而罔忒，世守屏翰之司也。以建皇極，以奉王章，而螽斯麟趾之祥，蓋與天相爲無極矣。是在子孫承之，固爲勿替之休，而在文王垂之，不爲有秩之祜乎？凡周之士，今固有德有造矣。由今而百世，皆文王一體之臣也，而天之陳錫猶夫今焉。喜起交孚，世際譽髦之盛；親賢並茂，永資篤棐之忠。在諸侯，則世脩六德而亮采有邦也；在大夫，則世脩三德而浚明有家也。以翊王室，以佐侯封，而菁莪棫樸之士，蓋與周相爲匹休矣。是在臣庶受之，固爲承家之慶，而在我周得之，不爲輔國之寶乎？吁！以百世之遠，而子孫臣庶皆能脩德以承休者，莫非文德之所貽也。嗣王可不念之哉？抑創業固難，守成尤不易，矧成王以冲年而
translation_en:
…could it merely have honored and ennobled his own person? Indeed, King Wen’s descendants are already fit to be lords and kings. From now through a hundred generations, all are his kin, sharing one body with him, and Heaven will bestow its blessings just as it did at the beginning. His designs and achievements will shine anew, and they will receive the great mandate among the subject states [?]; blessings will be bestowed perpetually upon his heirs, extending his splendid enterprise without limit. Those of the principal lineage will follow the Lord on High’s rules without deviation, wielding the authority to punish and reward generation after generation. Those of the collateral branches will observe the standards of the regional lords without error, maintaining their charge as the realm’s protective bulwarks generation after generation. Thus they will establish the August Standard and uphold royal statutes; the auspicious signs celebrated in “The Locusts” and “The Qilin’s Hooves” will endure as boundlessly as Heaven itself. For the descendants who inherit this, it is assuredly an unfailing blessing; viewed as King Wen’s bequest, is it not an enduring benediction?

All the officers of Zhou already possess virtue and accomplishment. From now through a hundred generations, all will be King Wen’s ministers, sharing one body with him, and Heaven will lavish its gifts just as it does today. The sovereign’s delight and his ministers’ energetic service will inspire mutual trust, and every generation will enjoy an abundance of celebrated talent. Royal kinsmen and worthy men will flourish together, providing enduring support through their devoted loyalty. As regional lords, they will cultivate the six virtues generation after generation and faithfully discharge their duties in their states. As grand masters, they will cultivate the three virtues generation after generation and display profound discernment in their houses. Thus they will support the royal house and assist the enfeoffed lords; the officers celebrated in “The Luxuriant Southernwood” and “The Oaks” will share in Zhou’s enduring glory. For the ministers and common people who receive this, it is assuredly the good fortune of perpetuating their houses; for our Zhou, which obtains their service, are they not treasures that sustain the state?

Ah! That, even a hundred generations hence, descendants, ministers, and common people should all be able to cultivate virtue and inherit these blessings is entirely the legacy of King Wen’s virtue. Can a succeeding king fail to bear this in mind? Yet founding an enterprise is certainly difficult, and preserving what has been achieved is still harder—how much more so when King Cheng, at so tender an age, …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
承大業其於天人相與之際尤有不可忽者故
周公戒之惓惓以天命祖德爲言無非欲其敬
天法祖而脩德以凝命也卒至成王學懋於緝
熈命基於宥密而爲守成之令主孰非周公輔
相之功哉噫若周之君臣眞可爲萬世法矣
春秋
秋九月齊侯宋公江人黃人盟于貫〔僖公二年〕
秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于陽穀
〔僖公三年〕
===
林繼志
同考試官教諭伍 批 盟會江黃皆爲攘楚計
兹作渾融題意詞語謹嚴宜錄以式
同考試官教諭吳 批 此題上主盟重盧義下主
會重奇正是作發明精確而詞亦嚴整
考試官教授吳 批 簡健渾成經義之佳者
考試官教授李 批 語精義正深得經旨
春秋於霸主有予其結遠以制外者有與其定
謀以攘外者此桓欲伐楚而先結江黃謀定陽
punctuated:
承大業，其於天人相與之際，尤有不可忽者。故周公戒之惓惓，以天命祖德爲言，無非欲其敬天法祖，而脩德以凝命也。卒至成王學懋於緝熈，命基於宥密，而爲守成之令主，孰非周公輔相之功哉？噫！若周之君臣，眞可爲萬世法矣！

春秋

秋九月，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫。〔僖公二年〕
秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。〔僖公三年〕

林繼志

同考試官教諭伍批：盟會江黃，皆爲攘楚計。兹作渾融題意，詞語謹嚴，宜錄以式。
同考試官教諭吳批：此題上主盟，重盧義；下主會，重奇正。是作發明精確，而詞亦嚴整。
考試官教授吳批：簡健渾成，經義之佳者。
考試官教授李批：語精義正，深得經旨。

春秋於霸主，有予其結遠以制外者，有與其定謀以攘外者。此桓欲伐楚，而先結江黃，謀定陽
translation_en:
…inherited the great enterprise, there was particular need for vigilance in the interaction between Heaven and humanity. Thus the Duke of Zhou earnestly admonished him, speaking of Heaven’s Mandate and his ancestors’ virtue. His sole purpose was to have him revere Heaven, emulate his ancestors, and cultivate virtue so as to secure the Mandate. In the end, King Cheng advanced in learning toward continuous illumination, established the Mandate upon profound tranquillity, and became an excellent ruler who preserved the achievements of his predecessors. What part of this was not due to the Duke of Zhou’s assistance? Ah! Such rulers and ministers as those of Zhou truly can serve as models for all ages!

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In autumn, in the ninth month, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and the men of Jiang and Huang made a covenant at Guan.” 〔Second year of Duke Xi〕
“In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and the men of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu.” 〔Third year of Duke Xi〕

Lin Jizhi

Associate Examiner Wu 伍, Instructor, comments: “The covenant and meeting with Jiang and Huang were both measures intended to repel Chu. This composition integrates the meaning of the topic into a coherent whole, and its language is careful and exact. It should be included as a model.”
Associate Examiner Wu 吳, Instructor, comments: “The first part of this topic centres on the covenant, emphasizing ‘lu yi’ [?]; the second centres on the meeting, emphasizing unconventional and conventional strategy. This composition elucidates these points precisely, and its language is also disciplined and orderly.”
Examiner Wu 吳, Professor, comments: “Concise, vigorous, and fully integrated: an excellent exposition of the meaning of the Classic.”
Examiner Li 李, Professor, comments: “Its language is precise and its interpretation correct; it deeply grasps the purport of the Classic.”

In its treatment of the hegemonic lords, the Spring and Autumn Annals sometimes approves their forging distant alliances to restrain external powers, and sometimes commends their settling plans to repel external powers. Here, Duke Huan wished to attack Chu, but first allied with Jiang and Huang and settled his plans at Yang…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
穀安攘之略見矣故春秋兩予之且貫澤曷盟
也桓結江黃也聞八國皆在矣獨舉江黃者何
曰許是盟也蓋攘夷之道非用兵之難而力有
弗協之患楚固崛強也使黨有未攜焉楚可得
而撓乎幸而桓有貫之盟焉偕我宋公離彼服
屬之黨結彼江黃成我掎角之勢在楚人則斷
其右臂而勢以孤在中國則免於左衽而義以
著此可見桓見天下之大勢而制楚無遺慮矣
故盟雖春秋所不取而貫澤之盟經獨言遠國
===
者許桓之能結遠也陽穀曷會也桓謀伐楚也
聞諸侯大會矣末言江黃者何曰善是謀也蓋
攘夷之道非克敵之難而謀有弗豫之患諸侯
皆新附也使約弗再申焉楚可得而伐乎幸而
桓有陽穀之會焉定八國爲正兵以當其前分
江黃爲奇兵以擬其後正則敦陳整旅而進無
所乘奇則藏機設伏而退無所據此可見桓識
天下之大機而服楚有勝算矣故會雖諸侯不
得爲而陽穀之會經末言江黃者善桓之能定
punctuated:
穀，安攘之略見矣，故春秋兩予之。且貫澤曷盟也？桓結江黃也。聞八國皆在矣，獨舉江黃者何？曰：許是盟也。蓋攘夷之道，非用兵之難，而力有弗協之患。楚固崛強也，使黨有未攜焉，楚可得而撓乎？幸而桓有貫之盟焉，偕我宋公，離彼服屬之黨，結彼江黃，成我掎角之勢。在楚人，則斷其右臂而勢以孤；在中國，則免於左衽而義以著。此可見桓見天下之大勢，而制楚無遺慮矣。故盟雖春秋所不取，而貫澤之盟，經獨言遠國者，許桓之能結遠也。

陽穀曷會也？桓謀伐楚也。聞諸侯大會矣，末言江黃者何？曰：善是謀也。蓋攘夷之道，非克敵之難，而謀有弗豫之患。諸侯皆新附也，使約弗再申焉，楚可得而伐乎？幸而桓有陽穀之會焉，定八國爲正兵以當其前，分江黃爲奇兵以擬其後。正則敦陳整旅而進無所乘，奇則藏機設伏而退無所據。此可見桓識天下之大機，而服楚有勝算矣。故會雖諸侯不得爲，而陽穀之會，經末言江黃者，善桓之能定
translation_en:
…at Yanggu, his strategy for securing the central states and repelling outsiders becomes apparent. Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals approves both actions. Why was a covenant concluded at Guanze? Duke Huan was forging ties with Jiang and Huang. We hear that all eight states were present; why, then, are Jiang and Huang alone singled out? The answer is that this expresses approval of the covenant. For in repelling the barbarians, the difficulty lies less in deploying troops than in the danger that their strength will not be coordinated. Chu was certainly powerful and defiant. If its allies had not been drawn away, could Chu have been checked? Fortunately, Duke Huan held the covenant meeting at Guan. Together with our Duke of Song, he detached Chu’s subordinate allies and bound Jiang and Huang to himself, creating a position from which to attack on two sides. For Chu, this severed its right arm and left its power isolated; for the central states, it spared them from wearing their robes fastened on the left, in the barbarian manner, and made their righteousness manifest. Here we can see that Duke Huan understood the broad configuration of power under Heaven and overlooked nothing in planning to restrain Chu. Thus, although the Spring and Autumn Annals generally disapproves of covenants, its naming only the distant states in the covenant at Guanze approves Duke Huan’s ability to win distant allies.

Why was there a meeting at Yanggu? Duke Huan was planning to attack Chu. We hear that the regional lords assembled in a great meeting; why, then, are Jiang and Huang named last? The answer is that this commends the plan. For in repelling the barbarians, the difficulty lies less in defeating the enemy than in the danger of failing to plan beforehand. The regional lords had all only recently joined him. If their agreement had not been reaffirmed, could Chu have been attacked? Fortunately, Duke Huan held the meeting at Yanggu. He assigned the eight states to form the regular force confronting Chu’s front, and separately assigned Jiang and Huang to form an unconventional force threatening its rear. The regular force would strengthen its formations and order its troops, leaving Chu no opening to exploit in advancing; the unconventional force would conceal its designs and lay ambushes, leaving Chu no position to rely upon in retreating. Here we can see that Duke Huan understood the great strategic opportunities under Heaven and possessed a winning plan for bringing Chu into submission. Thus, although the regional lords were not entitled to convene such meetings, the Classic’s naming Jiang and Huang last at the meeting of Yanggu commends Duke Huan’s ability to settle…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
謀也是則始而盟貫以結遠子之繼而爲會以
定謀予之聖人倦倦攘夷安夏之意其精矣乎
抑貫之盟陽穀之會桓得江黃則足以制楚矣
楚旣受盟而志已驕溢再乎陽穀之會寵樂竝
行而桓霸衰矣噫勿怠勿荒王者事也桓何足
以語之獨江黃以向義而蒙辜焉可惜也夫
冬公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕
子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭十
有二月己亥同盟于戲〔襄公九年〕夏公
===
會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷〔定公十年〕
蔡應科
同考試官教諭伍批發揮王道伯功語有分曉而
體格平正經學之優者
同考試官教諭吳批此題諸士類多塡塞事實是
作刋落時藝而詞意明盡讀之令人爽然宜錄以式
考試官教授吳批詞意純正取之
考試官教授李批發不戰不師意明切
聖賢之相君皆得待敵之道焉此見智筭以謀
punctuated:
謀也。是則始而盟貫以結遠，子之；繼而爲會以定謀，予之。聖人倦倦攘夷安夏之意，其精矣乎！抑貫之盟、陽穀之會，桓得江黃，則足以制楚矣。楚旣受盟，而志已驕溢；再乎陽穀之會，寵樂竝行，而桓霸衰矣。噫！勿怠勿荒，王者事也，桓何足以語之？獨江黃以向義而蒙辜焉，可惜也夫！
冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月己亥，同盟于戲。〔襄公九年〕夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。〔定公十年〕
蔡應科
同考試官教諭伍批：發揮王道伯功，語有分曉，而體格平正，經學之優者。
同考試官教諭吳批：此題諸士類多塡塞事實，是作刋落時藝，而詞意明盡，讀之令人爽然，宜錄以式。
考試官教授吳批：詞意純正，取之。
考試官教授李批：發不戰不師意，明切。
聖賢之相君，皆得待敵之道焉。此見智筭以謀
translation_en:
…planning. Thus, when he first made the covenant at Guan to establish ties with distant states, he received approval [?]; when he subsequently held the meeting to settle his plans, he received commendation. How subtle was the Sage’s tireless [?] concern to repel the Yi and bring peace to the Xia! Yet through the covenant at Guan and the meeting at Yanggu, Duke Huan secured the support of Jiang and Huang, sufficient to check Chu. Once Chu had accepted the covenant, his ambitions swelled with arrogance. At the second meeting at Yanggu, indulgence in favorites and pleasures went hand in hand, and Duke Huan’s hegemony declined. Alas! To be neither negligent nor heedless is the business of a true king; how could Huan measure up to this? It is especially regrettable that Jiang and Huang, through turning toward righteousness, suffered punishment!
“In winter, the duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Xiao Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, to attack Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the jihai day, they jointly entered into a covenant at Xi.” 〔Ninth year of Duke Xiang〕 “In summer, the duke met with the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding〕
Cai Yingke
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu 伍, Instructor: “The exposition of the kingly Way and the achievements of hegemons makes its distinctions clearly, while the composition is balanced and correct. An excellent example of classical scholarship.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu 吳, Instructor: “On this topic, most candidates tend to cram their essays with historical facts. This composition strips away the conventions of contemporary examination writing, while its wording and meaning are clear and fully developed. Reading it is refreshing. It should be recorded as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Wu 吳, Professor: “The wording and meaning are pure and correct. Accept it.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “Its exposition of the idea of neither fighting nor deploying armies is clear and pertinent.”
Sages and worthies who assisted their rulers all grasped the proper way to deal with enemies. Here we see Zhi [?], through planning …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
駕楚孔子以禮化齊皆春秋中之僅見者乎且
待敵之道王者尚德伯者尚謀春秋時知此道
者鮮矣何幸於智罃孔子見之耶以智罃言之
方晉悼之伐鄭也楚救未至鄭人行成將待强
而民是庇矣使好戰者處此則兵刃旣接大勞
其有艾乎幸智罃之相悼也而善陣之法明焉
許盟旋師欲以養我之銳分軍逆來務以摧彼
之鋒凡所以駕楚者不以戰而以謀也彼楚雖
橫也寧不爲謀阻耶自是驕悍者力屈攜貳者
===
心服不謂之善謀之效不可也美哉罃也非賢
而能若是乎以孔子言之方夾谷之講會也兩
君就壇犁彌獻策將辱魯而加之兵矣使昧禮
者處此則鼓譟一起俘獲其能免乎幸孔子之
相定也而古人之道明焉不曰干盟偪好以啓
其衷則曰不祥愆義以糾其失凡所以感齊者
不以師而以禮也彼齊雖强也寧不爲禮動耶
由是景公悔過而遽止定公飲至而復安不謂
之明禮之功不可也大哉孔子也非聖而能若
punctuated:
駕楚，孔子以禮化齊，皆春秋中之僅見者乎？且待敵之道，王者尚德，伯者尚謀，春秋時知此道者鮮矣，何幸於智罃、孔子見之耶！以智罃言之，方晉悼之伐鄭也，楚救未至，鄭人行成，將待强而民是庇矣。使好戰者處此，則兵刃旣接，大勞其有艾乎？幸智罃之相悼也，而善陣之法明焉。許盟旋師，欲以養我之銳；分軍逆來，務以摧彼之鋒。凡所以駕楚者，不以戰而以謀也。彼楚雖橫也，寧不爲謀阻耶？自是驕悍者力屈，攜貳者心服，不謂之善謀之效不可也。美哉，罃也！非賢而能若是乎？

以孔子言之，方夾谷之講會也，兩君就壇，犁彌獻策，將辱魯而加之兵矣。使昧禮者處此，則鼓譟一起，俘獲其能免乎？幸孔子之相定也，而古人之道明焉。不曰干盟偪好以啓其衷，則曰不祥愆義以糾其失。凡所以感齊者，不以師而以禮也。彼齊雖强也，寧不爲禮動耶？由是景公悔過而遽止，定公飲至而復安，不謂之明禮之功不可也。大哉，孔子也！非聖而能若
translation_en:
…to check Chu, while Kongzi used ritual propriety to transform Qi: were these not among the rare instances of their kind in the Spring and Autumn period? In dealing with an enemy, a true king prizes virtue, while a hegemon prizes strategy. Few in the Spring and Autumn period understood this way. How fortunate that we find it exemplified in Zhi Ying and Kongzi! To speak of Zhi Ying: when Duke Dao of Jin attacked Zheng, reinforcements from Chu had yet to arrive, and the people of Zheng sued for peace. They intended to rely on the stronger power and thereby protect their people. Had a lover of warfare faced this situation, once the blades had crossed, could the immense toil ever have ended? Fortunately, Zhi Ying assisted Duke Dao, and the methods of skillful military deployment became clear. He accepted the covenant and withdrew the army, intending to preserve his own troops’ vigor; he divided his forces to meet the approaching enemy, seeking to blunt their advance. All his means of checking Chu relied on strategy rather than battle. Though Chu was overbearing, how could it fail to be thwarted by such strategy? Thereafter, the arrogant and fierce were exhausted, while those wavering in their allegiance submitted in their hearts. This must be called the effect of skillful strategy. Admirable indeed was Ying! Could anyone but a worthy have achieved such things?

To speak of Kongzi: at the diplomatic meeting at Jiagu, the two rulers took their places on the platform, and Li Mi offered a scheme to humiliate Lu and bring armed force against it. Had someone ignorant of ritual propriety faced this situation, once the drumming and shouting began, could he have escaped capture? Fortunately, Kongzi assisted Duke Ding, and the way of the ancients became clear. He spoke of violating the covenant and using force against friendly relations to awaken their conscience, or of inauspicious conduct and offenses against righteousness to correct their faults. All his means of moving Qi relied on ritual propriety rather than troops. Though Qi was powerful, how could it fail to be moved by ritual propriety? Thus Duke Jing repented of his wrongdoing and promptly stopped, while Duke Ding held the ceremonial drinking upon his return and was once more secure. This must be called the achievement of understanding ritual propriety. Great indeed was Kongzi! Could anyone but a sage have achieved such…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
是乎夫至難駕者楚也智罃能以謀敝之至難
服者齊也孔子能以禮化之聖賢之有益於人
國也固如是夫抑駕楚者固智罃之功也然治
楚未幾而通吳之使繼至豈智罃不在側耶化
齊者固孔子之力也然能使萊人之不我侮而
不能使女樂之不受能使三田之歸而不能使
成邑之墮豈其致治之難耶蓋孔子之能行者
道也而道之所以行者則存乎其君也治功之
不成要亦定公用聖道之不專耳若晉之通吳
===
雖悼公之失而智罃諸臣不得不執其咎
禮記
君子曰大德不官大道不器大信不約大
時不齊察於此四者可以有志於本矣
潘維岳
同考試官教諭張批天道聖人以有本而充是作
體貼瑩徹而詞亦足以發之文之有本者也
同考試官教諭劉批平實中有逸趣冲淡中有
精思布帛菽粟之文也
punctuated:
是乎？夫至難駕者，楚也，智罃能以謀敝之；至難服者，齊也，孔子能以禮化之。聖賢之有益於人國也，固如是夫！抑駕楚者，固智罃之功也，然治楚未幾，而通吳之使繼至，豈智罃不在側耶？化齊者，固孔子之力也，然能使萊人之不我侮，而不能使女樂之不受；能使三田之歸，而不能使成邑之墮，豈其致治之難耶？蓋孔子之能行者，道也，而道之所以行者，則存乎其君也。治功之不成，要亦定公用聖道之不專耳。若晉之通吳，雖悼公之失，而智罃諸臣不得不執其咎。

禮記
君子曰：「大德不官，大道不器，大信不約，大時不齊。察於此四者，可以有志於本矣。」

潘維岳

同考試官教諭張批：「天道、聖人以有本而充。是作體貼瑩徹，而詞亦足以發之，文之有本者也。」

同考試官教諭劉批：「平實中有逸趣，冲淡中有精思，布帛菽粟之文也。」
translation_en:
…have achieved this? Chu was exceedingly difficult to rein in, yet Zhi Ying could wear it down through strategy; Qi was exceedingly difficult to subdue, yet Kongzi could transform it through ritual propriety. Such indeed are the benefits that sages and worthies bring to states! Yet although reining in Chu was certainly Zhi Ying’s achievement, scarcely had Chu been brought under control when envoys establishing relations with Wu followed. Was Zhi Ying not at the ruler’s side? Transforming Qi was certainly due to Kongzi’s efforts. Yet although he could prevent the people of Lai from insulting us, he could not prevent the acceptance of female musicians; although he could secure the return of the three tracts of land, he could not bring about the demolition of the fortifications of Cheng. Was bringing about good government really so difficult? What Kongzi could put into practice was the Way, but whether the Way was put into practice depended on his ruler. The failure to achieve good government ultimately arose simply from Duke Ding’s lack of single-mindedness in employing the sage’s Way. As for Jin’s establishment of relations with Wu, although this was Duke Dao’s error, Zhi Ying and the other ministers must nevertheless bear responsibility for it.

Book of Rites
The gentleman says: “Great virtue is not confined to an office; the great Way is not confined to a particular implement; great trustworthiness requires no covenant; great timeliness does not follow a uniform rule. By discerning these four things, one may set one’s aspiration on the root.”

Pan Weiyue

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “The Way of Heaven and the sage attain their fullness because they have a root. This composition grasps the meaning with luminous clarity, and its language is sufficient to express it. It is writing that itself has a root.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Within its plain solidity there is an unfettered charm; within its restrained simplicity there is subtle thought. This is writing like cloth, silk, beans, and grain—the essentials of daily life.”

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授吳批會註成文深得本旨
考試官教授李批是知務本者
記者歷舉天人有本之用而示人以本之當務
焉蓋聖人天道之用皆以有本而充也君子察
於是焉本其容於不務哉昔記者以務本之學
望天下也意曰體立用行固天人合一之理而
明體適用尤君子進脩之功是故道得於心之
謂德而德之大者則日新以裕富有之業官不
足以拘之也理率於性之謂道而道之大者則
===
溥博以協時措之宜器不足以泥之也自其大
信而言之誠意懇惻而眞精孚於有素期約孰
得而囿乎自其大時而言之元氣周流而化醇
妙於不測分限孰得而齊乎是聖道之用雖順
事無情也而所以綱維之者必有以爲聖之本
矣天道之用雖普物無心也而所以主宰之者
必有以爲天之本矣君子者以聖人天道爲已
責者也而可以弗察耶必遠宗諸聖冀以窮其
應感之由而上律於天期以玩其流行之故有
punctuated:
考試官教授吳批：會註成文，深得本旨。
考試官教授李批：是知務本者。
記者歷舉天人有本之用，而示人以本之當務焉。蓋聖人天道之用，皆以有本而充也。君子察於是焉，本其容於不務哉？昔記者以務本之學望天下也，意曰：體立用行，固天人合一之理；而明體適用，尤君子進脩之功。是故道得於心之謂德，而德之大者，則日新以裕富有之業，官不足以拘之也。理率於性之謂道，而道之大者，則溥博以協時措之宜，器不足以泥之也。自其大信而言之，誠意懇惻，而眞精孚於有素，期約孰得而囿乎？自其大時而言之，元氣周流，而化醇妙於不測，分限孰得而齊乎？是聖道之用，雖順事無情也，而所以綱維之者，必有以爲聖之本矣；天道之用，雖普物無心也，而所以主宰之者，必有以爲天之本矣。君子者，以聖人天道爲已責者也，而可以弗察耶？必遠宗諸聖，冀以窮其應感之由，而上律於天，期以玩其流行之故。有
translation_en:
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “The commentaries are brought together into an essay that thoroughly grasps the underlying meaning.”
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “Here is someone who understands attending to the root.”
The author of the Record of Rites enumerates the workings of Heaven and humanity that have a root, thereby showing people that they must attend to that root. For the workings of the sage and of Heaven’s Way attain their fullness because they have a root. Once the gentleman perceives this, how could he possibly neglect the root? In former times, the author of the Record looked to all under Heaven to pursue learning that attends to the root. His meaning was this: that substance is established and its workings proceed is indeed the principle whereby Heaven and humanity are united; but illuminating that substance and applying it appropriately are especially the achievements of the gentleman’s self-cultivation.
Thus, the Way apprehended in the heart is called virtue. When virtue is great, it renews itself daily, enriching its abundant accomplishments; official functions cannot confine it. Principle followed in accordance with one’s nature is called the Way. When the Way is great, it is all-embracing and accords with what is fitting in each timely application; particular implements cannot constrain it. Speaking of its great trustworthiness, its sincerity is earnest and heartfelt, and its authentic essence has long inspired trust: how could pledges and agreements circumscribe it? Speaking of its great timeliness, primal vital energy circulates everywhere, and the subtlety of its consummate transformations is unfathomable: how could fixed divisions and limits bring it into uniformity?
Thus, although the workings of the sagely Way respond to affairs without partial feeling, that which orders and sustains them must constitute the root of sagehood. Although the workings of Heaven’s Way extend to all things without deliberate intention, that which governs them must constitute the root of Heaven. The gentleman takes the sage and Heaven’s Way as his own responsibility: how could he fail to examine them? He must look far back to the sages as his exemplars, hoping to fathom the source of their responses to what moves them; and he must look upward to Heaven as his standard, seeking to contemplate the reason for its ceaseless circulation. Having …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
見於聖道之淵源也而下學以達希聖之功藏
脩游息之有事將不務聖心之所蓄極者而同
其含弘也哉有見於天道之於穆也而盡人以
體合天之撰正業居學之不倦將不契化機之
所充塞者而符其妙運也哉吁天人之用必有
本而周君子之功以探本而密學者其務之哉
抑志本者爲己之功而吾心獨覺之地尤大本
之所從出者是故君子防嚴於幽獨以慎察乎
莫見莫顯之機則聖人天道將於吾心而凝其
===
原矣否則情以欲動心以物交其所謂本者何
自而察哉此聖人之立人極必曰主靜而存天
之心者恒於復乎見之故善務本者其要只在
謹獨
故樂行而倫清耳目聰明血氣和平移風
易俗天下皆寧
陳相
同考試官教諭張批以樂行總承天人常變士子
類能言之而此作獨貫串有條流暢不滯蓋經義之難得者
punctuated:
見於聖道之淵源也，而下學以達希聖之功，藏脩游息之有事，將不務聖心之所蓄極者，而同其含弘也哉？有見於天道之於穆也，而盡人以體合天之撰，正業居學之不倦，將不契化機之所充塞者，而符其妙運也哉？吁！天人之用必有本而周，君子之功以探本而密，學者其務之哉！抑志本者，爲己之功，而吾心獨覺之地，尤大本之所從出者。是故君子防嚴於幽獨，以慎察乎莫見莫顯之機，則聖人天道將於吾心而凝其原矣。否則，情以欲動，心以物交，其所謂本者，何自而察哉？此聖人之立人極必曰主靜，而存天之心者恒於復乎見之，故善務本者，其要只在謹獨。
故樂行而倫清，耳目聰明，血氣和平，移風易俗，天下皆寧。
陳相
同考試官教諭張批：以樂行總承天人常變，士子類能言之，而此作獨貫串有條，流暢不滯，蓋經義之難得者。
translation_en:
…insight into the deep source of the Way of the sages, and, through learning below, attains the achievement of aspiring to sagehood. In his endeavors in study and cultivation, recreation and rest, will he not attend to what the sage’s mind stores up and brings to its utmost, thereby sharing its capacious inclusiveness? Having insight into the profound mystery of the Way of Heaven, and fully realizing human capacities so as to embody and accord with Heaven’s workings, he tirelessly pursues his proper studies and dwells in learning. Will he not accord with the all-pervading impulse of transformation and match its wondrous operation? Ah! The workings of Heaven and humanity become comprehensive only through having a root; the gentleman’s efforts become thorough through probing that root. Students should devote themselves to this!
Yet directing one’s resolve toward the root is an effort undertaken for one’s own moral cultivation, and the realm of solitary awareness within our minds is precisely where the great root originates. Thus the gentleman guards himself strictly in solitude and obscurity, carefully examining the incipient workings of that which is most manifest though unseen, and most evident though hidden. Then the source of the sages’ Way and Heaven’s Way will become firmly established within our minds. Otherwise, when feelings are stirred by desires and the mind becomes entangled with external things, by what means can one discern this supposed root? This is why, in establishing the ultimate standard for humanity, the sage necessarily speaks of making stillness the governing principle, and why those who preserve Heaven’s heart always perceive it in Return (Fu). Thus, for those who aptly attend to the root, the essential point lies solely in vigilance in solitude.
“Thus, when music is practiced, human relationships become clear; ears and eyes become keen; blood and vital energy become harmonious and balanced; customs and habits are transformed; and all under Heaven are at peace.”
Chen Xiang
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: In taking the practice of music as the overarching theme encompassing Heaven and humanity, constancy and change, candidates generally can offer an explanation. This composition alone, however, links its points into an orderly whole and flows freely without obstruction. It is indeed a rare achievement among essays on the meaning of the Classics.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭劉批格調平正詞理疏鬯讀之有味
石音可謂深於樂者矣
考試官教授吳批敷揚樂化順暢可嘉
考試官教授李批得和平之旨
記者論樂教之行極其功用之大焉甚矣樂之
感人深也則夫功用之無所不周其亦樂化之
自致者歟見于樂記者其旨若曰大樂之在天
下不觀其始固無以探制作之原不究其終亦
無以徵功用之盛然則先王作樂以廣化果何
===
如耶今夫樂也者通於倫理統夫吾身而達之
天下者也惟患樂教之未行耳苟協乎天人而
緣情以達文者流行而莫禦備乎常變而盡制
以宣和者充周而不窮是以見諸倫也其羣分
也文以相接而彝倫昭攸敘之則其類聚也恩
以相維而人紀著肇脩之休倫其有弗清乎自
其化之及于人身也吾見聽德惟聰視遠惟明
謀哲竝行而耳目之官得其職矣剛氣不怒柔
氣不懾德性用事而血氣之運中其節矣雖人
punctuated:
同考試官教諭劉批：格調平正，詞理疏鬯，讀之有味，石音，可謂深於樂者矣。
考試官教授吳批：敷揚樂化，順暢可嘉。
考試官教授李批：得和平之旨。
記者論樂教之行，極其功用之大焉。甚矣，樂之感人深也！則夫功用之無所不周，其亦樂化之自致者歟？見于樂記者，其旨若曰：大樂之在天下，不觀其始，固無以探制作之原；不究其終，亦無以徵功用之盛。然則先王作樂以廣化，果何如耶？今夫樂也者，通於倫理，統夫吾身而達之天下者也。惟患樂教之未行耳。苟協乎天人而緣情以達文者，流行而莫禦；備乎常變而盡制以宣和者，充周而不窮。是以見諸倫也，其羣分也，文以相接，而彝倫昭攸敘之則；其類聚也，恩以相維，而人紀著肇脩之休。倫其有弗清乎？自其化之及于人身也，吾見聽德惟聰，視遠惟明，謀哲竝行，而耳目之官得其職矣；剛氣不怒，柔氣不懾，德性用事，而血氣之運中其節矣。雖人
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “The style is balanced and correct, the language and reasoning lucid and fluent. It rewards reading; ‘stone tones’ [?]. The writer may indeed be called deeply versed in music.”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “It expounds the transforming influence of music with commendable fluency.”
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “It captures the purport of harmony and equanimity.”
The author of the Record discusses the implementation of musical education, setting forth the full greatness of its efficacy. How profoundly music moves people! That its efficacy extends everywhere—is this not the natural result of its transforming influence? The meaning of the passage in the Record of Music seems to be this: as for great music in the world, without observing its beginnings, one assuredly cannot investigate the source of its creation; without examining its ultimate effects, one likewise cannot verify the fullness of its efficacy. What, then, was it actually like when the former kings created music to extend their transforming influence?
Music penetrates the principles of human relationships, encompassing our own persons and extending throughout the world. Our sole concern is that musical education has yet to be put into practice. If that which accords with Heaven and humanity, following the feelings to give them patterned expression, circulates without hindrance; and if that which accommodates both constancy and change, fully realizing its forms to spread harmony, pervades everything without exhaustion—then its effects become visible in human relationships. Where people divide into groups, they engage one another through cultivated forms, and the enduring relationships clearly display the principles of their proper ordering. Where those of like kind gather, they sustain one another through kindness, and the bonds of human society manifest the excellence of their initial cultivation. Could human relationships then fail to be clear?
As its transforming influence reaches the human person, I see hearing made acute in attending to virtue and sight made clear in looking afar. Deliberation and discernment operate together, and the faculties of ears and eyes fulfill their offices. Firm vital energy does not turn to anger; yielding vital energy does not give way to fear. Virtuous nature governs, and the circulation of blood and vital energy attains its proper measure. Although the human…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
之形體自有本然之良而所以啓順正之機者
謂非樂有以助之哉自其化之被於天下也吾
見挽頹風以歸正易流俗以還淳而興仁興讓
旣盡夫人而不變焉由是溥至治於無疆顯時
雍於有象而大順大化自舉斯世而咸寧焉雖
天下之風俗固有自然之應而所以廣孚化之
神者非樂其何以成之哉夫樂一也而以惇人
倫以脩吾身以維世道胥于此乎繫焉其功用
亦大矣乎是以先王隆之也雖然此特就其感
===
化言之耳而本不與焉蓋聖王於樂之未作反
情以和志比類以成行而無聲之樂在我夫然
後以和贊和而家齊國治天下平舉而措之裕
如耳是以協和風動必本諸欽明濬哲而永清
遵化亦自徽柔懿恭者得之也故語曰樂云樂
云鐘鼓云乎哉欲作樂以宣化者可以知所本
矣
第貳場
論
punctuated:
之形體自有本然之良，而所以啓順正之機者，謂非樂有以助之哉？自其化之被於天下也，吾見挽頹風以歸正，易流俗以還淳，而興仁興讓，旣盡夫人而不變焉。由是溥至治於無疆，顯時雍於有象，而大順大化，自舉斯世而咸寧焉。雖天下之風俗固有自然之應，而所以廣孚化之神者，非樂其何以成之哉？夫樂一也，而以惇人倫，以脩吾身，以維世道，胥于此乎繫焉，其功用亦大矣乎！是以先王隆之也。雖然，此特就其感化言之耳，而本不與焉。蓋聖王於樂之未作，反情以和志，比類以成行，而無聲之樂在我。夫然後以和贊和，而家齊、國治、天下平，舉而措之裕如耳。是以協和風動，必本諸欽明濬哲，而永清遵化，亦自徽柔懿恭者得之也。故語曰：「樂云樂云，鐘鼓云乎哉？」欲作樂以宣化者，可以知所本矣。

第貳場

論
translation_en:
…physical forms inherently possess their original goodness; yet could one say that music does nothing to help awaken the impulse toward harmony and rectitude? As for its transforming influence spreading throughout the realm, I see it arrest declining manners and restore uprightness, change prevailing customs and restore simplicity, and foster benevolence and deference, reaching everyone so that none remains unchanged [?]. Thus consummate order extends without limit, and the harmony of the age becomes visibly manifest. Through great concord and transformation, the entire world is brought to peace. Although the customs of the realm assuredly respond of themselves, how could the wondrous power of transformation be made broadly effective without music?

Music is one thing, yet strengthening human relationships, cultivating oneself, and sustaining the moral order of the world all depend upon it. How great its efficacy is! This is why the former kings exalted it. Nevertheless, this speaks only of its power to move and transform people; its foundation has not yet been considered. Before instituting music, the sage king returns to his true feelings to harmonize his intentions and aligns himself with what is of the same kind to perfect his conduct. Thus soundless music resides within him. Only then does he use harmony to promote harmony, bringing order to the family, good government to the state, and peace to all under Heaven, accomplishing these things with ease.

Thus, bringing people into concord and moving them as the wind does must be rooted in reverence, enlightenment, profound understanding, and wisdom. Likewise, enduring tranquillity and compliance with moral transformation are attained through goodness, gentleness, admirable virtue, and reverence. Hence the saying: “Music, music—is it merely bells and drums?” Those who wish to institute music to spread moral transformation may thereby understand what its foundation must be.

Second Session

Discourse

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
君子深造之以道
陳公相
同考試官教諭伍批氣格渾涵理致精確非灼見
道體者不能爲此語敬服敬服
同考試官教諭張批深造處正自得之學故下文
資深逢原皆在本體上求之是篇指出眞源足破常談
考試官教授吳批理學精深出自心得
考試官教授李批氣勢昌大議論高古
斯道有本然之體也君子學以致道者亦惟求
===
以契其體焉耳夫斯道昭布於天下而人之求
道者孰不以爲道最淺近可以徑造之也而不
知道原於天維天之命於穆不已此道之所自
來也故道雖充周而不可窮而其體實深遠而
不可測惟知其本深而于其深者造之則不離
乎深以造於道而亦不徑造以求其深斯之謂
善契其體而其所得者不淺矣彼舍其道而不
求者固不知所謂造而從事於道者乃或滯於
聞見狃於事爲彷彿於矯飾卜度之私途以爲
punctuated:
君子深造之以道
陳公相

同考試官教諭伍批：氣格渾涵，理致精確，非灼見道體者不能爲此語。敬服！敬服！
同考試官教諭張批：深造處正自得之學，故下文資深逢原皆在本體上求之。是篇指出眞源，足破常談。
考試官教授吳批：理學精深，出自心得。
考試官教授李批：氣勢昌大，議論高古。

斯道有本然之體也，君子學以致道者，亦惟求以契其體焉耳。夫斯道昭布於天下，而人之求道者，孰不以爲道最淺近，可以徑造之也？而不知道原於天，維天之命，於穆不已，此道之所自來也。故道雖充周而不可窮，而其體實深遠而不可測。惟知其本深，而于其深者造之，則不離乎深以造於道，而亦不徑造以求其深。斯之謂善契其體，而其所得者不淺矣。彼舍其道而不求者，固不知所謂造；而從事於道者，乃或滯於聞見，狃於事爲，彷彿於矯飾卜度之私途，以爲
translation_en:
“The gentleman pursues profound attainment by following the Way”
Chen Gongxiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu 伍, Instructor: “The spirit and style are capacious and richly contained, and the principles and their implications precisely expressed. Only someone with penetrating insight into the substance of the Way could write these words. Admirable! Admirable!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Profound attainment here is precisely the learning through which one gains understanding for oneself. Thus, in the passage that follows, drawing deeply upon one’s resources and encountering the source wherever one turns are both to be sought in the fundamental substance. This essay identifies the true source and amply refutes commonplace explanations.”

Comment by Examiner Wu 吳, Professor: “A profound and refined understanding of the learning of principle, arising from personal insight.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “Expansive vigor; lofty and classically grounded argument.”

This Way has an inherent substance. When the gentleman studies to attain the Way, he seeks only to accord with that substance. The Way is manifestly spread throughout the world. Among those who seek it, who does not suppose that it is utterly plain and accessible, and can be reached directly? Yet they do not understand that the Way originates in Heaven: “Heaven’s mandate—ah, how profound and unceasing!” This is the source from which the Way comes. Thus, although the Way pervades everything and cannot be exhausted, its substance is truly profound, far-reaching, and unfathomable. Only by recognizing its fundamental depth and pursuing attainment within that depth does one advance toward the Way without departing from its profundity, while also avoiding a headlong approach in seeking its depths. This is what it means to accord well with its substance, and what one gains thereby is not shallow.

Those who abandon the Way and do not seek it assuredly do not understand what attainment means. Yet even those who devote themselves to the Way may become confined to what they have heard and seen, habituated to practical activities, and wander indistinctly along the private bypaths of affectation and conjecture [?], supposing that…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
道在是而不知道之體不若是之淺矣竟亦何
得於道哉孟子曰君子深造之以道請以是而
繹其意今夫道根於性情顯于事物昭著于人
倫日用之間而愚夫愚婦可以與知與能固若
是其淺且近也苟有以造之亦不出乎淺近而
可至者而何以深造爲哉故索隱行怪雖有述
而不爲而人之爲道而遠人不可以爲道宜不
必深求之也而不知道雖不離於淺近而其體
則至淺而深焉所謂愚夫愚婦可知可能而聖
===
人天地有所不能盡者此也故必知此者而後
可以造于道使不知道之所以爲道則雖造之
亦無當於道也已不觀之掘井者乎彼語天下
之至深者水之體也故掘井者不欲得水則已
矣苟欲得水必由漸而至九仞而及泉焉則水
之本體可得而井渫爲可汲矣苟非有九仞之
功則雖日汲汲而求水不免爲棄井耳蓋水之
體本深而淺求之不可也深者本由於淺而驟
求之亦不可也然則道猶水也道之體猶水之
punctuated:
道在是，而不知道之體不若是之淺矣，竟亦何得於道哉？孟子曰：「君子深造之以道。」請以是而繹其意。今夫道根於性情，顯于事物，昭著于人倫日用之間，而愚夫愚婦可以與知與能，固若是其淺且近也。苟有以造之，亦不出乎淺近而可至者，而何以深造爲哉？故索隱行怪，雖有述而不爲；而人之爲道而遠人，不可以爲道，宜不必深求之也。而不知道雖不離於淺近，而其體則至淺而深焉。所謂愚夫愚婦可知可能，而聖人天地有所不能盡者，此也。故必知此者，而後可以造于道。使不知道之所以爲道，則雖造之，亦無當於道也已。
不觀之掘井者乎？彼語天下之至深者，水之體也。故掘井者不欲得水則已矣，苟欲得水，必由漸而至九仞而及泉焉，則水之本體可得，而井渫爲可汲矣。苟非有九仞之功，則雖日汲汲而求水，不免爲棄井耳。蓋水之體本深，而淺求之不可也；深者本由於淺，而驟求之亦不可也。然則道猶水也，道之體猶水之
translation_en:
…that the Way lies here, without knowing that its substance is not so shallow. What, ultimately, can they gain of the Way? Mengzi said: “The gentleman advances deeply into it by following the Way.” Let us unfold his meaning through these words. The Way is rooted in human nature and feelings, manifests itself in affairs and things, and is clearly evident in human relationships and everyday life. Even ordinary men and women can share in knowing and practicing it: it certainly seems so simple and accessible. If one has a means of advancing into it, what one can attain likewise lies within the simple and accessible. Why, then, must one advance deeply? Thus, one does not probe into hidden mysteries or practice strange deeds, even though these may win recognition; and when someone pursues the Way in a manner remote from human beings, this cannot constitute the Way. It would seem that one need not seek it deeply. Yet this fails to recognize that, although the Way never departs from the simple and accessible, its substance is profound even in its utmost simplicity. This is what is meant by saying that ordinary men and women can know and practice it, yet even sages and Heaven and Earth cannot exhaust it. Only after understanding this can one advance into the Way. If one does not understand what makes the Way the Way, then even advancing into it will fail to accord with it.
Have you not considered those who dig wells? Among the deepest things under Heaven is the substance of water. If a well-digger does not wish to obtain water, there is nothing more to say. But if he does wish to obtain it, he must proceed gradually until he reaches a depth of nine ren and comes to a spring. Then water itself can be obtained, and the well, cleared of mud, becomes fit for drawing water. Without the effort of digging nine ren, however anxiously he seeks water each day, his well will inevitably remain abandoned. For water’s substance lies deep, and it cannot be sought at a shallow depth. Depth must itself be reached through the shallows, so neither can it be sought all at once. Thus the Way is like water, and the substance of the Way is like water’s…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
深也知掘井之義則知所以造道矣何也道原
於天上天之載無聲無臭而體備於人夫固至
近而遠至淺而深者也世之學者苟非暴棄之
甚而自諉於不為者夫孰不欲造於道哉然而
求之于聞見者則以貫穿為功而不知道不如
是之支也求之於事為者則以鋪張為務而不
知道不如是之粗也求之於矯飾卜度之間者
則以矜持見解為有得而不知道不如是之虛
且擾也以是而造道則是善于買櫝而不善于
===
買珠其與足蹄涔而忘井養之不窮者埒也不
亦淺之乎其為道哉故君子不欲造道則已矣
苟欲造于道其可不識其所謂深者而造之乎
是故道本無聲而涉於聲者非道也則洗心退
藏以求合其不覩之理道本無臭而涉於臭者
非道也則反觀默識以求契其不聞之眞由是
由知而好由好而樂其序不可亂也莫非所以
造其深也由善信而美大由美大而聖神其功
不可缺也莫非所以造其深也由志學而立由
punctuated: 深也。知掘井之義，則知所以造道矣。何也？道原於天，上天之載，無聲無臭，而體備於人，夫固至近而遠、至淺而深者也。世之學者，苟非暴棄之甚而自諉於不為者，夫孰不欲造於道哉？然而求之于聞見者，則以貫穿為功，而不知道不如是之支也；求之於事為者，則以鋪張為務，而不知道不如是之粗也；求之於矯飾卜度之間者，則以矜持見解為有得，而不知道不如是之虛且擾也。以是而造道，則是善于買櫝而不善于買珠，其與足蹄涔而忘井養之不窮者埒也。不亦淺之乎，其為道哉？故君子不欲造道則已矣，苟欲造于道，其可不識其所謂深者而造之乎？是故道本無聲，而涉於聲者非道也，則洗心退藏，以求合其不覩之理；道本無臭，而涉於臭者非道也，則反觀默識，以求契其不聞之眞。由是，由知而好，由好而樂，其序不可亂也，莫非所以造其深也；由善信而美大，由美大而聖神，其功不可缺也，莫非所以造其深也；由志學而立，由
translation_en:
…depth. To understand the meaning of digging a well is to understand how to attain the Way. Why is this? The Way originates in Heaven. The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell, yet their substance is fully present in human beings. Thus the Way is at once supremely near yet distant, supremely shallow yet deep. Among the scholars of the world, unless they have utterly abandoned themselves and make excuses for doing nothing, who does not wish to attain the Way? Yet those who seek it in what they hear and see take comprehensive mastery as their achievement, not knowing that the Way is not so fragmented. Those who seek it in practical affairs make elaborate display their business, not knowing that the Way is not so coarse. Those who seek it amid affectation and conjecture regard their studied composure and interpretations as an attainment, not knowing that the Way is not so empty and confused. To approach the Way like this is to be adept at buying the casket but inept at buying the pearl. Such people are on a par with those who are content with water in a hoofprint and forget the inexhaustible nourishment of a well. Is their pursuit of the Way not shallow indeed?

Thus, if the gentleman does not wish to attain the Way, there is nothing more to say; but if he does wish to attain it, can he fail to recognize what is meant by its depth and advance into it? The Way is inherently soundless, and what involves sound is not the Way. He therefore cleanses his heart and withdraws into concealment, seeking accord with its unseen principle. The Way is inherently odorless, and what involves smell is not the Way. He therefore turns his gaze inward and apprehends in silence, seeking accord with its unheard truth. Proceeding thus, he moves from knowing it to loving it, and from loving it to delighting in it. This sequence must not be disordered: every stage is a means of reaching its depths. He advances from goodness and genuineness to beauty and greatness, and from beauty and greatness to sagehood and spiritual perfection. No part of this work may be omitted: every stage is a means of reaching its depths. He advances from setting his mind on learning to taking his stand, and from…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
立而不惑由不惑而知命而耳順而從心其幾
不容息也莫非所以造其深也至是則即其深
以為造而其造者以深由所造以求深而其深
者以得愈深而愈有所造愈造而愈見其深是
之謂深造而非以淺近求之也是之謂深造以
道而非以躐等得之也將見其功愈密其用愈
神資深逢原一以貫之而於穆不已之妙將與
天道而同體矣不猶浚井之深者功全於九仞
而得井冽寒泉之盛者乎故善掘井者求之深
===
而得水善求道者亦求之深而得道否則深者
不造而所造者非深則雖日從事於道而與道
邈不相干矣其何以為道哉然深造之學孟子
非徒言之亦允蹈之者也彼其語養氣旣曰氣
難言而又以有事勿正心勿忘勿助長繼之夫
豈不欲徑造頓悟以成配塞之功哉蓋曰難言
者正以其體之深也有事勿忘者所以造其深
也勿正而勿助長者所謂造之以道而不以有
我累之也不然何義惟其集而不惟其襲哉知
punctuated: 立而不惑，由不惑而知命，而耳順，而從心，其幾不容息也，莫非所以造其深也。至是，則即其深以為造，而其造者以深；由所造以求深，而其深者以得。愈深而愈有所造，愈造而愈見其深。是之謂深造，而非以淺近求之也；是之謂深造以道，而非以躐等得之也。將見其功愈密，其用愈神，資深逢原，一以貫之，而於穆不已之妙，將與天道而同體矣。不猶浚井之深者，功全於九仞，而得井冽寒泉之盛者乎？故善掘井者，求之深而得水；善求道者，亦求之深而得道。否則，深者不造，而所造者非深，則雖日從事於道，而與道邈不相干矣，其何以為道哉？然深造之學，孟子非徒言之，亦允蹈之者也。彼其語養氣，旣曰氣難言，而又以有事勿正、心勿忘、勿助長繼之。夫豈不欲徑造頓悟，以成配塞之功哉？蓋曰難言者，正以其體之深也；有事勿忘者，所以造其深也；勿正而勿助長者，所謂造之以道，而不以有我累之也。不然，何義惟其集，而不惟其襲哉？知
translation_en:
…from standing firm to freedom from perplexity, from freedom from perplexity to knowing Heaven’s mandate, then to an ear attuned to truth, and then to following the heart’s desires: the incipient workings of this progress admit no cessation. All are means of reaching the Way’s depths. At this point, one takes its depths as the object of attainment, and one’s attainment thereby deepens; one seeks depth through what one has attained, and thereby gains that depth. The deeper one goes, the more one attains; the more one attains, the more one perceives its depth. This is what is meant by profound attainment, rather than seeking it through the shallow and superficial. This is what is meant by profound attainment through the proper Way, rather than obtaining it by skipping stages. One will then find one’s efforts ever more meticulous and their operation ever more wondrous. Drawing upon deep resources, one encounters the source on every side, with a single principle running through it all. The subtle mystery of that profound and unceasing activity will then share one substance with the Way of Heaven. Is this not like someone who digs a well deep, completing the work at nine ren and obtaining an abundance of clear, cold spring water?

Thus, those skilled at digging wells seek deep and obtain water; those skilled at seeking the Way likewise seek deep and obtain the Way. Otherwise, if one fails to reach what is profound, and what one reaches is not profound, then even though one works daily at the Way, one remains remote from it and wholly unconnected with it. How could this count as pursuing the Way?

Yet Mengzi did not merely speak of the learning that leads to profound attainment: he truly practiced it as well. When discussing the nourishment of qi, he first said that qi was difficult to explain, and then continued with the injunctions to keep working at it without anticipating results, neither forgetting it in one’s heart nor helping it grow. Would he not have wished to proceed directly to attainment and sudden understanding, thereby achieving a qi that accords with righteousness and the Way and fills the space between Heaven and Earth? His saying that it was difficult to explain was precisely because its substance was profound. Keeping at the work and not forgetting it are the means of reaching its depths. Neither anticipating results nor helping it grow is what is meant by attaining it through the proper Way, without encumbering it with self-conscious interference. Otherwise, why must righteousness be accumulated, rather than seized in a single act? To know…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
所謂集義則知所謂深造以道而孟子之所以
能自得者此矣其諸造道者之準乎雖然天道
雖無聲臭然易知而大生者未嘗息焉特其主
張是者於穆而已矣君子亦豈能外淺近易見
者以求深哉不過即日用事物之中專於爲己
而去其務外爲人之私即所以爲深造耳故觀
於自得之義則知深造即龍蛇之蟄而非窅冥
之謂也如欲離去日用而別求所謂深其不流
而爲枯寂者幾希矣故深造者又不可離淺以
===
爲深
表
擬宋學士孫奭進無逸圖表天聖五年
張履祥
同考試官教諭劉批布格莊嚴含情剴切不擬而
麗不斲而工是能以忠愛自獻者宜錄以式
同考試官教授何批無逸之垂帝王之龜鑑子能
本周公納誨之旨發明進圖之意而詞復駢麗可誦足占素
養矣
punctuated:
所謂集義，則知所謂深造以道，而孟子之所以能自得者此矣。其諸造道者之準乎！雖然，天道雖無聲臭，然易知而大生者未嘗息焉，特其主張是者於穆而已矣。君子亦豈能外淺近易見者以求深哉？不過即日用事物之中，專於爲己，而去其務外爲人之私，即所以爲深造耳。故觀於自得之義，則知深造即龍蛇之蟄，而非窅冥之謂也。如欲離去日用，而別求所謂深，其不流而爲枯寂者幾希矣。故深造者又不可離淺以爲深。

表

擬宋學士孫奭進無逸圖表，天聖五年。
張履祥

同考試官教諭劉批：布格莊嚴，含情剴切，不擬而麗，不斲而工，是能以忠愛自獻者，宜錄以式。

同考試官教授何批：無逸之垂，帝王之龜鑑。子能本周公納誨之旨，發明進圖之意，而詞復駢麗可誦，足占素養矣。
translation_en:
…what is meant by accumulating righteousness, then one understands what is meant by pursuing profound learning in accordance with the Way. This is how Mengzi was able to attain understanding for himself. Is this not a standard for those seeking to reach the Way? Nevertheless, although the Way of Heaven has neither sound nor smell, its readily apprehensible operation and its vast generation of life never cease; what governs these is simply profound and silent. How, then, could the gentleman seek profundity outside what is accessible, familiar, and readily seen? It is merely a matter of devoting oneself to learning for one’s own improvement amid everyday affairs and things, removing the selfish desire to pursue outward things and learn for others’ approval. This is precisely how one pursues profound learning. Thus, by considering the meaning of attaining understanding for oneself, one realizes that profound learning resembles the hibernation of dragons and snakes; it does not mean something obscure and inscrutable. If one seeks to abandon everyday life and separately pursue what one calls profundity, there is little chance of avoiding a descent into lifeless stillness. Hence those pursuing profound learning must not seek profundity by departing from what is accessible.

Memorial

A memorial composed in the person of the Song Academician Sun Shi, presenting the Illustration of “Against Idleness” (Wuyi), in the fifth year of Tiansheng [1027].
By Zhang Lüxiang.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: The composition is dignified in structure and earnest in feeling. It is beautiful without imitation and accomplished without carving and polishing. Here is someone able to offer himself in loyalty and affection for his sovereign. It should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Professor: “Against Idleness,” handed down to posterity, is an oracle and mirror for emperors and kings. You have grounded your work in the Duke of Zhou’s purpose in offering admonition and elucidated the intention behind presenting the illustration. Moreover, your language is elegantly parallel and worthy of recitation. This amply reveals your long-cultivated attainments.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授吳批意深調雅菁華絕類
考試官敎授李批詞意懇到得獻納體
天聖五年某月某日龍圖閣學士臣孫奭
謹以所繪無逸圖
上進者伏以
運際豐亨
聖主勵勤民之治道存乾惕詞臣效匡
辟之猷論思取象於前言觀省期資於
上智仰呈
===
睿鑒俯竭愚衷臣奭誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊惟
君民一體君心之無怠由念切於憂民今
古一揆今事之罔愆由學先於稽古况持
盈保泰在初服之勵精而憂治危明係老
成之却慮故篤忠貞如元聖嘵勤規戒於
成王念王業本自艱難顧聖學宜先寅畏
爰陳無逸用代有終俯恤民依備敘田功
之疾苦仰欽天命歷陳國祚之短長義取
守文迪哲鑒四人之戒志存繩武克艱述
punctuated:
考試官敎授吳批：意深調雅，菁華絕類。
考試官敎授李批：詞意懇到，得獻納體。
天聖五年某月某日，龍圖閣學士臣孫奭，謹以所繪《無逸圖》上進者。伏以運際豐亨，聖主勵勤民之治；道存乾惕，詞臣效匡辟之猷。論思取象於前言，觀省期資於上智。仰呈睿鑒，俯竭愚衷。臣奭誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。
竊惟君民一體，君心之無怠，由念切於憂民；今古一揆，今事之罔愆，由學先於稽古。况持盈保泰，在初服之勵精；而憂治危明，係老成之却慮。故篤忠貞如元聖，嘵勤規戒於成王。念王業本自艱難，顧聖學宜先寅畏。爰陳《無逸》，用代有終。俯恤民依，備敘田功之疾苦；仰欽天命，歷陳國祚之短長。義取守文迪哲，鑒四人之戒；志存繩武克艱，述
translation_en:
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “The conception is profound and the tone elegant; its brilliance is beyond compare.”
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “The language and sentiments are earnest and fully expressed, fitting the form for offering counsel to the throne.”
On a certain day of a certain month in the fifth year of Tiansheng, your servant Sun Shi, Academician of the Longtu Pavilion, respectfully submits the illustrated Admonitions against Idleness that he has painted.
I humbly consider that, in an age of abundance and prosperity, the sage sovereign diligently pursues government devoted to the people; where the Way rests upon unremitting vigilance, a literary attendant offers plans to guide his ruler aright. In deliberation and reflection, I take earlier teachings as my models; through viewing and contemplation, I hope to assist Your Majesty’s supreme wisdom. I reverently present this for your discerning inspection, pouring out my humble sincerity. Your servant Shi, in deepest fear and trepidation, bows his head to the ground and repeatedly kowtows.
I humbly reflect that ruler and people form one body: the ruler’s heart remains free from indolence because his concern for the people is so earnest. Present and past follow a single standard: present affairs remain free from error because learning gives priority to examining antiquity. Moreover, preserving fullness and maintaining peace depend upon energetic application at the beginning of a reign; concern amid good government and apprehension amid enlightened rule depend upon the forethought of seasoned elders [?]. Thus, the Primal Sage, so steadfast in loyalty and constancy, earnestly and insistently admonished King Cheng. He reflected that the royal enterprise had originated in hardship, and considered that reverent caution should come first in a sage ruler’s learning. Accordingly, he set forth Admonitions against Idleness, thereby providing for a worthy conclusion [?]. Looking down with compassion upon the people’s means of subsistence, he fully described the hardships of agricultural labor; looking upward in reverence for Heaven’s mandate, he recounted in turn the long and short durations of dynastic rule. Its purport was to preserve inherited institutions and advance in wisdom, taking warning from the examples of four rulers; its intent was to follow ancestral achievements and master difficulties, recounting …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
三后之傳理正詞嚴語不嫌於忌諱憂深
思遠道有裨於勸懲馴至三代以來惟成
周之治爲盛故今千載而下稱周公之功
不衰慨自謇諤風微遂致憂勤日懈因得
賢而獻頌奚裨時幾緣王會以進圖祗恣
逸豫千秋一鑑莫開內照之明□扆六箴
無救外遊之侈惟逆耳之言不用故格心
之效罕聞非際
昌期曷伸忠悃茲蓋伏遇
===
〇〇〇〇
仁孝因心
誠明盡性禮隆
慈幄常朝每謹於問安學懋
經筵盛暑不倦於
御講重民而却異物念切如傷策士而取直言
懷虛若渴
克勤克儉惜夏禹之分陰
亦保亦臨勞周文之旲日憂常先於天下惠
punctuated: 三后之傳。理正詞嚴，語不嫌於忌諱；憂深思遠，道有裨於勸懲。馴至三代以來，惟成周之治爲盛，故今千載而下，稱周公之功不衰。慨自謇諤風微，遂致憂勤日懈。因得賢而獻頌，奚裨時幾？緣王會以進圖，祗恣逸豫。千秋一鑑，莫開內照之明；□扆六箴，無救外遊之侈。惟逆耳之言不用，故格心之效罕聞。非際昌期，曷伸忠悃？茲蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，仁孝因心，誠明盡性。禮隆慈幄，常朝每謹於問安；學懋經筵，盛暑不倦於御講。重民而却異物，念切如傷；策士而取直言，懷虛若渴。克勤克儉，惜夏禹之分陰；亦保亦臨，勞周文之旲日。憂常先於天下，惠
translation_en:
…the tradition handed down by the three sovereigns. His principles were correct and his language stern; his words did not shrink from forbidden subjects. His concern was profound and his thought far-reaching; his teaching aided encouragement and admonition. In the course of the Three Dynasties, the government of Zhou attained preeminence. Thus, even a thousand years later, praise for the Duke of Zhou’s achievements has not diminished. Alas, once the spirit of forthright remonstrance declined, anxious diligence grew daily more lax. What help in addressing the critical affairs of the time was an ode presented to celebrate the acquisition of worthy men? A picture presented on the occasion of a royal assembly merely indulged pleasure and ease. The “Mirror for a Thousand Autumns” failed to awaken the clarity of inward reflection; the “Six Admonitions for the □ Screen” [?] did nothing to curb extravagant excursions. Because words displeasing to the ear were not accepted, the effects of rectifying the ruler’s heart were seldom heard of. Without encountering a flourishing age, how could one give expression to loyal sincerity?

Now, reverently, we have encountered 〇〇〇〇 [four circles in the text], whose benevolence and filial devotion spring from the heart, and whose sincerity and understanding fully realize his nature. You accord exalted ceremonial respect to the Empress Dowager’s apartments, taking care at every regular morning audience to inquire after her well-being. You diligently pursue learning at the Classics Colloquium, attending the imperial lectures without flagging even in the height of summer. Valuing the people, you reject exotic rarities, caring for them as though they were injured. Examining scholars through policy questions, you select forthright counsel, receiving it with an open mind and a thirst for advice. Diligent and frugal, you treasure every fraction of time, like Yu of Xia; protecting and watching over your people, you labor through the long day [?], like King Wen of Zhou. Your concerns always precede those of all under Heaven, and your beneficence…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
允浹於民間但
聖敬緝熙雖已嚴於穆穆而臣愚勤懇猶欲效
其區區伏念臣奭學非博古志切匡時微
言謬採於賢科薄技僭登於胄監早遇
先皇之眷愧叨良弼之稱說命三篇偶講讀之
悟
主抗疏十事恐封祀之勞民幸荷
優涵俾塵
法從仰
===
萬幾之重徒抱杞憂懷一得之愚每思芹獻
雖泰華不增高於土壤而涓流竊委潤於
滄溟謂治慎無虞怠勝無如敬勝之吉而
道形有象聞知不若見知之真逸戒爰取
諸周書圖畫因屬之繪事矢心模寫極意
編摩察閭里之怨咨務曲盡其情狀考廟
堂之鑒戒已備極其形容上下七君理亂
安危之畢備後先二代吉凶修短之俱陳
于遊于田展卷足為永戒攸訓攸若披圖
punctuated: 允浹於民間。但聖敬緝熙，雖已嚴於穆穆，而臣愚勤懇，猶欲效其區區。伏念臣奭，學非博古，志切匡時；微言謬採於賢科，薄技僭登於胄監。早遇先皇之眷，愧叨良弼之稱。《說命》三篇，偶講讀之悟主；抗疏十事，恐封祀之勞民。幸荷優涵，俾塵法從。仰萬幾之重，徒抱杞憂；懷一得之愚，每思芹獻。雖泰華不增高於土壤，而涓流竊委潤於滄溟。謂治慎無虞，怠勝無如敬勝之吉；而道形有象，聞知不若見知之真。逸戒爰取諸《周書》，圖畫因屬之繪事。矢心模寫，極意編摩。察閭里之怨咨，務曲盡其情狀；考廟堂之鑒戒，已備極其形容。上下七君，理亂安危之畢備；後先二代，吉凶修短之俱陳。于遊于田，展卷足為永戒；攸訓攸若，披圖
translation_en:
…truly reaches throughout the populace. Yet although Your Majesty’s reverence grows ever more luminous and is already manifest in solemn dignity, I, your ignorant servant, in my earnest devotion still wish to offer my humble service. I respectfully reflect that I, your servant Shi, lack broad learning in antiquity, yet am deeply committed to setting the age aright. My modest words were undeservedly accepted in the examination for worthy men, and my meager abilities presumptuously gained me a place in the Directorate of Education. Early on I received the late emperor’s favor, and felt ashamed to be undeservedly called a worthy counselor. In lecturing and reading on the three chapters of “The Charge to Yue,” I happened to enlighten my sovereign; in submitting a forthright memorial on ten matters, I feared that the sacrificial observances would overburden the people. Fortunately, I received generous indulgence and was permitted unworthily to join the emperor’s attendant officials.

Looking up to the weight of Your Majesty’s myriad affairs, I can only harbor fears like the man of Qi who feared the sky would fall. Cherishing the occasional insight of a foolish man, I constantly think of offering it, like a humble gift of celery. Though Mounts Tai and Hua gain no height from a little soil, a tiny stream may still contribute its moisture to the vast sea. I hold that government must remain vigilant when no danger is apparent: allowing negligence to prevail cannot compare with the good fortune of letting reverence prevail [?]. And when the Way is given visible form, knowledge gained through hearing is less immediate and true than knowledge gained through seeing. Thus I took warnings against ease from the Book of Zhou and commissioned their depiction in paintings. I devoted myself wholeheartedly to rendering them and applied my utmost care to compiling the work. Examining the grievances and sighs of the villages, I sought to convey their circumstances and feelings in every detail; investigating the lessons and warnings for the court, I fully represented their forms. The seven rulers, earlier and later, furnish a complete account of order and disorder, security and peril; the two successive dynasties display alike good and ill fortune, and long and short spans of rule. When going on excursions or hunts, unrolling this volume will provide an enduring warning; as for what to take as instruction and what to follow, opening the illustrations…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
已有明徵無煩告語之再三足備
鑒觀於萬一思如馭朽在觸目以驚心慮若臨
深貴由象而得意倘蒙置諸
座右可希戶牖之銘若常接於
御前庶比韋弦之義學非口耳道切身心未敢
謂臣之言可比周公之言惟日冀
君之治遠邁成王之治伏願
德隆廣運
業懋永圖
===
祗若乎無聲無臭之天
敬慎於不睹不聞之地
春祈秋報思周公之訓夢寐不忘
日就月將達成王之聰羹牆如見臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹以所繪無逸圖奉
表隨
進以
聞
punctuated: 已有明徵，無煩告語之再三，足備鑒觀於萬一。思如馭朽，在觸目以驚心；慮若臨深，貴由象而得意。倘蒙置諸座右，可希戶牖之銘；若常接於御前，庶比韋弦之義。學非口耳，道切身心。未敢謂臣之言可比周公之言，惟日冀君之治遠邁成王之治。伏願德隆廣運，業懋永圖，祗若乎無聲無臭之天，敬慎於不睹不聞之地。春祈秋報，思周公之訓，夢寐不忘；日就月將，達成王之聰，羹牆如見。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屛營之至，謹以所繪無逸圖奉表隨進以聞。
translation_en:
…there is already clear evidence, requiring no repeated verbal admonition and sufficient to furnish at least some guidance for Your Majesty’s scrutiny. Let your thoughts be as cautious as if driving with rotten reins: what meets the eye should stir vigilance in the heart. Let your concern be as keen as if standing above a deep abyss: what matters is to grasp the meaning through the images. If you graciously place this beside your seat, it may aspire to serve like the admonitory inscriptions on doors and windows; if it is constantly before Your Majesty, it may fulfill a purpose like the leather thong and bowstring worn as reminders of self-restraint. Learning is not merely a matter of mouth and ears; the Way bears directly upon one’s person and heart. I dare not claim that your servant’s words can compare with those of the Duke of Zhou. I hope daily only that Your Majesty’s governance will far surpass that of King Cheng.

I humbly pray that your virtue may grow exalted and extend far and wide, and that your achievements may flourish in plans for lasting rule; that you may reverently accord with Heaven, which has neither sound nor scent, and remain respectful and vigilant even where nothing is seen or heard. At the spring prayers and autumn thanksgiving sacrifices, ponder the Duke of Zhou’s admonitions, forgetting them not even in dreams. Advancing daily and progressing monthly, attain King Cheng’s discernment, as though seeing the Duke before you in your broth and upon the wall.

Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your sacred Majesty, cannot contain his intense emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit the illustrated Admonitions against Ease (Wuyi tu) together with this memorial for Your Majesty’s consideration.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
第叁場
策
第一問
李繼華
同考試官教諭吳批揄揚
聖學歸本於敬是涵濡
至教而有得者且美不忘規忠愛勃勃錄而薦之可以奉大對矣
同考試官教諭張批
聖學淵源子能揄揚其盛而末寓規諷語復諄切是大有神於論思者取
===
之非但以文也
考試官教授吳批縫掖之士有能鋪張
盛美陳見悃忱如子者耶敬服敬服
考試官教授李批得論思之旨取之
聖人所以繼天立極而君師乎天下者本
之以持敬之心而務學以明之虛受以廣
之夫是以德進於無疆而業垂於有永也
何也天之生人衆矣而顧以神聖授之一
人是天之獨厚之也天之所以獨厚之者
punctuated:
第叁場
策
第一問
李繼華

同考試官教諭吳批：揄揚聖學，歸本於敬，是涵濡至教而有得者。且美不忘規，忠愛勃勃，錄而薦之，可以奉大對矣。

同考試官教諭張批：聖學淵源，子能揄揚其盛，而末寓規諷，語復諄切，是大有神於論思者。取之非但以文也。

考試官教授吳批：縫掖之士，有能鋪張盛美、陳見悃忱如子者耶？敬服！敬服！

考試官教授李批：得論思之旨，取之。

聖人所以繼天立極而君師乎天下者，本之以持敬之心，而務學以明之，虛受以廣之。夫是以德進於無疆，而業垂於有永也。何也？天之生人衆矣，而顧以神聖授之一人，是天之獨厚之也。天之所以獨厚之者，
translation_en:
Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Li Jihua

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: He extols imperial learning and traces its foundation to reverent attentiveness. Here is someone who has been steeped in the highest teaching and has gained from it. Moreover, in praising he does not forget to admonish; loyalty and devotion brim over. Selected and recommended, he could worthily submit a response at the Palace Examination.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: You can extol the flourishing of imperial learning and its profound sources, while incorporating admonition and indirect remonstrance at the end. Your words are also earnest and forceful. You have a remarkable gift for deliberation and counsel. I select this essay for more than its literary merit.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: Among scholars in their broad-sleeved robes, is there anyone who can expound the splendid virtues and display heartfelt sincerity as you do? I admire you! I admire you!

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: He grasps the purpose of deliberation and counsel. Select this essay.

The sage succeeds Heaven, establishes the supreme standard, and acts as ruler and teacher of all under Heaven by taking a heart of sustained reverent attentiveness as his foundation, diligently pursuing learning to illuminate it, and receptively accepting instruction to broaden it. Thus his virtue advances without limit, and his achievements endure forever. Why is this? Heaven gives birth to multitudes of people, yet bestows divine sagacity upon just one person: this is Heaven’s exceptional favor toward him. The reason Heaven favors him alone is …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
豈慮一人之身非神聖不足以成之哉正
以天下之眾而非有神聖者以作之君師
則固無以治而教之耳是天之所以厚聖
人者乃所以厚天下也天以其厚天下者
而萃於聖人之一身聖人以其萃於一身
者而推之天下是天地聖人之心互相體
會若有意以營乎其間而必欲斯世斯民
之得所也然則聖人之心上以受命於天
而下以立命於民是其心宜有以自豫矣
===
而何必於憂惕之不遑其心宜有以自足
自用矣而何必於問學之不倦聽納之不
疑也殊不知聖人不以天之厚我者自恃
而常以天之所以厚我者自懼一日萬幾
懼吾未有以勝之也而豈容以不敬義理
無窮懼吾未有以明之也而豈容以不學
忠言逆耳懼吾未有以受之也而豈容以
不虛以是而考之古之帝王若堯舜禹湯
文武神聖天授莫之與京矣而其心則曷
punctuated: 豈慮一人之身非神聖不足以成之哉？正以天下之眾，而非有神聖者以作之君師，則固無以治而教之耳。是天之所以厚聖人者，乃所以厚天下也。天以其厚天下者而萃於聖人之一身，聖人以其萃於一身者而推之天下，是天地聖人之心互相體會，若有意以營乎其間，而必欲斯世斯民之得所也。然則聖人之心，上以受命於天，而下以立命於民，是其心宜有以自豫矣，而何必於憂惕之不遑？其心宜有以自足自用矣，而何必於問學之不倦、聽納之不疑也？殊不知聖人不以天之厚我者自恃，而常以天之所以厚我者自懼。一日萬幾，懼吾未有以勝之也，而豈容以不敬？義理無窮，懼吾未有以明之也，而豈容以不學？忠言逆耳，懼吾未有以受之也，而豈容以不虛？以是而考之古之帝王，若堯舜禹湯文武，神聖天授，莫之與京矣，而其心則曷
translation_en: …could it be out of concern that a single individual could not be brought to fulfillment without divine sagacity? It is precisely because, without someone possessed of divine sagacity to serve as ruler and teacher to the multitudes under Heaven, there would be no means of governing and instructing them. Thus, Heaven’s generosity toward the sage is its means of showing generosity toward all under Heaven. Heaven concentrates in the sage’s single person that through which it benefits all under Heaven; the sage extends to all under Heaven what has been concentrated in his single person. In this way, the hearts of Heaven and Earth and of the sage comprehend and embody one another, as though deliberately working together to ensure that this age and its people find their proper place. The sage’s heart thus receives its mandate from Heaven above and establishes the foundation of life for the people below. Surely, then, his heart ought to be at ease: why must he remain ceaselessly anxious and vigilant? Surely his heart ought to be content with itself and rely on its own judgment: why must he be tireless in inquiry and learning, and unhesitating in hearing and accepting counsel? Such questions fail to recognize that the sage does not take Heaven’s generosity toward him as grounds for self-assurance. Rather, he constantly finds cause for apprehension in the very reason Heaven has treated him so generously. With ten thousand affairs arising in a single day, he fears that he may not be equal to them: how could he permit himself to lack reverent attentiveness? With moral principles inexhaustible, he fears that he may not understand them: how could he permit himself not to learn? Since loyal counsel grates on the ear, he fears that he may not be able to accept it: how could he permit himself not to be receptive? If we examine the emperors and kings of antiquity in this light—Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu—their divine sagacity was bestowed by Heaven, and none could equal them. Yet how did their hearts ever…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
嘗以之自恃哉故人知其治化之成於天
下者有雍和熈皞之盛而不知其本原之
地隱微之中固有曰嚴曰慎而非人之所
能窺者是故曰兢兢曰業業曰祗台曰昭
格曰緝熈執競此其持敬之心所以畏天
者不敢怠也曰允執厥中曰惟精惟一曰
不自滿假曰日新又新曰望道未見敬義
交修此其務實之學所以憲天者不容已
也夫既有神聖之資而存之以無敢暇豫
===
之心濟之以惟日不足之學則德業之盛
固已各臻其極而當時輔理成化之臣宜
無有能增益之者然臯陶之謨益稷之戒
伊尹之訓周召之誥每惓惓焉蓋不因其
君之已聖而遂忘其獻納之忠而爲之君
者亦不自以爲聖而遂忽於聽受之益此
其君臣交相儆戒而均之以畏天爲心上
下互相資益而均之以憲天爲學唐虞三
代之治所以臻於隆盛之極而數聖人者
punctuated: 嘗以之自恃哉？故人知其治化之成於天下者，有雍和熈皞之盛，而不知其本原之地、隱微之中，固有曰嚴曰慎，而非人之所能窺者。是故曰兢兢，曰業業，曰祗台，曰昭格，曰緝熈執競，此其持敬之心，所以畏天者不敢怠也。曰允執厥中，曰惟精惟一，曰不自滿假，曰日新又新，曰望道未見，敬義交修，此其務實之學，所以憲天者不容已也。夫既有神聖之資，而存之以無敢暇豫之心，濟之以惟日不足之學，則德業之盛，固已各臻其極，而當時輔理成化之臣，宜無有能增益之者。然臯陶之謨、益稷之戒、伊尹之訓、周召之誥，每惓惓焉。蓋不因其君之已聖，而遂忘其獻納之忠；而爲之君者，亦不自以爲聖，而遂忽於聽受之益。此其君臣交相儆戒，而均之以畏天爲心；上下互相資益，而均之以憲天爲學。唐虞三代之治，所以臻於隆盛之極，而數聖人者
translation_en:
…ever relied complacently upon these gifts? Thus people know that their governance and transforming influence brought abundant harmony and radiant concord to All under Heaven. Yet they do not know that, at its source, within the hidden recesses of their hearts, lay a solemnity and vigilance beyond others’ ability to perceive. Hence the expressions “watchful,” “cautious,” “my reverence,” “reaching luminously above,” and “continuing in brightness and steadfast strength”: these describe their reverent hearts, through which they stood in awe of Heaven and dared not grow lax. The expressions “truly hold fast to the mean,” “be discerning and single-minded,” “do not complacently deem oneself accomplished,” “renew yourself daily, and renew yourself yet again,” and “look toward the Way as though you had not yet seen it,” together with the joint cultivation of reverence and righteousness, describe their learning directed toward substantive achievement, through which they unceasingly modeled themselves upon Heaven.

Possessing the endowments of divine sages, they preserved them with hearts that dared not indulge in leisure or ease, and supplemented them with learning for which even the whole day seemed insufficient. Their virtue and accomplishments thus each reached the highest degree of excellence, and it would seem that the ministers who assisted their government and brought their transforming influence to fruition could have added nothing further. Yet Gao Yao’s counsels, Yi’s and Ji’s admonitions, Yi Yin’s instructions, and the proclamations of the Dukes of Zhou and Shao were invariably earnest and devoted. Because their rulers were already sages, these ministers did not therefore forget their loyal duty to offer counsel; nor did the rulers consider themselves sages and therefore disregard the benefit of listening to and accepting it. Thus rulers and ministers warned and admonished one another, alike taking awe of Heaven as their guiding disposition; superiors and subordinates supported and benefited one another, alike making emulation of Heaven the aim of their learning. This was how the government of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties attained the utmost flourishing, while those several sages…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
固若乎曠世而相感也漢唐以來英誼間
出雖未可以神聖言而亦天之所厚寄以
君師之責者然不能體天之心而持敬務
學以濟其所不及則其所就之卑也固宜
自今觀之牢祀孔子若知所宗矣而不事
詩書雖陸生無以挽其習詔置博士若有
所興矣而未遑禮樂雖賈誼無以正其趨
表章六經者志非不銳也卒馳於窮兵而
輪臺之悔莫追召集名儒者講非不勤也
===
卒昵於恭顯而甘露之危途釀親幸太學
徒高息馬論道之風駕臨辟雍未究執經
問難之實考定五經者宜其有稽古之益
也其如貞觀之治大綱未正何更日侍讀
者宜其有納約之功也其如開元之政鮮
克有終何有宋諸君多稱好學然務博覽
而義理未明工書翰而身心無補賢如二
程而不見知學如朱子而不見用類皆外
侈美觀之具內無敬學之心卽其侍從諸
punctuated:
固若乎曠世而相感也。漢唐以來，英誼間出，雖未可以神聖言，而亦天之所厚寄以君師之責者。然不能體天之心而持敬務學，以濟其所不及，則其所就之卑也固宜。自今觀之，牢祀孔子，若知所宗矣，而不事詩書，雖陸生無以挽其習；詔置博士，若有所興矣，而未遑禮樂，雖賈誼無以正其趨。表章六經者，志非不銳也，卒馳於窮兵，而輪臺之悔莫追；召集名儒者，講非不勤也，卒昵於恭顯，而甘露之危途釀。親幸太學，徒高息馬論道之風；駕臨辟雍，未究執經問難之實。考定五經者，宜其有稽古之益也，其如貞觀之治大綱未正何？更日侍讀者，宜其有納約之功也，其如開元之政鮮克有終何？
有宋諸君，多稱好學，然務博覽而義理未明，工書翰而身心無補。賢如二程而不見知，學如朱子而不見用，類皆外侈美觀之具，內無敬學之心。卽其侍從諸
translation_en:
…indeed seemed to respond to one another across distant ages. From the Han and Tang onward, outstanding and righteous rulers [?] appeared from time to time. Though they could not yet be called divine sages, they were nevertheless men to whom Heaven had entrusted the weighty responsibility of serving as rulers and teachers. Yet they could not embody Heaven’s mind, maintain reverence, and diligently pursue learning to remedy their shortcomings. It was therefore only natural that their achievements should have been so modest. Viewed from our own day, offering sacrificial animals to Confucius seemed to show an understanding of whom to revere; yet the ruler did not apply himself to the Odes and Documents, and even Master Lu could not reform his habits. Decreeing the appointment of Erudites seemed to promise a revival of learning; yet the ruler found no time for rites and music, and even Jia Yi could not set his course aright. The ruler who gave prominence to the Six Classics certainly had ardent ambitions, but he ultimately plunged into exhausting warfare, and his repentance at Luntai came too late to undo the harm. The ruler who assembled renowned Confucian scholars certainly pursued their instruction diligently, but he ultimately became intimate with Gong and Xian, and danger was bred during the Ganlu era [?]. Personally visiting the Imperial University merely exalted the example of resting the warhorses and discussing the Way; an imperial visit to the Biyong did not fully realize the substance of taking up the classics and questioning difficult points. The ruler who had the Five Classics critically established should have benefited from examining antiquity; yet what are we to make of the fact that the fundamental principles of government remained unrectified during the Zhenguan reign? The ruler who had lecturers attend him on alternating days should have benefited from their conveying counsel in simple terms; yet what are we to make of the failure of the Kaiyuan government to sustain its good beginnings?
The rulers of the Song were often praised for their love of learning. Yet they pursued wide reading without clarifying moral principles, and excelled at calligraphy and literary composition without benefiting their own persons and minds. Men as worthy as the two Cheng brothers went unrecognized, and a scholar as learned as Master Zhu went unemploy­ed. For the most part, these rulers outwardly lavished attention on the trappings of fine appearances, while inwardly lacking a reverent commitment to learning. Even their attendant officials…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
臣或俳優而不根或靡麗而無當旣不足
以稱啓沃至於正言弼直經學淵源之士
則又厭而不聽甚者斥而遠之所謂聽古
樂惟恐臥聞新聲卽不知倦也欲論思之
有益而聖學之復明也得乎此所以雜霸
雜夷仁柔不振而其治去唐虞三代遠甚
矣天啓我
高皇帝應運而作得國之正本與帝王同符敬
學之傳又於精一默契初輯干戈卽遣祭
===
於闕里初置郡邑卽申誥乎學規操存之
要無暇逸則於學士宋濂發之堯舜之治
皆由中則於侍郎曾魯發之存心有錄見
人君以天之心爲心也而欽若之道以崇
省躬有錄見人臣以君之心爲心也而交
儆之誠益至疏尚書洪範於座右其揖箕
子於神交乎書大學衍義於兩廡其臣德
秀於異代乎雖
聖衷之蘊廣遠難窺而敷言具存焯爍可頌二
punctuated:
臣，或俳優而不根，或靡麗而無當，旣不足以稱啓沃。至於正言弼直、經學淵源之士，則又厭而不聽，甚者斥而遠之。所謂聽古樂惟恐臥，聞新聲卽不知倦也。欲論思之有益，而聖學之復明也，得乎？此所以雜霸雜夷，仁柔不振，而其治去唐虞三代遠甚矣。
天啓我高皇帝應運而作，得國之正，本與帝王同符；敬學之傳，又於精一默契。初輯干戈，卽遣祭於闕里；初置郡邑，卽申誥乎學規。操存之要，無暇逸，則於學士宋濂發之；堯舜之治，皆由中，則於侍郎曾魯發之。存心有錄，見人君以天之心爲心也，而欽若之道以崇；省躬有錄，見人臣以君之心爲心也，而交儆之誠益至。疏《尚書》洪範於座右，其揖箕子於神交乎？書《大學衍義》於兩廡，其臣德秀於異代乎？雖聖衷之蘊廣遠難窺，而敷言具存，焯爍可頌。二
translation_en:
…ministers attending them were either like entertainers, without grounding, or florid and extravagant, without substance; they were thus unworthy of being called men who enlightened and nourished the sovereign’s mind. As for scholars whose upright words offered frank correction and whose classical learning had deep roots, the rulers disliked them and would not listen; worse still, they dismissed them and sent them away. This is what is meant by fearing one will fall asleep when listening to ancient music, yet knowing no weariness when hearing new tunes. Could one expect deliberation and reflection to prove beneficial, and sagely learning to shine forth again? This is why their rule mingled hegemonic practices with barbarian ways, remaining soft and feeble in its benevolence, and fell far short of the rule of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties.
Heaven inspired our Emperor Gao to arise in response to the destined time. The legitimacy with which he acquired the realm accorded with that of the ancient emperors and kings; in transmitting reverence for learning, he also tacitly accorded with their teaching of refinement and single-mindedness. As soon as he had stilled warfare, he dispatched an envoy to offer sacrifice at Queli; as soon as he established prefectures and counties, he issued further instructions concerning school regulations. He explained to Academician Song Lian that the essential requirement for maintaining the mind was to allow no idle ease; he explained to Vice Minister Zeng Lu that the government of Yao and Shun proceeded entirely from within. His record on preserving the mind shows that a ruler takes Heaven’s mind as his own, thereby exalting the way of reverent conformity to Heaven. His record on examining oneself shows that a minister takes his ruler’s mind as his own, thereby bringing the sincerity of mutual admonition to still greater perfection. In setting out the Great Plan chapter of the Book of Documents beside his seat, was he not saluting Jizi in spiritual communion? In having the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning inscribed in the two side galleries, was he not making Zhen Dexiu his minister across the ages? Although the contents of his sagely mind were so vast and far-reaching as to be difficult to fathom, his pronouncements remain fully preserved, radiant and worthy of praise. The Two…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
帝三王此振其緒
聖子神孫此培其基矣在
文皇帝得之而敦崇道術故不惟表章經書以
廣聖賢傳心之典而又闡著心法以揭帝
王創守之規在
章皇帝得之而雅懋聖脩故不但編緝倫書秩
秩乎嘉言善行之具載而又
親製帝訓懍懍乎父作子述之維艱至若增籩
豆舞佾之儀於孔廟者我
===
純皇帝也心旣切於崇儒訓獨先於務學乃猶
日就經筵時歷寒暑而不輟則所以涵養
此心者無寧時矣廣校宮橫舍之制於闕
里者我
敬皇帝也志旣殷於慕聖禮不靳於尊師乃猶
虛受箴規語涉危亡而不忌則所以緝熙
此學者無逸志矣此皆學術之大後先一
揆者曁我
世宗肅皇帝則益闡揚而光大之朝御
punctuated: 帝三王，此振其緒；聖子神孫，此培其基矣。在文皇帝得之，而敦崇道術，故不惟表章經書，以廣聖賢傳心之典，而又闡著心法，以揭帝王創守之規。在章皇帝得之，而雅懋聖脩，故不但編緝倫書，秩秩乎嘉言善行之具載，而又親製帝訓，懍懍乎父作子述之維艱。至若增籩豆舞佾之儀於孔廟者，我純皇帝也。心旣切於崇儒，訓獨先於務學，乃猶日就經筵，時歷寒暑而不輟，則所以涵養此心者無寧時矣。廣校宮橫舍之制於闕里者，我敬皇帝也。志旣殷於慕聖，禮不靳於尊師，乃猶虛受箴規，語涉危亡而不忌，則所以緝熙此學者無逸志矣。此皆學術之大，後先一揆者。曁我世宗肅皇帝，則益闡揚而光大之，朝御
translation_en:
…the Emperors and Three Kings: through this their legacy was renewed; for his sagely sons and divine grandsons, through this the foundation was strengthened. Emperor Wen attained this and deeply honored the Way and its learning. Thus he not only gave prominence to the canonical books, extending the textual tradition through which sages and worthies transmitted the mind, but also elucidated the method of cultivating the mind, setting forth the principles by which emperors and kings establish and preserve their rule. Emperor Zhang attained this and earnestly cultivated sagely virtue. Thus he not only compiled a book on human relations, systematically recording worthy sayings and good deeds in full, but also personally composed Imperial Instructions, deeply mindful of the difficulty of a father’s founding work and a son’s continuation of it.

As for the emperor who augmented the ritual provisions for bamboo and wooden offering vessels and ranks of dancers in the temple of Confucius, this was our Emperor Chun. His heart was already intent on honoring Confucian learning, and his instructions gave foremost place to diligent study. Yet he still attended the Classics Colloquium daily, continuing without interruption through cold and heat. Thus he never rested in nurturing this mind. The emperor who expanded the provision of school buildings and instructional quarters [?] at Queli was our Emperor Jing. His aspiration to emulate the sage was already fervent, and he spared nothing in the rites honoring teachers. Yet he still received admonitions with an open mind, taking no offense even when their words touched upon peril and ruin. Thus he never relaxed his resolve to advance and illuminate this learning. These were all great achievements in learning and the practice of the Way, following one consistent standard from earlier reigns to later ones. When it came to our Emperor Shizong Su, he further expounded and magnified it. At court he attended…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
經筵集思廣益退臨
書幄寡欲清心敬一之旨發千聖未發之心
源箴解之文明諸儒未明之道體以此
敬天法祖以此恭巳臨民攬獨斷之權而六服
羣辟罔不共其令鑒先世之弊而中官外
戚無所售其私是蓋道根於心心一於敬
所以享國長久天下乂安有由然哉今我
皇上當作君作師之初隆善繼善述之道文命
所被薄海嚮風於時肇舉
===
===
經筵以資輔理
親臨大學以導敬敷
便殿之鼓載鳴而垂紳進講者玉立成均之
蹕甫駐而擊磬雅歌者雲從道闡圖書兆龜
龍之復出光生俎豆將麟鳳以來儀是誠
躬帝王之資而興唐虞三代之學者也謂
尚不足以風天下乎昔者辟雍創於鎬京
而周詠思服泮宮環於璧水而魯頌采芹
愚生竊在菁莪樂育之中敢自後於橋門
punctuated:
經筵，集思廣益；退臨書幄，寡欲清心。敬一之旨，發千聖未發之心源；箴解之文，明諸儒未明之道體。以此敬天法祖，以此恭巳臨民。攬獨斷之權，而六服羣辟罔不共其令；鑒先世之弊，而中官外戚無所售其私。是蓋道根於心，心一於敬，所以享國長久、天下乂安，有由然哉！
今我皇上當作君作師之初，隆善繼善述之道，文命所被，薄海嚮風。於時肇舉經筵，以資輔理；親臨大學，以導敬敷。便殿之鼓載鳴，而垂紳進講者玉立；成均之蹕甫駐，而擊磬雅歌者雲從。道闡圖書，兆龜龍之復出；光生俎豆，將麟鳳以來儀。是誠躬帝王之資，而興唐虞三代之學者也。謂尚不足以風天下乎？
昔者辟雍創於鎬京，而周詠思服；泮宮環於璧水，而魯頌采芹。愚生竊在菁莪樂育之中，敢自後於橋門
translation_en:
…at the Classics Colloquium, he gathered others’ ideas to broaden his understanding; withdrawing to his curtained study, he restrained his desires and cleared his mind. His teaching on reverent concentration disclosed the wellspring of the mind that a thousand sages had never disclosed; his explanations of admonitions illuminated the substance of the Way that earlier scholars had never illuminated. Through this he revered Heaven and followed his ancestors; through this he comported himself reverently and governed the people. He held the power of sole decision, and none of the lords throughout the six zones of submission failed to obey his commands. Taking warning from the abuses of former ages, he left eunuchs and imperial relatives by marriage no opportunity to advance their private interests. This was surely because the Way was rooted in his mind, and his mind was unified through reverence. There was indeed a reason why his reign endured so long and all under Heaven enjoyed peace and order!
Now, at the outset of his service as ruler and teacher, our present emperor exalts the Way of worthily continuing and carrying forward his predecessors’ work. Wherever his civilizing commands reach, even to the seas, people turn toward his influence. He has now inaugurated the Classics Colloquium to assist his governance, and personally visited the Imperial University to guide the reverent dissemination of instruction. As the drum sounds in the side hall, those presenting lectures stand upright as jade, their ceremonial sashes hanging down. Scarcely has the imperial procession halted at the Imperial University when those striking the chime stones and singing elegant songs gather like clouds. The Way is elucidated through the River Chart and Luo Writing, presaging the reappearance of auspicious tortoises and dragons; radiance shines upon the sacrificial vessels, about to draw qilin and phoenixes to grace the court. Truly, he embodies the qualities of the ancient emperors and kings and revives the learning of the ages of Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties. Can anyone say that this is still insufficient to transform all under Heaven?
In antiquity, the royal academy was founded at Haojing, and the songs of Zhou celebrated devoted remembrance and emulation; the academy of Lu was encircled by its jade-like waters, and the Hymns of Lu sang of gathering water celery. I, an unworthy student, have been fortunate to receive the joyful nurture celebrated in the ode of luxuriant mugwort. How could I presume to lag behind those at the bridge gate…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
圜聽之列但稽首揚厲莫罄名言至欲有
補論思槩乎莫知所以雖然竊聞之矣九
九之術敢於賓齊食芹而甘者不知有玉
食而思獻况明問及之敢不攄其一得之
愚哉是故責實者不徇其名美成者在端
其始然則有唐虞三代之舉動矣而猶未
覩其實功有唐虞三代之造端矣而尚未
臻其成效君子能無慮乎姑即今日
皇上之學言之
===
經筵之御崇儒之心也將
經筵之一御而謂足以盡崇儒之實也可乎
大學之臨重道之心也將大學之一臨而
謂足以盡重道之實也可乎故方其
御講之時蓋聞乎聖人之言矣義理之感發必
有勃然而聽之忘倦者吾不知退而優游
泮渙之時猶能尋而繹之以求其精義之
歸乎抑師保之不臨而惟其心之所好以
馳騖於他技已也方其
punctuated:
圜聽之列，但稽首揚厲，莫罄名言。至欲有補論思，槩乎莫知所以。雖然，竊聞之矣：九九之術，敢於賓齊；食芹而甘者，不知有玉食而思獻。况明問及之，敢不攄其一得之愚哉？是故責實者不徇其名，美成者在端其始。然則有唐虞三代之舉動矣，而猶未覩其實功；有唐虞三代之造端矣，而尚未臻其成效，君子能無慮乎？姑即今日皇上之學言之。
