Although these masters were not necessarily all alike in the purity or admixture of their learning, the one who served in the Palace Library won renown among foreign peoples; the one who served as district defender of Xiaoshan was as practiced as a veteran incumbent [?]. Summoned to court, they devised plans for securing the realm and repelling outsiders; governing prefectures, they won trust through benevolent administration. When were they ever deficient in practical achievement? Those who did not attain such achievements simply failed to encounter a favorable time.

As for practical achievement, Li Boji spoke out boldly in a time of peril and uncertainty concerning the administration of the Two He regions; Zeng Mingzhong took the lead in advocating the termination of tribute to the arrogant enemy when it defied the proper order. Military defenses were put in order and national policy settled; Liao and Xia were checked and the ruler’s authority enhanced. Both contributed…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
裨於朝政矣四諫馳聲蔡君謨倡敢言之
氣新法報罷鄭介夫進流民之圖減丁稅
而民利興攻惠卿而主心悟均之有補於
時事矣陳述古當神宗召對疏薦三十三
人於古靈先生之稱何忝劉彥脩以單騎
入秦召諸將分守要害其捍禦西蜀之功
居多呂安老知建康而有防守東南聯絡
淮甸荆蜀之議乃忠臣之謀國也劉仲偃
使金虜而貽主憂臣辱主辱臣死之書乃
===
節士之矢心也之數子者事功之難易未
必其一律然以上十事者明脩德之典擢
三府者審經術之訓講經筵而達知天之
說任防禦而植忠貞之操寧不本於學術
乎其不然者必其學之未純耳此則有宋
人才表著於一代而垂範於後世者也至
我
國家治敎休明英賢繼起尋考亭之緒而追
名德之烈者竊有聞焉以理學名者若蔡
punctuated:
裨於朝政矣。四諫馳聲，蔡君謨倡敢言之氣；新法報罷，鄭介夫進流民之圖。減丁稅而民利興，攻惠卿而主心悟，均之有補於時事矣。陳述古當神宗召對，疏薦三十三人，於古靈先生之稱何忝？劉彥脩以單騎入秦，召諸將分守要害，其捍禦西蜀之功居多。呂安老知建康，而有防守東南、聯絡淮甸荆蜀之議，乃忠臣之謀國也。劉仲偃使金虜，而貽「主憂臣辱，主辱臣死」之書，乃節士之矢心也。之數子者，事功之難易未必其一律，然以上十事者明脩德之典，擢三府者審經術之訓，講經筵而達知天之說，任防禦而植忠貞之操，寧不本於學術乎？其不然者，必其學之未純耳。此則有宋人才表著於一代而垂範於後世者也。
至我國家，治敎休明，英賢繼起。尋考亭之緒而追名德之烈者，竊有聞焉。以理學名者，若蔡
translation_en:
…contributed to the government of the court. As the Four Remonstrators won renown, Cai Junmo fostered a spirit of fearless speech; when the New Policies were ordered rescinded, Zheng Jiefu had submitted his Picture of Displaced People. Reducing the poll tax advanced the people's welfare; attacking Huiqing brought the ruler to his senses. All these acts helped address the affairs of their time. When Emperor Shenzong summoned Chen Shugu for an audience, he recommended thirty-three men in a memorial. How could he have been unworthy of the name Master Guling? Liu Yanxiu rode alone into Qin and summoned the generals to divide responsibility for defending strategic positions; his contribution to the defense of western Shu was especially great. As prefect of Jiankang, Lü Anlao proposed defending the southeast and coordinating the Huai region with Jing and Shu: this was a loyal minister's planning for the state. Liu Zhongyan went as envoy to the Jin barbarians and sent a letter declaring, “When the ruler suffers anxiety, his ministers suffer disgrace; when the ruler suffers disgrace, his ministers must die.” This was a man of integrity pledging his resolve. The accomplishments of these men were not necessarily alike in their difficulty. Yet the man who submitted ten proposals clarified the principles of cultivating virtue; the man promoted through the Three Prefectures [?] closely examined the teachings of classical scholarship. Those who lectured at the imperial Classics Colloquium expounded the doctrine of knowing Heaven, and those entrusted with defense established a steadfast commitment to loyalty. Were these achievements not rooted in learning? Where this was not so, it must have been because their learning was not yet pure. These were the talented men of the Song who distinguished themselves in their age and handed down examples to later generations.
As for our own dynasty, its government and moral instruction are excellent and enlightened, and outstanding worthies have arisen in succession. I have heard something of those who follow the intellectual lineage of Kaoting [Zhu Xi] and emulate the achievements of men renowned for virtue. Among those famed for the Learning of Principle is Cai…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
清之經義精到督學大江飭躬勵行而動
必準諸古人若陳眞晟之篤信好古詣闕
上書功先主敬而言有裨於正學淹貫詞
林一新士類介足以廉頑者其黃仲昭乎
隨事觀理詠歌一貫學足以貞俗者其周
瑛乎篤信力行求底無過者林棋也師道
尊嚴精於禮記者鄭閭也數君子之典刑
具在其有志游楊諸儒之學者乎以事功
顯者若楊榮之歷事四朝望重一代參謀
===
秘閣而剖決機務林聰之正色朝端風裁
屹立首重國本而抗言定儲轉輸不擾犯
顏敢諫論兵得上策而畏之如神明者非
陳俊乎茂敭中外名德益尊終日端坐以
求聖賢氣象者非彭韶乎詣闕登對以得
賢才爲國治之本者吳源也奏開鹽法以
助軍餉著旬宣之集者黃仲芳也數君子
之政績足稱其庶幾李曾諸公之軌者乎
雖然諸君子皆鄉之先哲也其學術事功
punctuated:
清之經義精到，督學大江，飭躬勵行，而動必準諸古人；若陳眞晟之篤信好古，詣闕上書，功先主敬，而言有裨於正學。淹貫詞林，一新士類，介足以廉頑者，其黃仲昭乎？隨事觀理，詠歌一貫，學足以貞俗者，其周瑛乎？篤信力行，求底無過者，林棋也；師道尊嚴，精於禮記者，鄭閭也。數君子之典刑具在，其有志游楊諸儒之學者乎？
以事功顯者，若楊榮之歷事四朝，望重一代，參謀秘閣而剖決機務；林聰之正色朝端，風裁屹立，首重國本而抗言定儲。轉輸不擾，犯顏敢諫，論兵得上策而畏之如神明者，非陳俊乎？茂敭中外，名德益尊，終日端坐以求聖賢氣象者，非彭韶乎？詣闕登對，以得賢才爲國治之本者，吳源也；奏開鹽法以助軍餉，著旬宣之集者，黃仲芳也。數君子之政績足稱，其庶幾李曾諸公之軌者乎？
雖然，諸君子皆鄉之先哲也，其學術事功
translation_en:
…Cai Qing’s interpretations of the Classics were precise and penetrating. Supervising education in the Great River region [?], he disciplined himself and strove to improve his conduct, taking the ancients as his standard in every action. Likewise, Chen Zhensheng held firm to his convictions and loved antiquity. He went to the imperial court to submit a memorial, gave priority in his efforts to maintaining reverent attentiveness, and spoke in ways that benefited orthodox learning. Profoundly versed in literary scholarship, renewing the community of scholars, and possessed of an integrity sufficient to make the morally obtuse honest—was this not Huang Zhongzhao? Observing principle in each affair, giving poetic expression to the single thread that unites all things, and possessing learning sufficient to rectify popular customs—was this not Zhou Ying? Lin Qi held firm to his convictions and put them resolutely into practice, seeking to attain freedom from error. Zheng Lü upheld the dignity of the teacher’s calling and was expert in the Book of Rites. The exemplary models of these gentlemen remain fully before us. Were they not men who aspired to the learning of such Confucians as You and Yang?
Among those distinguished by practical achievements were Yang Rong, who served four successive reigns, enjoyed great prestige in his age, and participated in deliberations in the palace’s inner councils, resolving crucial affairs of state; and Lin Cong, who maintained a stern bearing at court and stood unshakably firm in his principled judgment, placing the foundation of the state first and speaking out forcefully to secure the designation of an heir apparent. Managing transport of supplies without disturbing the people, daring to remonstrate even at the risk of imperial displeasure, and devising the best strategies in military deliberations, so that others feared him as though he were a divine being—was this not Chen Jun? Winning distinction in service both at court and in the provinces, gaining ever greater esteem for his reputation and virtue, and sitting upright throughout the day in pursuit of the bearing of the sages and worthies—was this not Peng Shao? Wu Yuan went to court and was received in audience, holding that obtaining worthy and talented men was the foundation of good government. Huang Zhongfang memorialized to open up the salt system to help fund military provisions and compiled the Collection on Proclaiming Imperial Benevolence (Xunxuan zhi ji) [?]. The administrative achievements of these gentlemen deserve praise. Did they not come close to following the path of such gentlemen as Li and Zeng?
Nevertheless, these gentlemen were all earlier worthies of our home region. As for their learning and practical achievements…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
吾不得而優劣之矣然以思齊之志而尚
論乎有宋諸賢則學術以朱元晦爲準焉
事功以李伯紀爲準焉元晦之學本於致
知而主於居敬至於上陳封事則以天下
大本今日急務爲言蓋惓惓然用世之心
也伯紀之志在於攘夷而主於死守至於
平生所得則著爲易傳內外篇論語詳說
蓋惓惓然窮理之學也嗟乎學術之不講
此事功之所以日卑也蓋甞聞之位天地
===
育萬物而其功始於慎獨治國平天下而
其功始於致知此則體用合一吾儒之事
也是故以萬古爲一心而後其道明學術
端矣以萬物爲一體而後其道行事功顯
矣愚也竊有志焉毋曰卑之無甚高論
第五問
林庭植
同考試官教諭伍 批 推究兵食之弊在於本源
處省約切中時宜而末復歸重得人尤識大體取之
punctuated:
吾不得而優劣之矣。然以思齊之志而尚論乎有宋諸賢，則學術以朱元晦爲準焉，事功以李伯紀爲準焉。元晦之學本於致知而主於居敬，至於上陳封事，則以天下大本、今日急務爲言，蓋惓惓然用世之心也。伯紀之志在於攘夷而主於死守，至於平生所得，則著爲《易傳內外篇》《論語詳說》，蓋惓惓然窮理之學也。嗟乎！學術之不講，此事功之所以日卑也。蓋甞聞之：位天地，育萬物，而其功始於慎獨；治國平天下，而其功始於致知。此則體用合一，吾儒之事也。是故以萬古爲一心，而後其道明，學術端矣；以萬物爲一體，而後其道行，事功顯矣。愚也竊有志焉，毋曰「卑之，無甚高論」。

第五問
林庭植
同考試官教諭伍批：推究兵食之弊，在於本源處省約，切中時宜；而末復歸重得人，尤識大體，取之。
translation_en:
…I cannot rank them as superior or inferior. Yet, aspiring to equal the worthy and looking back to discuss the worthies of the Song, I take Zhu Yuanhui as the standard in learning and Li Boji as the standard in practical achievement. Yuanhui’s learning was rooted in extending knowledge and centered on maintaining reverent attentiveness. When he submitted sealed memorials to the throne, he spoke of the fundamental basis of the realm and the urgent tasks of the day: this surely reveals his earnest desire to serve the world. Boji’s ambition lay in repelling the barbarians, and his guiding commitment was to defend to the death. Yet he set down what he had learned over his lifetime in the Inner and Outer Chapters of the Commentary on the Book of Changes and Detailed Explanations of the Analects: this surely reveals his earnest pursuit of learning through investigating principle.

Alas! The neglect of learning is why practical achievement declines day by day. I have heard that the work of bringing Heaven and Earth into their proper places and nurturing the myriad things begins with vigilance over oneself when alone; and that the work of governing the state and bringing peace to all under Heaven begins with extending knowledge. This unification of substance and function is the undertaking of us Confucians. Thus, only by sharing one mind with all ages can one illuminate the Way and set learning aright; only by forming one body with the myriad things can one put the Way into practice and make practical achievement manifest. In my humble way, I aspire to this. Do not say, “Bring it down; do not discourse too loftily.”

Fifth Question
Lin Tingzhi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: He traces the defects in military affairs and provisions to their source, proposing economy at the root of the problem in a way that precisely meets present needs. At the end, he again places the emphasis on securing the right men, showing an especially sound grasp of the larger essentials. Accept him.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教授何批兵食詘乏久矣比來欲得國
士共濟時艱子獨能推本弊源條陳經略豈其人耶
考試官教授吳批究心時政是抱先憂者
考試官教授李批經畫時務切中肯綮
執事以
國家大計下詢承學顧愚不足奉明問然竊
見鄉之父兄長老甞歷事
先朝多能明習世故其於財賦兵馬盈縮强
弱之筭往往條分縷析若指言家人事時
===
愚旣竊聽之以爲時事如此而當事者猶
或持之而不敢議何歟於是退而稽之史
冊則知古之忠臣智士其深謀遠慮每每
憂盛世而危明主非過計也以爲如此則
治不如此則亂當漢文時海內號稱乂安
矣乃賈誼則以爲今天下事勢譬如抱火
厝之積薪之下火未及燃因謂之安其戇
如此絳灌諸人忌之不卽見用殆其後卒
如誼言豈不有遺恨哉洪惟我
punctuated:
同考試官教授何批：兵食詘乏久矣，比來欲得國士共濟時艱，子獨能推本弊源，條陳經略，豈其人耶？
考試官教授吳批：究心時政，是抱先憂者。
考試官教授李批：經畫時務，切中肯綮。
執事以國家大計下詢承學，顧愚不足奉明問。然竊見鄉之父兄長老甞歷事先朝，多能明習世故，其於財賦兵馬盈縮强弱之筭，往往條分縷析，若指言家人事。時愚旣竊聽之，以爲時事如此，而當事者猶或持之而不敢議，何歟？於是退而稽之史冊，則知古之忠臣智士，其深謀遠慮，每每憂盛世而危明主，非過計也。以爲如此則治，不如此則亂。當漢文時，海內號稱乂安矣，乃賈誼則以爲：「今天下事勢，譬如抱火厝之積薪之下，火未及燃，因謂之安。」其戇如此，絳灌諸人忌之，不卽見用，殆其後卒如誼言，豈不有遺恨哉！洪惟我
translation_en:
Associate Examiner He, Professor, comments: “Troops and provisions have long been inadequate. Recently we have sought men of outstanding ability to help us through these difficult times. You alone have traced the abuses to their source and set out strategic measures point by point. Could you be such a man?”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “He devotes his mind to current government affairs: here is one who worries before others do.”
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “His plans for current affairs strike precisely at the crucial points.”
You, honored examiners, have condescended to consult us students on the great affairs of state, though I am unworthy to answer your discerning questions. Yet I have observed that the fathers, elder brothers, and elders of my native place who served under former reigns are often thoroughly versed in worldly affairs. In their reckoning of the abundance or shortfall of revenues and the strength or weakness of military forces, they frequently distinguish and analyze every detail, as though discussing their own household affairs. Having listened to them, I thought: if present affairs are in such a state, why do those responsible still sometimes hold back and dare not discuss them? I then withdrew and examined the historical records. I came to understand that the loyal ministers and wise men of antiquity, in their profound planning and far-reaching foresight, often worried in prosperous times and feared danger for enlightened rulers. Their calculations were not excessive. They believed that acting thus would bring order, while failing to do so would bring disorder. In the time of Emperor Wen of Han, all within the seas was reputed to be peaceful and well governed. Yet Jia Yi thought: “The present situation of the realm is like taking fire and placing it beneath a pile of firewood: because the fire has not yet flared up, one calls it safe.” Such was his blunt candor. The Marquis of Jiang and Guan Ying and their associates resented him, and he was not immediately employed. When events afterward ultimately turned out as Jia Yi had predicted, could this fail to leave lasting regret? Reverently considering our …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏建都金陵薄海内外悉
歸版圖財賦所入不可勝紀然邊防要害
獨重西北當時經略率皆勳舊重臣企我
成祖文皇帝再造邦家定鼎燕京金湯之固僅
隔山後與虜爲鄰其勢蓋岌岌矣
成祖深思遠處列爲重鎭以防守之猶且以兵
在内則内重在外則外重於是立爲三大
營以固根本以備征伐景泰以後又更爲
十二團營故當其時内自京師外自九邊
===
猛將材官雲興雷奮以討則强以守則固
執事所謂東南財賦西北戎馬蓋謂此也
然愚甞考當時太倉之粟在江南者其初
止運七十萬石其後乃運至二百四十萬
石乃其後則歲漕四百萬石矣折色之銀
每歲四百餘萬兩以其半輸在
内府至於馬價料銀供應之需又歲以數十
萬計此外又有抽分之稅餘鹽之括開納
之例財賦所入視昔不啻加倍矣
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏，建都金陵，薄海内外悉歸版圖，財賦所入不可勝紀。然邊防要害，獨重西北，當時經略率皆勳舊重臣。企我成祖文皇帝再造邦家，定鼎燕京，金湯之固，僅隔山後，與虜爲鄰，其勢蓋岌岌矣。成祖深思遠處，列爲重鎭以防守之，猶且以兵在内則内重，在外則外重，於是立爲三大營，以固根本，以備征伐。景泰以後，又更爲十二團營。故當其時，内自京師，外自九邊，猛將材官，雲興雷奮，以討則强，以守則固。執事所謂東南財賦、西北戎馬，蓋謂此也。
然愚甞考當時太倉之粟，在江南者，其初止運七十萬石，其後乃運至二百四十萬石，乃其後則歲漕四百萬石矣。折色之銀，每歲四百餘萬兩，以其半輸在内府。至於馬價料銀、供應之需，又歲以數十萬計。此外又有抽分之稅、餘鹽之括、開納之例，財賦所入，視昔不啻加倍矣。
translation_en:
…Taizu, the Gao Emperor, founded the realm and established his capital at Jinling. All lands within and beyond the seas came under his dominion, and the revenues received were beyond reckoning. Yet among strategic points of frontier defense, the northwest alone held overriding importance. Those entrusted with its strategic management at that time were generally senior ministers of longstanding meritorious service. Looking up to our [?] Chengzu, the Wen Emperor: he renewed the state and established the capital at Yanjing. Its defenses, firm as metal walls and a boiling moat, were separated from the enemy only by the mountains [?]; it neighbored the northern foes, and its position was indeed precarious. Chengzu deliberated deeply and planned far ahead, establishing a series of major garrisons for its defense. He further considered that stationing troops within strengthened the interior, while stationing them outside strengthened the frontier. He therefore established the Three Great Training Divisions to secure the foundations of the state and prepare for military campaigns. From the Jingtai period onward, these were reorganized into the Twelve Regimental Training Divisions. Thus, in those days, from the capital within to the Nine Frontier Commands outside, fierce generals and able fighting men rose like clouds and surged like thunder: powerful in attack and steadfast in defense. This, presumably, is what you mean by “revenues in the southeast and cavalry in the northwest.”
Yet I have examined the grain supplied from Jiangnan to the imperial granary at that time. Initially, only 700,000 shi were transported; subsequently, shipments reached 2,400,000 shi; still later, annual grain shipments by water amounted to 4,000,000 shi. Silver paid in commutation of payments in kind amounted to more than 4,000,000 taels annually, half of which was remitted to the palace treasury. Silver for purchasing horses and fodder, together with provisioning expenses, amounted to several hundred thousand more each year. Beyond these were taxes levied as a share of goods, exactions on surplus salt, and provisions allowing contributions in return for privileges. Compared with former times, revenue receipts had more than doubled.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承皆以樽節愛養爲事嘉靖初年太倉
之粟足支數十年外庫之銀未甞匱乏
內帑積至數千餘萬諸司所藏亦略稱是愚
甞攷弘治以前公私盈足減租寬稅之
詔猶屢下焉馴至今日內外遂稱詘乏此其故
何也得非土木荐興而賞賚無算乎抑
請討多而物力屈也團營之兵舊稱十二萬景
泰間縮三之一在今則又縮焉至於各邊
之兵尤可寒心宣大薊鎮今日所最急者
===
然將領所部每不能足額數督撫者甞招
募矣而鮮有應之者此又何也愚觀
成祖時甞頻年用兵而兵力最盛景泰弘治間
亦屢用兵西北而累立戰功頃自庚戌之
變虜數內犯然內外諸將兢兢固守未聞
以數萬營陣待敵者也今內自團營外至
九邊動稱兵數不足東抽西補朝募夕招
是何廩廩然也得非軍政廢弛而變通未
講乎抑繩法過而事權輕也夫以財賦則
punctuated:
列聖相承，皆以樽節愛養爲事。嘉靖初年，太倉之粟足支數十年，外庫之銀未甞匱乏，內帑積至數千餘萬，諸司所藏亦略稱是。愚甞攷弘治以前，公私盈足，減租寬稅之詔猶屢下焉。馴至今日，內外遂稱詘乏，此其故何也？得非土木荐興而賞賚無算乎？抑請討多而物力屈也？

團營之兵，舊稱十二萬，景泰間縮三之一，在今則又縮焉。至於各邊之兵，尤可寒心。宣大薊鎮，今日所最急者，然將領所部每不能足額數。督撫者甞招募矣，而鮮有應之者，此又何也？愚觀成祖時，甞頻年用兵，而兵力最盛。景泰弘治間，亦屢用兵西北，而累立戰功。頃自庚戌之變，虜數內犯，然內外諸將兢兢固守，未聞以數萬營陣待敵者也。今內自團營，外至九邊，動稱兵數不足，東抽西補，朝募夕招，是何廩廩然也？得非軍政廢弛而變通未講乎？抑繩法過而事權輕也？夫以財賦則
translation_en:
The successive sage emperors all devoted themselves to economy and to caring for and sustaining the people. In the early Jiajing reign, the grain in the Grand Granary was sufficient for several decades, and silver in the outer treasury was never lacking. The palace treasury accumulated several tens of millions of taels, and the stores held by the various offices were roughly commensurate. I have examined the period before Hongzhi: public and private resources were abundant, yet edicts reducing rents and easing taxes were still repeatedly issued. Gradually, however, we have reached the present situation, in which both inner and outer treasuries report shortages. What accounts for this? Could it be that building projects have repeatedly been undertaken and rewards bestowed without measure? Or have requests for grants [?] become so numerous that material resources are exhausted?

The troops of the combined training camps formerly numbered, it was said, 120,000. During the Jingtai reign their numbers were reduced by one-third, and now they have been reduced further. As for the troops along the various frontiers, their condition is especially alarming. Xuanfu, Datong, and Jizhou are the garrisons where the need is now most urgent, yet the forces under their commanders repeatedly fall short of their authorized strength. Supreme commanders and grand coordinators have attempted recruitment, but few have responded. Why is this, too? I observe that under Chengzu, campaigns were undertaken year after year, yet military strength was at its height. During the Jingtai and Hongzhi reigns, troops were likewise repeatedly deployed in the northwest and won military distinctions time and again. Since the gengxu crisis of 1550, the enemy has repeatedly invaded our territory, yet the generals both within and beyond the capital have anxiously held to their defenses. We have heard of none taking up positions with tens of thousands of men to await the enemy. Now, from the combined training camps at the capital to the Nine Frontier Garrisons beyond it, every report speaks of insufficient troops. Men are transferred from the east to fill gaps in the west; recruitment proceeds morning and evening. Why is the situation so precarious? Could it be that military administration has fallen into neglect and suitable reforms have not been considered? Or is legal discipline applied too severely, leaving commanders with too little authority? Now, as regards fiscal resources…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
如彼以兵力則如此然則謀國者計將安
出昔有大賈恃其貲裕而荒耽無度僕告
之曰財且匱矣乃驚愕莫知所計僕曰是
無庸慮但去其所以蠹財者耳主人聽之
不數年其裕如初愚竊謂今
國家亦有四蠹焉何者錦衣官校有常額亦
有常祿今傳陞日增投充無數此一蠹也
騰驤四衛卒皆冒遞廠衛緝訪無辜以冒
陞級廩秩日加倉庫日竭此二蠹也光祿
供應費用不貲傳奉口分有數十年仍在
冊者至於厨役多鑽籍冒領此三蠹也各
廠匠作影射百出不能計工程力而支討
眾多此四蠹也頃者言官疏言宜如嘉靖
初年故事汰除一切冗役歲可省粟數十
萬乃至今不見施行何也至於清查
內府儲積已有
明詔矣而尋復報罷自古小人欲蔽主聽而堅
私計不過曰是皆祖宗故事非外廷得與
punctuated:
如彼，以兵力則如此，然則謀國者計將安出？昔有大賈，恃其貲裕而荒耽無度。僕告之曰：「財且匱矣。」乃驚愕，莫知所計。僕曰：「是無庸慮，但去其所以蠹財者耳。」主人聽之，不數年，其裕如初。
愚竊謂今國家亦有四蠹焉。何者？錦衣官校有常額，亦有常祿。今傳陞日增，投充無數，此一蠹也。騰驤四衛卒皆冒遞，廠衛緝訪無辜以冒陞級，廩秩日加，倉庫日竭，此二蠹也。光祿供應，費用不貲。傳奉口分，有數十年仍在冊者；至於厨役，多鑽籍冒領，此三蠹也。各廠匠作，影射百出，不能計工程力，而支討眾多，此四蠹也。
頃者言官疏言，宜如嘉靖初年故事，汰除一切冗役，歲可省粟數十萬。乃至今不見施行，何也？至於清查內府儲積，已有明詔矣，而尋復報罷。自古小人欲蔽主聽而堅私計，不過曰：「是皆祖宗故事，非外廷得與
translation_en:
…are in such a state, while military strength is as described. What course, then, can those who plan for the state devise? Once there was a wealthy merchant who, relying on his ample resources, indulged himself without restraint. His servant told him, “Your wealth is about to run out.” Astonished, he did not know what to do. The servant said, “There is no need to worry about this. Simply eliminate whatever is consuming your wealth.” The master followed this advice, and within a few years he was as prosperous as before.
In my humble view, the state today likewise has four drains upon its resources. What are they? The officers and guardsmen of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard have fixed quotas and fixed stipends. Yet promotions conveyed by imperial command increase daily, and those seeking enrollment are beyond number. This is the first drain. The soldiers of the Four Tengxiang Guards all obtain their places through fraudulent substitution [?], while the secret-service depots and guards investigate and arrest innocent people to secure undeserved promotions. Stipends and salaries increase daily, and the granaries and treasuries are daily depleted. This is the second drain. The provisions supplied by the Court of Imperial Entertainments entail immense expenditure. Some food allowances granted by transmitted imperial commands remain on the registers for decades; moreover, many kitchen workers contrive to enter their names on the registers and claim allowances fraudulently. This is the third drain. In the artisan establishments of the various depots, countless fraudulent claims are made under cover of registered names. The work and labor required cannot be properly reckoned, yet disbursements claimed are numerous. This is the fourth drain.
Recently, remonstrance officials submitted memorials urging that the precedent of the early Jiajing years be followed and all superfluous service personnel eliminated, which could save several hundred thousand units of grain annually. Why has this still not been implemented? As for auditing the reserves of the palace treasuries, an explicit imperial edict had already been issued, yet shortly afterward the undertaking was again reported as canceled. From ancient times, petty men wishing to block their ruler’s access to information and secure their private interests have merely said: “These are all precedents established by the imperial ancestors; officials of the outer court have no right to take part in…”

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
議也然此不難辨矣昔成周以冢宰制國
用玉府天府掌珠玉器寶外府掌布之出
入內府藏九貢九賦之貨賄此皆天子府
藏也而悉太宰掌之漢唐及宋一應財賦
咸掌外府天子未甞置私藏以奸古法惟
我
國家以天下財賦輸其半于
內府以備異時非常之用雖內外賞賜取給
于此而積蓄之富前世莫及長老習聞
===
祖宗所以厚爲貯積者其
淵衷微意所以爲無窮之慮至深遠也豈徒爲
賞賜玩好之資巳乎然事不總於戶部登
耗之數至不可究詰言官所以屢乞查盤
者其慮深矣古者國無三年之蓄曰國非
其國今太倉之粟所贏僅僅如此假令遇
卒然之警漕運阻阨商販不至都城百萬
生靈翹首待哺將何所仰給乎神農之教
曰雖有石城拾仞湯池百步帶甲百萬而
punctuated: 議也。然此不難辨矣。昔成周以冢宰制國用，玉府、天府掌珠玉器寶，外府掌布之出入，內府藏九貢九賦之貨賄，此皆天子府藏也，而悉太宰掌之。漢唐及宋，一應財賦咸掌外府，天子未甞置私藏以奸古法。惟我國家以天下財賦輸其半于內府，以備異時非常之用。雖內外賞賜取給于此，而積蓄之富，前世莫及。長老習聞，祖宗所以厚爲貯積者，其淵衷微意，所以爲無窮之慮，至深遠也，豈徒爲賞賜玩好之資巳乎？然事不總於戶部，登耗之數至不可究詰。言官所以屢乞查盤者，其慮深矣。古者，國無三年之蓄，曰國非其國。今太倉之粟，所贏僅僅如此，假令遇卒然之警，漕運阻阨，商販不至，都城百萬生靈翹首待哺，將何所仰給乎？神農之教曰：「雖有石城拾仞，湯池百步，帶甲百萬，而
translation_en: …to deliberate upon. Yet this is not difficult to refute. In the Zhou dynasty, the Grand Steward regulated state expenditure. The Jade Treasury and Heavenly Treasury administered pearls, jade, precious vessels, and treasures; the Outer Treasury administered receipts and disbursements of currency; and the Inner Treasury stored the valuables received under the nine categories of tribute and nine categories of taxation. These were all the Son of Heaven’s treasuries, yet all were administered by the Grand Steward. Under the Han, Tang, and Song, all revenues were administered by the outer treasury. The Son of Heaven never established a private treasury in violation of the ancient system. Our dynasty alone transfers half the revenues of the realm to the Inner Treasury to provide for extraordinary needs in the future. Although rewards bestowed within and outside the palace are drawn from it, the abundance of its accumulated reserves surpasses that of all previous ages. Our elders have long heard that the ancestors’ purpose in amassing such substantial reserves—the subtle intention in their profound minds—was to provide for the limitless future, with the deepest foresight. Could these reserves have been intended merely to fund rewards and objects of pleasure? Yet because these affairs are not administered centrally by the Ministry of Revenue, even the figures for additions and depletion cannot be ascertained. The officials charged with remonstrance have repeatedly requested an inventory because their concerns run deep. In antiquity, it was said that a state without three years’ reserves was no longer truly a state. Now the grain surplus in the Imperial Granary is scarcely more than this. If a sudden emergency were to arise, grain transport by canal were obstructed, and merchants failed to arrive, on what would the capital’s million souls depend for sustenance as they craned their necks awaiting food? Shennong’s teaching says: “Even with stone walls ten ren high, moats of boiling water a hundred paces wide, and a million armored soldiers, yet…”

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
無粟不能守也若是豈可不爲寒心哉夫
夫庶民之家終歲經營必計口而議先期
而戒彼固未甞有敵國外患之虞也然猶
兢兢然若此而況公卿大夫爲
國家深長之思可以冥焉決事哉且愚所謂
四蠹者至易見也當事者固難之愚謂
主上所親信而甞禮貌者非左右與勳舊乎此
皆身享榮寵而世受爵祿也且當
主上虛心圖治臣子效忠之時而積蠹夙弊不
===
肯一洗而更之使當國之臣勞心焦思而
莫知所計臺諫之臣持議而不已此愚所
以竊致望於左右勳舊之臣也執事復謂
九邊惟宣大爲急當時所藉屯田鹽法今
皆廢壞督撫諸臣所以爲戰守計者非
請討則莫可爲計此誠今日坐困之術也顧愚
非知邊計者然甞竊聞宣大一鎭所以馴
致積弱而不可振起者其失有四而其弊
有五不可不知也何謂四失邊備乆弛醜
punctuated:
無粟不能守也。若是，豈可不爲寒心哉！夫夫庶民之家，終歲經營，必計口而議，先期而戒。彼固未甞有敵國外患之虞也，然猶兢兢然若此，而況公卿大夫爲國家深長之思，可以冥焉決事哉？且愚所謂四蠹者，至易見也，當事者固難之。愚謂主上所親信而甞禮貌者，非左右與勳舊乎？此皆身享榮寵而世受爵祿也。且當主上虛心圖治、臣子效忠之時，而積蠹夙弊不肯一洗而更之，使當國之臣勞心焦思而莫知所計，臺諫之臣持議而不已。此愚所以竊致望於左右勳舊之臣也。
執事復謂九邊惟宣大爲急，當時所藉屯田、鹽法，今皆廢壞，督撫諸臣所以爲戰守計者，非請討則莫可爲計。此誠今日坐困之術也。顧愚非知邊計者，然甞竊聞宣大一鎭所以馴致積弱而不可振起者，其失有四，而其弊有五，不可不知也。何謂四失？邊備乆弛，醜
translation_en:
…without grain, it cannot be defended.” In such circumstances, how could one fail to be chilled with apprehension? Now, an ordinary household [?] manages its affairs throughout the year, necessarily reckoning the mouths to feed when making its plans and taking precautions in advance. Such people have never had to fear enemy states or external troubles, yet even they exercise such vigilance. How much less, then, may the highest ministers and other officials decide matters blindly when devising far-reaching plans for the state? Moreover, the four sources of corruption I have mentioned are exceedingly easy to discern, yet those responsible find them difficult to address. I would ask: are those whom His Majesty trusts and has treated with courtesy not his close attendants and the veteran servants of meritorious service? They personally enjoy honor and favor, while their families receive titles and emoluments generation after generation. At this very time, when His Majesty seeks good government with an open mind and his servants should render loyal service, they are unwilling to sweep away accumulated corruption and longstanding abuses and reform them. They leave the ministers directing affairs to exhaust their minds in anxious deliberation, unable to devise a course of action, while the censors and remonstrance officials press their arguments without cease. This is why I venture to place my hopes in His Majesty’s close attendants and veteran meritorious servants.
You further state that, among the Nine Frontier Commands, only Xuanfu and Datong are in urgent straits. The military agricultural colonies and salt system on which they formerly depended have now both fallen into ruin. The supreme commanders and grand coordinators can devise no plans for warfare and defense unless they petition for funds and supplies. This is indeed a way of remaining trapped in our present difficulties. I am no expert in frontier affairs, but I have heard that the reason the Xuanfu–Datong command [?] gradually sank into entrenched weakness from which it could not recover lies in four failings and five abuses. These must be understood. What are the four failings? Frontier defenses have long been neglected, and the vile…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
虜跳梁擺邊築牆歲無寧日軍民所種屯
田虜歲蹂踐子粒所入不能侔本遂致抛
荒其失一也商人自括餘鹽爭趨便易邊
地苦寒孰肯委身荒塞以務耕作鹽法一
廢屯田愈壞其失二也山東河南坐派邊
糧逋負過半有司催迫後期法令不行其
失三也每歲糴買商人託藉勢要所買米
豆半係參和且拖欠數多雖重懲艾之莫
能止其失四也如是則邊費安得不耗
===
請討安得不困哉何謂五弊古者兵將同心乃
可制敵今各邊將領罷遷不常視所部卒
何異傳舍此一弊也兵法曰視卒如子乃
可俱死今各邊將領掊尅軍士習成故套
此二弊也兵法嚴隊伍均犒賞今挑選標
下名為選鋒隊伍缺亂賞賜偏異三軍之
心先自怨望如是欲其同冒矢石難矣此
三弊也妄報聲息輒移信地虛糜行糧習
為得計此四弊也醜虜內入競相規避及
punctuated:
虜跳梁，擺邊築牆，歲無寧日。軍民所種屯田，虜歲蹂踐，子粒所入不能侔本，遂致抛荒，其失一也。商人自括餘鹽，爭趨便易；邊地苦寒，孰肯委身荒塞以務耕作？鹽法一廢，屯田愈壞，其失二也。山東河南坐派邊糧，逋負過半，有司催迫後期，法令不行，其失三也。每歲糴買，商人託藉勢要，所買米豆半係參和，且拖欠數多，雖重懲艾之，莫能止，其失四也。如是，則邊費安得不耗，請討安得不困哉？
何謂五弊？古者兵將同心，乃可制敵。今各邊將領罷遷不常，視所部卒何異傳舍？此一弊也。兵法曰：「視卒如子，乃可俱死。」今各邊將領掊尅軍士，習成故套，此二弊也。兵法嚴隊伍，均犒賞。今挑選標下，名為選鋒，隊伍缺亂，賞賜偏異，三軍之心先自怨望。如是，欲其同冒矢石，難矣！此三弊也。妄報聲息，輒移信地，虛糜行糧，習為得計，此四弊也。醜虜內入，競相規避，及
translation_en:
…the enemy run rampant. Troops are deployed along the frontier and walls are built, yet no year passes in peace. The enemy trample each year the garrison farmland cultivated by soldiers and civilians. The grain harvested cannot cover the cost, and the fields are consequently abandoned. This is the first failing. Since the collection of surplus salt was instituted [?], merchants have competed to pursue easier profits. The frontier is bitterly cold: who would willingly settle in its desolate borderlands to cultivate the soil? Once the salt system fell into disuse, garrison farming deteriorated still further. This is the second failing. Shandong and Henan are assigned quotas of grain for the frontier, but more than half remains in arrears. Despite the responsible officials’ urgent demands, deadlines are missed, and the regulations go unenforced. This is the third failing. In the annual grain purchases, merchants rely on powerful patrons; half the rice and beans purchased are adulterated, and large quantities remain undelivered. Even severe punishment cannot stop this. This is the fourth failing. Under these circumstances, how can frontier funds avoid depletion, and how can requests for further supplies escape difficulty?
What are the five abuses? In antiquity, soldiers and commanders shared one purpose and could therefore subdue the enemy. Nowadays, commanders throughout the frontier are dismissed or transferred unpredictably. How is their treatment of the troops under them any different from their treatment of a posting inn? This is the first abuse. The Art of War says: “Regard your soldiers as your sons, and you can face death together.” Nowadays, commanders throughout the frontier exploit their soldiers, and habitual practice has become an established routine. This is the second abuse. Military principles require strict unit organization and equitable rewards. Nowadays, men are selected for the commander’s personal contingent, ostensibly as picked troops, leaving their units depleted and disordered. Rewards are distributed unequally, so resentment already fills the army’s ranks. Under these circumstances, it is difficult indeed to expect them to brave arrows and stones together! This is the third abuse. They submit false reports of enemy movements and readily shift away from their assigned posts, needlessly consuming marching provisions, and habitually regard this as a clever expedient. This is the fourth abuse. When the vile enemy invade, they compete to evade them, and when…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
至退邀冒殺平民以報功次此五弊也如
此則邊政安得不壞兵勢安得不弱哉執
事者更欲求為長策以救目前愚則謂四
失不去五弊不除雖使孫吳為將良平畫
策恐亦難矣雖然請試言之夫三軍之命
在將將得其人則事可成功可就兵法能
制生殺之謂將能專予奪禍福之謂將今
各邊所置總督鎮巡皆古大將之任也顧
今不能殺一偏裨建一奇策稍有更張則
===
持議者且接踵矣是欲其彎弓落羽而束
之手也豈事理也哉雖然所謂大將者未
易言也必極選才望出羣者然後可以當
之選才望矣必專事權以任之事權專矣
又必久任以責之成昔漢宣任充國宋祖
任郭進讒言無所投謗毀無所加斯可謂
能任將矣愚觀頃年所置大將其初固皆
以才推也一遭人言非罪則罷此於
國家御將之體亦稍陵夷矣在今日所當急
punctuated: 至退，邀冒殺平民以報功次，此五弊也。如此則邊政安得不壞，兵勢安得不弱哉？執事者更欲求為長策以救目前，愚則謂四失不去，五弊不除，雖使孫吳為將，良平畫策，恐亦難矣。雖然，請試言之。夫三軍之命在將，將得其人，則事可成，功可就。兵法：能制生殺之謂將，能專予奪禍福之謂將。今各邊所置總督鎮巡，皆古大將之任也。顧今不能殺一偏裨、建一奇策，稍有更張，則持議者且接踵矣。是欲其彎弓落羽而束之手也，豈事理也哉？雖然，所謂大將者未易言也。必極選才望出羣者，然後可以當之。選才望矣，必專事權以任之；事權專矣，又必久任以責之成。昔漢宣任充國，宋祖任郭進，讒言無所投，謗毀無所加，斯可謂能任將矣。愚觀頃年所置大將，其初固皆以才推也，一遭人言，非罪則罷，此於國家御將之體亦稍陵夷矣，在今日所當急
translation_en:
…when the enemy withdraws, they intercept them and fraudulently claim credit, killing ordinary civilians to report military achievements [?]. This is the fifth abuse. Under such circumstances, how could frontier administration fail to deteriorate, and military strength fail to weaken? You gentlemen in charge further seek a long-term strategy to remedy the immediate situation. In my humble view, unless the four failings and five abuses are eliminated, even with Sun Wu and Wu Qi as generals, and Zhang Liang and Chen Ping devising strategies, success would remain difficult, I fear.

Nevertheless, let me attempt to explain. The lives of the entire army depend upon its general. With the right man as general, undertakings can be accomplished and achievements secured. According to the principles of warfare, one who controls life and death is called a general; one who has sole authority to grant and withdraw, to punish and reward, is called a general. The supreme commanders, regional commanders, and grand coordinators now appointed along the frontiers all bear the responsibilities of the great generals of antiquity. Yet today they cannot execute even a subordinate commander or put forward an unconventional strategy. At the slightest change, critics come one after another. This is to ask a man to draw his bow and bring down a bird while binding his hands. How can that accord with reason?

Nevertheless, appointing such a great general is no simple matter. One must select with the utmost care a man whose ability and standing surpass those of his fellows; only then can he fill the post. Once such a man has been selected, he must be entrusted with exclusive authority over his responsibilities. Once that authority is secured, he must also be retained for a long tenure and held accountable for results. When Emperor Xuan of Han employed Zhao Chongguo, and the founding emperor of Song employed Guo Jin, slander found no opening and calumny could not touch them. This may truly be called knowing how to employ generals.

I observe that the great generals appointed in recent years were indeed all initially recommended for their abilities. Yet once someone speaks against them, they are either punished or dismissed. In this, the state's manner of managing its generals has also somewhat declined. This is something that today urgently requires…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
圖也雖然愚前所謂四失五弊則何如以
處之亦曰誠得大將而任之專託之久而
又不能去四失除五弊是則將之罪也始
則切責之甚則罷斥之又甚則加罪焉恐
未有不思奮者矣雖然猶未也執事欲求
國家長久至計愚以為其本不在邊鎮而在
朝廷其患不在夷狄而在紀綱執事倘與其
進則願更僕以對焉
punctuated: 圖也。雖然，愚前所謂四失五弊，則何如以處之？亦曰：誠得大將而任之專，託之久，而又不能去四失、除五弊，是則將之罪也。始則切責之，甚則罷斥之，又甚則加罪焉，恐未有不思奮者矣。雖然，猶未也。執事欲求國家長久至計，愚以為其本不在邊鎮而在朝廷，其患不在夷狄而在紀綱。執事倘與其進，則願更僕以對焉。
translation_en: …a matter to be addressed. Yet how should the four failings and five abuses I mentioned earlier be dealt with? I would simply say: if a truly capable commander is found, entrusted with exclusive authority, and retained for a long term, yet still cannot eliminate the four failings and five abuses, then the fault lies with him. First reprimand him sternly; in more serious cases dismiss him; in still more serious cases impose punishment. I doubt that any would then fail to exert themselves. Yet even this is not enough. If you, sir, seek the best plan for the enduring security of the state, I believe its foundation lies not in the frontier garrisons but in the imperial court, and that the danger lies not in the foreign peoples but in the governing order and discipline. If you, sir, permit me to advance my argument further [?], I would willingly continue my reply even until the attendants must be relieved.

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄後序
是歲我
皇上文命肇敷屬天下有司大比
士閩雖遠在海隅顧其士業
已聞
皇上仁孝久及覩
登極以來
===
璽書頒布炳炳乎視聽一新莫不
嚮應景從願爲帝臣與天下
士相望奮翼起也雲龍風虎
玆非其期哉御史王宗載蓋
自
上前受
明詔來策有司諸執事有司諸執
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄後序

是歲，我皇上文命肇敷，屬天下有司大比士。閩雖遠在海隅，顧其士業已聞皇上仁孝久，及覩登極以來璽書頒布，炳炳乎視聽一新，莫不嚮應景從，願爲帝臣，與天下士相望奮翼起也。雲龍風虎，玆非其期哉？御史王宗載蓋自上前受明詔，來策有司諸執事。有司諸執
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In this year, our emperor’s civilizing influence began to spread, and it was time for the responsible officials throughout the realm to conduct the triennial examination of scholars. Though Fujian lies far away in a corner by the sea, its scholars had long heard of the emperor’s benevolence and filial piety. When they witnessed the promulgation of imperial letters under seal following his accession, their brilliance renewed all that they saw and heard. All responded like an echo and followed like a shadow, wishing to become servants of the emperor and, looking toward their fellow scholars throughout the realm, to spread their wings and rise. Clouds follow the dragon, winds follow the tiger: was this not the appointed moment?

The Censor Wang Zongzai had received the illustrious edict in the emperor’s presence and came to spur on the responsible officials and all those charged with administering the examination. The responsible officials and all those charged with…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
事莫不凜凜奉
詔冀得名實純粹之士而登用之
庶幾稱
上意事旣竣御史又率所得士就
有司賓禮之迪不佞從諸執
事後得有言曰夫士以一日
之遇至見賓禮有司則人人
以為華卽有司者亦以為人
人賢且能而收之華固宜也
將人人賢且能乎結軔入
帝庭當使閩重於九鼎大呂不則
徒豪舉耳迪竊懼焉蓋聞知
人則哲自昔難之故百年一
聖猶浹旬也千里一賢猶比
punctuated: 事莫不凜凜奉詔，冀得名實純粹之士而登用之，庶幾稱上意。事旣竣，御史又率所得士就有司賓禮之。迪不佞，從諸執事後，得有言曰：「夫士以一日之遇，至見賓禮有司，則人人以為華。卽有司者，亦以為人人賢且能而收之，華固宜也。將人人賢且能乎？結軔入帝庭，當使閩重於九鼎大呂；不則徒豪舉耳，迪竊懼焉。蓋聞『知人則哲』，自昔難之。故百年一聖，猶浹旬也；千里一賢，猶比
translation_en:
…all the functionaries reverently obeyed the imperial decree, hoping to obtain and promote men whose reputations and actual qualities alike were pure, and thereby perhaps fulfill His Majesty’s wishes. When the proceedings were completed, the Censor also led the selected scholars to the responsible officials, who honored them with the rites accorded to guests. I, Di, unworthy as I am, followed behind the other functionaries and had occasion to say:

“When scholars, through a single day’s fortunate encounter, come to be honored as guests by the responsible officials, each regards it as a distinction. The officials, too, have selected them believing every one worthy and capable, so such distinction is certainly fitting. But will every one prove worthy and capable? When they prepare their carriages [?] and enter the imperial court, they ought to make Fujian weightier than the Nine Tripods and the great Lü bell. Otherwise, this will have been merely a grandiose undertaking. I, Di, privately fear this outcome. For I have heard that ‘to know men is wisdom,’ and this has been considered difficult since antiquity. Thus, even one sage in a hundred years would be like one in every ten days; even one worthy in a thousand li would be like men standing side by …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
肩也况一日而舉九十人又
欲人人賢且能不已過望乎
顧臣子以人事君之義誠欲
有所託以自效爾且閩故無
諸裔壤也入漢始以提封通
中國唐宋以來人文較著儒
術彬彬視鄒魯間逮我
===
國家政教畫一遠邇同文閩士
尤多崛起纓紱相屬金石流
輝非復無諸時風氣矣然文
勝則史聖人敝之今之閩士
豈患不文患文之過而掩質
其執宜亟挽也會
明詔方以質文取士士遂能以質
punctuated:
肩也。况一日而舉九十人，又欲人人賢且能，不已過望乎？顧臣子以人事君之義，誠欲有所託以自效爾。

且閩故無諸裔壤也，入漢始以提封通中國。唐宋以來，人文較著，儒術彬彬，視鄒魯間。逮我國家，政教畫一，遠邇同文，閩士尤多崛起，纓紱相屬，金石流輝，非復無諸時風氣矣。然文勝則史，聖人敝之。今之閩士，豈患不文？患文之過而掩質，其執宜亟挽也。會明詔方以質文取士，士遂能以質
translation_en:
…would still stand shoulder to shoulder. How much more so when ninety men are selected in a single day: to wish that every one of them be worthy and capable—is this not hoping for too much? Yet, in keeping with a subject’s duty to serve his ruler by providing men of talent, I sincerely wish to entrust this responsibility to others and thereby render service myself.

Moreover, Fujian was formerly the remote territory of Wuzhu. Only under the Han did its lands enter into relations with the Central States. Since the Tang and Song, its cultural achievements have been conspicuous and Confucian learning has flourished, comparable to that of Zou and Lu. Under our dynasty, government and instruction have been unified, and places far and near share a common written culture. Particularly numerous are the scholars of Fujian who have risen to prominence: one officeholder follows another, and their glory shines forth in inscriptions on metal and stone. The prevailing spirit is no longer that of Wuzhu’s time. Yet when refinement outweighs substance, one becomes a mere scribe—a fault the Sage deplored [?]. Could today’s Fujian scholars possibly be deficient in refinement? The concern is that excessive refinement obscures substance; this tendency [?] should urgently be checked. It so happens that an enlightened imperial edict now calls for selecting men on the basis of substance and refinement, and the scholars have accordingly been able to respond with substance …

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
文應之譬則縣黎結緑不眩
而珎干將鏌耶不拭而銛其
俗稡然一變則
聖人之興風動之乎孟氏甞謂有
王者作其間必有名世者此
一時也士豈無以名世自待
具曰有司望之過乎且夫元
===
聖誦讀于莘丘尚父屠釣于
棘澤非不至微賤也一遭湯
文則釋耒投竿舉商周而大
造之功加四海澤流無窮茲
我
皇上明聖在位鼎運方隆湯文不
足王矣然且拊髀降顔拔沈
punctuated: 文應之。譬則縣黎、結緑，不眩而珎；干將、鏌耶，不拭而銛。其俗稡然一變，則聖人之興風動之乎？孟氏甞謂有王者作，其間必有名世者。此一時也，士豈無以名世自待，具曰有司望之過乎？且夫元聖誦讀于莘丘，尚父屠釣于棘澤，非不至微賤也。一遭湯、文，則釋耒投竿，舉商、周而大造之，功加四海，澤流無窮。茲我皇上明聖在位，鼎運方隆，湯、文不足王矣。然且拊髀降顔，拔沈
translation_en:
…refinement in responding to it. They are like the precious jades Xuanli and Jielü, treasured without dazzling the eye, or the swords Ganjiang and Moye, sharp without polishing. If their customs have suddenly undergone a complete transformation, has the rise of the sage moved them as the wind does? Master Meng once said that when a true king arose, there would surely be men renowned in their age among his contemporaries. This is such a time. How could scholars fail to expect themselves to attain such renown, and all say [?] that the officials expect too much of them?

Moreover, the Primal Sage, Yi Yin, recited and studied at Shenqiu, while the Grand Preceptor, Lü Shang, butchered and fished at Jize. Their circumstances were indeed exceedingly humble. Yet once they encountered Tang and King Wen, they laid aside their ploughs and cast away their fishing rods, taking up the affairs of Shang and Zhou and accomplishing great things for those dynasties. Their achievements reached throughout the Four Seas, and their beneficence flowed on without end. Now our Emperor, enlightened and sagely, occupies the throne, and the fortunes of the dynasty are flourishing. Even Tang and King Wen cannot equal him as rulers [?]. Yet still he slaps his thigh in eagerness, assumes a gracious countenance, and raises up those sunk in obscurity…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
搜逸思得莘丘棘澤之賢與
共理諸士得無意乎始迪得
士之文也其言侃侃便便各
軌於道計不須臾見其人今
予得士之容也其儀濟濟師
師各度于衷計不須臾試諸
事此無他心竊愛之故望之
===
不敢不過也謂言不足概則
叔向之薦鬷蔑魏子之舉賈
辛不惟其言乎謂容不足符
則胥臣之遇卻缺然明之知
國僑不惟其容乎至謂言與
容可以盡人則雖孔門之徒
猶以為失之宰予失之子羽
punctuated:
搜逸，思得莘丘、棘澤之賢，與共理，諸士得無意乎？始迪得士之文也，其言侃侃便便，各軌於道，計不須臾見其人；今予得士之容也，其儀濟濟師師，各度于衷，計不須臾試諸事。此無他，心竊愛之，故望之不敢不過也。
謂言不足概，則叔向之薦鬷蔑、魏子之舉賈辛，不惟其言乎？謂容不足符，則胥臣之遇卻缺、然明之知國僑，不惟其容乎？至謂言與容可以盡人，則雖孔門之徒，猶以為失之宰予、失之子羽，
translation_en:
…seeking out those living in obscurity, wishing to find worthies like those of Shenqiu and Jize with whom to share the work of governing. Can you gentlemen have no such aspirations? When I, Di, first obtained the candidates’ writings, their words were forthright and eloquent, each conforming to the Way, and I expected shortly to meet the men themselves. Now that I have observed their bearing, their deportment is dignified and respectful, each conforming to the proper measure within, and I expect shortly to put them to the test in practical affairs. There is no other reason for this: in my heart I cherish them, and so I cannot help setting exceptionally high hopes upon them.
If one says that words are insufficient to gauge a man, were not Shuxiang’s recommendation of Zong Mie and Weizi’s promotion of Jia Xin based precisely on their words? If one says that bearing is insufficient evidence, were not Xuchen’s encounter with Xi Que [卻缺, transcription doubtful] and Ran Ming’s recognition of Guo Qiao based precisely on their bearing? Yet if one claims that words and bearing can reveal a person completely, even among the disciples of Confucius there were what he regarded as errors of judgment concerning Zai Yu and Ziyu…

title: 隆慶元年福建鄉試錄
text:
迪閔然滋惑矣此無他心竊
望之故懼之不敢不至也且
取士數十人一人爾遇者縣
次續食登名天府不遇者返
其蓬蒿居焉使遇者之言徒
以自媒而卒不爲賴於民社
卽蓬蒿之士猶得脩其質而
===
全之比見自媒者之不爲賴
也且相與目笑之矣諸士其
圖之昔者宋人得寶於梧臺
之東周客索而觀之曰此燕
石也越人學遠射彎弓仰天
而發矢落五步之內諸士行
矣射當及遠且使有司者得
punctuated:
迪閔然滋惑矣。此無他，心竊望之，故懼之不敢不至也。且取士數十人，一人爾。遇者縣次續食，登名天府；不遇者返其蓬蒿居焉。使遇者之言徒以自媒，而卒不爲賴於民社，卽蓬蒿之士猶得脩其質而全之。比見自媒者之不爲賴也，且相與目笑之矣。諸士其圖之！

translation_en:
…I, Di, am troubled and increasingly perplexed. This is for no other reason than that I privately place hopes in them, and therefore cannot help being deeply apprehensive for them. Moreover, of several dozen candidates, only one is selected. Those who find favor receive provisions at successive county stages and have their names entered in the registers of the imperial government; those who do not return to their weed-grown dwellings. If the words of those who find favor serve merely to recommend themselves, and they ultimately prove of no benefit to the people and the altars of the soil and grain, the scholars among the weeds can still cultivate their essential character and preserve it intact. When they see that those who recommended themselves prove of no benefit, they will exchange glances and laugh at them. You scholars should consider this!
Once a man of Song found a treasure east of Wutai. A visitor from Zhou asked to examine it and said, “This is a stone from Yan.” A man of Yue learned to shoot at distant targets: he bent his bow, aimed at the sky, and let fly, but his arrow fell within five paces. 愉快哉
江西廣信府儒學敎授吳迪

punctuated:
無若宋人有失寶也，豈不爲愉快哉？

江西廣信府儒學敎授吳迪謹序。
translation_en:
…not be like the man of Song who lost his treasure. Would that not be a delight?

Preface respectfully composed by Wu Di, Professor of the Prefectural Confucian School of Guangxin, Jiangxi.
